subject: chore(ty): bump ty to 0.0.74 (#26496)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Bumps the pinned `ty` (Astral type checker) version from `0.0.69` to `0.0.74` and fixes the 19 errors surfaced by the new version (→ 0/0). 0.0.74 is the latest release >=48h old.

### Pin + lockfiles

`pyproject.toml` + `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml`: `ty==0.0.69` → `ty==0.0.74`. Both relocked (`just rebuild_uv_lock_file` for the root lock; `python dagster-oss/scripts/update_lockfiles.py dagster` for the dagster per-package lock) so all three ty envs (`master`, `data-platform`, `internal`) and the workspace venv pick up the new version. Both lock diffs are exactly the ty swap.

### Code fixes

The 19 errors reduce to 6 root causes, all fixed with minimal narrowing/annotation changes:

- **`EntitySubset` generic mixing in `dep_operators.py`** (2): ty now flags `compute_union`/`compute_intersection` calls mixing `EntitySubset[AssetKey]` with `EntitySubset[T_EntityKey]` — two targeted `# ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]`, matching that file's existing style for the same pattern.

- **TypedDict dynamic-key assignment in `dagster_cloud_agent.py`** (6): `resource_limits` is a `CloudContainerResourceLimits` TypedDict keyed by deployment type, but the write site keys it dynamically with the enum's `.value` (which includes `docker`/`unknown`, excluded at runtime by a `supports_utilization_metrics` guard ty can't see) and assigns a generic dict. One `cast("dict[str, Any]", ...)` at the write site.

- **`asyncio.to_thread` TypeVar inference in ursula** (5): ty 0.0.74 no longer solves `_zlib_deserialize`'s `T_PackableValue` through `to_thread`'s ParamSpec, leaving an unsolved TypeVar in the result union. Wrapped both call sites in a zero-arg lambda so the TypeVar resolves at the direct call; behavior identical.

- **Deliberately-invalid args in `test_check.py`** (2): tests exercising runtime `CheckError` on wrong-typed args (`check.failed(0)`, `check.not_implemented(None)`) get inline `# ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]`, matching the file's existing style.

- **Optional narrowing in `test_utils.py`** (3): `span_ref` starts as `None` and is assigned inside `with` blocks; `assert span_ref is not None` before each `.error` check.

- **`alert_policy_ids` contract in `test_notifications.py`** (1): `_replace(alert_policy_ids=...)` passed a `list[str]` where the field is declared `AbstractSet[str]`; wrapped in `set(...)`.

- **Stale email snapshots in `test_notifications.ambr`** (piggybacked fix): the alert email logo was moved from the Webflow CDN to S3 without regenerating snapshots, and the path-triggered e2e alert suite doesn't run on master, so the breakage only surfaced when this PR touched `test_notifications.py`. Updated the 185 snapshot occurrences to the S3 URL.

## Test Plan

- `just ty` → 0 errors / 0 warnings across all three envs (7277 files).
- `just ruff` → clean.
- ty conventions tests (`tox -e py312-conventions -- -k ty`, includes `test_ty_version_pins_agree` and `test_ty_config_consistency`): 454 passed.
- Full e2e alert suite (`tox -e py312 -- dagster_cloud_e2e_tests/alert_tests` in dagster-cloud-e2e): 1075 passed.

Internal-RevId: ff6839d8f64f8442f968a317778faacf52e013e9

subject: Split serverless v2 IO storage into assets and runs keyspaces (#26455)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

First half of the retention work from the memo [IO storage handling in
serverless
v2](https://app.notion.com/p/dagster/IO-storage-handling-in-serverless-v2-3bc18b92e4628022bf95f32a92f0c5b8):
make run-scoped op outputs (unique key per run, currently retained
forever) targetable by an S3 lifecycle policy. The policy itself lands
in the stacked #26482.

- S3 lifecycle rules can only filter on a leading key prefix, but op
outputs live at `io_storage/org-{org}/dep-{dep}/storage/{run_id}/...` —
the discriminating segment is mid-key, so no rule can target them today.
- Ursula now presigns against **split keyspaces, unconditionally**:
asset values under `io_storage/assets/org-{org}/dep-{dep}/...` and
run-scoped op outputs under `io_storage/runs/org-{org}/dep-{dep}/...`. A
key is run-scoped only when its second segment is a UUID (the run id) —
a bare `storage/` check would misclassify user asset keys that
legitimately start with `storage/`, and misclassification into the runs
keyspace would mean silent expiration of asset data.
- No feature gate: every org on v2 is internal (7 dogfood test orgs,
`devsuccess` + one test org in prod) and the v2 buckets hold <1000
objects (<100 KB) across all environments, so the layout flips at deploy
for everyone and the legacy `io_storage/org-...` root is deprecated
immediately. Splitting both classes now gives a clean terminal state
instead of the root prefix permanently doubling as the asset namespace.
- GET/HEAD requests fall back to the legacy keyspace when the primary
misses (objects written before the deploy, including in-flight runs
during the rollout), then to the serverless v1 bucket. The v1 fallback's
Statsig gate is removed too: it is now enabled per-environment by the v1
storage env configuration, since forgetting to enable it per-org before
cutover would break a migrated org's reads — orgs without v1 data are
unaffected (a fallback presign against their empty v1 prefix 404s
exactly like the primary would have). After deploy, a one-time sweep
moves legacy objects to their split keys; a small follow-up PR then
deletes the legacy fallback and the exists-check HEAD it adds to reads.
- The v1→v2 copy job targets the assets keyspace, skips run-scoped keys
by the same UUID discriminator (so `storage/`-prefixed *assets* are now
copied — previously they were skipped and depended on the v1 fallback
forever), and never overwrites a value present in either v2 keyspace.
- The serverless IO manager's missing-input error now mentions that
non-asset outputs expire, so re-executing an old run fails with an
explanation instead of a bare "not found".
- Cutover now needs exactly two Statsig gates, in order:
`serverless_v1_io_storage_copy_on_provision`, then
`serverless_k8s_provisioning`.

Deferred: the legacy-fallback removal follow-up (after the post-deploy
sweep), and a dagit-side warning when re-executing runs older than the
retention window.

## Test Plan

- Ursula endpoint tests: per-method keyspace targeting (runs and
assets), UUID-only run-scoped classification (`storage/`-prefixed asset
keys land in the assets keyspace), legacy-keyspace fallback and
primary-keyspace preference for both key classes, v1 fallback chaining
and its env-configuration switch. `tox -e py312-default -- -k
test_io_storage`: 35 passed.
- Copy-job tests: assets-keyspace destination, UUID skip discriminator,
and either-keyspace never-overwrite (a stale v1 value must not shadow a
legacy-keyspace v2 write).
`dagster_cloud_backend_tests/serverless_tests`: 83 passed.
- `just ruff`, `just quick-ty` clean.
- The v1→v2 migration path with the pre-split revision of this change
was verified end-to-end on dogfood (org `sean-v1v2-migration-test`: v1
seed → cutover → copy → fallback reads → v2 writes); after merge +
deploy, the split layout and the post-deploy legacy sweep will be
re-verified there before customer cutovers.

Internal-RevId: 554d743fb709fb6354d5fc054eda6c0e220f5449

subject: Fix docs Vercel builds: ignore Vercel's curated uv Python index (#26467)
body:
Docs preview deploys have failed since ~Aug 18 with `error: No download
found for request: cpython-3.11-linux-x86_64-gnu` on every docs-touching
PR.

**Root cause (confirmed by the passing run on this PR):** Vercel's
updated build image preinstalls uv and injects
`UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS_JSON_URL=/uv/python_metadata.json`, pointing Python
downloads at a local curated metadata file that does not include CPython
3.11 for linux-x86_64. uv therefore reports 'No download found' even
though the build exists in the official index. Ruled out along the way:
uv version regressions (0.12.5 resolves 3.11 fine locally and in x86_64
Amazon Linux 2 Docker), `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=automatic` handling, and
glibc floors.

**Fix:** unset Vercel's uv download/mirror overrides and pass
`--no-config` before `uv python install`, so uv uses the official
python-build-standalone index. Also logs the resolved uv binary and
injected `UV_*` env in build output for future forensics.

The docs deploy on this PR is green with these changes.

- This follows up on #26451 (merged earlier): no revert needed — it's
orthogonal and mildly good (consistent uv version every build instead of
image roulette).

- Heads up for platform team: (1) the Vercel project is pinned to Node
20.x, and Vercel says deployments will hard-fail after Oct 1 — the
"engines": {"node": "24.x"} bump is a ticking clock, and moving off the
old image might also get Vercel's curated index updated as a side
effect; (2) worth telling Vercel their /uv/python_metadata.json omits
CPython 3.11 — we can't be the only ones hitting this.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [dagster-ui] Abort sensor tick apply on dynamic partition permission errors (#26293)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

`SensorDryRunDialog`'s "Apply requests & commit tick result" flow
launched runs even
when `createPartition` / `deletePartition` had failed. The backend
returns
`UnauthorizedError` and `PythonError` as *members of the union*
(`AddDynamicPartitionResult`, `DeleteDynamicPartitionsResult`), so
Apollo resolves
the mutation successfully and the frontend never inspected `__typename`.

For a user without `EDIT_DYNAMIC_PARTITIONS` — e.g. a Launcher-role user
in
Dagster+ — the partition was silently not created and the run launched
against it
anyway.

Two layers now guard it:

1. **Up front** — the dialog reads `canEditDynamicPartitions` via
`usePermissionsForLocation` and refuses to apply when the tick carries
dynamic
   partition requests, surfacing the permission's own disabled reason.
2. **Per mutation** — each result is switched on `__typename`, so an
`UnauthorizedError` / `PythonError` returned *despite* the permission
check
   aborts the apply instead of falling through to launching runs.

The correct fix is an atomic mutation that creates partitions and
launches runs
together; that's out of scope here.

### Note on copybara

`copy.bara.sky` syncs `origin_files = glob(["dagster-oss/**"])` from
internal
master → `dagster-io/dagster` master with `authoring.pass_thru`. So
**merging this
also lands the upstream change**, which is why #34054 could stay closed
rather
than being reopened separately.

## Test Plan

Applied the OSS diff verbatim (`git apply --directory=dagster-oss
--3way`); all 4
files applied cleanly against current master.

In `dagster-oss/js_modules/ui-core`:

```
tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json                     0 errors
eslint (the 4 changed files)                       clean
jest src/ticks/__tests__/SensorDryRunDialog.test.tsx   9 passed, 9 total
```

Backend contract checked — the string the frontend now looks up is the
one the
Dagster+ backend emits:

```
dagster_cloud_backend/permissions/constants.py:119
  CloudPermissions.EDIT_DYNAMIC_PARTITIONS = "edit_dynamic_partitions"
```

**Dogfood verification (the point of this PR):** as a user *without*
`EDIT_DYNAMIC_PARTITIONS`, open a sensor dry run whose tick requests
dynamic
partitions and hit "Apply requests & commit tick result" — expect an
"Insufficient permissions" dialog and **no run launched**. Then confirm
a user
*with* the permission still applies successfully, since layer 1 gates on
the
permission being present in the location's permission set.

## Changelog

Sensor dry run "Apply requests & commit tick result" no longer launches
runs when
creating or deleting dynamic partitions fails due to insufficient
permissions.

Internal-RevId: d869a1bb005376b1d44ec71285f74f566e613fd2

subject: chore(ruff): bump ruff to 0.16.2 and clear surfaced lint (#26359)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Bumps `ruff` from `0.15.15` to `0.16.2` and clears the lint/format diff
the new version surfaces. This is a bigger bump than usual because
0.16.0 made two significant default-behavior changes: the default lint
rule set expanded from 59 to 413 rules, and the formatter now formats
Python code blocks in Markdown files.

## Pin sites and lockfiles

All six pin sites updated: root `pyproject.toml`,
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml` (×2: `test` and
`ruff` extras), `python_modules/purina/pyproject.toml`,
`public/skills/dagster-skills-evals/pyproject.toml`, and
`required-version` in `dagster-oss/config/ruff.toml`.

Beyond the usual two lockfiles (root `uv.lock` via `just
rebuild_uv_lock_file`, dagster's via `update_lockfiles.py`), seven more
dagster-oss lockfiles pinned the old ruff through their path dependency
on dagster's extras and were relocked with `update_lockfiles.py`:
`docs`, `examples/docs_snippets`, `examples/with_great_expectations`,
`examples/assets_pandas_type_metadata`,
`examples/docs_projects/project_components_pdf_extraction`,
`libraries/dagster-ge`, and `libraries/dagster-dg-cli`. These would
otherwise fail lockfile-staleness checks in CI.

## Lint changes

`just ruff` at 0.16.2 found 178 diagnostics; 108 auto-fixed at default
safety and 48 more with `--unsafe-fixes`. The autofix diff is dominated
by RUF036 (`None` moved to the end of unions, newly stabilized) plus
assorted comprehension cleanups, stale-`noqa` removals, and typing
modernization. One explanatory comment dropped by the union-reordering
fix in `dagster_shared/serdes/serdes.py` was restored by hand.

Hand fixes for the non-autofixable residue:

- **UP035** in `_core/types/{config_schema,dagster_type,decorator}.py`:
replaced deprecated `typing.AbstractSet` with `collections.abc.Set as
AbstractSet` (existing repo convention) and `typing.Type` with builtin
`type`.
- **B020/PLR1704** in `_core/types/python_dict.py`: renamed a loop
variable that shadowed the `value` argument it iterates.
- **DTZ005** in `project_multi_tenant` schedules and the
`databricks-delta` lakehouse component: `datetime.now()` →
`datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (demo-data timestamps and schedule-tag
fallbacks are now tz-aware).

Config-level ignores where the newly-defaulted rules are wrong for the
context:

- `project_dspy`: `BLE001` (example code deliberately catches broad
exceptions when scoring LLM output) and `RUF012` (same class-attribute
false-positive class the shared config ignores globally). These files
are embedded in docs via snippet markers, so `noqa` comments would leak
into rendered docs.
- `dagster-skills-evals`: `PLR0917` (too-many-positional-arguments,
newly stabilized) alongside the existing `PLR0913` ignore — typer CLI
commands legitimately take many parameters.
- `project_multi_tenant`: `UP017` — the project targets py311 so ruff
wants `datetime.UTC`, but the ty master env type-checks examples at
Python 3.10 (dagster's minimum) where that symbol doesn't exist.

## Markdown formatting

102 `.md` files had their Python code fences reformatted (~1,700 lines)
by the new default Markdown formatting. Kept rather than excluded via
`format.exclude`: CI's `ruff format --check` enforces it, and the repo
precedent (0.15.0 bump) was to adopt new formatter defaults wholesale.
Spot-checked the largest diffs (`MIGRATION.md`, `CHANGES.md`, docs
guides) — all benign style normalization inside valid-Python fences.

## Test Plan

- [x] `just ruff` clean (`All checks passed!`, formatter no-op on second
run).
- [x] `just ty` clean (`Found 0 errors / Found 0 warnings`, 7257 files)
across all three ty environments — confirms the unsafe-fix import
deletions and the `typing.AbstractSet`/`typing.Type` replacements don't
break annotation resolution.
- [x] `rg` confirms no lockfile anywhere still references
`ruff==0.15.15`.

Internal-RevId: 56253058f2358df14a7a0ea4345dbf4eca23f75c

subject: [app-managed-components] forward RefreshComponentState through the pex proxy (#26277)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Clicking "refresh" on a component state failed on PEX/serverless
deployments with `UNIMPLEMENTED: Method not implemented!`, surfaced as a
`DagsterUserCodeUnreachableError`. `DagsterPexProxyApiServer` never
forwarded the RPC, so the call died at the proxy hop even though both
the agent and the code server implement it correctly.

### Root cause

`DagsterPexProxyApiServer` (dagster_cloud/pex/grpc/server/server.py)
subclasses the generated `DagsterApiServicer` and proxies through an
explicit hand-written allowlist. Any method not in that list inherits
the generated stub, which returns UNIMPLEMENTED / "Method not
implemented!".

- #24231 (RefreshComponentState) added the RPC to the proto, generated
stubs, client.py, server.py, and proxy_server.py — but not to the pex
proxy.
- #24008 (ReloadCodeWithState), one day later, did add its pex forward.

That asymmetry is why fast reload worked and refresh didn't, from the
same UI on the same deployment. Both ends were healthy: the agent has
the client, and 1.13.16 contains the server handler (the commit ships in
the 1.13.15 and 1.13.16 tags). Only the middle hop was missing.

### Changes

- dagster_cloud/pex/grpc/server/server.py — add the
RefreshComponentState forward.
- dagster/_grpc/client.py — extract
DEFAULT_REFRESH_COMPONENT_STATE_TIMEOUT = 300 (was an inline literal)
and use it on both sides.

## Test plan

ruff and ty clean; the 6 existing test_refresh_component_state.py tests
pass.

Internal-RevId: 900242b72694a757f7ca95af236031ba177c2ba7

- `pyproject.toml` + `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml`: `ty==0.0.44` → `ty==0.0.69`. Both relocked (`just rebuild_uv_lock_file` for the root lock; `python dagster-oss/scripts/update_lockfiles.py dagster` for the dagster per-package lock) so all three ty envs (`master`, `data-platform`, `internal`) and the workspace venv pick up the new version.
- The root relock also prunes `aiomonitor` and six transitive deps (`aioconsole`, `janus`, `telnetlib3`, etc.) — stale lock entries whose declaring dependency was removed long ago; no pyproject references them.

## Config: `pydantic-discarded-extra-argument` ignored

ty 0.0.69 ships a new `pydantic-discarded-extra-argument` rule that misfires on Dagster's dynamically-generated pydantic models (the `Resolvable` machinery, `AssetAttributesModel`, dbt/sling component models) — it can't see the synthesized fields, so it flagged 36 kwargs in passing tests as "discarded". The rule is set to `ignore` in the shared `[tool.ty.rules]` block, applied identically to all four config files per the `test_ty_config_consistency` lint.

## Code fixes

The remaining 61 errors + 4 warnings reduce to ~20 root causes, all fixed with minimal narrowing/annotation changes:

- **`get_log_keys_for_log_key_prefix` return type** (`Sequence[Sequence[str]]` → `Sequence[list[str]]`, base + 5 impls): abstract `Sequence` has no `__lt__`, so `sorted()` over the result failed in 7 test files. All impls already return list-of-lists. One follow-up in `read_log_lines_for_log_key_prefix` (`log_keys.index(list(...))`).
- **New `invalid-method-override` rule**: 5 inline `# ty: ignore[invalid-method-override]` on long-standing diamond-inheritance designs (`ConfigurableIOManagerFactoryResourceDefinition`, `NestedResourcesResourceDefinition`, `CodeReferencesMetadataValue`, `DgClickCommand`/`DgClickGroup`), keeping the rule live for new code. Two more targeted `# ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]` in `dep_operators.py`, matching that file's existing style for `EntitySubset` generic mixing.
- **Closed-TypedDict precision** (ty now checks `closed=True` TypedDicts precisely): the internal buildkite pipeline uses the existing `is_group_step` type guard for sub-step iteration, coerces `label` via `str()`, and `_is_refresh_step` narrows commands with `isinstance` checks.
- **Optional narrowing where `None` was genuinely possible**: tableau `refresh_and_poll_*` return `str | None` — `None` results are now skipped instead of being added to sets typed `AbstractSet[str]`; `asset_failure_emitter` sort key wraps `event.asset_key` in `check.not_none`; back-compat backfill tests assert `end_time is not None` before appending (previously a `None` would have crashed at `max()` anyway); admin-panel deployments listing and docs validator get equivalent guards.
- **`filter_valid_partition_keys` (`MultiPartitionsDefinition`)** now adds the constructed `MultiPartitionKey` instead of the raw `str`, matching its declared `set[MultiPartitionKey]` return type. String value is identical since dimensions are stored name-sorted.
- **Unbound `ParamSpec` annotations dropped** in `dagster_graphql/implementation/utils.py`: `require_permission_check`/`check_permission` used `*args: P.args` in decorators not generic over `P`, so the annotations never bound anything.
- **Duplicate `T` TypeVars**: dropped the shadowing redefinition in `_core/utils.py`; renamed the second, differently-bounded one in `defs_module.py` to `T_LoadContext`.
- **Heterogeneous-dict inference**: explicit `dict[str, Any]` at the declaration site for k8s `pipes.py` pod spec, `docker_run_launcher.py` container kwargs, ECS executor `_run_task_kwargs`, and k8s workspace `container_config`.
- **Misc**: wrong `list[dict[str, None]]` annotations in `test_secrets.py` → `dict[str, Any]`; `re.compile(x).search(y)` → `re.search(x, y)` in two asset-job tests (untyped pattern arg made ty infer `Pattern[str] | Pattern[bytes]`); redundant `cast("bytes", ...)` removed in azure-live tests; telemetry `metadata` annotated `dict[str, Any]`; `keywords: list[str]` annotation in `interpolate_sql.py`.

# How I Tested These Changes

- `just ty` → 0 errors / 0 warnings across all three envs (7257 files).
- `just ruff` → clean.
- ty conventions tests (`test_ty_version_pins_agree`, `test_ty_config_consistency`, and the rest of the monorepo-integrity conventions suite matching `ty`): 454 passed.

subject: [oss+cloud] Expose WARNING materialization status through GraphQL, alerts, and UI (#26005)
body:
## Summary

Exposes the WARNING materialization status (an asset whose current
failures are all pending an auto-retry) through GraphQL and alerts. This
PR is deliberately the **rollout-safe half** of the change — see
"Rollout" below.

**GraphQL**: adds `AssetHealthMaterializationWarningPartitionedMeta` /
`WarningNotPartitionedMeta` records and registers matching graphene
types on the `AssetHealthMaterializationMeta` union, but
`get_materialization_status_and_metadata` keeps returning WARNING with
the degraded metadata shapes (which existing frontends and API clients
already fragment on, so they keep receiving `failedRunId` / partition
counts for warning assets).

**Alerts**: `materialization_status_and_details` previously handled only
HEALTHY/DEGRADED and returned None otherwise, which would have silently
dropped the materialization line from Slack/Teams/email notifications
for assets in WARNING. It now renders a "Failed, retry pending" line,
reading the degraded metadata shapes the server currently emits for
WARNING. PagerDuty and webhooks pass raw status strings through and need
no changes. Issue creation links remain DEGRADED-only: a transient
retry-pending failure should not spawn an issue.

**UI**: the asset health popover metadata switch now renders no detail
line for union members this bundle does not know, instead of throwing
(`assertUnreachable`), so future union additions degrade gracefully in
cached bundles. WARNING assets render the existing "Execution warning"
header with the degraded failure detail line.

## Rollout

The union types ship in the schema one release before anything queries
or returns them. The release-branch `gql (new JS, old server)`
backcompat check typechecks the current JS against the deployed prod
schema, so a PR that adds fragments on new union types in the same
release that introduces them fails at release time — and worse, deployed
bundles throw on unknown metadata typenames. Splitting means: this
release makes the schema and bundles ready; #26300 (do not merge until
this release is deployed) flips the server to the Warning metadata
shapes and renders the "retry pending" details in the UI.

## How I tested

`yarn tsgo`, `yarn eslint`, and jest on `AssetHealthSummary.test.tsx`
(10 tests, including WARNING rendering with degraded metadata and the
unknown-typename fallback). All materialization-health GraphQL tests
pass via `tox -e py312-graphql_test_suites`, including a new partitioned
up-for-retry test. Warning/materialization notification snapshot tests
pass via the dagster-cloud-e2e suite. OSS health-state unit tests, `just
ruff`, and `just ty` clean. GraphQL codegen artifacts regenerated via
`scripts/generate_graphql.py`.

subject: SnowflakeDbtProjectComponent follow-up: sensor cursor/dedup fixes, subset-safe results, configurable defs_state (#26056)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Follow-up to dagster-io/dagster#33926 (`SnowflakeDbtProjectComponent`,
preview) addressing findings from review of that PR. All changes are in
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-snowflake`.

**Observation-sensor cursor could eventually double-report
Dagster-triggered runs.** The sensor dedupes runs via a `QUERY_TAG`
lookup in `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY`, which retains only ~7 days
(and at most 10k rows). Previously the cursor only advanced past runs
that produced events, so a Dagster-triggered run (or a run without
locatable artifacts, e.g. `parse`) kept the cursor pinned before it;
once its tag aged out of `QUERY_HISTORY`, the sensor would mis-report it
as an external run. The cursor now advances past every processed history
row, and the tag lookup is bounded with `END_TIME_RANGE_START` so
`RESULT_LIMIT` can't truncate away the window under consideration on
busy accounts.

**State-refresh `parse` runs are now query-tagged** like execution runs,
so they can never be mistaken for externally-triggered runs by the
sensor.

**Subset execution no longer fails on out-of-subset results.** dbt can
build models beyond the Dagster subset (indirect selection, graph
operators in a user-provided `select`); yielding a `MaterializeResult`
for an unselected asset raises at yield time. Results for unselected
assets are now dropped, mirroring the existing filter for asset checks.

**`defs_state` is now configurable** via the same `DefsStateConfigArgs`
field as `DbtCloudComponent` (previously hard-coded to
`LOCAL_FILESYSTEM`), so Dagster+ deployments can opt into
`VERSIONED_STATE_STORAGE`.

**Optional-dependency gating no longer swallows real import errors.**
The three `__init__.py`s gated the component behind `try/except
ImportError`, which would silently hide it if `dagster_dbt` was
installed but one of the internal symbols the component imports had
moved. They now gate on `importlib.util.find_spec("dagster_dbt")` so
genuine import errors surface. (Whether `dagster-snowflake` should
depend on `dagster-dbt` private APIs at all is left as a separate
question for the dbt integration owners.)

## Test Plan

Extended the unit suite (34 → 36 tests, all passing): cursor advancement
past Dagster-tagged and artifact-less history rows (fails without the
fix), dropped results for unselected assets, bounded `QUERY_HISTORY`
SQL, query-tagged parse run ordering in state refresh, and `defs_state`
default/override behavior. `just ty` clean on the package; ruff
format/check clean.

subject: FE-1181: Scope asset sidebar search to the assets shown in the sidebar (#26146)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Second half of
[FE-1181](https://linear.app/dagster-labs/issue/FE-1181/sort-sidebar-asset-list-alphabetically-and-scope-search-to-visible).
The alphabetical-sort half is #26145 .

The asset graph sidebar's "Jump to…" search was built from
`allAssetKeys` — every asset in the workspace — while the tree beneath
it is built from the current graph selection (`assetGraphData`, falling
back to `fullAssetGraphData` when the selection is empty). So the search
could surface assets that aren't in the sidebar at all, and picking one
silently rewrote the explorer's `opsQuery` to go fetch them — a
surprising way to lose your current view.

Search entries now come from the same `graphData.nodes` the tree is
built from, so every result is a row the user can actually be taken to.
Purely client-side filtering/sorting over data already in memory; no new
queries.

## Changes

- Added `sidebar/searchValues.ts` with `buildSidebarSearchValues()`,
which turns the sidebar's graph nodes into search entries sorted
alphabetically by displayed label (full key as tiebreaker), matching the
order of the sidebar rows.
- `Sidebar.tsx` builds `SearchFilter` values from `graphData.nodes`
instead of `allAssetKeys`.
- Dropped the now-unused `allAssetKeys` prop from
`AssetGraphExplorerSidebar` and its call site in
`AssetGraphExplorer.tsx`. The outer `AssetGraphExplorer` still uses
`allAssetKeys` for its loading/error gate — only the prop threading into
the sidebar is gone.

Two refinements that follow from the candidate set now being smaller and
able to contain assets that share a leaf name:

- Queries match the fully-qualified key as well as the displayed label,
so both `orders` and `raw/orders` find the asset keyed `['raw',
'orders']`.
- Results whose label is ambiguous within the candidate set show their
**namespace** (the key minus its leaf segment) after the label — `orders
raw` / `orders staging`. Menu items are also keyed on the full key
instead of the label, which was never unique.

## Storybook

There was no story coverage for the sidebar search box, so this adds
four stories under **Asset Graph/Sidebar SearchFilter**, rendered at the
sidebar's real width and autofocused so the menu is open on load:
`Distinct Labels`, `Duplicate Labels`, `Long Paths`, `Searchable By
Namespace`. Values are built through `buildSidebarSearchValues` so the
stories exercise the same derivation and ordering as production rather
than a hand-written list.

The `Long Paths` story earned its keep immediately — it exposed a layout
bug in the first version of this PR. `MenuItem`'s `right` slot has
`flex-shrink: 0`, so a long qualifier placed there never yields and
instead crushes the label, which is the primary information. With deeply
nested keys the label was reduced to a single glyph on one row and
disappeared entirely on the next. Two fixes, neither touching the shared
`.menuItemRight` rule (it governs every menu in the app):

1. The qualifier now renders inside the label slot, which already
truncates with an ellipsis, so the pair degrades as one string and the
label stays readable.
2. Showing the namespace rather than the full key removes the redundant
leaf, which shortens the qualifier enough that realistic keys no longer
truncate at the sidebar's width at all.

Verified in both light and dark themes.

## Test Plan

- New `sidebar/__tests__/searchValues.test.ts` (9 cases): entries scoped
to the given graph, empty graph, label/path/namespace shape, empty
namespace for single-segment keys, namespace for deeply nested keys,
value resolvable via `graphData.nodes[value]` (what `selectNode` does),
sorting by displayed label rather than full key, tiebreak ordering for
shared labels, and independence from graph insertion order.
- New `sidebar/__tests__/SearchFilter.test.ts` (6 cases) covering
`ambiguousLabelsIn`, including the >2-duplicates and case-differing
edges.
- `yarn jest src/asset-graph` in `ui-core` — 80 passed, 7 suites.
- `yarn tsgo` and `yarn lint` clean in `ui-core`; `yarn tsgo` clean in
`app-cloud`. `yarn build-storybook` succeeds with all four stories in
the index.

A render test asserting the qualifier appears was attempted and
abandoned: the Suggest menu is virtualized and renders no rows under
jsdom even with element measurements stubbed. The ambiguity logic is
unit-tested via `ambiguousLabelsIn` and the rendering is covered by the
stories.

## Notes for review

- Both this PR and #26145 edit the import block of `Sidebar.tsx`, so
whichever lands second needs a one-line fixup there (#26145 removes
`getDisplayName` from the `./util` import along with its only remaining
caller; this PR adds `./searchValues` and removes the `AssetKey`
import). No logical overlap otherwise.
- Both PRs independently define a "sort by displayed label, tiebreak on
full key" comparator, in `sidebar/util.tsx` and
`sidebar/searchValues.ts` respectively. Worth collapsing into one helper
once both have landed.

## Changelog

The asset graph sidebar's search now only matches assets that are
present in the sidebar, matches on the full asset key as well as the
displayed name, lists results alphabetically, and shows the namespace of
results whose name is ambiguous.

subject: FE-1181: Fix asset sidebar sorting to use display names instead of full keys (#26145)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

https://linear.app/dagster-labs/issue/FE-1181/sort-sidebar-asset-list-alphabetically-and-scope-search-to-visible

https://linear.app/dagster-labs/issue/UI-22/sort-sidebar-asset-list-alphabetically-and-scope-search-to-visible

The asset sidebar was sorting assets by their full asset key IDs rather
than by the display names shown to users. This caused confusing ordering
where assets with different key prefixes but the same leaf name (e.g.,
`raw/orders` and `staging/orders` both displaying as "orders") would be
sorted by their full paths instead of alphabetically by the visible
label.

This change fixes the sorting to use the display name (leaf segment of
the asset key) as the primary sort key, with the full key as a
tiebreaker to maintain stable ordering when multiple assets have the
same display name.

## Changes

- Extracted `SIDEBAR_COLLATOR` to `util.tsx` as a shared constant
- Added `compareAssetNodesByDisplayName()` function that sorts by
display name first, then by full key path as a tiebreaker
- Updated `buildRenderedNodes()` and `flattenGroupTree()` to use the new
comparison function instead of sorting by asset ID
- Exported `buildRenderedNodes()` and
`buildRenderedNodesWithCodeLocations()` for testing
- Removed unused `rootNodes` memoization that was computing root assets
- Updated dependency in scroll effect from `rootNodes` to `graphData`

## Test Plan

Added comprehensive unit tests in `Sidebar.test.tsx` covering:
- Assets within a group sorted by display label, not full key
- Groups sorted alphabetically by name
- Assets sorted alphabetically within each group
- Sorting is independent of asset arrival order
- Nested group segments sorted alphabetically at each level

All new tests pass and verify the sorting behavior matches user
expectations.

subject: Bugcrowd CWE 78 spark command injection (#26067)
body:
## Summary & Motivation
Fixes an issue with the Spark integration that was executing a
subprocess with `shell=True`, allowing for `application_arguments` to be
executed as shell instructions instead of being passed to Spark as plain
data.

This could also result in swallowing errors with Spark configuration, as
only the final command's exit code was use to determine whether to
record the result as `SUCCESS`.

See the issue
[here](https://linear.app/dagster-labs/issue/OPER-2963/bugcrowd-cwe-78-os-command-injection-in-dagster-spark-resourcespy)
for the full explanation.

## Test Plan

## Changelog
Fixed the dagster-spark Spark launch path (`create_spark_op` /
`spark_resource`) to invoke `spark-submit` directly as an argument list
rather than through a shell. `application_arguments` is now parsed with
`shlex.split`, so multiple and quoted arguments continue to work, but
shell metacharacters in argument values are no longer interpreted by a
shell.

subject: Bundle PEX-configured serverless builds into tagged Docker images (#26044)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

When a fast-deploy (PEX) build targets Serverless v2 (Kubernetes) — which does not run PEX — the CLI transparently redirects it to a Docker image, so existing fast-deploy customers migrate without changing their build:

- Broadens agent-platform detection to resolve `(SERVERLESS, K8S)` = v2 (previously only Hybrid was inspected).
- Resolves the PEX as usual (`deps.pex` + `source.pex`), then bakes both into a standard Docker image, unpacked into the **default** site-packages via a checked-in Dockerfile template (`pex_bundle.Dockerfile`) — no custom `PYTHONPATH`, since the agent's code-server launch doesn't preserve one.
- Emits a deprecation warning: the fallback is temporary; migrate via `ENABLE_FAST_DEPLOYS=false`.
- Writes a `pex_bundle` marker into the deploy document so the server can identify bundle images.

**Depends on #26046** (server-side `pex_bundle` schema acceptance) being deployed first — otherwise the marker is rejected as an unexpected config entry.

## Test Plan

- `test_pex_to_docker_serverless_v2.py` — detection, redirect predicate, env-var auth, Dockerfile-installs-into-default-site-packages.
- `test_pex_bundle_marker.py` — marker passthrough into the deploy doc.
- `test_plus_deploy_command.py` — end-to-end redirect (warning + `pex_docker` strategy + `ENABLE_FAST_DEPLOYS=false` copy).
- Live (dogfood): redirect → pex resolve → bundle build → Harbor push confirmed. Location load blocked by an unrelated dogfood tenant RBAC issue.

## Changelog

Serverless: fast-deploy (PEX) builds targeting Serverless v2 are now transparently built and deployed as Docker images.

subject: Fix/dagster airbyte single request retry loop (#34032)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

`AirbyteClient._single_request` in `dagster_airbyte/resources.py` placed
`raise Failure` inside the `while` loop at the same indent as
`try/except`, so on any `RequestException` the function raised after one
attempt instead of retrying up to `request_max_retries` times. The `"Max
retries (N) exceeded"` message read the config value via f-string (not
the actual attempt count), which masked the bug at runtime.

Anyone using `dagster-airbyte` with `request_max_retries > 0` (default
3) did not receive retry protection despite the config suggesting
otherwise. In production, this caused a scheduled sync to be cancelled
after ~10 seconds on a single 502 from Airbyte Cloud's
`/v1/applications/token` endpoint, instead of the expected seconds of
retry tolerance.

This PR moves `raise Failure` outside the loop (matching the working
`legacy_resources.py:149` pattern) and drops the now-unreachable `return
{}`.

Fixes #34031.

## Test Plan

Two new tests in `dagster_airbyte_tests/beta/test_resources.py`, both
parametrized across the `cloud` and `oss` fixtures:

- **`test_single_request_retries_on_transient_failure`**: scripts a
fail-fail-success sequence on the token endpoint and asserts (a) the
retry loop iterates through the retries, (b) all three registered
responses are consumed, (c) the client ends up with the refreshed token.
- **`test_single_request_raises_after_exhausting_retries`**: registers
`request_max_retries + 1` persistent 502s and asserts `Failure` is
raised with the exact expected message + the correct total number of
attempts.

Existing tests (`test_refresh_access_token`,
`test_basic_resource_request`) continue to pass, confirming no
regression on the healthy path.

Ran locally:

```
uv run pytest dagster_airbyte_tests/beta/test_resources.py -k "test_refresh_access_token or test_single_request or test_basic_resource_request"
```

All 8 tests pass (4 tests × cloud/oss parametrization).

## Changelog

[dagster-airbyte] Fixed a bug where `AirbyteClient._single_request`
raised `Failure` after one attempt instead of retrying up to
`request_max_retries` times on transient `RequestException`.

subject: [u][fast-reload] K8s orphan defs-state ConfigMap garbage collection (#24355)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fourth PR of the fast-reload sub-stack: garbage-collects defs-state
ConfigMaps whose owning Deployment incarnation no longer exists. Runs
from the launcher's periodic `_graceful_cleanup_servers` pass, after the
base-class server cleanup.

Orphan sources:

- The agent crashed between CM-create and Deployment-create (spinup
deliberately writes the CM first so a racing pod sees the current pin).
- An operator `kubectl delete`'d a Deployment directly, bypassing
`_remove_server_handle` (which normally deletes the CM alongside its
Deployment).

A CM is an orphan iff its name doesn't match
`defs_state_config_map_name(handle.name)` for any live managed
Deployment — the same per-incarnation derivation used at
spinup/reload/removal, so all four paths agree on ownership.

Safety guards:

- Only CMs matching **both** the `managed_by=K8sUserCodeLauncher` label
selector **and** the `dagster-defs-state-` name prefix are considered —
never user-owned ConfigMaps.
- **5-minute creation-age grace period**: because spinup writes the CM
*before* its Deployment, a sweep racing a spinup would otherwise see a
just-created CM as orphaned and delete it. Younger CMs are skipped and
re-judged on a later sweep.
- 404s on delete (lost race with another deleter) are swallowed;
list/delete failures are logged per-namespace without aborting the
sweep; the whole sweep is exception-guarded so it can never break server
cleanup.

## Test Plan

Unit tests: live-incarnation CM skipped; dead incarnation's CM deleted
while the same location's new incarnation CM survives; young orphan
skipped (grace period); missing creation timestamp treated as old;
non-prefixed CM untouched even with our label; 404 swallowed; sweep
ordered after base-class cleanup in `_graceful_cleanup_servers`.

---------

Co-authored-by: Maxime Armstrong <maxime@retain.ai>
Internal-RevId: c0c826dbda243436c15458345d7a9f557d915419

subject: [u][fast-reload] K8s emit override env var; enable fast pin reload for v2 Deployments (#24354)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Third PR of the fast-reload sub-stack: activates the mechanism that the
previous two PRs staged.

1. **Injects `DAGSTER_DEFS_STATE_INFO_OVERRIDE_PATH`** into v2
Deployments, pointing at the CM-mounted file. Env var rather than CLI
arg on purpose: an old `dagster` version in the customer's user-code
image silently ignores an unknown env var, while an unknown CLI flag
would crash-loop the pod. Rollout stays safe when the image lags the
agent.
2. **`supports_in_place_pin_reload`** (K8s override): opts into the base
reconciler's fast path only when (a) non-pex, (b) replica count is 1,
and (c) the *running* Deployment carries the `server-spec-version: v2`
label — read from the cached server handle, so a legacy Deployment
created before the mount existed can never fast-path. Legacy Deployments
keep destroy-and-recreate until a code push naturally rolls them to v2.
3. **`_reload_pin_in_place`** (K8s override): upserts the running
incarnation's ConfigMap (name derived from the cached `handle.name`,
namespace from the handle) and then delegates to the base RPC path.
Ordering matters: the CM is written first so that a pod restart racing
the reload mounts the *new* pin. If the RPC fails, the base class does
not advance `_actual_entries`, so the reconciler retries (and falls back
to full recreate) — the CM being ahead of in-memory state is safe by
design.

Version-skew note: `ReloadCodeWithState` support and the env-var boot
reader ship in the same OSS version. An image too old for the boot
reader is also too old for the RPC, so the RPC fails ⇒ reconciler falls
back to full recreate ⇒ the boot override is never load-bearing on an
image that can't read it.

Known residual window (documented in the `_reload_pin_in_place`
docstring): a brand-new pod mounts the CM fresh from etcd, but a
container restart *within* an existing pod can read the pre-update file
projection for up to the kubelet sync period (~1 min) after a reload,
booting with the previous pin while actual == desired. Closing it
requires the server to report its live pin (e.g. on heartbeat) for the
reconciler to compare — tracked as a follow-up.

## Test Plan

Unit tests: env var injected iff mounted; capability gate true for v2
label and false for legacy label / multi-replica / pex / no cached
server; CM write ordered before the RPC; CM write survives RPC failure
with `_actual_entries` not advanced.

## Changelog

[agent] The Kubernetes agent can now apply state-backed component
updates to a running code server in place (via the new
`ReloadCodeWithState` API) instead of recreating the server, when only
the code location's defs state pin has changed.

---------

Co-authored-by: Maxime Armstrong <maxime@retain.ai>
Internal-RevId: 71efafce9ed59f3796d8ace4dfbf34643a4bc9e6

subject: [u][fast-reload] K8s ConfigMap mount + spec-version label (dormant) (#24353)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Second PR of the fast-reload sub-stack: the K8s launcher creates and
mounts a per-server ConfigMap holding the current serialized
`defs_state_info`, and stamps new Deployments with a
`dagster.io/server-spec-version: v2` label. **Dormant**: the
`DAGSTER_DEFS_STATE_INFO_OVERRIDE_PATH` env var is NOT yet injected
(next PR), so nothing reads the file yet — this PR just starts rolling
out pods with the mount + label so the capability gate can flip upstack.

Design invariants, each of which the tests pin down:

- **Per-incarnation CM naming.** The CM is named
`dagster-defs-state-<sha1(k8s deployment name)>` — keyed on the
uuid-suffixed k8s Deployment resource name, NOT on `(deployment,
location)`. During an update, old and new Deployments for the same
location coexist; if the CM were shared per-location, removing the old
server (including via a delayed pending-delete retry) would delete the
CM out from under the live replacement, and a later pod restart would
boot from stale spec args while the agent believes actual == desired.
Each incarnation owns exactly one CM: created before it, deleted with it
(`_remove_server_handle` derives the name from `handle.name`), strays
covered by the orphan GC sweep (two PRs up). Hashed because prefix(19) +
name(≤63) would exceed the 63-char resource-name limit.
- **CM created BEFORE the Deployment**, so a racing new pod sees the
current pin at mount time. The CM being ahead of the running server's
in-memory state is the safety property.
- **No `subPath` on the mount** — ConfigMap live-updates only propagate
to non-subPath mounts, and the pod-restart path depends on reading
current contents.
- **`optional: true` on the volume** — a manually-deleted CM must not
block pod startup with `CreateContainerConfigError`; boot falls back to
the spec args.
- **Empty CM data means "explicitly no pin"** (matches the OSS-side
reader semantics one PR down), not "fall back to args".
- **v2 spec-version label on Deployment + pod template.** The upstack
capability gate reads the *running* Deployment's label, so pre-v2
Deployments never take the fast path; they roll to v2 on the customer's
next code push.
- Skipped for multipex (pins arrive via `CreatePexServerArgs`) and
multi-replica (no fan-out story yet); explicit error on user-supplied
volume-name collisions with the reserved name.

## Test Plan

Unit tests: per-incarnation name determinism/uniqueness/length, CM
shape, mount/volume/label injection (and absence by default), collision
rejection, CM-before-Deployment ordering at spinup, 409 ⇒ replace
idempotency, pex/multi-replica skip, removal deletes exactly its own CM,
404 swallowed on removal.

---------

Co-authored-by: Maxime Armstrong <maxime@retain.ai>

subject: [dj] Add job entity GraphQL schema, resolvers & UI for automation evaluations (#22186)
body:
Add GraphQL schema, resolvers, and UI for job entity automation
evaluations, enabling users to view automation history for jobs with
automation conditions.

This is part of Objective #22159 (Nodes 5.1–5.5). Prior phases
established the backend pipeline for job entity automation. This PR adds
the full GraphQL→UI pipeline: new GraphQL types for job entity keys,
resolver dispatch for evaluation queries, entity key utilities in the
UI, and a new Automation tab on job pages.

**Objective #22159:** Objective: Declarative Automation for Jobs — Clean
Implementation

## Key Changes

- Add `GrapheneAssetJobKey` type, `GrapheneJobEntityKeyInput` input, and
extend `EntityKey` union in the GraphQL schema to support job entities
- Wire `assetJobKey` parameter through
`assetConditionEvaluationRecordsOrError` query and backend resolver
dispatch
- Add `automationCondition` field to `GraphenePipeline` type, exposing
automation conditions in workspace queries
- Update all UI entity key utilities (`flattenEvaluations`,
`EvaluationDetailDialog`, etc.) to handle `AssetJobKey` with null-safe
`assetKey` patterns
- Add Automation tab to job pages with new `JobAutomationRoot` component
and routing

subject: fix: don't support running jobs on user code server sensor (#26022)
body:
## Summary & Motivation
Prevents using user code server sensors to evaluate job conditions.

The user code server sensor evaluates the job condition agent-side
against the code location's live definitions, where job nodes exist for
free. But the run request it produces only carries a job name, which the
host must resolve into an actual job (repository handle, execution plan)
from its workspace snapshots. That means job-awareness has to exist in
the host's remote asset graph too, however Dagster+'s
`CloudServerRemoteWorkspaceAssetGraph` doesn't handle `AssetJobKey`s
yet.

subject: [u][refresh] refresh_component_state on workspace contexts (#24233)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Here we start getting into some sightly subtle stuff. Basically:

- we expect for some non-trivial subset of state refresh operations, the
update will take more than 1 minute, which means if we try to do it w/in
a single dagit request, we'll get nginx timeout'd
- while ideally the state refreshes people are doing regularly through
the UI would take less than a minute (and the ones that take longer
would be relegated to a separate out-of-band process, e.g. do it from a
dagster job), we want to have not-terrible behavior in the cases that we
do have those longer refreshes (at least letting the user know what's
going on)
- so there's basically four scenarios here:
- we fire off the request, it succeeds within 50 seconds (most common)
-> all good
- we fire off the request, if fails explicitly within 50 seconds (e.g.
there's some connectivity issue with the external system) -> we get an
explicit error
- we fire off the request, it succeeds after > 50 seconds -> after 50
seconds, we the UI is updated to know that the request went through but
has not yet completed, and we start polling to see if we can detect a
new defs state version getting written for the relevant keys (which
would be the net result of that update)
- we fire off the request, it fails after > 50 seconds -> this is the
worst case, as we don't get any visibility into this error. user would
have to check the agent logs or something. that being said, this would
ideally be one of the rarer cases and we could have language at the 50
second mark basically saying "it's best effort from here on out, but if
this regularly takes > 50 seconds to complete you should consider having
this handle its state via some other mechanism"

## Test Plan

subject: Feature/snowflake dbt project component (#33926)
body:
## Summary & Motivation
This PR introduces the SnowflakeDbtProjectComponent (in @preview),
allowing Dagster to orchestrate dbt projects natively on Snowflake's
managed runtime (via EXECUTE DBT PROJECT).

Modeled after DbtCloudComponent, this execution path requires no local
dbt-core installation. State is managed by fetching the manifest
directly from Snowflake.

Key architectural highlights and improvements over the initial scaffold:

Async Execution & Cancellation: Uses execute_async with a polling
mechanism. Registers an on_cancel hook to issue
SYSTEM$CANCEL_QUERY(<query_id>) if the Dagster run is interrupted,
preventing orphaned Snowflake warehouse compute.

Robust Sensor Deduplication: Drops ARGS string-matching. Instead,
Dagster runs inject a QUERY_TAG at the session level. The sensor
accurately identifies external vs. Dagster-triggered runs by polling
INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY.

Zero-Compute Metadata Fetching: Replaced sequential SELECT count(*) and
DESCRIBE TABLE per model with a single, batched cloud-services query to
INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS, drastically
reducing run time and credit consumption.

Feature Detection: Fails gracefully on unsupported accounts by probing
SHOW FUNCTIONS LIKE 'SYSTEM$LOCATE_DBT_ARTIFACTS' during state refresh.

##Test Plan
Unit Tests: Added 34 rigorous unit tests using a mocked
SnowflakeResource.

Coverage: Validated subsetting (--select passthrough), SQL construction,
async execution/polling, cancellation hooks, and sensor deduplication
logic.

Linting/Type-checking: Passed repo-wide make ruff and make
quick_pyright.

Environment: Tested local .venv dependencies, including the recent
removal of the project kwarg in _build_column_lineage_metadata.

##Changelog
[dagster-snowflake] Add SnowflakeDbtProjectComponent (Preview) to
support natively orchestrating dbt Projects on Snowflake.

subject: fix: send deployment header from serverless presigned-URL IO manager (#25897)
body:
## Summary

Materializing assets in a serverless org with **more than one full
deployment** fails with a 401 from the IO manager:

```
requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url:
  https://<org>.agent.<env>.dagster.cloud/gen_io_storage_url?key=raw_orders&method=PUT
  File ".../dagster_cloud/serverless/io_manager.py", line 138, in _get_presigned_url
    resp.raise_for_status()
```

**Root cause.** `ServerlessPresignedURLIOManager._get_presigned_url`
builds its headers with the raw `get_dagster_cloud_api_headers(token,
DagsterCloudInstanceScope.DEPLOYMENT)` and **never passes a
`deployment_name`**, so the `Dagster-Cloud-Deployment` header is
omitted. Ursula's auth (`_get_deployment`) then falls back to "if the
org has exactly one deployment, use it; otherwise 401":

```
Organization has multiple deployments, but no deployment specified
```

Single-deployment serverless orgs hit the one-deployment branch and
worked; with per-deployment tenancy an org can now have `prod` +
`stage`, so it 401s.

Every other run-pod callback (compute logs, insights, defs-state,
GraphQL) goes through `instance.dagster_cloud_api_headers` →
`get_agent_headers`, which derives `deployment_name` from the instance
config. This IO manager was the only path that bypassed that helper.

## Fix

Thread `init_context.instance.deployment_name` into the manager and send
it in the header — matching how the non-presigned S3 path already reads
`instance.deployment_name`, and how every other caller sets the header.

## Test Plan

- `dagster_cloud_tests/serverless_tests/test_io_manager.py` → 13 passed.
Added an assertion that `dump_to_path` sends `Dagster-Cloud-Deployment`,
and that the factory threads `deployment_name` onto the manager.
- `just ty` → 0 errors.

## Changelog

Fix a 401 from the serverless IO manager when materializing assets in an
org with more than one full deployment.

subject: [components] improve app-managed component form rendering (#25842)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Improves how app-managed component schemas render in the UI form editor,
and adds an `advanced` flag to `ComponentFormConfig` that tucks tuning
knobs into a collapsed **Advanced (n)** section.

Driving three sample components (simple / medium / complex) through the
editor in an editable-install project surfaced six problems, all fixed
here:

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| `multiline=True` on `Optional[str]` crashed the dialog (the schema
filter dropped the *real* string variant, keeping the null one) |
`split_form_schema` drops `null` variants, then collapses any single
surviving `anyOf` variant into the parent field |
| Fields rendered alphabetically (`sort_keys=True` serialization
destroys declaration order) | derived models emit `ui:order`, honored
natively by RJSF |
| Meaningless "option 1 / option 2" variant pickers with duplicated
lowercase labels on every Optional/enum/int field | same single-variant
collapse |
| Union options showed raw derived names (`SnowflakeDestinationModel`) |
derived models emit a humanized `title` ("Snowflake Destination") |
| Freshly opened forms covered in red `must have required property
'Name'` ajv errors | errors display only after a field is touched, with
friendly wording; submit-gating (`validate.ts`) unchanged |
| Arrays rendered as unthemed fieldsets; dict fields had no way to add
an entry | custom `ArrayFieldTemplate` (item cards with index + remove)
and `WrapIfAdditionalTemplate` (key/value/remove rows + Add entry) |

Also: number-aware `TextWidget` (real numbers in the YAML, not strings),
and headings for array/dict fields which previously rendered nameless.

subject: [components] resolve app-managed component location name from the loading harness (#25833)
body:
## Summary

App-managed component discovery currently keys entirely off a location
name derived from user project config: `ComponentTree.for_project` uses
`[tool.dg.project].code_location_name` (or the project root directory
name), and the legacy `load_defs()` entry point leaves it `None` — which
skips discovery entirely and silently. Meanwhile the writer side (the
`setAppManagedComponent` mutation) keys state under the *workspace*
location name. Any mismatch between those two names means components
added via the UI silently never load. This is exactly what happened on
the `data-eng-pipeline` location in the hooli branch-deployment repro.

This PR makes the loading harness — the thing that actually knows the
workspace location name — the authoritative source:

- **`RepositoryLoadData`** gains a `code_location_name` field
(serdes-safe additive field, default `None`), exposed via a new
`DefinitionsLoadContext.code_location_name` property. Riding on the load
data means run-worker RECONSTRUCTION loads resolve the same name (and
therefore the same app-managed components) as the original
initialization load.
- **The gRPC server** threads its existing `--location-name` /
`DAGSTER_LOCATION_NAME` value (already set by the cloud agent and
`dagster dev`) through `LoadedRepositories` into the seed load context;
**`InProcessCodeLocation`** passes its origin's location name the same
way.
- **The `@repository` machinery** captures the ambient name onto the
stamped `RepositoryLoadData`, and the INITIALIZATION→RECONSTRUCTION
conversion in `reconstruct_repository_def_from_pointer` preserves it.
- **`ComponentTree`** resolves the discovery name ambient-first, falling
back to the project-config-derived name only when no harness-reported
name is available (e.g. `dg` CLI loads outside a workspace). A mismatch
between the two logs a warning naming both values; app-managed state
that exists but is unreachable because no name resolved also warns
instead of failing silently.

Notably, this fixes app-managed components for projects using the
deprecated `load_defs()` entry point (previously they could never load
app-managed components in any environment) and for any project whose
config-derived name doesn't match its `dagster_cloud.yaml` / workspace
location name.

## How I tested

- New unit tests for ambient-first resolution, config fallback, mismatch
warning, and the exists-but-unreachable warning
(`test_app_managed_components_integration.py`).
- New plumbing test covering name capture through the repository
machinery and preservation into run-worker-style reconstruction
(`test_definitions_load_context.py`).
- Existing suites pass: app-managed integration + state tests,
definitions load context, component tree, state-backed component,
reconstructable/cacheable-assets, gRPC repository snapshot api tests,
and the OSS graphql app-managed component e2e tests.

subject: Serdes CLI Tool (#25870)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Adds a `serdes` subcommand to `dagster-dev` for inspecting registered
serdes types. This is useful for understanding the full shape of the
serdes type registry for a given package — including objects, enums,
unions, and builtin types — without having to manually trace through
code.

The CLI supports three commands:

- **`list`** — lists all registered types, with optional `--detailed`,
`--json`, or `--html` output
- **`show <typename>`** — shows detailed info for a specific type
- **`tree <typename>`** — shows a type and all types it transitively
references, with optional \`--html\` output

The `--html` flag generates a self-contained HTML page with a table of
contents, cross-linked type references, hover tooltips showing full type
strings, and collapsible "Referenced by" backlink sections for each
type.

Type discovery works by scanning a package's source files for
`@whitelist_for_serdes` usage and importing those modules to populate
the whitelist map, then introspecting the registered serializers to
extract field types, base classes, field mappings, old fields, and other
compatibility metadata.

This is heavily claude-coded.

## Test Plan

Manual testing. Attaching screenshots.

`just serdes dagster list --html`

![image.png](https://app.graphite.com/user-attachments/assets/92de4477-34ce-4c16-9d37-b1391ec54a7d.png)

Click into an object:

![image.png](https://app.graphite.com/user-attachments/assets/84bf10a3-0d43-435a-a459-a367ff62801f.png)

Enums and unions listed separately:

![image.png](https://app.graphite.com/user-attachments/assets/b86adb1d-5c6b-4646-8efc-a5340e46e30b.png)

Union details:

![image.png](https://app.graphite.com/user-attachments/assets/2f7e1d58-ae41-487a-8261-f6595986a31c.png)

Console inspection:

```
> just serdes dagster list | grep Asset
  AllAssetCheckSelection
  AndAssetSelection
  AssetBackfillData
  AssetCheckEvaluation
  AssetCheckEvaluationPlanned
  ...
```

Can also target a specific object:

```
> just serdes dagster tree AssetDetails
AssetDetails
  Storage Name: AssetDetails
  Type: dagster._core.assets.AssetDetails
  Serializer: NamedTupleSerializer
  Fields (1):
    - last_wipe_timestamp: float | None
```

subject: Fix layout-fragile git-root assertion in source code metadata test (#25855)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

The `test_link_code_references_to_git_if_cloud_cloud_context[github]`,
`[gitlab]`, and
`test_link_code_references_to_git_if_cloud_override_cloud_context` cases
were failing in buildkite. The expected git URLs hardcoded
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud`, but
`link_code_references_to_git_if_cloud` derives the repository path as
the file path relative to the nearest `.git` ancestor (via
`_locate_git_root` + `AnchorBasedFilePathMapping`). That is
checkout-layout-dependent: it resolves to
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/...` in an internal dev
checkout (so the test passed locally) but to
`python_modules/dagster-cloud/...` in buildkite, where the package sits
at the OSS-style layout under its own git root. The code is correct —
the test was layout-fragile.

The fix asserts only the layout-independent parts of the URL: the
branch-base prefix (`startswith`) and the stable
`dagster-cloud/.../file#Ln` tail (`endswith`). The repo prefix in
between (`dagster-oss/python_modules/` vs `python_modules/`) is exactly
the env-dependent segment that shouldn't be pinned — pinning it was the
original bug. It also drops the dead, wrong-depth `GIT_ROOT_PATH`
constant. Since this file is copybara-synced, the fix propagates to
`dagster-io/dagster`, whose identical copy has the same fragility.

## Test Plan

`tox -e py312-default -- -k link_code_references` — all 6 cases pass.
ruff and ty clean. The assertions no longer depend on where `.git` sits
relative to the package, so they hold in every layout (internal dev,
buildkite, OSS).

subject: [da] Fix crash building run requests for partitioned asset checks (#25789)
body:
## Summary

A partitioned asset check that owns an `AutomationCondition` can be
requested by declarative automation on a tick where the asset it checks
is **not** being materialized. In that case the check arrives at
`build_run_requests` as its own entity subset (keyed on the
`AssetCheckKey`, not the asset).

`_get_mapping_from_entity_subsets` then expanded that subset via
`expensively_compute_asset_partitions()`, which is undefined for a check
key (it builds `AssetKeyPartitionKey`s, whose key must be an `AssetKey`)
and raised:

```
CheckError: Failure condition: Unsupported operation for type <class 'dagster._core.definitions.asset_key.AssetCheckKey'>
```

This failed the **entire** automation tick for the deployment — the
daemon makes no progress on any asset until the offending check is
removed. Observed in prod against a deployment using daily-partitioned
asset checks with automation conditions.

## Fix

The mapping only needs the partition keys for each bucket, which can be
read off any entity subset regardless of key type. For a check-keyed
subset, read them directly with `expensively_compute_partition_keys()`
instead of expanding into `AssetKeyPartitionKey`s. The standalone
partitioned check then flows through as a proper partitioned check run.

The asset-keyed path — including a check grouped into the same run as
the asset it checks — is unchanged.

## Test

Added `test_partitioned_check_requested_without_its_asset`, which builds
a daily-partitioned asset check with an automation condition, requests
only the check (not its asset) for one partition, and asserts a single
partitioned check run is produced. Verified it reproduces the exact
`CheckError` above without the fix and passes with it.

subject: Recovery for locations stuck after failed refresh (#33642)
body:
I have enough context. Here's the updated PR summary:

---

## Summary & Motivation

Fixes #17319 and #32216.

A code location can be left permanently stuck in an error state after a
failed `refresh_code_location()`. The gRPC server watcher detects a
server change (new server ID, or server reachable again after a
transient blip) and triggers a refresh, but the refresh itself fails —
typically during a Kubernetes rolling deployment where the gRPC call
routes to a dying pod via the EndpointSlice. After the failure, the
watch thread keeps polling successfully, sees no further changes, and
never retries. The location stays errored until something external
(manual reload, daemon/webserver restart, or a new `server_id` change)
forces a retry. The recent `--fixed-server-id` change (commit e32df69)
removed pod-restart as a reliable recovery path, making this a
long-lived failure mode in some configurations. (Manually clicking
Reload in the UI can also recover, but in multi-replica webserver
deployments it has to land on the affected pod, so it may take several
clicks.)

Recovery is implemented as an independent periodic check inside the
existing gRPC watch thread. On a fixed cadence
(`ERROR_RECOVERY_INTERVAL`, default 10s), the watch thread inspects the
workspace entry's `load_error`. If it is a
`DagsterUserCodeUnreachableError`, it calls `refresh_code_location`
directly. The check fires no `on_*` event. The server-id watch and the
disconnect/reconnect loop continue to handle only server-id changes and
actual server unreachability.

Recovery is intentionally scoped to `DagsterUserCodeUnreachableError`.
Other load errors (e.g. `DagsterUserCodeProcessError` from a user-code
syntax error) are non-transient and not retried, to avoid log spam on
permanently broken locations. A related rolling-deploy race — where
individual gRPC calls within a single `_load_location` route to
different pods and produce a stale-but-not-errored `version_key` — is
intentionally out of scope and tracked separately.

Other changes:
- `create_grpc_watch_thread` now requires all `on_*` callbacks (no
longer optional) and adds `get_location_entry` and
`refresh_code_location` parameters.
- The internal `server_id` dict is replaced with a typed `ServerId`
inner class; full type annotations added throughout `server_watcher.py`.

Identification and fixing of the issue was tool assisted, as was writing
this commit message, but both the code and the commit message have been
significantly reviewed and edited by me.

## How I Tested These Changes

New unit tests in
`dagster_tests/general_tests/grpc_tests/test_watch_server.py` covering
the periodic recovery check (asserting it refreshes a stuck location and
fires no events). New integration tests in
`dagster_graphql_tests/graphql/test_watch_grpc_server.py` exercising the
full recovery flow end-to-end against a real gRPC server. Existing test
suite.

## Changelog

Fixed a bug where a code location could be left stuck in an error state
after a transient gRPC failure during refresh (common during Kubernetes
rolling deployments). The gRPC server watcher now periodically retries
refresh for locations whose load error is a
`DagsterUserCodeUnreachableError`.

---------

Co-authored-by: Daniel Gibson <daniel@elementl.com>

subject: fix: resolve asset check keys (#25686)
body:
## Summary & Motivation
Update the logic that selects which asset checks are run with DA.

The logic is now to resolve to `asset_check_keys` that
- target one of the keys in `asset_keys`
- are in the same repo that we're targeting
- do not have an automation condition defined on it
- are explicitly requested

I've also included the optimization: if no checks on the `asset_key` set
have an automation condition, we pass None.

This is all behind a `AUTOMATION_RESOLVE_ASSET_CHECK_KEYS` feature gate.

Here's a summary of the behavior now when a DA run is kicked off (gate
OFF is the current behavior in production).

```
case                     gate  checks that EXIST                       checks that RUN       pills on the run
-----------------------  ----  --------------------------------------  --------------------  --------------------
unconditioned            OFF   row_count (u), not_null (u)             row_count, not_null   2 (row_count, not_null)
unconditioned            ON    row_count (u), not_null (u)             row_count, not_null   2 (row_count, not_null)
mixed                    OFF   row_count (c), not_null (u)             row_count             row_count
mixed                    ON    row_count (c), not_null (u)             row_count, not_null   2 (row_count, not_null)
conditioned_not_firing   OFF   yearly (c), not_null (u)                yearly, not_null      2 (yearly, not_null)
conditioned_not_firing   ON    yearly (c), not_null (u)                not_null              not_null
conditioned_only         OFF   row_count (c)                           row_count             row_count
conditioned_only         ON    row_count (c)                           row_count             row_count

(c) = conditioned (has its own automation_condition)   (u) = unconditioned (rides along)
```

## Test Plan
Unit & manual (local).

## 🔍 The Problem

In EMR Serverless, Spark UI URLs are short-lived and expire after
approximately one hour. When a new Spark UI URL is requested, AWS
automatically invalidates previous URLs. The `PipesEMRServerlessClient`
previously hardcoded the dashboard refresh interval to 15 minutes (900
seconds), which frequently invalidated active user sessions and
disrupted log access.

## 🛠️ The Solution

* Added an optional `dashboard_refresh_interval` parameter (defaulting
to 3300.0 seconds / 55 minutes) to the `PipesEMRServerlessClient`
constructor.

* Validated the parameter using `check.opt_numeric_param`.

* Refactored `_wait_for_completion` to replace the hardcoded 900-second
interval check with `self.dashboard_refresh_interval`.

subject: Replace Blueprint Select and Suggest with custom implementations (#25105)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Removes the `@blueprintjs/select` peer dependency from `ui-components` by reimplementing `Select` and `Suggest` entirely in-house. The Blueprint `Select` and `Suggest` wrappers have been replaced with custom implementations built on top of the existing `Popover` and `TextInput` components, with a new `useListItems` hook handling filtering, active-item tracking, and keyboard navigation (ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Escape).

Key changes:

- `useListItems` — new hook encapsulating query state, item filtering (`itemPredicate` / `itemListPredicate`), active-item state, keyboard handling, and `getItemProps` generation.
- `selectTypes.ts` — new file defining `ItemRenderer`, `ItemListRenderer`, `ItemPredicate`, `ItemListPredicate`, `SelectPopoverProps`, and related interfaces that previously came from `@blueprintjs/select`.
- `Select` — rewritten to use `Popover` + `TextInput` directly; supports controlled/uncontrolled query and active item, `filterable`, `resetOnSelect/Close/Query`, and a custom `itemListRenderer`.
- `Suggest` — rewritten similarly; manages its own open/close state driven by input focus/blur, syncs `selectedItem` → query display value, and supports `rightElement` via an absolutely-positioned overlay.
- CSS updates remove Blueprint-specific class selectors and add padding/layout helpers for the new implementations.
- `IssueStatusSelector` adds `popoverProps={{placement: 'bottom-end'}}` to correct dropdown alignment.

## Test Plan

Verify `Select` and `Suggest` render correctly, filter items, respond to keyboard navigation, open/close on interaction, and respect `resetOnSelect`/`resetOnClose`/`resetOnQuery` flags. Confirm `IssueStatusSelector` dropdown opens aligned to the bottom-end of its trigger.

subject: docs: fix invalid pool config in dbt snapshot component examples (#33933)
body:
## Summary

The "Preventing concurrent dbt snapshots" section of the dbt patterns
docs shows how to put dbt snapshots in a concurrency pool. The example
component YAMLs set the pool via `post_processing` asset attributes:

```yaml
post_processing:
  assets:
    - target: "*"
      attributes:
        pool: "dbt-snapshots"
```

This doesn't work: `pool` is **not** a valid asset attribute (it is
op-level). Loading such a component raises a pydantic `ValidationError`:

```
Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden]  # on AssetSpecUpdateKwargsModel, field "pool"
```

so the examples as written fail to load.

## Fix

Set the pool via `attributes.op.pool`, which `DbtProjectComponent`
applies to the generated multi-asset op (`pool=op_spec.pool`):

```yaml
attributes:
  project: '{{ project_root }}/dbt'
  select: "resource_type:snapshot"
  op:
    pool: "dbt-snapshots"
```

Updated three snippet files referenced by
`docs/docs/integrations/libraries/dbt/dbt-patterns.md`:

- `integrations/dbt/component/snapshot/snapshot.yaml`
- `integrations/dbt/component/snapshot/snapshot_sales.yaml`
- `integrations/dbt/component/snapshot/snapshot_inventory.yaml`

A separate snippet (`pythonic/custom_component_incremental_defs.yaml`)
uses `post_processing` with `partitions_def`, which **is** a valid asset
attribute, and is left unchanged.

Verified against dagster 1.13.9 / dagster-dbt 0.29.9.

subject: [ui] Virtualize the catalog page (single flattened list) (#25655)
body:
## Summary

The catalog page (`CloudAssetsCatalog2`) renders accordion sections
where each entry is a `ListItem` containing a `MiddleTruncate` (which
measures text on a **canvas** and forces layout). The **Asset groups**
and **Code locations** sections render their *entire* list when
expanded, un-windowed. For orgs with many groups/locations, expanding a
section mounts thousands of `MiddleTruncate` instances in one commit and
freezes the main thread (profiled: a single ~23s task — ~12s
`measureText` + ~6s forced layout).

Not a recent regression — this rendering has existed since the catalog
redesign (#19111, Dec 2025); it became a beach-ball as the org's
group/location count grew.

## Approach

The whole catalog body is rendered as a **single flattened virtualized
list** (the `OverviewJobsTable` / `AssetCatalogV2VirtualizedTable`
pattern). The top section (search + summary tiles), every section
header, and every row are flattened into one array and rendered **by
type using the existing components** (`CollapsibleSectionHeader`,
`ListItem`, the summary tiles), so the page looks the same but only
viewport rows mount. Single page scrollbar.

### Why a single virtualizer (commit history shows the path)

1. `Virtualize the Asset groups and Code locations sections` —
bounded-height internal scroll. Worked, but **nested second scrollbar**.
2. `Virtualize against the page scroll` — one virtualizer per section
against the shared scroll container, each tracking its own
`scrollMargin`. Single scrollbar, but **buggy**: when a section above
expanded/collapsed, a section's offset went stale vs. the virtualizer's
internal computation, leaving a large whitespace gap above the rows.
3. `Render the catalog body as a single virtualized list` *(current)* —
one virtualizer owns the entire scroll content starting at offset 0, so
there is **no `scrollMargin` and no per-section offset bookkeeping**.
The whitespace-gap class of bug is gone.

The search query is **lifted** into the page component (and
`AssetCatalogSearch` made optionally-controlled) so the input survives
unmounting/remounting as it scrolls in and out of the list.

## ⚠️ Risks / downsides (please weigh in review)

- **Not yet verified in a real browser.** Type-checks and lints; the
virtualization math has not been run against live layout. Needs manual
QA: scroll accuracy (no gaps/overlap), expand/collapse of every section,
the 940px tile-wrap breakpoint, and a large dataset. Recommend
validating against a synthetic large-group workspace.
- **Row-height estimates + dynamic measurement.** Rows use
`measureElement` with per-type estimates (top section 220, empty state
200, rows 48). If actual heights differ, expect minor scroll-position
adjustment as rows measure in — most visible for the tall, variable top
section.
- **Lost the expand/collapse opacity fade.** The old `contentWrapper`
opacity transition is gone — sections now show/hide instantly. Minor
visual change.
- **Top section scrolls away (now an `item`).** Matches prior behavior
(it scrolled before too). The lifted search state covers unmount; the
summary tiles refetch/remeasure if scrolled away and back.
- **Inherent virtualization trade-offs:** off-screen rows aren't in the
DOM, so browser find-in-page (Ctrl+F) and tab/focus order won't reach
rows not currently rendered.
- **`index` passed to `ListItem` is `0` for all rows.** Verified
`ListItem` only uses `index` for `data-index` (no styling depends on
it), so this is cosmetically irrelevant — but worth a glance.
- **`view.icon as any`** retained from the original (pre-existing).

## Relationship to the other PRs

- **#25658** (CSS-truncation bandaid) — overlaps the same lines; becomes
unnecessary once this lands (only viewport rows mount, so
`MiddleTruncate` is fine). Close it then.
- **#25566 / cached-canvas** — per-instance `MiddleTruncate` cost;
orthogonal and still fine to keep.

## Test plan

- `yarn tsgo` + `yarn lint` clean on changed files. (Repo-wide `tsgo`
shows only pre-existing, unrelated `@rjsf/*` install-gap errors.)
- Confirmed `ListItem` has no `:nth-child`/index-based styling, so
flattening is visually safe; hover-keyline dedup works on the per-row
wrappers.
- **TODO before merge:** manual browser QA per the risks above, ideally
re-profiling against a large-group workspace to confirm the long task
collapses.
