subject: Show asset checks in run header for asset-job runs (#25679)
body:
## Problem

On an individual Run's page, the header showed only the targeted **assets** (e.g. "299 assets") and omitted the targeted **asset checks**, even though the runs table row rendered both pills.

Two underlying issues:

1. **Frontend guard.** `RunAssetCheckTags` skipped its query for hidden asset-group jobs (`__ASSET_JOB`) and fell back to `run.assetCheckSelection`. That field is `None` whenever a run targets *every* check on its selected assets (the common case for an asset materialization), so the header rendered nothing.
2. **Expensive resolver.** The `Run.assetChecks` resolver (`get_asset_checks_for_run_id`) determined the targeted checks by scanning the *entire run event log* (`instance.all_logs(run_id, of_type=ASSET_CHECK_EVENTS)`).

## Fix

The execution plan snapshot already records the concrete targeted asset-check keys on its step outputs (`StepOutputProperties.asset_check_key`) — the same place `get_assets_for_run` reads `asset_selection`. Asset checks are statically declared, so every check a run executes is planned; the plan is the authoritative set and is cheap to read, and it correctly expands the `None`-selection case into concrete keys.

- **`ExecutionPlanSnapshot.asset_check_keys`** — new property mirroring `asset_selection`.
- **`get_asset_checks_for_run(graphene_info, run)`** — reads the plan snapshot, falling back to the event-log scan only for runs that predate execution plan snapshots.
- **Frontend** — `RunAssetCheckTags` always uses the (now cheap, `None`-correct) `assetChecks` query instead of the `assetCheckSelection` fallback.

## Scope / performance

Only the **single-run header** queries `Run.assetChecks` (via `RunAssetCheckTags`, rendered solely in `RunRoot`). The **runs feed is unaffected** — it reads `assetCheckSelection` directly off the list fragment in `RunTargetLink`, with no per-row resolver. Net effect per run-detail page: a full event-log scan is replaced by one indexed execution-plan-snapshot fetch (and one added snapshot fetch for `__ASSET_JOB` headers that previously rendered nothing).

Known pre-existing limitation (out of scope): the feed pill still undercounts when `assetCheckSelection` is `None`, since fixing that without a per-row snapshot load would need a stored count or batched resolver.

## Testing

- `ExecutionPlanSnapshot.asset_check_keys` unit test (`test_execution_plan.py`).
- GraphQL test that creates a run with a plan snapshot but **no events** and asserts `assetChecks` resolves from the plan (`test_asset_checks.py`); existing end-to-end `None`-selection tests still pass.
- Frontend `RunAssetCheckTags.test.tsx` updated to mock the resolved query.
- `just ruff` ✅ · `just ty` (changed files) ✅ · `yarn tsgo`/`eslint`/`jest` ✅

subject: Bump pyjwt from 2.12.1 to 2.13.0 in /dagster-oss/docs (#25606)
body:
Bumps [pyjwt](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt) from 2.12.1 to 2.13.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pyjwt's releases.

2.13.0

PyJWT 2.13.0 — Security Release

This release bundles five security fixes plus three additional hardening / spec-compliance changes. We recommend all users upgrade.

Security

  • GHSA-xgmm-8j9v-c9wx — JWK JSON accepted as HMAC secret (algorithm confusion). HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key previously rejected PEM- and SSH-formatted asymmetric keys but did not catch a JWK passed as a raw JSON string. In a verifier configured with both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms in algorithms=[…] and a raw-JSON JWK as the key, an attacker could forge HS256 tokens using the JWK text as the HMAC secret. The guard has been extended to reject any JWK-shaped JSON. Reported by @​aradona91.

  • GHSA-jq35-7prp-9v3f — Algorithm allow-list bypass with PyJWK / PyJWKClient. When verifying with a PyJWK, the caller's algorithms=[…] allow-list was checked against the token header alg as a string only; actual verification used the algorithm bound to the PyJWK. An attacker who controlled a registered JWKS key could sign with one algorithm and advertise another on the header. PyJWT now requires the token header alg to match the PyJWK's algorithm before verification. Reported by @​sushi-gif.

  • GHSA-w7vc-732c-9m39 — DoS via base64 decode of unused payload segment when b64=false. For detached-payload JWS (b64=false), the compact-form payload segment was base64-decoded before being discarded in favor of the caller-supplied detached_payload. An attacker could inflate the unused segment to force CPU + memory cost without holding a valid signature. The segment is now required to be empty per RFC 7515 Appendix F, and is no longer decoded. Reported by @​thesmartshadow.

  • GHSA-993g-76c3-p5m4 — PyJWKClient accepts non-HTTP(S) URIs. PyJWKClient.fetch_data passed its URI to urllib.request.urlopen, which by default also handles file://, ftp://, and data: schemes. An application that fed an attacker-influenced URI into PyJWKClient could be coerced into reading local files or reaching other unintended schemes. PyJWKClient now rejects any URI whose scheme isn't http or https. Reported by @​KEIJOT.

  • GHSA-fhv5-28vv-h8m8 — PyJWKClient cache wiped on fetch error. A finally-block put(jwk_set=None) cleared the JWK Set cache whenever a fetch raised, turning a transient JWKS-endpoint outage into application-wide auth failure. The cache write was moved into the success path; transient errors no longer evict valid cached keys. Reported by @​eddieran.

Fixed

  • Reject empty HMAC keys outright in HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key with InvalidKeyError instead of accepting them with only a warning. Defends against the os.getenv("JWT_SECRET", "") footgun. Thanks to @​SnailSploit and @​spartan8806 for the reports.
  • Forward per-call options (including enforce_minimum_key_length) from PyJWT.decode through to PyJWS._verify_signature. The option was previously silently dropped between the two layers, so it only took effect when set on the PyJWT instance. Thanks to @​WLUB for the report.
  • RFC 7797 §3 compliance for b64=false: the encoder now auto-adds "b64" to crit, and the decoder rejects tokens that set b64=false without listing it in crit. Thanks to @​MachineLearning-Nerd for the report.

Changed

  • Migrate the dev, docs, and tests package extras to dependency groups, by @​kurtmckee in #1152.

Upgrade notes

Most fixes are invisible to correctly-configured callers. A few behavioral changes you may encounter:

  • Empty HMAC keys now raise. If your app passed "" or b"" as a secret (often via a missing env var, e.g. os.getenv("JWT_SECRET", "")), encode/decode will now raise InvalidKeyError. This is the intended behavior — fix the configuration.
  • PyJWK decoding now requires the token's alg to match the JWK's algorithm. Previously a mismatch was silently honored if the header alg appeared in the allow-list. Tokens that relied on this mismatch will now fail with InvalidAlgorithmError.
  • PyJWKClient now rejects non-HTTP(S) URIs at construction time. Tests or dev environments that fetched JWKS from file:// URIs need to switch to a local HTTP server or load the JWKS by other means (e.g. construct PyJWKSet.from_dict(...) directly).
  • b64=false tokens are now strictly RFC 7515 / 7797 compliant. Tokens with a non-empty compact-form payload segment, or that omit "b64" from crit, will be rejected. PyJWT-produced tokens always satisfy both invariants, so round-trips through PyJWT are unaffected.
  • enforce_minimum_key_length set per-call now takes effect. Callers who passed options={"enforce_minimum_key_length": True} to jwt.decode() previously got no enforcement; they will now get InvalidKeyError on undersized keys, as documented.

Full changelog: https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/compare/2.12.1...2.13.0

Changelog

Sourced from pyjwt's changelog.

v2.13.0 <https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/compare/2.12.1...2.13.0>__

Security


- Reject JWK JSON documents passed as raw HMAC secrets in
  ``HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key`` to close an algorithm-confusion gap that
  the existing PEM/SSH guard did not cover. Reported by @aradona91 in
`GHSA-xgmm-8j9v-c9wx
<https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-xgmm-8j9v-c9wx>`__.
- Bind the JWT header ``alg`` to ``PyJWK.algorithm_name`` during
  verification so the caller's ``algorithms=[...]`` allow-list cannot be
bypassed when decoding with a ``PyJWK`` / ``PyJWKClient`` key. Reported
by @sushi-gif in `GHSA-jq35-7prp-9v3f
<https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-jq35-7prp-9v3f>`__.
- Reject non-``http(s)`` URI schemes in ``PyJWKClient`` so attacker-
influenced URIs cannot read local files or reach unintended schemes via
urllib's default ``file://`` / ``ftp://`` / ``data:`` handlers. Reported
by @KEIJOT in `GHSA-993g-76c3-p5m4
<https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-993g-76c3-p5m4>`__.
- Preserve the cached JWK Set on fetch errors in
``PyJWKClient.fetch_data``.
  The previous ``finally``-block ``put(None)`` pattern cleared the cache
on any transient outage, turning one bad JWKS request into application-
wide auth failure. Reported by @eddieran in `GHSA-fhv5-28vv-h8m8
<https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-fhv5-28vv-h8m8>`__.
- Skip the unconditional base64 decode of the compact-form payload
segment
  when ``b64=false`` is set in the protected header, and require that
  segment to be empty (RFC 7515 Appendix F detached form). Closes an
  unauthenticated DoS amplifier. Reported by @thesmartshadow in
`GHSA-w7vc-732c-9m39
<https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-w7vc-732c-9m39>`__.

Fixed



- Reject empty HMAC keys outright in ``HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key`` with
  ``InvalidKeyError`` instead of accepting them with only a warning.
  Thanks to @SnailSploit and @spartan8806 for independently flagging the
  footgun.
- Forward per-call ``options`` (including
``enforce_minimum_key_length``)
  from ``PyJWT.decode`` through to ``PyJWS._verify_signature`` so the
option actually takes effect when set at the call site rather than only
  on the ``PyJWT`` instance. Thanks to @WLUB for the report.
- RFC 7797 §3 compliance for ``b64=false``: the encoder now auto-adds
``"b64"`` to the ``crit`` header parameter, and the
decoder rejects
tokens that set ``b64=false`` without listing it in ``crit``. Thanks to
  @MachineLearning-Nerd for the report.

Changed

subject: [ui] Reuse a single offscreen canvas in MiddleTruncate (#25569)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up cleanup, **stacked on #25566**. This is the more structural change and is *not* a regression fix — it addresses a pre-existing cost.

`MiddleTruncate` measured text by creating a fresh `<canvas>` and `appendChild`/`removeChild`-ing it on `document.body` for **every** measurement (every mount, every resize). Mutating `document.body` invalidates layout, so when many instances measure in a single React commit, the interleaved DOM writes and `getBoundingClientRect` reads cause a forced-reflow storm. A profiled catalog load showed **~6s** of self-time in `getBoundingClientRect`.

An unattached canvas measures text identically, so this reuses a single module-level offscreen canvas and never touches the DOM — removing the `appendChild`/`removeChild` churn and the layout invalidation it caused.

## Relationship to #25566

- **#25566** (base) fixes the actual regression (the slow `measureText` fast-path loss from #25178). Low-risk, ship-first.
- **This PR** removes the residual reflow cost. Higher review surface (changes the canvas lifecycle), so it's split out and can land independently afterward.

The diff shown here is only the canvas-lifecycle delta on top of #25566.

## Test Plan

- `yarn tsgo`, `yarn lint`, and the `calculateMiddleTruncation` tests pass.
- Re-profiling shows the `getBoundingClientRect`/reflow self-time drop after this lands on top of #25566.

subject: try to fix various reconciler scaling problems (#25541)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fix Compass org reconciliation: thundering herd, stuck partial reconciliations, and the WAF wall

Background

At least two prod orgs (onepassword, zocdoc) silently stopped reconciling their Dagster+ Compass orgs, with no recent reconciliation logs. Investigating in DD discovered that the reconciliation system was in a pathological steady state affecting basically all prod prod orgs, driven by four interacting problems:

1\. \*\*The Compass WAF rate limit was tripping nightly.** All of cloud-prod egresses Compass traffic through a few NAT IPs, and the CloudFront WAF `RateLimitRule` aggregates per-IP at 2,000 req / 5 min. There was a nightly reconcile burst which peaked at ~2,700 req / 5 min and tripped the limit; every request mid-sweep got a blanket `403 Forbidden`. (Confirmed: successes flowed until 23:58:26 and the \*next* request 15 ms later was the first 403 — a hard global cutoff after ~3,000 calls.)

2\. \*\*Thundering herd.** The cron reconciled every org every minute, and failed orgs all shared a fixed 24h retry delay — so the entire failed population unlocked in the same ~30-min window every night, re-tripped the wall, and re-synchronized for the next night.

3\. \*\*Overlapping cron runs clobbered metadata.** The full sweep takes ~50-min, and a 50 minute sweep running on every org every minute stacks up concurrent runs, creating race conditions that clobber the final state, including success/failure, stale JWTs, timestamps, associated IDs, etc.

4\. \*\*A non-self-healing block.** Clobbering dropped `service_account_id` from some orgs' metadata. On the next retry `_ensure_service_account` tried to \*create* the`AI_AGENT` service user, hit the name-uniqueness constraint, and failed \*before* any reconciliation — so none of the expected changes ever appeared. ~300 orgs, including onepassword and zocdoc, were stuck here with no path out.

Althogh there was a feature flag gate on the reconciler, which allowed it to work for a while despite these scaling problems, at some point every single prod org was added to that gate.

The Dogfood environment was unaffected because it reconciles only a handful of orgs per tick against staging Compass: sweeps finish in seconds, so no herd, no overlap, no wall.

Changes

**Heal the wedged orgs (`compass_utils.py`,** **`service_user.py`)**

\- `_ensure_service_account` now adopts an existing `AI_AGENT` service user / custom role by name when the persisted id is missing, instead of blindly creating and hitting the uniqueness constraint. These orgs should self heal on their next reconcile.

**Kill the herd (`compass_utils.py`,** **`compass.py`,** **`create_or_update_compass_orgs.py`)**

\- New `next_update_timestamp` field on `CompassOrganizationMetadata`. Every create / reconcile (success \*or* failure) sets it to `now + jitter`, where jitter is drawn per-org, per-pass (`60 * randint(1, 60)` → 1–60 min). The cron skips any org whose`next_update_timestamp` is still in the future.

\- Removed the fixed 24h `COMPASS_ERROR_RETRY_DELAY` and the separate`orgs_to_retry_reconcile` / `orgs_to_retry_create` branches. Failures now retry on the same jittered cadence as everything else, so a correlated mass failure won't re-synchronize into a nightly herd. Steady-state load drops from ~1,500 reconciles/min to ~50/min spread evenly.

**Stop tripping the wall (`cloudfront.tf`)**

\- Raised the prod CloudFront WAF `RateLimitRule` from 2,000 to 10,000 req / 5 min, with a comment explaining that the whole fleet aggregates onto a few NAT IPs.

\*\*Cleanup**

\- Removed the dead `DAGSTER_PLUS_COMPASS_ENABLED` feature gate (effectively 100% in prod; reconciliation now runs for all active orgs).

\- Improved structured logging in `organization_client.py`.

Rollout

\- \*\*Watch the first post-deploy sweep.** Existing orgs have `next_update_timestamp = NULL`, so the entire eligible population reconciles on the first tick (recovery sweep), before jitter spreads it out. _Expected_ to clear under the raised limit.

\- After recovery, audit orgs still in `RECONCILE_FAILURE` for stale/dead JWTs left behind by earlier clobbering.

Followup

## Test Plan

unit tests, deploy and watch DD logs

## Summary

The serverless v2 (k8s) IO manager (`ServerlessPresignedURLIOManager`)
does not use boto3 — it talks to S3 indirectly via presigned URLs handed
out by the host cloud API. But `dagster_cloud.serverless.io_manager`
still imports boto3 at module load time for the legacy ECS-based
`PickledObjectServerlessIOManager`. This blows up on v2 user pods built
from a plain `dagster-cloud` dependency (no `[serverless]` extra), which
is what the `dg`-scaffolded projects ship.

Move the boto3 import inside
`PickledObjectServerlessIOManager._refresh_boto_session`. The ECS path
still loads boto3 the first time it instantiates the legacy class; the
v2 path now loads `dagster_cloud.serverless` cleanly without boto3
installed.

subject: [ui] Fix MiddleTruncate canvas text-measurement perf regression (#25566)
body:
## Summary

Minimal fix for the perf regression introduced by #25178. **Scoped to the regression only** — a follow-up PR handles the pre-existing forced-reflow cost.

#25178 began copying `letterSpacing`, `textRendering`, `fontKerning`, `wordSpacing`, and `fontStretch` onto the canvas 2D context used to measure text for middle truncation. Assigning text-shaping properties like `letterSpacing`/`textRendering` forces the browser **off its fast text-measurement path**, making every `measureText` call dramatically slower. That cost is multiplied by the per-instance binary search in `calculateMiddleTruncation` and by the number of rendered rows.

A profiled asset-catalog load (group-by-Group, expanding groups) showed a single ~25s main-thread task with **~14s** of self-time in `measureText`.

### Origin

The header tracking that exposed this came from #25091 (`Heading` component → `letter-spacing: -0.02em`). #25178 then made the measuring canvas honor that tracking — correct, but on the slow path.

### Fix

Assign only `font` (which carries font-stretch via the shorthand) to the context, and account for `letterSpacing` **arithmetically** in the measure callback. This preserves #25178's correctness fix (headers no longer mis-wrap) while restoring the fast `measureText` path.

The canvas create/append/remove lifecycle is **intentionally unchanged** here. The remaining ~6s of forced-reflow cost (`document.body` append/remove per measurement) predates #25178 and is addressed in a stacked follow-up.

## Test Plan

- `yarn tsgo`, `yarn lint`, and the `calculateMiddleTruncation` tests pass.
- Re-profiling the affected catalog load shows the `measureText` self-time collapse.

subject: [dagster-graphql] Push partition-set backfills query down to storage by selector_id (#25548)
body:
## Problem

`GraphenePartitionSet.resolve_backfills` fetched **every backfill in the
deployment** to return the most recent few for one partition set:

```python
matching = [
    b for b in instance.get_backfills(cursor=cursor)   # no limit, no filter
    if b.partition_set_origin and ...name/repo match
]
return [... for b in matching[:limit]]
```

With no `limit` or filter passed to storage, the SQL is unbounded:

```sql
SELECT bulk_actions.body FROM bulk_actions
WHERE organization_id=… AND deployment_id=…
ORDER BY bulk_actions.id DESC
```

It loads and deserializes the `body` blob of every backfill in the
deployment on each request — cost scales with the deployment's total
backfill count and body size, independent of the job's partition count.
The `limit`/`partitionSetName` are pure Python post-processing. On large
deployments this read is enough to **OOM a `host-dagit` replica** (and
trips `statement_timeout` on the read replica at ~44s).

This was found via a production incident: three `host-dagit` replicas
OOM'd ~60s apart, traced to this query being re-polled from a job's
Partitions tab and round-robined across replicas.

## Fix

Push the filter and limit down to storage using `selector_id` — a hash
of `(code location, repository, partition set name)` that's already
stored on each job backfill and indexed
(`idx_bulk_actions_selector_id`):

- Add `selector_id` to `BulkActionsFilter`.
- Apply it in the OSS (`sql_run_storage`) and cloud
(`host_cloud/run_storage`) backfills queries.
- Resolver passes
`BulkActionsFilter(selector_id=self._remote_partition_set.get_remote_origin().get_selector_id())`
plus the `limit`.

`selector_id` encodes all three dimensions the resolver previously
checked in Python, so the per-row filter and the `matching[:limit]`
slice are dropped — the query becomes a single indexed, limited lookup.
Asset backfills have a null `selector_id` and are correctly excluded
(matching prior behavior, which required `partition_set_origin`).

Assumes the `bulk_actions.selector_id` column/migration is present (it
has been for a long time).

## Test

Adds `test_backfill_selector_id_filtering` to the shared run-storage
suite (passes across storage implementations). `just ruff` and `just ty`
clean.

subject: Fix k8s test suite IsADirectoryError from stale .test_durations dir (#25560)
body:
## What

The four `k8s-test-suite` py3.12 jobs have failed on every master build
since #25478 with:

```
INTERNALERROR> File ".../pytest_split/plugin.py", line 127, in __init__
INTERNALERROR>   with open(config.option.durations_path) as f:
INTERNALERROR> IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '.test_durations'
```

This raises before any test is collected, so it blocks the whole suite
deterministically (e.g. [build
155827](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/155827)).

## Root cause

An interaction between two recent changes:

- **#25434** committed `.test_durations/-default` and
`.test_durations/-subchart` for the k8s suite — i.e. `.test_durations`
became a *directory*. Harmless on its own, because at that point the k8s
factors used `use_durations=True` and always passed `--durations-path
.test_durations/-default`, opening the file inside.
- **#25478** set the k8s `-default`/`-subchart` split factors to
`use_durations=False`. Normal runs then omit `--durations-path`, so
pytest-split falls back to its **default** path `.test_durations`. That
name is now a directory, and `open()` raises `IsADirectoryError`.

The k8s suite is the only one combining `splits > 1` with
`use_durations=False` — the single combination that activates
pytest-split's split mode while omitting `--durations-path` — so it's
the only affected suite.

The underlying inconsistency: refresh mode (`packages.py`) stored
durations for these factors even though normal runs never read them,
which is what created the colliding directory in the first place.

## Fix

- Exclude `use_durations=False` factors from refresh-mode storing, so
the colliding `.test_durations/` directory is never (re)created for
them.
- Remove the orphaned `.test_durations/` directory already committed for
the k8s suite. With no file present, pytest-split warns and falls back
to count-based splitting — exactly what `use_durations=False` intends.

subject: fix: get_latest_materialization_event returns stale pre-wipe materialization (#25511)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes
[dagster-io/dagster#15806](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/15806):
`instance.get_latest_materialization_event` returned a stale, wiped
materialization after `dagster asset wipe`, instead of `None` as
documented. Also fixes the Dagster Plus analogue of the bug for
partition wipes (reported by a cloud customer).

Asset wipes are soft deletes: `wipe_asset` records a wipe timestamp on
the `asset_keys` row, and readers treat the asset as live when
`last_materialization_timestamp > wipe_timestamp`. The problem is that
`ASSET_MATERIALIZATION_PLANNED` and `ASSET_OBSERVATION` events also bump
`last_materialization_timestamp` (intentionally, so planned/observed
assets show in the catalog) without updating the cached
`last_materialization` record — which `wipe_asset` never cleared. So the
moment any new run targeting a wiped asset started (or an observation
was reported), the row passed the wipe filter and
`_get_latest_materialization_records` returned the stale pre-wipe
record. A post-wipe observation resurfaced the stale materialization
indefinitely. This also affected `get_asset_records`
(`AssetRecord.asset_entry.last_materialization_record`) and
`get_latest_materialization_code_versions`, which share the same path.

### OSS fixes (`SqlEventLogStorage`)

- **Write side:** `wipe_asset` now also nulls out
`last_materialization`, so newly wiped rows are self-consistent. (This
matches what the Plus event log storage has always done.)
- **Read side:** `_get_latest_materialization_records` only trusts the
cached record when its timestamp postdates the wipe; otherwise it falls
back to the backcompat event-log query, which now has
`_add_assets_wipe_filter_to_query` applied. This covers rows wiped by
older Dagster versions where the stale blob is already in the database,
and also fixes the same latent staleness for legacy old-format rows that
always took the backcompat path.
- **Legacy visibility path:** `_fetch_backcompat_materialization_times`
(used by the pre-`ASSET_KEY_INDEX_COLS`-migration read path to decide
whether a wiped asset is live) now only counts
materialization/observation/planned events, mirroring what bumps
`last_materialization_timestamp` on the migrated path. Previously it
took `max(timestamp)` over *all* events, so the `ASSET_WIPED` event
stored by `instance.wipe_assets` immediately after the wipe made the
wiped asset appear live in `all_asset_keys`. This was latent until the
write-side fix above stopped the stale blob from short-circuiting that
path — it broke `TestAssetWipe::test_asset_wipe` in the postgres graphql
CI jobs, whose fixture creates tables via alembic without marking the
secondary index (postgres gates `last_materialization_timestamp` writes
on that index, so those storages stay on the legacy path forever).

### Plus fix (`HostCloudEventLogStorage`)

Full-asset wipes already clear `last_materialization`, but
`wipe_asset_partitions` deleted the per-partition materialization rows
while leaving the cached `last_materialization` on the asset row
untouched. If the latest materialization belonged to a wiped partition,
`get_latest_materialization_events` / `get_asset_records` kept returning
it. The partition wipe now recomputes the cached record from the
remaining materializations when it points at a wiped partition (falling
back to `None` when none remain). The cached-value read locks the
`asset_keys` row (`FOR UPDATE`) through the recompute, so a
materialization committing mid-wipe either lands before the recompute
reads (and is included) or after the wipe commits (and overwrites with
the newer value) — the recomputed value can never clobber a newer
concurrent materialization. The lock is acquired in the same order as
the store path (`asset_keys` last), so it adds no deadlock risk. Note
the adjacent caches (`last_observation`,
`last_failed_to_materialize_event`, `last_skipped_materialize_event`)
have the same staleness after partition wipes and are left for
follow-up.

## Test Plan

- Extended the shared-suite `test_asset_wipe`: after a wipe, a planned
event and then an observation must not resurface the old materialization
from `get_latest_materialization_events` or `get_asset_records`, and a
re-materialization must surface the new event. Runs against sqlite,
consolidated sqlite, in-memory, legacy, postgres, mysql, and the Plus
storages (host cloud, archive-aware, ursula graphql).
- Extended the shared-suite `test_asset_partitioned_wiped_event` (Plus
storages only): wiping the latest-materialized partition falls back to
the latest remaining materialization, wiping a non-latest partition
leaves it untouched, and wiping the only remaining partition clears it.
Verified to fail without the Plus fix.
- New
`test_get_latest_materialization_ignores_stale_cached_row_after_wipe`
(sqlite) simulates a row wiped by an older version (stale cached record
restored via direct SQL after the wipe) to exercise the read-side guard.
Verified to fail without the read-side fix.
- New `test_all_asset_keys_excludes_wiped_asset_on_legacy_index_path`
(dagster-postgres) simulates the unmigrated-index condition from the
graphql CI fixture and reproduces the exact `assert AssetKey(...) not in
[AssetKey(...)]` failure from build 155619 without the legacy-path fix;
passes with it.
- Locally green: `dagster_tests/storage_tests/test_event_log.py` (519
passed), `dagster_postgres_tests/test_event_log.py` (142 passed), the
previously-failing `TestAssetWipe` postgres graphql variants,
cloud-backend `test_event_log_storage.py` +
`test_archive_aware_storage.py` via tox (553 passed), and the ursula
graphql storage wipe tests.

## Changelog

Fixed a bug where `DagsterInstance.get_latest_materialization_event`
(and `get_asset_records`) could return a stale pre-wipe materialization
for a wiped asset once a new run targeting the asset started or an
observation was reported. In Dagster+, fixed the analogous bug where
wiping partitions could leave the wiped partition's materialization as
the asset's latest materialization.

subject: Refine pytest-split durations workflow: per-factor opt-out, data filter, stale-file cleanup (#25478)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Followup to #22765 (REFRESH_DURATIONS mode) and #25434 (the first
duration data drop). Comparing master CI builds before and after #25434
surfaced two distinct failure modes where the new `--durations-path` arg
made shard balancing *worse* than the count-based fallback. Net
Σ-slowest-shard across all sharded suites moved -0.8% on one post-merge
build and -5.2% on the next (so directionally correct), but a handful of
suites consistently regressed by 200-600s/shard. This PR fixes the two
root causes and adds a generic cleanup pass to the refresh PR script.

### What was actually broken

**Failure mode 1: pytest-split's algorithms mishandle zero-duration
entries.** Tests skipped by `@pytest.mark.parametrize` variants (e.g.
adapter-gated tests on adapters that aren't installed) get recorded with
`report.duration == 0.0`. pytest-split's "place each test in the shard
with the smallest current total" rule sees `min(totals)` not change when
you add 0, so every zero-duration test piles into the same shard. In
`dbt19-core-derived-metadata` (77 tests, 48 of them recorded as zero),
the simulated split correctly balances *test* time at 147 / 144 / 146s —
but shard 2 ends up with 57 of 77 tests vs 10 each in shards 1 and 3,
and the per-test fixture/collection overhead lands on the same shard ~6×
more often. Known upstream — see pytest-split issues
[#78](https://github.com/jerry-git/pytest-split/issues/78) and
[#110](https://github.com/jerry-git/pytest-split/issues/110), both open
with no maintainer response.

**Failure mode 2: freezegun + pytest's perf_counter interact badly.**
pytest's `TestReport.duration` is `time.perf_counter() -
time.perf_counter()` across the call phase. freezegun freezes
`time.monotonic` and `time.perf_counter` by default. Tests in
`dagster-cloud-backend/dagster_cloud_backend_tests/serverless_tests/test_serverless_manager.py`
use `frozen_time.move_to(manager.session_expires)` to fast-forward by 1
hour, which makes pytest record the test as having taken 1 hour of real
time even though wall-clock was milliseconds. The recorded values:
`test_refresh_boto_session = 7200s` (two `move_to` calls),
`test_refresh_ecr_session[on/off] = 3600s` each. These three tests
accounted for **92.9% of recorded time** in the cloud-backend `default`
durations file. pytest-split obediently scattered them across shards,
breaking balance.

**Failure mode 3 (no fix needed in code, just opt-out):
fixture-dominated suites.** k8s integration suites record near-zero
per-test time because the entire shard is dominated by kind-cluster
fixture setup, image loads, and deploys — none of which pytest can see.
`k8s-test-suite-default` (40 tests) recorded only one test at 39.4s and
39 at zero; `-subchart` (17 tests) recorded one at 38.3s and 16 at zero.
Balancing against that data is balancing noise; count-based grouping was
empirically better.

## Changes

### 1. Per-factor `use_durations` opt-out (`tox.py` + `packages.py`)

New `use_durations: bool = True` field on `ToxFactor`. In normal
(non-refresh) mode, `--durations-path` is only added when the flag is
set. Refresh mode still writes the file unconditionally — the data stays
current even for opted-out suites in case the underlying conditions
change later.

### 2. Opt the k8s suites out (`steps/integration.py`)

Flipped `use_durations=False` on `ToxFactor("-default", splits=2)` and
`ToxFactor("-subchart", splits=2)` in `build_k8s_suite_steps`. They'll
fall back to count-based grouping, restoring pre-#25434 behavior for
these specific factors.

### 3. Filter misleading durations before commit
(`create_test_durations_pr.sh`)

Adds a post-validation pass that drops entries with `v == 0.0` or `v >
600s`. Dropped entries become "missing" from pytest-split's point of
view, which triggers its built-in fallback: substitute the suite's
average duration. That's a more honest estimate than either 0s or 7200s
for the misleading entries. The 10-minute cap is also a useful sanity
floor — any test that genuinely runs more than 10 minutes wouldn't be a
candidate for duration-balanced sharding anyway.

### 4. Delete stale `.test_durations/*` files
(`create_test_durations_pr.sh`)

After resetting to master and before re-staging the new artifacts, the
script now enumerates every `.test_durations/*` file in master's tree
and `git rm`s any that aren't in the current refresh build's artifact
set. This keeps the directory in sync with the current set of refresh
tox steps — without it, a renamed factor or removed `label_suffix` would
leave its old durations file in master forever.

## What this PR doesn't do

- **Doesn't address `dagster-cloud-backend-default`'s underlying test.**
The freezegun-skewed durations are filtered out by change #3, which is
enough to fix shard balance, but the tests themselves still actually
take seconds of real wall-clock (the recorded values are spurious from
pytest's measurement angle, not from the test itself). No fix needed in
the test code; that's just how freezegun + perf_counter interact.
- **Doesn't add xdist.** Local benchmarking of
`dbt19-core-derived-metadata` showed `pytest -n 3 --dist=load` (xdist
round-robin) cut wall-clock from 393s baseline to 165s (2.4× speedup),
so it's a real option for suites where pytest-split's data-driven
balancing hits limits. But xdist comes with its own debt
(process-isolation bugs, memory multiplier, fixture cost paid
per-worker) and rolling it out belongs in its own change once we have a
couple suites where #3 + #4 still leave us short.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI on this PR passes — verifies the new `use_durations=False` path
in `packages.py` doesn't break step emission for k8s suites, and that
the rest of the splitter still emits the right `--durations-path` arg
for the suites that opted in.
- [ ] Kick off a fresh `[REFRESH_DURATIONS]` build on master after
merge. Confirm: (a) the auto-generated PR drops zero-duration entries
and any >600s entries from each `.test_durations/*` file; (b) if any
factor was renamed since #25434, its old durations file gets deleted in
the PR.
- [ ] On the next post-refresh master build, check that the k8s shards
are back to their pre-#25434 balance (both `-default` and `-subchart`
split evenly), and that the dbt `*-core-derived-metadata` suites improve
relative to the regressions observed on builds 155444 / 155446.

subject: ty: convert internal env from workspace-kind to project-kind (#24505)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Convert the `internal` ty env from workspace-kind to project-kind.
Eliminates the ~18s of `uv run --frozen --isolated --extra ty`
ephemeral-overlay-build overhead that was dominating every `just ty`
run, with no change to type-check coverage or strictness. With the
conversion done, every ty env is the same kind, so workspace-kind env
support is removed from `run-ty.py` entirely.

End-to-end timing on `just ty` from internal root (full run, all three
envs):

| | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wall | 34.6s | 8.3s | **4.2×** |
| `internal` env alone | 21.1s wall / 14.2s ty | 3.4s wall / 3.3s ty |
6.2× |

The `internal` env was the only workspace-kind ty env left. The other
envs (`master`, `data-platform`) already use the project-kind pattern:
dedicated `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` + persisted `.venv`, invoked via
`uv tool run --from ty==<pin>`. This PR brings `internal` in line.

The 18s wasn't ty — `ty check` itself was ~13s of CPU. The gap was uv
resolving + linking a fresh overlay venv every invocation, because
`--isolated` was load-bearing for correctness (the workspace's plain
`.venv` is missing test-deps the `[ty]` extra installed). Persisting the
env in `ty/internal/.venv` pays that cost once at sync time, not every
`just ty`.

## Changes

### New project-kind env

- **New `ty/internal/pyproject.toml`** (and generated
`ty/internal/uv.lock`) — project-kind env mirroring
`dagster-oss/ty/master`'s shape: dep list, `[tool.uv.sources]` editable
paths, and the `[tool.ty.*]` config block.
- **`justfile`** — `ty` and `quick-ty` recipes swap `--env-dir .` →
`--env-dir ty/internal`.
- **Root `pyproject.toml`** — drops the `[ty]` optional-dependency entry
and the env `[tool.ty.*]` block; root `uv.lock` rebuilt accordingly.
- **All three ty env pyprojects declare `[tool.uv] package = false`** —
they are virtual, dependency-only projects; uv installs the deps and
never builds the synthetic package itself. (The env locks already
recorded the roots as `virtual` since none declare a build-system; this
makes it explicit.)

### `run-ty.py`: workspace-kind support removed

With all envs now one kind, the `EnvSpec.kind` field, the
`[tool.uv.workspace]` auto-detection, the `_run_ty_workspace` invocation
path (`uv run --extra ty`), the kind dispatch in `run_ty`, and the
workspace special-cases in `normalize_env` /
`validate_editable_installs` are deleted. Every env venv now goes
through the same sync + legacy-`.pth` validation path.

### Env hygiene: installed-or-excluded invariant, no more `extra-paths`

The env enforces a simple invariant: **every python package under a
`[tool.ty.src].include` dir is either installed in the env (listed as a
dependency) or explicitly excluded.** Previously a long tail of packages
(integration test suites, toys, product-operations, dogfood,
agent-schema, host-schema, serverless agents, ...) was checked as loose
source with imports resolving only via a 47-entry `extra-paths` list
that pointed ty at uninstalled package sources. All of those packages
are now real editable installs, their third-party dep closures resolve
from the env venv, and `extra-paths` is deleted entirely.

Notes from making that resolve:

- uv applies `[tool.uv.sources]` only to requirements declared in the
same pyproject, so in-repo dagster libs that the new packages need only
transitively (`dagster-gcp`, `dagster-sling`, `dagster-helm`,
`dagster-dlt`, `dagster-fivetran`, `dagster-hightouch`,
`dagster-pandas`, `dagster-databricks`, `dagster-datahub`, `automation`)
are listed as direct deps to force the editable `1!0+dev` resolution.
- Two packages are documented checked-but-not-installed exceptions:
`services/dagster-cloud-user-code` (image-definition project, not a
buildable package) and `dagster-cloud-datahub` (`acryl-datahub`
hard-requires `sqlalchemy<2` vs the cloud stack's 2.x — hence its own
self-contained `uv.lock` and in-file `ty: ignore[unresolved-import]`).
- Explicitly excluded: `python_modules/platform-perf` (pins published
`dagster==1.10.16`, requires python <3.12) and the nine `services/*`
image-definition pyprojects (no python source).
- `product-operations` is installed without its `[tests]` extra
(`responses>=0.25` conflicts with `dagster[test]`'s `<=0.23.1` pin; it
has no test files).
- `agent_tests/pyproject.toml` becomes an explicit dependency-only
hatchling project (`bypass-selection = true`) — with no build-system
declared, the setuptools fallback refused to build it (flat-layout
auto-discovery: "Multiple top-level packages discovered"). Inert for CI:
its tox sets `skipsdist = True`.
- One real diagnostic surfaced once pyspark was actually installed:
`import_module("pyspark.sql").functions` →
`import_module("pyspark.sql.functions")` in the
dagster-ai-operational-data Glue template (the direct submodule import
is guaranteed; the attribute access was not).

### ty version pin

The env pyprojects no longer pin `ty` at all. The pin lives in root
`pyproject.toml` `[dependency-groups].dev` as a pure dev dep — `uv sync`
installs it into the workspace venv (so editors / the ty LSP run the CI
version), and `run-ty.py::get_dagster_ty_version` now reads it from
there, falling back to dagster's `[project.optional-dependencies].ty`
(needed post-OSS-sync where the internal root pyproject doesn't exist).
A new conventions lint (`test_ty_version_pins_agree`) keeps the two pins
in lock-step. `skills/update-ty` updated to describe the new structure.

### Editor-default `[tool.ty]` at the repo root

Editor-launched `ty server` discovers config from the workspace root and
never sees the env configs (`run-ty.py` always passes `--config-file`).
The root pyproject now carries an editor-default `[tool.ty]` block:
`python-version = 3.12`, the lint-mandated mirrored `[tool.ty.rules]`,
both graphene override blocks (internal + dagster-oss, root-anchored
paths), and default-include src with `respect-ignore-files` plus a small
exclude list for red-by-construction code (vendored/generated, awsglue
runtime scripts, platform-perf, notebook fixtures, docs snippets). Any
open file gets diagnostics, checked against the workspace venv; known
divergences from CI (non-workspace-member packages lack their
third-party deps; dagster-oss is 3.10 in CI) are documented in the
block. A gitignored local `/ty.toml` still takes precedence for personal
variants. Note: `include = ["."]` does NOT work (matches nothing) — the
block deliberately omits `include`.

### `--diff` routing bugfix

`run-ty.py` now passes `--force-exclude`: diff-routed paths are explicit
CLI paths, which otherwise bypass the env's `src.exclude`. Without this,
editing any env-excluded file spuriously fails `just quick-ty` — first
observed on this branch, where editing `scripts/run-ty.py` (excluded
from the 3.10 master env for its 3.11+ stdlib usage) produced
`tomllib`/`NotRequired` unresolved-import errors.

### Incidental fixes

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`: the pre-push ty hook ran `make quick_ty`, a
target that no longer exists (lost in the just migration). Now `just
quick-ty` with `pass_filenames: false` (filenames would conflict with
`--diff`).
- `test_dagster_module_publisher`: the dry-run test asserted the root
pyproject is always rewritten by the release pin-setter, which was only
true because the root `[ty]` extra contained `dagster-cloud==1!0+dev`.
With the extra gone the root pyproject carries no internal pins; the
assertion is loosened to "at least one pyproject modified".
(`ty/internal/pyproject.toml` needs no publisher attention — its deps
are unpinned and resolve editable via sources.)

### Version pins

The new env's free resolution surfaced 47 latent diagnostics — almost
all from third-party packages resolving newer than the workspace
lockfile, with stricter type stubs. To keep type-check parity,
`[tool.uv].constraint-dependencies` pins six packages to the workspace's
current lock versions:

- `sqlalchemy==2.0.36` (resolved to 2.0.49 → 28
`possibly-missing-submodule` warnings on `sqlalchemy.exc` / `.event` /
`.dialects`)
- `confluent-kafka==2.12.2` (resolved to 2.14.0 → 7
`invalid-argument-type` on `Producer.__init__` / `.produce`)
- `statsig==0.49.0` (resolved to 0.71.6 → 2 `missing-argument` on
`FeatureGate.__init__`)
- `boto3*==1.42.68` family (newer surfaced 4 `S3Credential` TypedDict
mismatches)
- `python-gitlab==5.0.0` (resolved to 8.3.0 → 1 `redundant-cast`
warning)
- `typer==0.16.1` (0.26's `Option` stub rejects `click.Choice[str]` in
dagster-cloud-worker)

These are flagged in the pyproject comment as bit-rot pins to revisit
when the latent diagnostics get triaged. Several look like real issues
hidden by the older stubs (e.g. `s3_client.py`'s `S3Credential`
TypedDict accepting `str | None` where it's declared `str`); future PR
territory.

## Known issue (pre-existing, not addressed here)

`uv lock` in `dagster-oss/ty/master` currently fails independent of this
PR: `docs-snippets[full]` now requires `apache-airflow>=3.2` while
`starlift-demo` pins `<3.0.0`, and the committed lock predates that
metadata. `just ty` is unaffected (`uv sync --frozen` doesn't
revalidate), but the next relock of that env will hit it.

## Test Plan

- [x] `just ty` from internal root: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 7138 files
across all three envs (exercises the single remaining runner path, env
sync, and `.pth` validation for every env).
- [x] `just quick-ty` on the branch diff: clean (exercises the
`--force-exclude` fix — `run-ty.py` itself is in the diff).
- [x] Conventions lint
(`conventions_tests/test_ty_config_consistency.py`): 6/6 passed,
including the new `test_ty_version_pins_agree` and the root
editor-default config in the rules-parity check.
- [x] Editor path verified end-to-end: bare `.venv/bin/ty check` from
repo root (config discovered from root pyproject, env auto-detected)
passes on member packages and both graphene override subtrees.

subject: [dagster] Recognize explicit minute lists in get_fixed_minute_interval (#25533)
body:
## Problem

`get_fixed_minute_interval` only recognized `*/N` minute fields as fixed-interval crons. An equivalent explicit list like `0,30 * * * *` (every 30 min) returned `None`.

That matters because `TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition.get_num_partitions_in_window` uses this to choose between:
- a fast arithmetic path (`minutes_in_window // fixed_minute_interval`), and
- enumerating **every** partition in the window through the cron iterator (`_iterate_time_windows` → `cron_string_iterator` → `_find_hourly_schedule_time` / `dst_safe_strftime`).

So for a `0,30 * * * *` asset, `num_partitions` / `SerializableEntitySubset.size` is **O(partitions-in-subset)** of pure-Python cron math.

This was the root of a production incident: when a large backfill grows such a subset, the streamline `asset-materialization-health` consumer rebuilds the minimal health state — which sizes the subset — on **every event**, making the run **O(N²)** and pegging a single core for hours. (A profile showed `_find_hourly_schedule_time` / `dst_safe_strftime` dominating, all under `num_partitions`.)

## Fix

Recognize an explicit minute list as a fixed interval when every higher field is a wildcard (so the schedule repeats identically each hour) **and** the ticks — including the wrap from the last tick to the first tick of the next hour — are evenly spaced:

- `0,30 * * * *` → 30
- `0,15,30,45 * * * *` → 15
- `0,20,40 * * * *` → 20
- `5,35 * * * *` → 30 (evenly spaced even though it doesn't start at `:00`)

Unevenly-spaced lists (`0,20`, `0,30,45`) and lists with a constrained higher field still return `None`. (Even spacing across `[0,60)` guarantees the gap divides 60, matching the existing `*/N` rule.)

This is a pure optimization: it only turns previously-`None` results into correct fixed intervals; no previously-non-`None` result changes.

## Test

Added cases to `test_cronstring.py` covering the evenly-spaced lists (→ interval), the unevenly-spaced ones (→ `None`), and the offset-but-even case `5,35`.

subject: Make @record honor AbstractSet annotation in runtime checks (#25525)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a production 500 on the Insights **by-asset** GraphQL query
(`reportingMetricsByAsset` / `InsightsAssetsQuery`) when an all-assets
selection (`assetSelection: "*"`) is used.

### Root cause

A `@record` field annotated `AbstractSet[X]` accepts any
`collections.abc.Set` per the type system (a `dict_keys` view **is** an
`AbstractSet`). But `@record`'s generated runtime check routed both
`set[X]` and `AbstractSet[X]` to `check.set_param`, which only accepts
concrete `set`/`frozenset` via `isinstance(obj, (frozenset, set))`. So a
type-valid `AbstractSet` instance like a `dict_keys` raised
`ParameterCheckError` at construction:

```
ParameterCheckError: Param "asset_keys" is not one of ['frozenset', 'set']. Got dict_keys([...])
```

The trigger: `assetSelection: "*"` resolves to a single-operand
`AndAssetSelection`, and `reduce(operator.and_, (one,))` returns that
operand **unchanged** — so the `dict_keys` returned by the asset graph's
`get_all_asset_keys()` flowed straight into an `AbstractSet`-annotated
`@record` field (`AssetKeySet.asset_keys`). With ≥2 operands the `&`
would have coerced it to a `set`, masking the bug.

`set_param` was the lone container check that ignored its ABC —
`Mapping`/`Sequence`/`Iterable` annotations already accept any instance
of their ABC (with a fast-path for the concrete type). This change
mirrors the existing `dict`→`dict_param` / `Mapping`→`mapping_param`
split for sets.

### Changes

- Add `abstract_set_param` / `opt_nullable_abstract_set_param`
validating against `collections.abc.Set`, still enforcing the `of_type`
element check.
- Route `AbstractSet[X]` and `AbstractSet[X] | None` `@record` fields to
the new lenient checks.
- Concrete `set[X]` fields stay strict via `set_param`; direct
`check.set_param(...)` callers are unchanged.
- Tests: extended `BUILD_CASES` (concrete `Set` rejects `dict_keys`;
`AbstractSet` accepts it but still type-checks elements) and added
direct unit tests for both new functions.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files
- [x] Builder-case + direct-function assertions verified against source
(incl. the exact prod scenario)
- [x] `just ty` on the check module — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [x] `dagster-shared` pytest (`test_check.py` + `test_record.py` +
`test_record_jit.py`) — 322 passed, including the new set-leniency cases

subject: Fix stuck backfills when a parent skips holidays and its child does not due to subsets containing invalid windows (#25484)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where an asset backfill gets stuck — it stops emitting runs but never completes — when an asset whose partitions definition **includes** holidays depends on an asset whose definition **excludes** them.

### Root cause

`TimeWindowPartitionsSubset.__sub__` and `__and__` operate purely on timestamps. They can produce time windows that span only excluded dates (e.g. a weekend plus a holiday in a partitions definition that excludes holidays). Such a window contains **zero partition keys**, but it is still kept in `included_time_windows`. As a result the subset reports `is_empty == False` while `num_partitions`/`size == 0`.

The backfill daemon (`_should_backfill_atomic_asset_subset_unit`) uses `EntitySubset.is_empty` to decide whether a child is still waiting on a parent. For a child that includes holidays depending on a parent that excludes them, `parent_target − parent_materialized` leaves these phantom holiday-only windows. `is_empty` then lies (returns `False`), so the daemon believes the child still can't be grouped with its already-fully-materialized parent, takes the "parent is requesting a different set of partitions" branch, and filters out the **entire** child subset. This repeats every iteration → the backfill never makes progress.

### Fix

Normalize the results of `__sub__` and `__and__` to drop any window that contains no partitions, reusing the existing `TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition.has_any_partitions_in_window` helper (added in #20753). This restores the invariant — already relied on elsewhere — that every window in a subset contains at least one partition, mirroring the exclusion-aware merging done when building a subset from partition keys.

### Verification

- Reproduced against a real stuck backfill via the `simulate_backfills` shadow script: before the fix it raised `Backfill stopped emitting runs but is not complete` at iteration 3; after the fix it completes in 4 iterations, correctly requesting the previously-stuck child.
- Added two regression tests (`test_subtract_leaves_no_exclusion_only_windows`, `test_intersection_leaves_no_exclusion_only_windows`) that fail without the fix and pass with it.
- Full `test_time_window_partitions.py` suite passes (151 tests); `just ruff` clean.

subject: [ui] Allow creating a saved selection from lineage view (#25415)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

When clicking "Save selection" from the Asset Graph Explorer, the catalog view dialog was not capturing the current graph's asset selection (the `opsQuery` from the explorer path). Instead, it relied solely on `currentAssetSelection` from the `CatalogViewContext`, which may not reflect what's displayed in the graph.

This fix passes the `explorerPath.opsQuery` directly to `CreateCatalogViewButton` as an `assetSelection` prop. When provided, the button sets the internal asset selection before opening the create view dialog, ensuring the correct selection is pre-populated. The visibility logic also now uses this explicit selection when determining whether to render the button.

Additionally, the default label casing was corrected from `'Save Selection'` to `'Save selection'`.

subject: Fix SqlPollingEventWatcher.close() deadlock when callback re-enters unwatch_run (#25432)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes a teardown deadlock in `SqlPollingEventWatcher.close()` that
surfaced as `Failed: Timeout (>240.0s) from pytest-timeout` in
`TestPostgresEventLogStorage.test_watch_unwatch` ([master build
155280](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/155280#019eacad-a73d-4453-b8f0-1ce503877bac)).

PR #33732 (`8750f882227`, May 27) fixed the original
`_callback_fn_list_lock` self-deadlock by snapshotting the callback list
before firing callbacks outside the lock, and re-enabled the
previously-skipped `test_watch_unwatch` regression. That fix exposed a
second, distinct deadlock cycle on `_dict_lock`:

1. A watcher thread fires a user callback (now outside any lock).
2. The callback — e.g. the test's `_unsub` at
`event_log_storage.py:2724` — calls `storage.end_watch(...)` →
`SqlPollingEventWatcher.unwatch_run()` → blocks on `with
self._dict_lock`.
3. Concurrently, the test's `instance_for_test` exits and runs
`dispose()` → `close()`, which grabs `_dict_lock` first.
4. Inside the lock, `close()` calls `join()` on each watcher thread. The
watcher is blocked on `_dict_lock`. The main thread waits forever on
`join()`.

The Buildkite timeout dump shows the hung thread parked at
`polling_event_watcher.py:82` inside `unwatch_run`, called from
`_unsub`, which matches this cycle exactly. The test body passed
(279/279); only teardown deadlocked.

## Fix

Hold `_dict_lock` only long enough to snapshot the watcher list, set
`should_thread_exit`, and clear the dict. Then `join()` the snapshot
**outside** the lock. The thread's pending `unwatch_run()` call can now
acquire the lock briefly (finds no entry, since the dict was cleared)
and return, letting the thread exit cleanly and `join()` complete.

```python
def close(self) -> None:
    if not self._disposed:
        self._disposed = True
        with self._dict_lock:
            watcher_threads = list(self._run_id_to_watcher_dict.values())
            for watcher_thread in watcher_threads:
                if not watcher_thread.should_thread_exit.is_set():
                    watcher_thread.should_thread_exit.set()
            self._run_id_to_watcher_dict = {}
        # Join outside _dict_lock — see comment.
        for watcher_thread in watcher_threads:
            watcher_thread.join()
```

`self._disposed = True` is set before the lock release, so any racing
`watch_run` call still trips the `not self._disposed` invariant check.

## Test plan

- [x] `just check_ruff` clean
- [x] `just ty` clean (4775 files, 0 errors)
- [ ] Buildkite green on the existing `test_watch_unwatch` regression
across the SQL polling-watcher matrix (sqlite, consolidated-sqlite,
postgres). This is the regression test re-enabled by #33732 — it was
passing flakily before this fix; it should now be stable.

subject: Add REFRESH_DURATIONS mode to internal pipeline for pytest-split duration refresh (#22765)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Stacked on #22715 (pytest-split adoption). That PR introduces splitting
via `pytest-split` but, without `.test_durations*` files, splitting
falls back to count-based balancing. This PR wires up the machinery to
produce and consume per-suite duration data.

Rather than maintain a separate Buildkite pipeline whose suite list
duplicates the split config in `python_packages.py` / OSS `packages.py`,
refresh runs as a **mode** of the existing `internal` pipeline. The same
split config drives both normal sharded CI and the periodic refresh — no
separate list to keep in sync. Refresh is triggered manually (no
schedule); a Buildkite block step gates the final PR-creation step so a
human can inspect the collected artifacts before they're committed.

## How it works

**`REFRESH_DURATIONS=1` flag.** A new `BuildConfig.refresh_durations`
boolean lives in `buildkite-shared/context.py` and is settable via the
`REFRESH_DURATIONS` env var or `[REFRESH_DURATIONS]` magic string in the
build message.

**Step generation diverges in `PackageSpec.build_steps`.** For each tox
factor:

- **`splits > 1` in refresh mode:** collapse the parallel fan-out to a
single un-sharded step with `--store-durations --durations-path
.test_durations-<factor>[-<label_suffix>]`. Soft-fails so one broken
suite doesn't lose the rest. A `command_wrapper` does `set +e; <tox>;
status=$?; cd "$BUILDKITE_BUILD_CHECKOUT_PATH"; buildkite-agent artifact
upload "<dir>/.test_durations-..."; exit $status` — disables `set -e` so
the upload always runs, and `cd`s back to repo root so the artifact is
stored with its full repo-relative path (basenames would collide across
packages).
- **`splits <= 1` in refresh mode:** emit a normal step (which the
top-level filter drops). Not emitting nothing keeps OSS helpers like
`build_helm_steps` (`assert len(pkg_steps) == 1`) working.
- **Normal mode:** unchanged behavior plus `--durations-path
.test_durations-<factor>[-<label_suffix>]` so pytest-split reads exactly
the file refresh writes. Naming includes `label_suffix` to keep OSS
dagster-dbt's four `<deps>-core-main` ToxFactors (rest / test_resource /
test_asset_checks / cli) from clobbering each other's files.

**Top-level transform via `apply_transforms`.**
`InternalBuildkiteContext.apply_transforms` is overridden to run
`refresh_durations.apply` before delegating to the shared transform. The
transform:

1. Drops every step that doesn't carry `--store-durations` (i.e. lint,
kaniko, helm, dogfood, etc. — emitted normally during pipeline
construction, pruned here).
2. Scrubs dangling `depends_on` references on surviving steps (e.g. OSS
k8s-test-suite refresh leaves carry `depends_on: [test-project-3-12]`
pointing at an image-build step that was just filtered out — without
scrubbing, BK rejects the pipeline upload).
3. Appends a `BlockStepBuilder("approve-test-durations-pr")` step
depending on every refresh tox step's key, and a
`create-test-durations-pr` step depending on the block. The PR step runs
only after a reviewer clicks unblock.

In refresh mode the buildevents / AI-assessment steps get stripped too
(they don't carry `--store-durations`); acceptable for a manual refresh.

**`inject_flakes_clones` opt-out.** The quarantine flake-clone injector
early-returns in refresh mode — clones would inherit the
`--store-durations` flag, survive the filter, and race the original on
the same artifact path with `RUN_QUARANTINED=1`'s different test set.

**`get_python_package_step_skip_reason` left unchanged.** Refresh-mode
bypass of change-detection happens inside `_append_steps_for_cell`
(`skip_reason=None` only for the refresh-step emit), so external callers
like `skip_release_pipeline` and `_get_app_cloud_step_skip_reason` keep
their normal semantics.

**Aggregation step.** `scripts/buildkite/create_test_durations_pr.sh`:

- Downloads `**/.test_durations*` artifacts; treats "no artifacts" as a
clean no-op.
- Validates each file is non-empty + parseable JSON; skips invalid files
so a half-written durations file from a crashed tox run never lands in
the repo.
- Uses `find -print0 | xargs -0 git add` so any future
whitespace-in-path doesn't split.
- Pushes via `GIT_ASKPASS` helper with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, so
`ELEMENTL_DEVTOOLS_PAT` never appears in argv or git's error output.
- Opens the PR via the GitHub REST API (slim image has no `gh` CLI).
Retries on HTTP `000`/`5xx`/`429`; treats `422` (PR already exists for
this branch) as success.

**Internal-pipeline conditional carves out
`auto/refresh-test-durations/*`.** The existing `(build.author.name !=
"elementl-devtools") && ...` filter would otherwise skip CI on the
auto-PR (it's authored by elementl-devtools). The carve-out runs
internal CI on the durations PR so the new files get validated by the
pipeline that consumes them before merge.

## Changes

- `dagster-oss/.buildkite/buildkite-shared/buildkite_shared/context.py`
— `BuildConfig.refresh_durations` field.
- `dagster-oss/.buildkite/buildkite-shared/buildkite_shared/packages.py`
— refresh-mode branch in `_append_steps_for_cell` + extracted
`_append_refresh_step` helper; `--durations-path` added to normal split
mode.
-
`.buildkite/dagster-internal-buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/context.py`
— `InternalBuildkiteContext.apply_transforms` override calling
`refresh_durations.apply` before `super`.
-
`.buildkite/dagster-internal-buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/steps/refresh_durations.py`
— filter + scrub-deps + block + PR step builder.
-
`.buildkite/dagster-internal-buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/steps/quarantine.py`
— early-return in refresh mode.
- `infra/terragrunt/modules/buildkite-pipelines/pipelines.tf` —
`auto/refresh-test-durations/*` carve-out on the internal pipeline's
author conditional.
- `scripts/buildkite/create_test_durations_pr.sh` — REST-API PR creation
+ HTTPS push with PAT via `GIT_ASKPASS` + JSON validation + retries.

### Removed (superseded by this PR's earlier iteration)

- The previously-added dedicated `refresh-test-durations` pipeline:
`pipelines/refresh_test_durations.py`, its `cli.py` entry, the
`pyproject.toml` script, the Terragrunt module, and the steps YAML — all
replaced by the in-pipeline mode above.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Merge #22715 first; this PR is a no-op on its own for normal CI
runs (files don't exist yet, pytest-split falls back to count-based
balancing).
- [ ] After merge, kick off a manual `internal` build with
`REFRESH_DURATIONS=1` in the build env (or include `[REFRESH_DURATIONS]`
in a commit message on a feature branch) and confirm:
- [ ] Only split tox suites run, each as one un-sharded job with
`--store-durations`.
- [ ] After the suites finish, the `approve-test-durations-pr` block
step appears for manual unblock.
- [ ] Clicking unblock runs `create-test-durations-pr`, which downloads
artifacts and opens an `auto/refresh-test-durations-<date>-<build>` PR.
- [ ] That PR's internal-pipeline CI build runs (carve-out works) and
the `.test_durations-*` files balance subsequent normal-mode shard
distributions after merge.

subject: fix(dagster-cloud-cli): use OSS-internal-compatible relative path to dagster-shared (#25430)
body:
## Summary

`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/pyproject.toml`
is the only dagster-oss pyproject whose `[tool.uv.sources]` references
`dagster-shared` via the longer
`../../../python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared` form. Every other
pyproject uses the simpler `../dagster-shared`. Normalize this one to
match.

```diff
 [tool.uv.sources]
-dagster-shared = { path = "../../../python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared", editable = true }
+dagster-shared = { path = "../dagster-shared", editable = true }
```

Both forms resolve to the same on-disk path in the OSS-standalone repo
and in the internal repo's `dagster-oss/` mirror, so this is purely a
normalization — but the shorter form is robust to one CI scenario where
the longer form silently breaks.

## What the longer form breaks (and the shorter one fixes)

The `elementl-code-locations / deploy-toys` GHA workflow stages the
Docker build context with:

```bash
cp -r dagster-oss/python_modules python_modules/toys/deps
```

Inside the container after `COPY . /opt/dagster/app`:

- `dagster-cloud-cli` lands at
`/opt/dagster/app/deps/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/`
- The old `../../../python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared` walks up to
`/opt/dagster/app/` then descends into a `python_modules/` directory
that no longer exists (the workflow renamed it to `deps/`). uv fails
with:
  ```
error: Distribution not found at:
file:///opt/dagster/app/python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared
  ```
- The new `../dagster-shared` only references the sibling name, so it
resolves to `/opt/dagster/app/deps/libraries/dagster-shared` ✓ — same as
in the OSS source tree.

This break was latent on master: no PR has touched
`python_modules/toys/**` (the path filter that gates `deploy-toys`) for
~a month, so the deploy job hadn't actually run.

The `uv.lock` already encodes `editable = "../dagster-shared"`, so no
relock is needed and the lockfile diff is empty.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduce the deploy-toys failure locally on master HEAD by
extracting `master:dagster-oss/python_modules` into a fresh `deps/`
build context and running the Dockerfile's `uv pip install` command →
matches the CI error exactly.
- [x] Apply this fix and re-run the same reproduction → 189 packages
resolve and build successfully.
- [x] `uv run --frozen python dagster-oss/scripts/update_lockfiles.py
dagster-cloud-cli` → no lockfile changes (already consistent).
- [ ] CI / next deploy-toys run.

subject: Fix PyYAML parser converting date-like strings to datetime objects in YAML config (#22450)
body:
## Summary

Fixes [GH-6465](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/6465)
(Linear GHIR-668): PyYAML's `safe_load` runs the
`tag:yaml.org,2002:timestamp` implicit resolver, so date-like strings
(e.g. `"2021-10-30"`, ISO timestamps) silently turn into `datetime.date`
/ `datetime.datetime` objects. That breaks any user-facing config that
expects those values as strings.

The fix is structural rather than per-call-site:

1. **Add `safe_load_yaml`** in `dagster_shared.yaml_utils` as a drop-in
replacement for `yaml.safe_load` that routes through the existing
date-resolver-stripped loader.
2. **Ban `yaml.safe_load` / `yaml.load`** via ruff `TID251`
(`flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api`) so new call sites can't regress.
3. **Migrate every existing call site** (~110 files across the monorepo,
OSS and internal) to `safe_load_yaml`.
4. **Rename `DagsterRunConfigYamlLoader` → `DagsterYamlLoader`** (and
the matching Dumper). The class is no longer run-config-specific; it's
the canonical "no datetime coercion" loader/dumper for
`dagster_shared.yaml_utils`.

## Key Changes

### `dagster-shared`
- New `safe_load_yaml(stream: str | IO) -> Any` in
`dagster_shared/yaml_utils/__init__.py`. Accepts a string or file-like
object; returns the same shape as `yaml.safe_load` minus the timestamp
coercion.
- `DagsterRunConfigYamlLoader` → `DagsterYamlLoader`,
`DagsterRunConfigYamlDumper` → `DagsterYamlDumper`. No external imports
referenced the old names, so the rename is contained to the one file.
- New test `test_safe_load_yaml_preserves_date_strings` asserting date
strings stay strings and that bare `yaml.safe_load` would coerce them
(the comparison baseline).

### Ruff configuration
- `dagster-oss/config/ruff.toml`: adds `yaml.safe_load` and `yaml.load`
to `[lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]` with a pointer to
`safe_load_yaml`.
- Per-file ignores for `dagster_shared/yaml_utils/__init__.py`
(implements the wrapped loader) and `dagster_shared_tests/test_yaml.py`
(asserts the bare-loader behavior for comparison). Mirrored in both the
internal `pyproject.toml` and `dagster-oss/pyproject.toml`.
- One inline `# noqa: TID251` in `automation_internal/cloud/deploy.py`
where CloudFormation custom tags require the full `yaml.Loader`; date
coercion isn't a concern there.

### Call-site migration
~110 files across `dagster-oss/`, `dagster-cloud/`, `python_modules/`,
`services/`, `infra/`, `dagster-internal-buildkite`, and
`buildkite-shared` are migrated from `yaml.safe_load` / `yaml.load(...,
Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)` to `safe_load_yaml`. Imports lifted to module
scope (no inline imports introduced by the migration).

### Buildkite package dependency wiring
The migration introduced `dagster_shared.yaml_utils.safe_load_yaml`
imports into three buildkite packages (`dagster-internal-buildkite`,
`buildkite-shared`, `dagster-buildkite`) that previously didn't depend
on `dagster-shared`. Each had `dagster-shared` added to its
`pyproject.toml` dependencies, with `tool.uv.sources` entries pointing
to the local editable path for the OSS standalone packages
(`buildkite-shared`, `dagster-buildkite`). Lockfiles relocked via
`update_lockfiles.py` and `just rebuild_uv_lock_file`.

## Verification

- `just ruff` clean — `TID251` ban active, all call sites migrated.
-
`dagster_shared_tests/test_yaml.py::test_safe_load_yaml_preserves_date_strings`
passes.
- `buildkite-shared` tox env: 19/19 tests pass.
- `dagster-buildkite` tox env: 12/12 tests pass.
- `dagster-internal-buildkite` tox env: 67/67 tests pass.

subject: chore(ty): bump ty to 0.0.44 (#25393)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Bumps the pinned `ty` (Astral type checker) version from `0.0.42` to
`0.0.44` and fixes the two diagnostics surfaced under the new version.

Both diagnostics stem from ty 0.0.44's tighter narrowing on TypedDict
subscripts and `callable()`-narrowed callable types — both expressions
previously typed concretely now fall back to `object`, breaking
downstream attribute access / return-type matching.

### Changes

- `pyproject.toml` +
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml`: `ty==0.0.42` →
`ty==0.0.44`. Both relocked (`just rebuild_uv_lock_file` for the root
lock; `python dagster-oss/scripts/update_lockfiles.py dagster` for the
dagster per-package lock) so all three ty envs (`master`,
`data-platform`, `internal`) pick up the new version.
-
`dagster-cloud/integration_tests/python_modules/dagster-cloud-e2e/dagster_cloud_e2e_tests/alert_tests/test_notifications.py`:
inside the `notification_type == INSIGHTS` branch, cast `test_spec.data`
to `InsightsNotificationData` (the subclass of `BaseNotificationData`
that declares `insights_url: str`). This matches the existing
`cast("MetricMonitorNotificationData", test_spec.data)` pattern used in
the sibling `METRIC_MONITOR` branches further down. With the narrowed
type in scope, the previously-needed `# ty: ignore[invalid-key]` on
`test_spec_data["insights_url"]` becomes redundant and is removed.
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/_core/definitions/input.py`:
in `InputDefinition.get_asset_key`, after `callable(self._asset_key)`
narrowing, ty 0.0.44 loses the call's return type (`AssetKey`) and
infers `object`, which fails to match the `AssetKey | None` annotation.
Cast `self._asset_key` to `Callable[[InputContext], AssetKey]` at the
call site, which restores the return-type narrowing and replaces the
older `# ty: ignore[call-top-callable]` suppression.

## Test Plan

- `just ty` → `Found 0 errors / Found 0 warnings` across all three envs
(`master`, `data-platform`, `internal`), 7093 files analyzed.
- `just ruff` → clean.
- Both lockfile bumps verified to reflect `ty==0.0.44` (`git diff
uv.lock dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/uv.lock | grep ty==`).

subject: release: unify pin rewriting via tomlkit (#25397)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Unifies the release-tag pin-rewriting machinery and switches the OSS tag
commit to a minimal-diff path so downstream PR (#25394) can reuse the
same helper.

Background: the OSS release pipeline currently uses
`mutate_dependencies` + `tomli` + `tomli_w` to rewrite intra-repo
dependency pins on the release-tag commit. That has two problems:

1. **It clobbers any matching dep, not just the dev sentinel.** Bare
`dagster-shared` in `dagster-cloud-cli/pyproject.toml` gets silently
auto-pinned to `dagster-shared==1.13.8`. That's correct behavior for
publishable wheels, but it bakes a code path that's wrong for internal
pyprojects where bare deps are intentional (editable-resolved via
`[tool.uv.sources]`).
2. **`tomli_w` round-trips the entire document.** Comments are lost;
lists are reformatted from single-line to multi-line; quote style
changes. The 1.13.8 OSS tag commit was ~2400 lines of churn, almost all
of it noise. Future tag commits would be reviewable.

## Approach

- **New shared helper `rewrite_dev_pins(content, new_versions)`** in
`dagster_module_publisher.py`. Uses tomlkit so the only diff on the
rewritten file is the changed pins — comments, list formatting, and
surrounding tables are byte-identical. Selective: only `==1!0+dev` pins
for known packages are touched.
- **`PyProjectDagsterModule.set_pin_info`** now delegates to the helper.
The post-rewrite verifier (`_verify_all_dagster_packages_are_pinned`)
still runs and still enforces strict pinning for publishable
distributions.
- **`PyProjectDagsterModule.set_version_info`** now uses tomlkit
(instead of `tomli`+`tomli_w`) to rewrite the `[project].version` field,
so the line change is the only churn.
- **`mutate_dependencies`** and its helpers (`_normalize_package_name`,
`_parse_dep_name_and_extras`, `parse_module_name_from_dep`,
`parse_version_from_dep`) are removed — fully subsumed.
- **Three OSS source pyprojects** had bare dagster deps in
`[project.dependencies]` / non-test extras that the old
`mutate_dependencies` silently fixed. With strict selective rewriting,
the verifier would catch them — so they're explicitly pinned to
`==1!0+dev` at source:
  - `dagster-cloud-cli`: `dagster-shared`
  - `dagster-airlift` (extras=tutorial): `dagster-webserver`
  - `dagster-aws` (extras=pyspark): `dagster-pyspark`
- **tomlkit** added to `automation-internal` deps.

## Test Plan

- 13 unit tests in `test_dagster_module_publisher.py` cover: selective
rewriting, PEP 503 name normalization (`dagster_k8s` ↔ `dagster-k8s`),
comment + formatting preservation, environment-marker preservation (`;
python_version >= '3.10'`), `[project.dependencies]` /
`[project.optional-dependencies]` / `[dependency-groups]` coverage,
no-op when no matches.
- Smoke test: dry-run `set_pin_info` against every one of the 76
publishable OSS modules with a synthetic version mapping — all pass the
verifier post-rewrite.
- `tox -e py312-conventions` passes 454/454 (including
`test_intra_repo_pins`, which is the relevant convention enforcement).
- `tox -e py312` (release tests) passes 20/20.

## What this unlocks

The next PR in the stack (#25394) extends the rewriter to also walk
internal workspace pyprojects, fixing the 1.13.8 serverless-agent
image-build break described in [shipit build
2083](https://buildkite.com/dagster/shipit-release-dagster-cloud/builds/2083)
and the [Slack

subject: ruff: enable PLW1514 (unspecified-encoding) and fix violations (#25376)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Enables Ruff's [PLW1514
(`unspecified-encoding`)](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unspecified-encoding/)
and fixes the 576 violations it surfaced. `open()`, `Path.read_text()`,
and `Path.write_text()` calls in text mode default to the platform's
locale encoding, which is non-portable — on Linux/macOS that's typically
UTF-8, but it's not guaranteed and can produce silent decode mismatches
across environments. Making the encoding explicit removes that footgun.

This brings our ruff config one step closer to alignment with dignified
python.

PLW1514 is a preview-status rule. The repo's ruff config sets `preview =
true` with `explicit-preview-rules = true`, so adding the `"PLW"` prefix
to `select` doesn't pull it in — the rule has to be listed by exact code
(the existing `DOC102` entry follows the same pattern). This PR adds
`"PLW1514"` in that same block in `dagster-oss/config/ruff.toml`.

## Changes

- **`dagster-oss/config/ruff.toml`** — adds `"PLW1514"` to the `select`
list in the explicit-preview block, with a comment explaining why it's
listed by exact code.
- **243 `.py` files across 244 file edits** — `ruff check --fix
--unsafe-fixes` applied to every callsite: adds `encoding="utf-8"` to
`open()` / `read_text()` / `write_text()` / `codecs.open()` calls in
text mode. Followed by `ruff format` to re-wrap lines that became too
long after the kwarg was inserted.

Distribution by top-level directory:

| Directory | Files touched |
|-----------|---------------|
| `dagster-oss/` | 171 |
| `python_modules/` | 31 |
| `dagster-cloud/` | 23 |
| `scripts/` | 12 |
| `public/` | 2 |
| Other (`.buildkite`, `.github`, `infra`, `integration_tests`,
`skills`) | 5 |

The `dagster-oss/` portion will sync out to OSS.

## Why `--unsafe-fixes` is safe here

Ruff marks PLW1514's fix as "unsafe" because hardcoding
`encoding="utf-8"` could mask a real locale dependency on a non-UTF-8
system. I confirmed by file-extension audit that every affected callsite
reads/writes UTF-8 text formats — `.py`, `.yaml`, `.json`, `.toml`,
`.env`, `.md`, `.sql`, `.csv`, `.cfg`, `.log` — with zero binary-mode
(`"rb"` / `"wb"`) calls touched (ruff only flags text-mode opens, so
binary callsites are untouched by construction).

## Test Plan

- [x] `uv run --frozen ruff check` — passes.
- [x] `uv run --frozen ruff format --check` — passes.
- [x] Verified violation count went from 576 → 0 after autofix.
- [ ] CI green.

subject: dg: parse DG_PROJECT_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE .env via python-dotenv (#25358)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Closes dagster-io/dagster#31346. Refs GHIR-138.

The temporary backdoor for non-standard venv layouts (set `DG_PROJECT_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE` in a project's `.env` to override the python executable that `dg dev` launches) was parsing `.env` with a hand-rolled `startswith` + `shlex.split` loop. That parser only recognized bare `KEY=value` lines and silently ignored `export KEY=value`, quoted values, and trailing comments. The reporter on [dagster#31346](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/31346) (the venv-configurability issue this backdoor was added for) hit the `export` case and asked us to use `python-dotenv` so anything dotenv accepts works.

`python-dotenv` is already a runtime dependency of `dagster-dg-core`, so the swap is a few lines in `DgContext.project_python_executable`. The previous parser's only call site is this property, so behavior outside the backdoor is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_project_python_executable_env_file_formats` in `dagster_dg_core_tests/test_context.py` exercises each format dotenv handles (bare, `export`, single- and double-quoted, leading/trailing comments, sibling variables) plus the fallback to `.venv` when the variable is absent.
- Full `dagster-dg-core` test_context.py suite (68 tests) green under `tox -e py312`.
- `just ruff` and `just ty` clean.

## Changelog

[dg] `DG_PROJECT_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE` in a project's `.env` is now parsed via `python-dotenv`, so `export KEY=value`, quoted values, and trailing comments are honored.
