subject: Sphinx build does not catch missing docstring on public (#25154)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

The check guarding `@public` docstrings used `not hasattr(obj,
"__doc__")`, but every Python object always has a `__doc__` attribute
(it's just `None` when there's no docstring), so the condition was never
true and the check silently never fired. The fix changes it to not
`getattr(obj, "__doc__", None)`, which tests the docstring's actual
value so missing docstrings once again raise an error.

subject: daemon-test-suite: parallelize tox env with -n 4 --dist loadgroup (#23512)
body:
## Cause

The `daemon-test-suite` `py312` tox env runs ~527s on CI for 38 tests, all serial. `pytest-xdist` 3.6.1 is loaded transitively via `dagster[test]`, but the tox `commands = pytest -s -vv {posargs}` line has no `-n` flag, so xdist never gets used.

The 3 tests in `monitoring_daemon_tests/test_monitoring.py` share a session-scoped `hostnames` fixture wrapping `docker_compose_cm` — the same anti-pattern that broke PR #23506 (4 xdist workers each tried to bring up the same compose stack; 3 failed). This needs handling specifically; the remaining 35 tests don't share a docker compose stack and parallelize freely.

## Fix

- Change tox `commands =` to `pytest -s -vv -n 4 --dist loadgroup {posargs}`.
- Mark the 3 monitoring tests with `@pytest.mark.xdist_group(name="monitoring_compose")` so loadgroup co-locates them on a single worker (one compose stack per group, never racing).

`--dist loadgroup` (rather than `worksteal`) is the right scheduler when some tests *must* go to the same worker; pytest-xdist guarantees same-group tests share a worker. Worker count is fixed at 4 because `os.cpu_count()` inside K8s pod runners returns 1, defeating `-n auto`.

## Before / after

CI baseline: ~527s pytest serial (38 tests).

Estimated CI: ~3 minutes saved per run. The 3 monitoring tests stay on one worker (their docker compose runtime is the floor); the remaining 35 spread across the other three workers, so wall-clock goes from `serial(38)` to roughly `max(serial(3 monitoring), serial(35) / 3)`.

**Observed (job wall-clock, including tox setup):**

| Build | Branch | daemon-test-suite-3-12 |
|---|---|---|
| [155030](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/155030) | master | 417s (6m 57s) |
| [155046](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/155046) | this PR | **237s (3m 57s)** |

**−180s, 1.76× speedup.** Lands at the optimistic end of the predicted floor (`max(monitoring_compose ≈ 240s, test_memory ≈ 150s)`) — the `monitoring_compose` group is now the bottleneck as designed.

Local validation skipped — daemon-test-suite needs docker compose plus many dagster packages installed, so CI is the first real signal. Verified the Python `pytest.mark.xdist_group` decoration parses, and `tox.ini` parses as INI.

## Same assertions

No tests added, removed, skipped, marked `xfail`, or modified. The decorator only affects worker assignment; xdist scheduling is the only behavior change.

## Notes

`pytest-xdist` is already in the resolved deps via `dagster[test]` — no lockfile change required.

This PR explicitly avoids the trap that bit PR #23506: marking the docker-compose-bound tests with an `xdist_group` is the simple alternative to making the underlying fixture xdist-safe. PR #23507 takes the deeper-fix approach for the dagster-cloud-e2e suite where many more tests share the same compose stack.

subject: Fix get_fixed_minute_interval for time-constrained cron schedules (#25361)
body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/33912.

`get_fixed_minute_interval` is supposed to return a fixed per-tick
minute interval only for schedules that tick uniformly throughout every
hour of every day (e.g. `*/15 * * * *`), and `None` otherwise. It
guarded against constraints on the hour/day/month/weekday fields with:

```python
if not is_wildcard[1:]:
    return None
```

`is_wildcard[1:]` is a *slice of a list*, so `not is_wildcard[1:]` only
tests whether that slice is empty — which it never is for a valid
5-field cronstring. The guard therefore never fired, and a schedule like
`*/15 9-16 * * 1-5` (every 15 min, 9am–5pm, weekdays) was treated as a
plain `*/15` with a fixed 15-minute interval.

The downstream effect (per the issue): partition counting over a window
where the schedule doesn't tick gets wildly overcounted — e.g. an
overnight 4:45pm→9am window that contains a single partition was counted
as 65 — producing oversized backfills that get stuck.

## Fix

```python
if not all(is_wildcard[1:]):
    return None
```

Any constraint on a non-minute field now returns `None`, falling back to
the correct per-tick counting path.

## Test

Adds `dagster_tests/utils_tests/test_cronstring.py` covering basic
hourly/minutely schedules, valid `*/N` divisor schedules, non-divisor
`*/N`, and the previously-misclassified time-constrained schedules from
the issue.

subject: [helm] Give user-deployment replicas a consistent gRPC server id (#25359)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Followup to dagster-io/dagster#33908, which exposed `replicaCount` for
user code deployments.

With `replicaCount > 1`, each replica's gRPC server generates a random
uuid for its server id. dagit's `watch_grpc_server_thread` polls
`GetServerId` through the round-robining k8s Service, so it sees the id
flip-flop between replicas and treats every change as a redeploy —
firing continuous spurious code-location reloads.

This passes `--fixed-server-id` to `dagster api grpc`, set to the
deployment config checksum already computed for the
`checksum/dagster-user-deployment` rollout annotation. So:
- every replica reports the same server id, and
- the id changes *exactly* when the deployment is redeployed (the arg
moves in lockstep with the annotation that already triggers the rollout
— no new pod restarts are introduced).

Only the `dagster api grpc` branch is pinned. `dagster code-server
start` reloads in place by *changing* its own server id, so a fixed id
would suppress reload detection; and with multiple replicas a Reload
request only reaches one replica behind the Service, leaving the rest
stale. We therefore reject `codeServerArgs` combined with `replicaCount
> 1` via a template `fail`.

## Test Plan

- New schema tests: grpc server id equals the checksum, is stable across
identical renders, changes when config changes, code servers get no
`--fixed-server-id`, and code-server + `replicaCount=2` fails with a
clear message.
- Full `test_user_deployments.py` suite passes (81 tests).
- Manual `helm template` checks: id matches the checksum across
replicas, changes on an image-tag bump, and the multi-replica
code-server guard fails.

subject: [ui] Fix backfill "View runs" dialog not opening from step status modal (#25242)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the reported bug where clicking **"View runs"** inside the **"Step status for backfill"** modal does nothing — no dialog appears, no console error, no network request / 4xx.

### Root cause (most likely theory)

The "Step status for backfill" modal (`BackfillStepStatusDialog`) renders the partition step status matrix (`PartitionPerOpStatus` → `PartitionStepStatus`). That matrix opens its **own nested `Dialog`** (controlled by `focused` state, `PartitionStepStatus.tsx:272`) when a partition square's **"View runs"** menu item is clicked (`PartitionStepStatus.tsx:497-501`, which just calls `setFocused(...)`).

So this is a Blueprint **dialog nested inside another dialog**. Both use Blueprint defaults (`enforceFocus={true}`), and both portal to `document.body` as siblings. When the nested "View runs" dialog opens, the outer dialog's focus trap sees focus move to a node that isn't a DOM descendant of itself and yanks focus back — the well-known Blueprint nested-overlay focus-trap conflict. The net effect is that the inner dialog never takes focus, so clicking "View runs" *silently does nothing*. The absence of any network request / 400 is consistent with this being purely client-side overlay/focus management — the click never reaches a data fetch.

This matches the "it used to work at one point" report: the same `PartitionPerOpStatus` matrix is also used on the **non-modal** job Partitions page, where the nested "View runs" dialog works fine because it isn't nested inside another dialog. The regression appears tied to step-status being surfaced through a modal in the backfill context.

### Fix

Set `enforceFocus={false}` on the **outer** `BackfillStepStatusDialog` dialog so the nested "View runs" dialog can take focus. This is the standard Blueprint workaround for nested overlays and is scoped to the backfill modal only — the shared matrix on the Partitions page is untouched.

## Testing

⚠️ I was **not** able to run the UI verification suite (`yarn tsgo` / `yarn lint` / `yarn jest`) in this environment: the network policy blocks the Yarn 4 download (`HTTP 403` from `repo.yarnpkg.com` via corepack), so dependencies couldn't be installed.

The change is a single, standard Blueprint prop: `enforceFocus` is part of Blueprint's `OverlayableProps`, and the `ui-components` `Dialog` wrapper spreads `...rest` straight to `BlueprintDialog`, so it is type-valid.

**Please run locally before merge:**
- `cd js_modules && yarn tsgo && yarn lint && yarn jest`
- Manually: open a job backfill → "Step status" modal → click a partition square → **"View runs"** → confirm the runs dialog now opens.

## Notes / follow-ups (not in this PR)

While tracing this I noticed a separate, latent correctness issue: even once the dialog opens, `PartitionRunList` filters runs only by `pipelineName` + partition tag (`PartitionRunList.tsx:13-19`) — it ignores the captured `stepName`, and the `dagster/backfill=<id>` filter computed in `BackfillStepStatusDialog.tsx:81-84` is never threaded down. So the dialog can surface runs from *other* backfills touching the same partition. Happy to follow up with a separate PR for scoping if desired.

subject: Authenticate release changelog branch-tip fetch with devtools PAT (#25303)
body:
## Summary

The `:memo: changelog` step in the release pipelines runs `check_changelog.py --branch`, which does a `git fetch origin <branch>` to read `CHANGES.md` from the remote branch tip. This kept failing:

- Original code (plain fetch, inherits origin's SSH URL): `Permission denied (publickey)`
- #24807 (forced HTTPS): `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com'`

**Root cause:** on the k8s buildkite agents the *command* container is separate from the *checkout* container and has **no git credentials of its own**. The checkout container's SSH key is mounted via `gitEnvFrom: git-ssh-credentials` and is not shared with the command container, and no HTTPS credentials are configured there either. So a runtime `git fetch` of *any* protocol fails — neither #24807 nor the pre-#24807 code could ever work; they just produced different auth errors. (The alembic-check step hit this same wall and sidesteps it by not fetching — see `alembic_check/__init__.py`.)

**Fix:** the command container *does* get `buildkite-dagster-secrets` via `envFrom` (see `command_step_builder.py`), which exposes `ELEMENTL_DEVTOOLS_PAT` — a token with private-repo access. Use it to authenticate the fetch:

- Pass the PAT as an HTTP `AUTHORIZATION: basic` header via `git -c http.https://github.com/.extraheader=...`, rather than embedding it in the remote URL, so it never lands in argv-derived error output.
- Rewrite origin's SSH URL → HTTPS for the command (`url.https://github.com/.insteadOf=git@github.com:`) so the header actually applies.
- On failure, raise a `RuntimeError` built only from git's stderr (not the command), so the header is never surfaced.
- Outside CI the token is absent and git uses the local checkout's own credentials.

No pipeline plumbing was needed — `buildkite-dagster-secrets` is already mounted on every k8s command container.

Failing build that surfaced this: https://buildkite.com/dagster/release-dagster-oss/builds/138

## Test plan

- Ran `check_changelog.py 1.13.8 --branch release-1.13.8` locally (no PAT, ambient HTTPS creds) — fetched and the version check passed (exit 0); bogus version correctly trips the assertion.
- Ran with a dummy `ELEMENTL_DEVTOOLS_PAT` — confirmed the auth-header path is exercised (git attempts an authenticated HTTPS fetch) and that **the token does not leak**: the error contains only git's stderr, no header/argv/command echo.
- `just ruff` and `just ty` clean.
- The step is `.soft_fail()` so it never blocked, but it should now go green on the k8s agents.

subject: fix(buildkite): correct repeat_steps label and group multiplication (#25294)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fix two bugs in `[REPEAT=N]` and `[STEP_FILTER=…]` build-message directives and make them usable on the dagster-oss Buildkite pipeline. Two issues:

### 1. Bugs in `repeat_steps`

`buildkite_shared/transform.py:repeat_steps` had two bugs:

- **Label suffix discarded.** The code built a labeled `step_copy` with ` [i+1]` appended, then appended the *original* `step` to the output list. All N repeats showed up with identical labels in the Buildkite UI.
- **Group steps over-multiplied.** A group containing `k` leaves with `REPEAT=N` produced `N` outer group copies, each containing `k×N` substeps via the recursive call — `k×N²` total executions instead of `k×N`.

Restructured the function so the outer loop only repeats leaf steps; groups are emitted once with their substeps recursively expanded. Net behavior: every leaf step runs exactly `N` times in parallel, regardless of nesting depth, with distinct labels.

### 2. `apply_transforms` not wired into the OSS pipeline

`dagster_buildkite/cli.py` (both `dagster()` and `prerelease_package()` entry points) never called `ctx.apply_transforms(...)`, so `STEP_FILTER` / `REPEAT` / `NO_SKIP` were silently no-ops on OSS-pipeline builds. The internal pipeline already calls `apply_transforms`; this just brings OSS to parity.

`apply_transforms` is internally gated on `is_feature_branch`, so this remains a no-op on master/release builds — `simplify_steps` is the only effect there, which is harmless (unwrapping single-step groups).

## Test Plan

No existing tests cover `repeat_steps` in `buildkite-shared`. Validation strategy:

- Trigger a feature-branch build with `[REPEAT=3]` against a step inside a group and confirm the BK UI shows distinct `<label> [1] / [2] / [3]` jobs and a total leaf count of `3 × k` (not `9 × k`).
- Trigger a feature-branch build with `[STEP_FILTER=<substring>]` and confirm only matching steps (and their dependency closure) appear.

At some point, we made the `refresh` fn argument to
`useRefreshAtInterval` take a `Promise<void> | void`, but the
synchronous version does not actually work. The hook assumes it will see

subject: Replace custom --split with pytest-split for duration-based test balancing (#22715)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Replaces the custom `--split k/n` pytest plugin (defined in
`dagster-oss/conftest.py`) with the
[pytest-split](https://pypi.org/project/pytest-split/) plugin, which
supports duration-based test balancing across shards.

The old implementation divided the collected test list into contiguous
chunks of roughly equal **count**. Shards could be highly imbalanced
when slow tests cluster, since the slowest shard determines total CI
wall-clock time. pytest-split can balance by recorded test duration once
`.test_durations` files exist; without them it falls back to round-robin
equal-count chunks, so behavior is effectively unchanged on day one.

## What this PR does

- **Removes the custom plugin** — drops `pytest_addoption` /
`pytest_collection_modifyitems` for `--split` from
`dagster-oss/conftest.py`.
- **Defensive re-export in root `conftest.py`** — switches the per-hook
list of `pytest_*` re-exports to a `for`-loop with `hasattr`, so adding
or removing a hook in the OSS conftest no longer requires touching the
internal root.
- **Adds `pytest-split` as a test dependency** to the two packages whose
test extras drive split Buildkite steps: `dagster` (OSS core `[test]`
extra) and `dagster-cloud-dagit` (internal `[test]` extra). Relevant
`uv.lock` files are regenerated, including
`examples/docs_snippets/uv.lock` (which now picks up pytest-split
transitively via `dagster[test]` after the recent airflow-pin fix on
master).
- **Updates the OSS Buildkite step builder**
(`dagster-oss/.buildkite/buildkite-shared/buildkite_shared/packages.py`)
to emit `--splits N --group K` (pytest-split syntax) instead of the old
`--split K/N`.

## Behavior

Without `.test_durations` files (this PR does not add any), pytest-split
distributes tests by round-robin (every test gets duration 1). Same
number of tests per shard as before, but assigned in a striped pattern
instead of contiguous slices — effectively equivalent total runtime.
Once duration files are generated and committed, shards will start
balancing by recorded runtime automatically. That'll be done in a
follow-up.

## Test Plan

- CI should pass — pytest-split's no-durations fallback is functionally
equivalent to the old splitting.
- Confirmed no remaining references to the old `--split K/N` flag in
Python sources.

subject: fix(copybara): unstick sync pipeline (set -eu + drop treeless dest clone) (#25257)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Two fixes that need to land together to unstick the copybara sync
pipeline.

### 1. Drop `--filter=tree:0` from the destination clone

`dagster-dev monorepo-sync run` (added in #23251) clones the dest repo
with `--filter=tree:0` before pointing copybara at it via a `file://`
remote. This breaks copybara's first internal `git fetch`:

```
ERROR: Error executing 'git fetch file:///tmp/.../dest --verbose --progress -f refs/heads/master:refs/copybara_fetch/refs/heads/master' (exit code 128).
Stderr: remote: warning: lazy fetching disabled; some objects may not be available
remote: fatal: bad tree object fe1dd56e9197c41b5562c5064bc486c0c28717ef
fatal: protocol error: bad pack header
Error: Copybara failed with exit code 3.
```

Promisor-style partial clones can lazy-fetch missing objects for the
local checkout, but `git upload-pack` (what serves a `file://` fetch)
does not — it has to serve from local pack files. With `--filter=tree:0`
the tree objects copybara walks aren't present and aren't reachable
through `upload-pack`. No clean way to make a partial clone serve as a
promisor remote; the right fix is a full single-branch clone.

This bug has been latent since #23251 (Jun 2). The image was broken by
the same PR (no `python3` for `uv pip install --system`), so the sync
script silently no-op'd on every master commit, masking the clone bug
until the image was fixed by #25245 and the pin landed via #25247. First
observed at [build
9465](https://buildkite.com/dagster/copybara-internal-to-public/builds/9465).

### 2. Wrap each yaml's `commands:` into a single literal-block script
and add `set -eu`

The original silent-passing-while-broken behavior was: `uv pip install`
failed on the broken image, but bash continued to the next `commands:`
entry without `set -e`, then the `else` branch of the path-filter `if`
block exited 0, so the job reported **passed**. The only thing noticing
was the `monorepo-integrity` (formerly `copybara-integrity`) pipeline
failing on the unsynced backlog.

A naive fix would be to add `- set -eu` as a separate first entry in the
`commands:` list — but **Buildkite's Kubernetes agents run each
`commands:` entry in its own shell** (documented in this repo at
`.buildkite/dagster-internal-buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/pipelines/dogfood.py:152`),
so flags from one entry don't propagate. Each yaml now has a single
literal-block-scalar `commands:` entry with `set -eu` at the top, so the
flag covers every line.

`-o pipefail` is omitted because the image's `/bin/sh` is dash, which
rejects it ([build
9456](https://buildkite.com/dagster/copybara-internal-to-public/builds/9456)
showed `Illegal option -o pipefail`).

## What changes

-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/automation/automation/dagster_dev/commands/monorepo_sync.py`:
drop `--filter=tree:0` from the clone args. `--single-branch --branch
master` stays.
-
`infra/terragrunt/modules/buildkite-pipelines/steps/copybara-{internal-to-public,dagster-to-internal,skills-to-internal}.yaml`:
fold all `commands:` items into one `- |` literal-block script with `set
-eu` at the top.

## Test Plan

- `just ruff` clean.
- Atlantis plan on `buildkite-pipelines` shows the rendered yamls now
have one merged shell script per step starting with `set -eu`.
- After merge + apply, the next master commit that touches
`dagster-oss/` triggers a `copybara-internal-to-public` build whose
`dagster-dev monorepo-sync run -s dagster-outbound` actually clones the
dest, runs copybara cleanly, and pushes the catch-up commits. Then
re-running the `monorepo-integrity` pipeline should pass.

subject: fix(dagster-rest-resources): relock to capture pytest conditional deps for py310 (#25241)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Master `dagster-rest-resources` is broken under Python 3.10. pytest
crashes at import:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'exceptiongroup'
```

(seen on [build 154600 job
019e8e0b](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154600#019e8e0b-8946-4893-be8f-6ce7d9972e44)).

The cause is a stale lockfile. PyPI metadata for `pytest==9.0.3`
declares two conditional deps that the stdlib backfills on 3.11+:

- `exceptiongroup>=1; python_version < "3.11"`
- `tomli>=1; python_version < "3.11"`

`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-rest-resources/uv.lock`
had pytest's `dependencies = […]` listing only `colorama / iniconfig /
packaging / pluggy / pygments` — neither `exceptiongroup` nor `tomli`
appeared anywhere in the lock. py311/py312 worked because both modules
are stdlib there; py310 didn't get them installed, so pytest's `from
exceptiongroup import BaseExceptionGroup` blew up before any tests ran.

Plain `uv lock` was a no-op (the lock was internally self-consistent,
just wrong). `uv lock --upgrade-package pytest` forced a re-resolve from
current PyPI metadata and produced a lock that includes the two missing
packages plus the cp310/cp311 wheel rows that several already-pinned
deps (`black`, `pydantic-core`, `pytokens`, `pyyaml`) were also missing.
This is the only dagster-oss package lockfile that exhibited this bug —
every sibling lockfile already has the entries.

## Test Plan

- `python dagster-oss/scripts/update_lockfiles.py dagster-rest-resources
--check` → OK
- Buildkite `dagster-rest-resources` py310 step in this PR's build

subject: fix(dagster-shared): match_type Required/NotRequired support for TypedDict on Python 3.10 (#25240)
body:
## Summary

PR #22307 added `Required` / `NotRequired` support to `match_type()` in
`dagster-shared`, but the implementation read `__required_keys__` off
the TypedDict to decide which keys must be present. On Python 3.10,
`typing.TypedDict` does not honor `typing_extensions.Required` /
`NotRequired` wrappers when populating that attribute — it marks every
annotated key as required regardless of the wrapper. A class like

```python
class RequiredTypedDict(TypedDict):
    name: Required[str]
    count: NotRequired[int]
```

ends up with `__required_keys__ == {"name", "count"}` on 3.10, so
`match_type({"name": "x"}, RequiredTypedDict)` returned `False` instead
of `True`. This tripped the `dagster-shared-3-10` suite on the 1.13.8
release-cut build
([154600](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154600#019e8e0b-894d-427d-92ed-74856db1d719))
with `test_match_type[obj41-RequiredTypedDict-True]`.

## Fix

For each field, compute required-ness as a hybrid of `__required_keys__`
and the annotation wrapper:

- If the annotation is wrapped in `Required` → required.
- If the annotation is wrapped in `NotRequired` → optional.
- Otherwise → fall back to `k in __required_keys__`.

Reading `__required_keys__` for the fallback (rather than the enclosing
class's `__total__`) is important so that **inherited** TypedDict fields
keep the per-class `total` of the class that declared them. A child with
`total=False` does not relax an inherited required field, and vice
versa.

`is_typeddict` is also moved to the `typing_extensions` import for
parity — on 3.10, `typing.is_typeddict` does not recognize classes
derived from `typing_extensions.TypedDict`.

## Test plan

New parametrized cases cover both inheritance directions:

- `TotalFalseChild` inherits a required field from a `total=True` base —
still required.
- `TotalTrueChild` inherits an optional field from a `total=False` base
— still optional.

Local:

- [x] `tox -e py310 -- -k test_match_type` → 51 passed (was 1 failed
pre-fix)
- [x] Full `tox -e py310` for dagster-shared → 312 passed
- [x] Full `tox -e py312` for dagster-shared → 312 passed
- [x] `just ruff` clean

Internal-RevId: 2fbda888ed00a113ba4956c6843431167eead261

subject: [ui] Fix partition step status labels/squares broken by CSS Modules migration (#25223)
body:
The styled-components -> CSS Modules migration (#23753) left two
elements in
the partition step status grid using literal class-name strings that no
longer
match the now-hashed CSS Module selectors:

- TopLabelTilted rendered `<div className="tilted">`, so the
  `.topLabelTiltedInner > div.tilted` rule (rotate(-41deg), absolute
  positioning) never applied. The tilted date/key labels collapsed into
  overlapping horizontal text.
- PartitionSquare rendered `className={`square ${squareStatus}`}`, so
the
  `.gridColumn .square` styling never applied.

Use the hashed class names from the CSS Modules instead. The square
classes
live in RunMatrixUtils.module.css (alongside `.gridColumn`), so
reference them
via an explicit import of that module.

Note: jest maps CSS via identity-obj-proxy, so `styles.x === 'x'` and
the
hashing mismatch is invisible to the test suite -- only the real Next.js
build
hashes the class names, which is why this regression shipped.

subject: refactor(dagster-dg-cli): inline test-fixture recorder, drop automation dep (#25225)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

`dg api` command tests use recorded GraphQL responses checked into
`dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/api_tests/<domain>_tests/recordings/`.
The tool that regenerates those recordings (`dg-api-record`) used to
ship as a subcommand of the `dagster-dev` CLI in
`dagster-oss/python_modules/automation/`. That meant `dagster-dg-cli`
listed `automation` in its `[dependency-groups].test` solely so
contributors could run `make rerecord` — an unrelated OSS package pulled
in as a dev dependency for one fixture-regeneration script.

The script's audience is also already Labs-only: it authenticates to a
live Dagster Plus deployment via `DagsterPlusGraphQLClient`, so a
pure-OSS contributor without Plus credentials can't run it regardless of
where it lives. The `automation` indirection was buying nothing.

This PR moves the recorder into `dagster-dg-cli`'s own test tree as a
private helper, and drops the `automation` dependency.

## What changed

- **Move**:
`automation/automation/dagster_dev/commands/dg_api_record.py` →
`dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/api_tests/_record.py`.
Co-located with the fixtures it writes; the `find_repo_root()`
six-level-`parent` walk becomes `API_TESTS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent`.
- **Invocation**: the 11 `<domain>_tests/Makefile` (and the parent
`api_tests/Makefile`) `rerecord` targets now call `python ../_record.py
<domain>` (or `python ./_record.py` at the parent) instead of
`dagster-dev dg-api-record <domain>`.
- **Drop the dep**: removed `"automation"` from
`dagster-dg-cli/pyproject.toml`'s `[dependency-groups].test` and the
matching `[tool.uv.sources]` entry. Relocked `dagster-dg-cli/uv.lock`
via `dagster-oss/scripts/update_lockfiles.py dagster-dg-cli` (~1.4k
lines of transitive editable graph collapse out).
- **Docs**: `dagster-dg-cli/README.md` and
`dagster-oss/RUN_API_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` updated to the new
invocation.
- **dignified-python cleanup** (now possible because the file no longer
lives in a package that can't import `dagster_dg_cli`): four inline
imports inside `record_graphql_for_fixture` (`CliRunner`, `cli`,
`DgApiTestContext`, `get_config_or_error`) hoisted to module-level, and
both `open()` call sites gained `encoding="utf-8"`.

## What did NOT change

- The `<domain>` argument and `--recording <name>` option are unchanged.
- The on-disk recording layout
(`<domain>_tests/recordings/<fixture>/NN_response.json`) is unchanged.
- `scenarios.yaml` schema is unchanged.
- No `dagster-*` runtime package imported `automation` to begin with, so
no production code is affected.

## Test Plan

- `just ruff` — clean.
- `just ty
dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/api_tests/_record.py`
— 0 errors.
- `grep -r 'automation'
dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/uv.lock` returns
nothing — editable source genuinely removed from the lock graph.
- `grep -r 'dg-api-record' dagster-oss` returns nothing — no stale
callers.
- **Manual (reviewer)**: after pulling, with Plus auth in place, `cd
dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/api_tests/asset_tests && make rerecord`
should regenerate the asset recordings against your dev deployment
identically to the old `dagster-dev dg-api-record asset` invocation. The
recorder isn't exercised by automated CI (it needs live Plus creds), so
this verification has to be local.

subject: fix(dagster-test): poll for dg dev child-process exit instead of fixed sleep (#25198)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes a teardown-race flake in
`dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/test_dev_command.py`. The shared helper
`assert_projects_loaded_and_exit` (in
`dagster-test/dagster_test/dg_utils/utils.py`) sent SIGINT to `dg dev`,
called `proc.communicate()`, then slept a fixed 3 seconds and
hard-asserted that every previously-recorded child PID was gone. Under
CI load that fixed window was sometimes too short: a `dagster
code-server` child process was still in the middle of shutting down when
the assertion fired.

Seen on master build
[154407](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154407#019e8951-a231-417b-9c8f-36ff0909c5c9)
(`dagster-dg-cli-serial-3-12`):

```
AssertionError: Process 1529 (['/tmp/.../project-1/.venv/bin/python', '-m', 'dagster', 'code-server', 'start', ...]) is still running
```

The change replaces the fixed sleep + strict per-PID `is_running()`
check with `psutil.wait_procs(child_procs, timeout=30)`, which polls
until each child actually exits or the bounded timeout elapses. The
assertion now fires only on processes that are genuinely still alive
after 30s — preserving the "no leaked children" invariant without
depending on wall-clock luck. `cmdline()` lookup for the error message
is wrapped in `_safe_cmdline` so a process that exited between
`wait_procs` returning and the message being built doesn't itself raise.

## Test Plan

- CI: `dagster-dg-cli-serial-3-12` and the broader `test_dev_command`
suite pass.
- Local: existing tests in `test_dev_command.py` exercise this helper;
behavior on the happy path is unchanged (children exit well under 30s).

subject: infra(buildkite): retire legacy EC2 queues, default to kubernetes-eks (#25185)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Retire the legacy EC2-backed Buildkite queues for the Dagster cluster
now that all jobs run on `kubernetes-eks`. The cluster default queue is
flipped from `buildkite-medium-october22` to `kubernetes-eks` via the
`buildkite_cluster_default_queue` resource (newly available after
bumping the `buildkite/buildkite` Terraform provider to 1.33.0), the
legacy queues are destroyed by removing their resource declarations, and
their EC2 CloudFormation stacks are stripped from `modules/buildkite/`.
The only EC2 stack that survives is `buildkite-docker` (queue
`buildkite-docker-october22`), which is still in use by
`.buildkite/dagster-internal-buildkite/` pipelines. Also removes the
dead `BuildkiteQueue.KUBERNETES_GKE` / `kubernetes-gke` references — GKE
was already retired but the enum value, helper-emoji branch, and
error-message text were still in place.

This addresses the situation Joe & I hit in [this slack
thread](https://dagsterlabs.slack.com/archives/C0AT2A1QJ6A/p1777411678042829)
on 2026-04-28 where the trigger-step bug forced us to manually mark
`buildkite-medium-october22` as the cluster default in the UI — that
workaround is now replaced with proper TF-managed configuration pointing
at EKS.

## What changes

**Provider:** `buildkite/buildkite` 1.16.2 → 1.33.0 in
`infra/terragrunt/root.hcl`. Multi-platform lockfiles regenerated in
`elementl/_global/buildkite/` and `elementl/us-west-2/buildkite/`
(darwin_arm64 / darwin_amd64 / linux_amd64).

**Cluster default → `kubernetes-eks`:** new
`buildkite_cluster_default_queue.dagster` in
`modules/buildkite-pipelines/clusters.tf`.

**Queue deletions** in `modules/buildkite-pipelines/clusters.tf`:
- `buildkite-medium-october22` → destroyed (resource + import removed;
was the existing cluster default)
- `buildkite-windows-october22` → destroyed (resource + import removed;
never had an EC2 stack to back it)
- `default` (id `12f7d3ac-99ae-4c3c-8abf-ebde770f596b`) → **delete
manually via the BK UI after apply.** Import + `removed { destroy = true
}` isn't supported in a single TF plan and a 2-PR import-then-destroy
dance isn't worth it for one idle queue.

**EC2 CF stacks stripped** in `modules/buildkite/main.tf`,
`modules/buildkite/cloudformation.tf` (deleted),
`modules/buildkite/variables.tf`, and
`elementl/us-west-2/buildkite/terragrunt.hcl`:
- Hardcoded `aws_cloudformation_stack.buildkite-default`,
`buildkite-medium`, `buildkite-medium-next` (and their IAM role/policy
attachments)
- The for_each `aws_cloudformation_stack.stack` scaffolding (the entire
`cloudformation.tf`) + `var.buildkite_stacks` input — the `medium` and

subject: fix(dagster-airlift): retry get_dag_run on 5xx to absorb SQLite-lock flakes (#25201)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

The `airlift-federation-tutorial-3-10` job flaked on master build
[154441](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154441#019e898c-9434-4ba9-ab63-5121cd7132c9):
`test_load_warehouse` hit `dagster_shared.error.DagsterError: Failed to
fetch dag run … Status code: 500` even though the Airflow scheduler had
logged the underlying `TaskInstance` as `state=success` ~5s earlier. The
500 came from the Airflow webserver's basic-auth `find_user` query
hitting `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` while the
scheduler was writing — a known SQLite contention window that the prior
4 vCPU bump (#24970 → `packages.py:387-396`) reduces but does not
eliminate, because the federation tutorial co-locates two `airflow
standalone` stacks + `dagster dev` in one pod.

`AirflowInstance.get_dag_run` raised on any non-200, so a single
transient 5xx during a `wait_for_run_completion` poll fails the whole
test. This PR adds a small bounded retry on 5xx responses inside
`get_dag_run` so a momentary lock-window 500 is absorbed without
altering the public surface.

## What changed

`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-airlift/dagster_airlift/core/airflow_instance.py`:

- New private helper `_get_with_5xx_retry(url, *, retries=3,
sleep_seconds=1.0, **kwargs)` that calls
`auth_backend.get_session().get(...)` and retries on any 5xx status,
returning the final response (success or terminal 5xx) for the caller's
existing error handling to surface.
- `get_dag_run` now routes through the helper. `wait_for_run_completion`
and `get_run_state` inherit the retry transitively since both call
`get_dag_run`.
- 4xx responses (e.g. nonexistent run id) still fail fast — no retry.

Scope is intentionally narrow: only `get_dag_run` is wired up, since
that's the path that just flaked. Other read endpoints can opt in later
if they exhibit the same symptom; gating the helper behind a per-call
switch keeps mutating endpoints (`trigger_dag`, `unpause_dag`,
`delete_run`) out of scope for any future retry expansion.

## Test plan

- New unit tests in
`dagster_airlift_tests/unit_tests/core_tests/test_airflow_instance_retry.py`:
- `test_get_dag_run_retries_on_5xx_then_succeeds` — 500-then-200
succeeds; `session.get` called twice; `time.sleep` called once.
- `test_get_dag_run_raises_after_exhausting_5xx_retries` — persistent
500 surfaces as `DagsterError` after 4 attempts (1 initial + 3 retries).
- `test_get_dag_run_does_not_retry_on_4xx` — 404 fails fast on the first
attempt.
- All 3 pass locally (`uv run … pytest …
test_airflow_instance_retry.py`).
- `just ruff` and `just ty` clean against the diff.

subject: [u][core][ui] Disable component id field, default to ComponentName[N] (#24006)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

This is a bit of a cross-cutting change, where we add in a new
configurable field to the json schema, and make the "Component ID" field
something that the user no longer needs to think about too hard, as
we'll auto-populate it from an available field.

The basic issue is thus:

- Each component instance needs a unique id
- For regular code based components, this is easy! Just use the
filepath, as of course that will be unique
- For ui-based components, we have no such luck -- we could randomly
generate an id, but that wouldn't be very user-friendly
- So instead, this PR does two things
- First, it allows you to set some metadata in your component schema
that will link a field of your choosing (e.g. job_name for an
AssetJobComponent) to the component id
- Then, it auto generates a component id that's basically just
ClassName[\<field name>] to use as the component id
- If you don't set this in the component schema, it just uses
ClassName[N] where N is an int that autoincrements as necessary

We could consider having a user-editable display name that layers on top
of this and can override it, but we do need to have consistent ids
somehow, and this seemed like a nice solution

subject: [dg] prevent committing of AI dispatch prompt artifacts into version control (#25160)
body:
## Summary

This PR simplifies the Dagster+ AI dispatch flow used by both:

- the Dagster+ Issues UI (`dispatchIssueAgent`), and
- `dg labs ai dispatch`.

Previously, dispatch created a branch by committing
`.dg/ai-dispatch/prompt.md` into the user's repository, and the GitHub
Actions workflow read that checked-in prompt file. The workflow then
generated a plan and stored the durable copy in the PR description.

This changes the flow so the prompt is passed as a `workflow_dispatch`
input, the dispatch branch is created with an empty commit, and the PR
description remains the durable source of truth for the generated plan.

## Why

This is primarily a simplification and artifact-cleanup change:

- Avoid leaving behind `.dg/ai-dispatch/prompt.md` artifacts in customer
branches.
- Keep implementation branches focused on actual code changes, not
dispatch bookkeeping files.
- Make the PR description the single place humans and the implementation
job look for the generated plan.
- Preserve the ability to create a draft PR immediately by using an
empty commit instead of a prompt-file commit.

## Changelog

- [dg] `dg labs ai dispatch` no longer creates a `plan.md` artifact in
version control

subject: Add `dagster-dev monorepo-sync run` command to orchestrate copybara syncs with fix-commit (#23251)
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `dagster-dev monorepo-sync run` command that orchestrates the
full copybara sync pipeline with automatic correctness checking. Instead
of invoking copybara directly (which pushes straight to the remote
destination), the `run` command:

1. **Clones the destination repo locally** (treeless clone for speed).
2. **Rewrites the copybara config** to push to the local clone instead
of the remote.
3. **Runs copybara** against the local clone.
4. **Inspects new commits** for extra files (caused by tree-overlay
reconciliation against a stale base — see
[#25133](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/25133)) and amends
them via the `fix-commit` logic from the parent branch.
5. **Pushes the corrected commits** to the real remote.

This is a safer alternative to the current approach where copybara
pushes directly to master on the destination repo, which can silently
revert internal-only changes to `dagster-oss/**` when an OSS PR lands
while internal hasn't yet synced its corresponding changes out.

### Changes

- **`monorepo_sync.py`**: Extracted `_fix_commits_in_range()` from the
`fix-commit` CLI handler so both `fix-commit` and the new `run` command
can share it (the extracted function carries the post-cherry-pick
recompute behavior introduced in the parent branch). Added
`_adapt_copybara_config()` helper for URL substitution. Implemented the
`run` command with `--dest-repo-url` override for testability.
- **Push error handling**: the final `git push origin master` in
`run_sync` is wrapped in `try/except subprocess.CalledProcessError`. On
failure it raises a `ClickException` that names the destination URL,
attributes the most common cause (the destination's master advancing
between clone and push), and tells the operator to rerun — copybara is
incremental, so the next attempt picks up both sides' new commits and
converges.
- **`config.py`**: Added `copybara_workflow` and `dest_repo_url` fields
to `SyncConfig` for all 4 sync configs.
- **Buildkite pipeline YAMLs**: Replaced direct `copybara` invocations
with `dagster-dev monorepo-sync run` in all 3 copybara pipelines
(outbound, dagster-inbound, skills-inbound). Added `uv pip install`
steps to make the CLI available.
- **`services/copybara/Dockerfile`**: Added `uv` installation so the
copybara container can run Python/dagster-dev CLI.
- **`test_copybara_sync.py`**: Added 4 tests for the `run` command
covering outbound sync, inbound sync, noop, and fix-commit integration
(with monkey-patched race condition simulation).

## Known limitation: hunk-level drift

The correctness check this layer applies is **filepath-set comparison
only** — it detects files present in dest but absent from source. It
does not detect line-level drift inside a file that both source and dest
touched: if internal modified `OpTags.tsx` for an unrelated UI reason
and an OSS PR also modified `OpTags.tsx` for icon entries, the resulting
dest commit will include both the OSS additions and a revert of
internal's drift on the unrelated lines — `OpTags.tsx` is in both
filechange sets, so the file-level check considers it fine. Tightening
to hunk-level would require diffing patches and comparing hunks across
the rename/move boundary; left as a follow-up.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Existing copybara-config-tests pass (run via tox in
`integration_tests/copybara-config-tests/`).
- [ ] New `run` command tests pass:
`test_run_outbound_syncs_and_pushes`,
`test_run_inbound_syncs_and_pushes`, `test_run_noop_exits_cleanly`,
`test_run_fixes_extra_files`.
- [ ] `dagster-dev monorepo-sync run --help` shows correct options.
- [ ] `just ruff` passes.

Internal-RevId: 44fe259e87c2b1eb13e64a703bc3156e8057c0f2

subject: Add fix-commit command to revert extra files from mismatched copybara syncs (#23083)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Adds a `dagster-dev monorepo-sync fix-commit` command that fixes
correctness mismatches by amending dest commits to remove extra files
introduced when an inbound copybara sync overwrites internal-only
changes (e.g. an OSS PR landing while internal-side commits to shared
files haven't propagated back to OSS yet — see
[#25133](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/25133) for the
failure mode that motivated this work).

When copybara syncs a commit from source to dest, divergence between the
two sides' tree states can cause the dest commit to include file changes
that weren't in the original source commit. This command automates the
fix by processing a range of commits from a starting point to HEAD:

1. Pre-computes which commits need fixing by comparing changed files
between source and dest commits (same logic as the correctness audit) —
used as a fast early-exit guard for "nothing to fix anywhere".
2. For a single commit at HEAD: directly amends to remove extra files.
3. For a range of commits: performs a cherry-pick rebase, amending each
affected commit and replaying subsequent commits on top. On each
cherry-pick the extras are **recomputed against the cherry-picked HEAD**
rather than reused from the precomputed table, since amending earlier
commits can shift the tree state of later cherry-picked commits in ways
the precompute can't anticipate.

**Usage:**
```
# Fix all commits from abc123 to HEAD
dagster-dev monorepo-sync fix-commit -s dagster-outbound --dagster-repo /path/to/dagster abc123
```

This is intended for use in a pipeline where copybara syncs to a local
copy of the dest repo, commits are inspected and fixed, and only then
pushed to the remote (the wrapping orchestration lives in
[#23251](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/23251)).

Also renames `_normalize_internal_files` to `normalize_internal_files`
and extracts `denormalize_file_path` into the audit module alongside it,
since both are now used outside the module.

## Behaviour when a commit can't be read

`_compute_extra_files` distinguishes two failure modes for
`get_changed_files` returning `None`:

- **Source commit missing** (e.g. force-pushed remote, shallow clone).
Operational and recoverable — emits a `WARNING` to stderr that names the
missing hash and tells the operator that any unintended file reverts in
the corresponding dest commit will not be caught. Returns `[]` and keeps
going.
- **Dest commit missing.** This is unexpected since `dest_hash` comes
from a walk of `dest_repo` itself. Raises a `ClickException`.

## Test Plan

- `test_fix_commit_amends_single_commit`: creates a mismatched HEAD
commit and verifies fix-commit amends it to remove the extra file.
- `test_fix_commit_rebases_range`: creates two synced commits, corrupts
the first, runs fix-commit from the corrupted commit, and verifies both
commits end up correct after the cherry-pick rebase. Exercises the
post-cherry-pick recompute path.
- Both pass under tox `py312`.

subject: fix(k8s-test-suite): preload helm-dependency images via kind load on Buildkite (#25137)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

On Buildkite, the supporting images for the k8s-test-suite helm install
(`postgres:14.6`, `rabbitmq:3.8.12`, `localstack`, `busybox`) were
pulled lazily by kubelet through the kind-registry → EKS
`dockerhub-mirror` chain at test-pod schedule time. That chain
occasionally returns a layer whose bytes don't hash to the manifest's
digest, containerd rejects the commit with `failed commit on ref ...
unexpected commit digest ... failed precondition`, and because every
test in the suite shares the same helm-installed postgres, a single
corruption event fails the whole run together — see the 3 `:gear:
k8s-test-suite-*-3-12` failures on internal build
[154116](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154116).

This PR moves the supporting-image pulls from kubelet-at-test-time to
fixture-init-time via a new `_kind_node_crictl_pull_with_retry` helper.
`crictl pull <image>` runs inside the kind node and routes through the
same CRI mirror chain kubelet would have used, but at preload time we
can wrap it in the existing exponential-backoff retry pattern
(`_docker_pull_with_retry` style: 6 attempts, ~155s envelope) so the
rare digest-mismatch flake retries loudly here instead of fatally
surfacing as `ErrImagePull` at test-pod schedule time — the dagster-k8s
client (`client.py:768`) treats that as terminal. Once the bytes are in
the kind node's containerd content store, `imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent`
(helm default) keeps kubelet off the network entirely for the rest of
the test session.

The test-project image still uses `kind load docker-image` (it lives in
private ECR; the kind-registry mirror only covers docker.io). I went
down two unrelated paths first that didn't work and want to record them
so future-me doesn't re-tread the same ground:

- **`docker pull + kind load docker-image` for the supporting images**
([build 154134](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154134)).
`docker save` produced a tarball whose manifest referenced the OCI image
index digest (`sha256:bea0c648fa6e...`), and `ctr image import` on the
kind node rejected it with `content digest ... not found`. Test-project
(private ECR, no multi-arch index) loaded fine; the docker.io images all
blew up.
- **`docker pull --platform linux/amd64`** to try to coerce docker into
dropping the index reference ([build
154151](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154151)). Same
exact `bea0c648` digest — pinning platform doesn't strip the OCI-index
ref that `docker save` preserves. Reverted.

`crictl pull` sidesteps docker entirely, so neither save-side issue
applies.

## Why the previous design didn't do this

The lazy-pull path was deliberately chosen in #24373 (5 days ago, DOCKER
→ KUBERNETES_EKS queue migration). The threat model that drove building
the kind-registry / EKS-mirror chain was **Docker Hub anonymous
rate-limiting** under shared NAT egress, not layer corruption. Once the
mirror chain dissolved the rate-limit problem, lazy pull at test time
was kept because the mirror's cold-cache cost was deemed not worth
paying eagerly. Corruption wasn't on the original threat list; now that
we have data on it, moving the pull earlier (where we can retry) is a
strict-improvement ratchet.

## Test Plan

- [x] Branch CI run — exercises the new preload path on Buildkite for
both k8s-test-suite and celery-k8s-test-suite (which share
`define_cluster_provider_fixture`).
- [ ] Watch first-pod-up time on the first few master runs (the
supporting-image pulls now happen at fixture init instead of at first
test-pod schedule).

Internal-RevId: 728d72d6b2eea5002149be4917507bf89124cd51

subject: fix(launcher-tests): ignore tempdir cleanup errors to fix history/runs race (#25141)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes a teardown-race flake in
`dagster_tests/launcher_tests/test_state_backed_component_lifecycle.py::test_state_backed_component_lifecycle`
first seen on master build
[154136](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154136#019e83bb-1a01-4a10-b20f-37c092da52e1):

```
OSError: [Errno 39] Directory not empty: '/tmp/tmp5aksn1m6/history/runs'
```

The test body completes (`RUN_SUCCESS` is logged) but
`instance_for_test()`'s `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory.__exit__` races a
gRPC code-server child still flushing run history under
`<tempdir>/history/runs`. `cleanup_test_instance` already `join()`s the
run launcher and the instance is configured with
`code_servers.wait_for_local_processes_on_shutdown: True`, but neither
fully closes the window on the children's SqliteRunStorage writes. Same
flake class as the airflow-standalone teardown races (see #24976) — fix
is the same: tell the stdlib to swallow rmtree errors on a directory
that is by definition ephemeral.

Two spots in the launcher_tests surface area can race this way:

1. `instance_for_test()` itself, when called with no `temp_dir=` it
creates its own `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` — this is the tempdir at
`/tmp/tmp5aksn1m6` in the failure above. Patched here covers every test
that lets `instance_for_test` create its own dir.
2. `test_invalid_instance_run` in `test_default_run_launcher.py` creates
an outer `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` and feeds it into
`instance_for_test(temp_dir=..., overrides={... SqliteRunStorage ...
base_dir: <tempdir>/history ...})` — same race, in the outer test's
hands. Patched defensively.

Both fixes are one-line:
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(ignore_cleanup_errors=True)` (Py3.10+,
already required by this repo). The cleanup error is purely cosmetic —
`/tmp` is system-managed; whether one stale dir lingers does not affect
test correctness.

Wider scan of `launcher_tests/`, `grpc_tests/`, and `api_tests/` turned
up no other outer-`TemporaryDirectory()` + run-storage patterns. The
remaining `TemporaryDirectory()` in
`test_state_backed_component_lifecycle.py` is only used to hold a
sentinel file (`write_state_calls.txt`), not run-history; left alone.

## Test Plan

CI exercises `test_state_backed_component_lifecycle` and
`test_invalid_instance_run` on every push; the flake is rare enough that
pattern review is more useful than a single green run.

subject: Fix YAML-based translation in DbtProjectComponent subclasses to translate dependency keys (#22302)

when a `DbtProjectComponent` subclass overrides `get_asset_spec`. The
root cause was that `get_asset_spec` delegated to `_base_translator` (a
plain `DagsterDbtTranslator`), so recursive dep resolution bypassed the

`DagsterDbtTranslator.get_asset_spec(self.translator, ...)` instead of

dependency resolution goes through the `DbtProjectComponentTranslator`
which applies YAML translation
- Added regression test
`test_subclass_with_yaml_translation_translates_dep_keys` that verifies
both asset keys and dep keys are translated when using a subclass with
YAML translation
- Extended `test_subclass_override_get_asset_spec_translator_metadata`

path

subject: Fix Databricks workspace job list pagination and rate-limit retry (#22303)
body:
## Summary

The Databricks Jobs API list endpoint returns paginated results, but the
previous implementation only fetched the first page. This change
implements proper pagination by checking the `has_more` field and using
`next_page_token` to fetch all remaining pages. Additionally, the
rate-limit status code constant has been renamed for clarity.

## Key Changes

- Implemented pagination loop in `fetch_jobs()` to iterate through all
job pages using `has_more` and `next_page_token`
- Added test coverage for pagination across multiple pages
(`test_databricks_fetch_jobs_pagination`)
- Added test coverage for rate-limit retry behavior with HTTP 429
responses (`test_databricks_fetch_jobs_rate_limit_retry`)
- Renamed `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` to `RATE_LIMIT_STATUS_CODE` for
improved code clarity

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Modified (2 files)
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-databricks/dagster_databricks/components/databricks_asset_bundle/resource.py`
- Implemented pagination loop and renamed rate-limit constant
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-databricks/dagster_databricks_tests/components/databricks_workspace/test_component.py`
- Added pagination and rate-limit retry tests

</details>

<details>
<summary>original-plan</summary>

# Fix Databricks Workspace Component Job List Pagination

## Context

The `DatabricksWorkspaceComponent` calls the Databricks Jobs API 2.1
`/list` endpoint to discover all jobs in a workspace. Currently, it
makes a **single API call** and uses whatever comes back — but the
Databricks API paginates results (default page size varies, typically
≤100 jobs). Workspaces with more than one page of jobs silently lose
jobs.

**GitHub Issue**: dagster-io/dagster#33590

Additionally, there is a **secondary bug** on the same code path: the
rate-limit retry check on line 86 of `resource.py` compares `resp.status
== MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` (value `10`) instead of `resp.status ==
RATE_LIMIT_STATUS_CODE` (value `429`). This means rate-limit retries
never trigger for individual job fetches. This should be fixed in the
same change.

## Changes

### File:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-databricks/dagster_databricks/components/databricks_asset_bundle/resource.py`

**1. Add pagination loop to `fetch_jobs` (lines 63-68)**

Replace the single API call:

```python
async with aiohttp.ClientSession(headers=headers) as session:
    list_url = f"{base_url}{DATABRICKS_JOBS_API_PATH}/list"
    async with session.get(list_url) as resp:
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = await resp.json()
        all_jobs_lite = data.get("jobs", [])
```

With a pagination loop:

```python
async with aiohttp.ClientSession(headers=headers) as session:
    list_url = f"{base_url}{DATABRICKS_JOBS_API_PATH}/list"
    all_jobs_lite = []
    params: dict[str, str] = {}
    while True:
        async with session.get(list_url, params=params) as resp:
            resp.raise_for_status()
            data = await resp.json()
            all_jobs_lite.extend(data.get("jobs", []))
            if not data.get("has_more"):
                break
            params["page_token"] = data["next_page_token"]
```

The Databricks Jobs API 2.1 `/list` response includes:
- `has_more` (bool): whether more pages exist
- `next_page_token` (str): token to pass as `page_token` query parameter
for the next page

**2. Fix rate-limit check bug (line 86)**

Change:
```python
if resp.status == MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS:
```

To:
```python
if resp.status == RATE_LIMIT_STATUS_CODE:
```

The constant `RATE_LIMIT_STATUS_CODE = 429` already exists at the top of
the file but was never used. The current code incorrectly checks for
HTTP status 10 (matching `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 10`).

### File:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-databricks/dagster_databricks_tests/components/databricks_workspace/test_component.py`

**3. Add a pagination test**

Add a new test `test_databricks_fetch_jobs_pagination` that verifies the
pagination loop works correctly. The test should:

- Mock `aiohttp.ClientSession` to return multiple pages of job listings
- First page returns jobs + `has_more: True` + `next_page_token:
"token1"`
- Second page returns more jobs + `has_more: False`
- Verify all jobs from both pages are collected
- Verify the `page_token` parameter was passed on the second request

The test should directly test `DatabricksWorkspace.fetch_jobs()` rather
than going through the component, since the pagination logic is in the
resource.

**4. Add a rate-limit retry test**

Add a new test `test_databricks_fetch_jobs_rate_limit_retry` that
verifies:

- When an individual job fetch returns HTTP 429, the code retries after
a sleep
- The retry succeeds on the second attempt

## Implementation Details

### Databricks API 2.1 Pagination Contract

The `/api/2.1/jobs/list` endpoint returns:
```json
{
  "jobs": [...],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_page_token": "eyJ..."
}
```

To fetch the next page, pass `page_token` as a query parameter. When
`has_more` is `false` or absent, there are no more pages.

### Key Decisions

- Use `params` dict with `aiohttp` rather than manually constructing URL
query strings — cleaner and handles encoding
- Keep the existing `aiohttp.ClientSession` pattern (one session for
listing, separate sessions for individual job fetches)
- The pagination loop uses `while True` with a `break` when `has_more`
is falsy, which handles both `has_more: false` and the field being
absent

### Edge Cases

- Empty workspace (no jobs): First page returns `{"jobs": []}` with no
`has_more` — loop exits immediately
- Single page of results: `has_more` is `false` or absent — loop exits
after first iteration (current behavior preserved)
- Rate limiting on the list endpoint: Not handled in this change (same
as before). The existing rate-limit retry is only for individual job
fetches. A future enhancement could add retry logic to the list call as
well, but that's out of scope.

## Files NOT Changing

- `component.py` — The component calls `workspace.fetch_jobs()` which
already returns a full list of jobs. No changes needed.
- `schema.py` — Filter logic is applied after fetching, no changes
needed.
- `configs.py` — Data models unchanged.
- Any other files outside the databricks package.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Per instructions, never modify.

## Verification

1. **Run existing tests**: All existing tests in `test_component.py`
should pass unchanged since they mock `fetch_jobs` at the workspace
level.

2. **Run new pagination test**: The new test should verify multi-page
fetching works.

3. **Run new rate-limit test**: The new test should verify the 429 retry
fix.

4. **Run ruff**: `make ruff` from the dagster-oss root to ensure
formatting/linting passes.

5. **Run the full test suite for the package**:
   ```bash
   cd dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-databricks
tox -e py312 -- -k "test_databricks_workspace or test_databricks_fetch"
   ```

</details>

subject: fix(copybara): re-apply ruff/ty/Aikido reverts clobbered by #33834 (#25133)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Re-applies the eight reversion hunks that the OSS sync of
[#33834](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/...) ("Add
Microsoft Fabric and OneLake icons") silently carried into master,
breaking every build since [build
154115](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/154115).

The proximate breakage is a ruff version pin mismatch: `internal[tools]`
and friends pin `ruff==0.15.15` (per #25127), but the OSS sync of #33834
reset `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml` and
`dagster-oss/config/ruff.toml` back to `0.15.14`. uv resolves the
workspace as unsatisfiable, so every step that does `uv sync` (or `uv
run`) fails — `:zap: ruff`, `victoria-metrics-service-check`, all three
`:alembic: alembic-merge-conflict-*` jobs.

The same OSS-sync diff also clobbered:

- the TC001/TC002 import deletions in
`_core/execution/context/{invocation,system}.py` and
`_core/workspace/context.py` (from #25127);
- the per-package `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/uv.lock` (which
additionally reverted `ty 0.0.40→0.0.39`);
- the subprocess-security fix in `automation/git.py` (from [Aikido
#24599](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24599)).

This PR restores all eight files to their post-#25127 state. The blob
index hashes for every restored file match #25127's outputs exactly;
this is a true revert of the unintended reverts, not a re-derivation.

## Why this happened

#33834 is an OSS-side PR (5-digit number `33834` is the
`dagster-io/dagster` numbering). The OSS → internal copybara import
produces an internal commit whose diff is `(OSS-state-after-PR) −
(current-internal-state-of-dagster-oss)`. Because OSS master had not yet
synced internal's #25127 (ruff bump) and #24599 (Aikido) when #33834 was
authored, those files' OSS state was "behind" internal, and the importer
treated internal's content as drift to reconcile toward OSS.

There is no automated guard against this in the current importer config
— for files under `dagster-oss/` the OSS direction is treated as
authoritative, full-tree, and the importer doesn't restrict to only the
hunks actually touched in the OSS PR's diff. Worth raising with whoever
owns the copybara workflow, but out of scope for this PR.

## One sling-test deviation from #25127

#25127 *deleted* a top-level `AssetsDefinition` import from
`dagster-sling/.../test_sling_replication_collection_component.py` and
relied on an existing `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block at line 37 to satisfy
the annotations. That TYPE_CHECKING block still exists today, but a
separate intermediate commit appears to have re-added the top-level
import alongside it — and `0.15.15`'s TC002 then flags the top-level one
as movable. This PR keeps the existing `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block as-is
and removes only the duplicate top-level import, which is the
post-#25127 state.

## Test Plan

- [x] `just ruff` — `All checks passed!`, formatter no-op.
- [x] `just ty` — `Found 0 errors / Found 0 warnings` across all three
envs (`data-platform`, `internal`, `master`), 7073 files analyzed.
- [ ] CI on this PR: `:zap: ruff`, `victoria-metrics-service-check`,
`alembic-merge-conflict-{main,reporting,xregion}` should all flip from
failing → passing.

## Summary & Motivation

Bumps `ruff` to `0.15.15` (from `0.15.14`) and clears the lint
diagnostics that the new version surfaces. Stacked on top of #25126 (ty
bump) so the `uv.lock` updates don't conflict.

## Pin sites updated

Ruff is pinned in more places than ty — six sites in this repo:

- `pyproject.toml` (root, `[project.optional-dependencies].tools`) —
what `just ruff` resolves from.
- `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml` (×2: `test` and
`ruff` extras).
- `python_modules/purina/pyproject.toml`.
- `public/skills/dagster-skills-evals/pyproject.toml`.
- `dagster-oss/config/ruff.toml` — `required-version`. Easy to miss
because it's not a `pyproject.toml` and grepping for `"ruff=="` alone
won't catch it. Without bumping this one, `just ruff` errors out at
config-load time before any rules run.

## Lint changes

`just ruff` at 0.15.15 found 21 diagnostics; 16 were auto-fixed at
default safety. The remaining 5 were `TC001` / `TC002` ("Move type-only
import into a type-checking block"). Re-running with `--unsafe-fixes`
cleared those plus 4 additional `F401` / `TC` follow-ons for a total of
9 fixes, all dead-import deletions across 6 files:

- `dagster-cloud-e2e/.../test_notifications.py` —
`MetricMonitorNotificationData` (used only in `cast("X", ...)`
stringified casts).
- `dagster-cloud-backend/.../slack/utils.py` — `AlertPolicy`,
`DagsterCloudAlert` (stringified annotations only).
- `dagster-oss/.../execution/context/invocation.py` —
`TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition` (duplicate of a TYPE_CHECKING import
already present).
- `dagster-oss/.../execution/context/system.py` —
`TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition` (duplicate inside TYPE_CHECKING block;
the module-scope import elsewhere shadowed it).
- `dagster-oss/.../workspace/context.py` — `PartitionConfigSnap`,

(duplicates of module-scope imports).
- `dagster-sling/.../test_sling_replication_collection_component.py` —
`AssetsDefinition` (used only in local variable annotations, which
Python does not evaluate at runtime per PEP 526).

Net diff outside of pyproject/lockfile: **13 lines deleted, zero lines
added**.

- [x] `just ty` clean (`Found 0 errors / Found 0 warnings`, 7073 files)
— confirms the autofix's import deletions don't break stringified-cast /
annotation resolution for the type checker.

subject: chore(ty): bump ty to 0.0.40 and fix surfaced type errors (#25126)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Bumps `ty` to `0.0.40` (from `0.0.39`) in both root `pyproject.toml` and
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml`, relocks the root
`uv.lock` so the `internal` ty env (which resolves via `uv run --frozen
--isolated --extra ty`) actually picks up the new version, and fixes the
9 newly-surfaced type errors that 0.0.40 caught.

The `master` and `data-platform` envs invoke ty via `uv tool run --from
ty==<pin>`, so they upgrade just from the pyproject bump. The `internal`
env is lockfile-bound — without relocking, it would have silently kept
running 0.0.39.

## What 0.0.40 caught

All 9 errors were in the `internal` env. `master` (OSS, ~7k files) and
`data-platform` stayed clean.

- **`dagster-cloud-backend/.../asset_health_alert_emitter.py:74`** —
`invalid-return-type`. `get_latest_event_by_asset` returns
`Mapping[AssetKey, EventLogEntry]`, but
`event.get_dagster_event().asset_key` is `AssetKey | None`, so the dict
ended up `dict[AssetKey | None, EventLogEntry]`. Added a `None` skip in
the loop — the function's contract excludes `None` keys, so any
non-asset event is simply not tracked.
- **`automation-internal/.../shard_initialize.py:597`** —
`unresolved-attribute`. Calling `.append` on `output[...]["replicas"]`
which had value type `str | int | list[Unknown]`. Hoisted `replicas:
list[dict[str, Any]] = []` as a typed local and reference it directly;
the literal dict still gets it under the `"replicas"` key, so the JSON
output is unchanged.
- **`automation-internal/.../shadow/cli.py:115`** —
`invalid-argument-type`. The function annotated `command: str`, but the
click decorator uses `nargs=-1`, which makes `command` a `tuple[str,
...]`. Corrected the annotation. ty's stub for `list.insert` was
over-narrowing through the (incorrect) `str` annotation.
- **`compass-data/.../bigquery/assets.py`** — 6 diagnostics, 1 root
cause. `results = []` got inferred as `list[dict[str, str | int |
Unknown]]`, so every subsequent read at lines 157, 161, 162, 169, 171,
175 failed against `Sequence[str]` / `int` / `str` argument
expectations. Annotated `results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []`.

## Test Plan

- [x] `just ty` reports `Found 0 errors / Found 0 warnings` across all
three envs (`data-platform`, `internal`, `master`), 7073 files analyzed.
- [x] `just ruff` clean.

subject: [dagster-dbt] Omit per-manifest metadata from shared source deps (#25119)
body:
## Problem

When a dbt source is upstream of assets built by **two different
`DbtProjectComponent` instances** (e.g. one project feeding a model and
another feeding a snapshot), each project's manifest assigns that source
a different `unique_id` — the dbt project name is embedded in it
(`source.<project>.<source>.<table>`).

With `enable_source_metadata=True` (the default), the translator copies
the source's per-manifest metadata onto the source `AssetDep`. Because
`dagster_dbt/unique_id` differs between the two projects, the shared
stub asset ends up with conflicting `AssetDep` metadata and
`resolve_stub_assets_defs` raises:

```
DagsterInvalidDefinitionError: Conflicting metadata found on AssetDeps referencing ["<source>", "<table>"]: ... All metadata for AssetDeps referencing a given key must be identical or empty.
```

This can prevent the code location from loading, and also surfaces later
at job-subset time (e.g. when declarative automation launches a run and
a subset job is built).

The existing `_colliding_source_keys` guard only suppresses ambiguous
metadata *within a single manifest*, so it has no visibility into the
cross-project case.

## Fix

When emitting source dep metadata, strip the keys whose values are
per-manifest/per-translator objects — `manifest`,
`dagster_dbt_translator`, `unique_id`, and `project` — keeping only
value-stable keys such as `dagster/table_name` and
`dagster/column_schema`. A source referenced by multiple projects then
produces identical dep metadata, so the shared stub resolves.

Genuinely divergent data (e.g. two projects declaring different column
schemas for the same source) still conflicts loudly, which is intended.

## Test

`test_dbt_enable_source_metadata_across_distinct_manifests` builds two
manifests that share a source AssetKey but differ in the
project-embedded `unique_id` and asserts the graph resolves, that
`dagster/table_name` survives on the dep, and that the per-manifest
identifiers do not. Verified it reproduces the original `Conflicting
metadata` error when the fix is reverted.

subject: Fix dg check defs to auto-detect definitions.py as fallback (#22455)
body:
## Summary

The `dg check defs` command previously only resolved the standard
`defs/` directory structure and would fail on projects using a top-level
`definitions.py` file. This change adds auto-detection logic that falls
back to `definitions.py` when the default `defs` path doesn't exist,
while respecting explicit user configuration.

## Key Changes

- Add auto-detection fallback to `definitions.py` module in
`defs_module_name` property
- Check both directory and `.py` file forms when auto-detecting
- Preserve explicit `defs_module` configuration when set by user
- Add test coverage for projects using `definitions.py` instead of
`defs/` directory

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Added (1 file)
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/test_check_defs_command.py`
- Test for definitions.py project structure

### Modified (1 file)
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-core/dagster_dg_core/context.py`
- Add auto-detection logic for definitions.py fallback

</details>

## User Experience

**Before:**
```
$ dg check defs  # project with definitions.py instead of defs/
Error: Unable to resolve defs module
```

**After:**
```
$ dg check defs  # project with definitions.py instead of defs/
Checking definitions...
✓ All checks passed
```

Now projects can use either `defs/` directory or top-level

# Fix: `dg check defs` can't resolve `definitions.py`, only works with
`defs.py`

## Context

**GitHub Issue:** https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/29817

When a user creates a Dagster project with a `definitions.py` file as
their defs module (instead of the standard `defs/` directory or
`defs.py`), `dg check defs` fails because the default module resolution
only looks for `defs` as the submodule name.

The standard `create-dagster` scaffold creates BOTH `definitions.py`
(code location target) AND `defs/` (component directory). However, users
who set up projects manually or use older project structures may only
have `definitions.py`. The `dg check defs` command should auto-detect
this and work with either naming convention.

### Root Cause

In `dagster-shared/dagster_shared/utils/config.py:53`, the default defs
submodule is hardcoded:
```python
_DEFAULT_PROJECT_DEFS_SUBMODULE: Final = "defs"
```

`get_canonical_defs_module_name()` (line 110-111) uses this default when
no explicit `defs_module` is configured:
```python
def get_canonical_defs_module_name(defs_module_name: str | None, root_module_name: str) -> str:
    return defs_module_name or f"{root_module_name}.{_DEFAULT_PROJECT_DEFS_SUBMODULE}"
```

Then `DgContext.defs_module_name` (in
`dagster-dg-core/dagster_dg_core/context.py:407-413`) calls this
function and `DgContext._defs_path` converts the module name to a
filesystem path. If the user has `definitions.py` instead of `defs.py`
or `defs/`, the path resolution fails.

## Changes

### File 1:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-core/dagster_dg_core/context.py`

**What to change:** Modify `DgContext.defs_module_name` (cached property
at line 407-413) to auto-detect `definitions` as a fallback when `defs`
doesn't exist and no explicit `defs_module` is configured.

**Current code:**
```python
@cached_property
def defs_module_name(self) -> str:
    if not self.config.project:
        raise DgError("`defs_module_name` is only available in a Dagster project context")
    return get_canonical_defs_module_name(
        self.config.project.defs_module, self.root_module_name
    )
```

**New code:**
```python
@cached_property
def defs_module_name(self) -> str:
    if not self.config.project:
        raise DgError("`defs_module_name` is only available in a Dagster project context")
    canonical = get_canonical_defs_module_name(
        self.config.project.defs_module, self.root_module_name
    )
    # If the user explicitly configured a defs_module, use it as-is
    if self.config.project.defs_module:
        return canonical
    # Auto-detect: if the default "defs" path doesn't exist, try "definitions"
    default_path = self.get_path_for_local_module(canonical, require_exists=False)
    if not default_path.exists() and not default_path.with_suffix(".py").exists():
        alt_module = f"{self.root_module_name}.{_ALTERNATIVE_DEFS_SUBMODULE}"
        alt_path = self.get_path_for_local_module(alt_module, require_exists=False)
        if alt_path.exists() or alt_path.with_suffix(".py").exists():
            return alt_module
    return canonical
```

Also add a new constant near the existing
`_DEFAULT_PROJECT_CODE_LOCATION_TARGET_MODULE` (around line 49):
```python
_ALTERNATIVE_DEFS_SUBMODULE: Final = "definitions"
```

**Important implementation notes:**
- `get_path_for_local_module` with `require_exists=False` returns the
directory form of the path. We need to check both the directory and the
`.py` file form (since the user may have `definitions.py` as a file, not
a package).
- The `_defs_path` property (line 416-418) already calls
`get_path_for_local_module(defs_module_name, require_exists=False)`, and
`get_path_for_local_module` (line 633-655) checks for `.py` first, then
directory. So once `defs_module_name` returns the right module name, the
path resolution handles both file and directory cases.
- The auto-detection should only trigger when no explicit `defs_module`
is configured (i.e., using the default).

### File 2:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/test_check_defs_command.py`

**What to change:** Add a test that verifies `dg check defs` works when
the project uses `definitions.py` instead of a `defs/` directory.

**New test to add** (after `test_check_defs_project_context_failure`,
around line 63):

```python
@pytest.mark.skipif(is_windows(), reason="Temporarily skipping (signal issues in CLI)..")
def test_check_defs_project_context_with_definitions_py():
    """Test that dg check defs works when project uses definitions.py instead of defs/ directory."""
    with ProxyRunner.test() as runner, isolated_example_project_foo_bar(runner):
        # Remove the default defs/ directory and create definitions.py instead
        import shutil
        defs_dir = Path("src") / "foo_bar" / "defs"
        if defs_dir.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(defs_dir)

        definitions_file = Path("src") / "foo_bar" / "definitions.py"
        definitions_file.write_text(
            "from dagster import Definitions\ndefs = Definitions()\n"
        )

        # Also update the code location target to point at definitions.py
        # since the default definitions.py that was scaffolded may reference defs/
        code_location_target = Path("src") / "foo_bar" / "definitions.py"
        # definitions.py already exists from the write above

        result = runner.invoke("check", "defs", "--no-check-yaml")
        assert_runner_result(result)
```

**Note on test approach:** Use `--no-check-yaml` since there's no
`defs/` directory to scan for YAML files. The test verifies that the
definitions loading (the core function of `dg check defs`) works when
`definitions.py` is used as the defs module. The `check_yaml` feature is
specific to the component-based `defs/` directory and is orthogonal to
this fix.

Look at the existing `isolated_example_project_foo_bar` helper and the
existing test patterns to understand the exact scaffolded structure. The
scaffolded project will have both `defs/` and `definitions.py`. The test
should remove `defs/` and ensure `definitions.py` serves as both the
defs module and the code location target.

## Files NOT Changing

- **`dagster-shared/dagster_shared/utils/config.py`**: The
`_DEFAULT_PROJECT_DEFS_SUBMODULE` constant and
`get_canonical_defs_module_name()` function stay as-is. The fallback
logic belongs in `DgContext` which has filesystem access, not in the
shared config utility.
- **`dagster-dg-core/dagster_dg_core/config.py`**: No changes to
`DgProjectConfig` — the `defs_module` field remains optional with the
same semantics.
- **`dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli/cli/check.py`**: The check command
itself doesn't need changes — it already delegates to `DgContext` for
path resolution.
- **CHANGELOG.md**: Never modify.

## Verification

1. **Run the new test:**
   ```bash
   cd dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli
tox -vv -e py312-default -- -k
test_check_defs_project_context_with_definitions_py
   ```

2. **Run existing check defs tests** to verify no regressions:

   ```bash
   cd dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli
   tox -vv -e py312-default -- -k test_check_defs
   ```

3. **Run ruff** for formatting:

4. **Run pyright** on modified files:

   ```bash
just pyright
   ```
