subject: fix(docs_snippets): per-parametrization duckdb path in customizing_existing_component test (#25101)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes a flake in `test_components_docs_adding_attributes_to_assets` — the failure mode seen on Buildkite build [153932 job `019e748b`](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153932#019e748b-dc97-418b-9279-53567a3eeba1):

```
IO Error: Could not set lock on file "/tmp/jaffle_platform.duckdb":
  Conflicting lock is held in /tmp/.sling/bin/duckdb/1.5.2/duckdb (PID 5091).
```

The test is parametrized over `component_type ∈ {"local", "global"}` and both parametrizations wrote their DuckDB to the same hardcoded path: `/tmp/jaffle_platform.duckdb`. Each parametrization invokes `dg launch --assets '*'` three times; each invocation spawns sling which spawns a `sling/bin/duckdb/.../duckdb` helper that takes an exclusive OS-level lock on the instance file.

When pytest-timeout (1200s) kills the `[local]` parent with SIGKILL, the duckdb child is reparented and keeps holding the lock. `[global]` then runs in the same agent pod, hits the same path, and every stream materialization fails the probe query (`select 1 /* nD */`) with "Conflicting lock is held … PID 5091". The first parametrization shows up as a timeout, the second as a `subprocess.CalledProcessError` from `dg launch`. Same root cause.

## Fix

Use a per-parametrization runtime path (`/tmp/jaffle_platform_local.duckdb` vs `/tmp/jaffle_platform_global.duckdb`) so a leaked child from one variant can't lock-out the other. Canonicalize the runtime path back to `/tmp/jaffle_platform.duckdb` in the saved docs snippet via `global_snippet_replace_regexes`, so the published docs and snapshot files are byte-identical.

## Latent issues left untouched

Three other tests reference the same `/tmp/jaffle_platform.duckdb` path (or `/tmp/my_project.duckdb`), but none have the same root-cause pattern (shared path across parametrizations of a single test):

- `docs_snippets_tests/snippet_checks/guides/dg/test_adding_components_to_existing_project/test_components_existing_project.py:147`
- `docs_snippets_tests/dagster_basics_tutorial_tests/test_pipeline.py:19`
- `docs_snippets_tests/snippet_checks/guides/components/integrations/test_sling_component.py:144,168` (different path, two writes in one test)

These are latent cross-file hazards if multiple tests share an agent and one leaks duckdb — but in each case the literal `/tmp/...` string appears in user-facing docs snippet content, so changing them changes published docs. Out of scope for this flake fix; flagged here for awareness.

## Test Plan

- `tox -e py312-docs_snapshot_test -- -k test_components_docs_adding_attributes_to_assets` passes for both parametrizations.
- Snapshot files under `examples/docs_snippets/docs_snippets/guides/components/customizing-existing-component/` are unchanged (the snippet regex canonicalizes the path back).
- CI run on this branch.

subject: Widen docker pull retry budget for ECR/Docker Hub 5xx blips (#25075)
body:
## Summary

Widens `_docker_pull_with_retry` in `dagster-k8s-test-infra` from 3 attempts × 5s linear backoff (~10s cumulative wait) to 6 attempts × exponential backoff with ±20% jitter, capped at 60s per sleep (~155s cumulative wait).

The helper is used by the kind-based integration suites (`k8s-test-suite`, `celery-k8s-test-suite`, etc.) to pull both the per-build ECR test-project image and the docker.io supporting images into the dind sidecar before `kind load`. Docker Hub's blob CDN and ECR's S3 layer-blob backend (`prod-us-west-2-starport-layer-bucket.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com`) both intermittently return 5xx for tens of seconds at a time — the old 10s budget couldn't ride out a typical outage window, so a single 503 during fixture setup cascaded into every test in the suite ERRORing at the `docker pull` step.

## Motivating incident

Build [153844](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153844#019e7071-acfe-4bfa-b5b5-00ffcfd35767), job `:gear: celery-k8s-test-suite-markredis-3-12`:

```
unknown: failed to copy: httpReadSeeker: failed open: unexpected status from GET request
to https://prod-us-west-2-starport-layer-bucket.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/...
503 Service Unavailable
```

All four tests in the suite (`test_execute_on_celery_k8s_default`, `test_execute_on_celery_k8s_with_termination`, `test_run_monitoring_fails_on_interrupt`, `test_run_monitoring_startup_fail`) errored at the same fixture, with `subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['docker', 'pull', '968703565975.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/test-project:...-3.12']' returned non-zero exit status 1.`

## Why not other approaches

- **Buildkite step-level auto-retry**: heavier (full kind teardown + multi-minute EKS pod startup) and overlapping. Worth adding on top if this in-process retry proves insufficient, not in place of it.
- **Pull-through cache for ECR**: the existing kind-registry pattern only mirrors docker.io. The test-project image is built fresh per build (tag = `$BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID-<py>`) and pulled exactly once per job, so a pull-through cache has 0% hit rate. Not worth the operator burden.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on the kind-based integration suites (`k8s-test-suite`, `celery-k8s-test-suite`).
- [ ] On the next ECR/Docker Hub blip, confirm the retry sleeps log out and the suite recovers without ERRORing all tests.

subject: fix(dagster-aws): retry SIGTERM in ECS pipes interruption test to defeat finalizer-swallowed-signal race (#25089)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

`test_ecs_pipes_interruption_forwarding` is master-flaking on a new signature, distinct from the prior moto-orphan (#25004) and timeout (#25052) fixes. Build 153905 ([dagster-aws-3-12 job](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153905#019e7426-a133-4606-b80d-f3ef51a84500)) failed with `assert 0 == 1` at `test_ecs.py:225` — the child's container exited with code 0, meaning the SIGTERM was never effectively delivered.

### Root cause

Python silently drops exceptions raised from a signal handler that fires inside a `__del__`/weakref finalizer. The captured stderr makes this explicit:

```
Exception ignored in:
  File ".../sqlalchemy/event/registry.py", line 103, in _collection_gced
  File ".../dagster/_utils/interrupts.py", line 81, in _new_signal_handler
    raise error_cls()
dagster._core.errors.DagsterExecutionInterruptedError:
```

The child's early-setup phase (`instance_for_test()` + pipes session construction) is dense with sqlalchemy GC callbacks. When the parent's `p.terminate()` lands during a `_collection_gced` weakref callback, the raised `DagsterExecutionInterruptedError` is swallowed by Python's "Exception ignored in:" path. With no exception propagating, `PipesECSClient._terminate()` is never invoked, `stop_task` is never called, and the simulated subprocess completes its `SLEEP_SECONDS=10` work normally — so `fake_ecs.describe_tasks` reports `exitCode=0` instead of `1`.

`dagster/_utils/interrupts.py:80` `_new_signal_handler` only `raise`s — it doesn't latch a flag — so a swallowed raise is unrecoverable for the caller.

### Fix

Re-send SIGTERM in a bounded loop until the child acknowledges (`materialization_done_event` set), exits, or the 180s window closes. Up to 5 retries spaced 2s apart cover the early-setup finalizer window; the cap prevents a stray SIGTERM from interrupting the child's own interrupt-handling (`_terminate` + the `describe_tasks` call in `_materialize_asset`'s `finally` block).

This is a targeted, test-scoped fix. The deeper root-cause fix — latching `_received_interrupt["received"]` inside `raise_interrupts_as` and polling it in `PipesECSClient._wait_for_completion` — is tracked separately; it touches a hot production path (`_core/execution/plan/active.py` `pop_captured_interrupt`, daemon main loop) and needs an audit rather than a hot patch.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI: dagster-aws-3-12 passes
- [ ] Spot-check: the happy path is unchanged — the first `p.terminate()` typically propagates within one retry interval, so most runs send exactly one SIGTERM. The retry path only fires when the first delivery is swallowed.

subject: Fix dg plus deploy python-executable failing with No module named pip in uv environments (#22301)
body:
Fix `dg plus deploy --build-strategy python-executable` failing with `No module named pip` in uv environments. When `uv` is available on PATH, `_build_local_package` now uses `uv pip install` instead of `python -m pip install` for pyproject.toml-based packages, with automatic fallback to pip when uv is not present.

Fixes https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/33685

## Key Changes

- `_build_local_package` in `source.py` now detects `uv` via `shutil.which("uv")` and prefers `uv pip install --python <interpreter>` for pyproject.toml builds
- Falls back to `python -m pip install` when uv is not available, preserving backward compatibility
- Updated existing test to mock `shutil.which` returning `None` to verify pip fallback path
- Added new test `test_build_local_package_with_pyproject_toml_uses_uv` to verify uv code path

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Modified (2 files)
- `dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/dagster_cloud_cli/core/pex_builder/source.py` - pyproject.toml build strategy: prefer uv over pip
- `dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/dagster_cloud_cli_tests/test_pyproject_toml_support.py` - Updated and added tests for uv/pip code paths

</details>

## User Experience

**Before:**
```
$ dg plus deploy --build-strategy python-executable
...
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pip'
```

**After:**
```
$ dg plus deploy --build-strategy python-executable
Building package at '/path/to/project' using uv pip install
...
```

When uv is on PATH (standard for uv-managed projects), the build succeeds without requiring pip in the venv.

# Fix `dg plus deploy --build-strategy python-executable` failing with `No module named pip` in uv environments

## Context

When using `dg plus deploy --build-strategy python-executable` with a uv-managed project that has local path dependencies (via `[tool.uv.sources]`), the deploy process fails because the `_build_local_package` function in `source.py` shells out to `python -m pip install` to build packages with `pyproject.toml`. uv virtual environments don't include pip by default, causing a `No module named pip` error.

GitHub issue: https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/33685

## Changes

### File to modify: `dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/dagster_cloud_cli/core/pex_builder/source.py`

**What to change:** In the `_build_local_package` function (lines 49-76), the `elif` branch for `pyproject.toml` projects currently runs:

```python
command = [
    python_interpreter,
    "-m",
    "pip",
    "install",
    "--target",
    build_dir,
    "--no-deps",
    ".",
]
subprocess.run(command, check=True, cwd=local_dir)
```

Replace this with logic that:

1. First tries `uv pip install` if `uv` is available on PATH (detected via `shutil.which("uv")`)
2. Falls back to `python -m pip install` if `uv` is not available

The implementation should be:

```python
elif os.path.exists(os.path.join(local_dir, "pyproject.toml")):
    uv_path = shutil.which("uv")
    if uv_path:
        ui.print(f"Building package at {local_dir!r} using uv pip install")
        command = [
            uv_path,
            "pip",
            "install",
            "--python",
            python_interpreter,
            "--target",
            build_dir,
            "--no-deps",
            ".",
        ]
    else:
        ui.print(f"Building package at {local_dir!r} using {python_interpreter} -m pip install")
        command = [
            python_interpreter,
            "-m",
            "pip",
            "install",
            "--target",
            build_dir,
            "--no-deps",
            ".",
        ]
    subprocess.run(command, check=True, cwd=local_dir)
```

Key design decisions:
- **`shutil.which("uv")`** is used to detect uv availability at runtime, which is the standard Python way to check for executables on PATH
- **`--python` flag** is passed to `uv pip install` to specify the target Python interpreter, mirroring how the original code used `python_interpreter` as the first argument
- **Fallback to pip** preserves backward compatibility for users who don't use uv
- **`shutil` is already imported** in `source.py` (line 5), so no new imports are needed
- The `uv pip install` command uses the same `--target` and `--no-deps` flags as the original pip command — `uv pip install` supports these flags with identical semantics

### File to modify: `dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/dagster_cloud_cli_tests/test_pyproject_toml_support.py`

**What to change:** Update the existing test `test_build_local_package_with_pyproject_toml` (lines 165-196) and add a new test to cover both the uv and pip code paths.

1. **Update `test_build_local_package_with_pyproject_toml`**: This test currently asserts the exact pip command. It should be updated to mock `shutil.which` returning `None` (no uv available) and verify the pip fallback path works correctly. The assertion stays the same since it tests the pip fallback.

2. **Add `test_build_local_package_with_pyproject_toml_uses_uv`**: A new test that mocks `shutil.which("uv")` to return `/usr/bin/uv` (or similar) and verifies that `uv pip install --python <interpreter> --target <dir> --no-deps .` is the command constructed.

Specifically:

```python
@patch("subprocess.run")
@patch("shutil.which", return_value=None)
def test_build_local_package_with_pyproject_toml(mock_which, mock_run, temp_dir):
    """Test building a package with pyproject.toml falls back to pip when uv is not available."""
    mock_run.return_value = None

    pyproject_path = Path(temp_dir) / "pyproject.toml"
    pyproject_path.write_text("""
[project]
name = "test-package"
version = "0.1.0"
""")

    build_dir = Path(temp_dir) / "build"
    build_dir.mkdir()

    source._build_local_package(temp_dir, str(build_dir), "python")

    mock_run.assert_called_once()
    args, _kwargs = mock_run.call_args
    command = args[0]

    expected_command = [
        "python",
        "-m",
        "pip",
        "install",
```

subject: [dagster-dbt] Fix #33856 - incorrect asset key translation when generating column lineage and using DbtProjectComponent (#33857)
body:
## Summary

Fixes [#33856](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/33856) —
column lineage emitted by `.fetch_column_metadata()` referenced
default-derived `AssetKey`s instead of the translated keys actually
present in the asset graph when assets were defined via
`DBTProjectComponent`.

`_build_column_lineage_metadata()` resolved upstream dependencies by
calling `dagster_dbt_translator.get_asset_key(parent_resource_props)`.
But `DbtProjectComponentTranslator` (and any translator that customizes
translation via `get_asset_spec`) does **not** override `get_asset_key`
— it overrides `get_asset_spec`. As a result, every upstream
`TableColumnDep` pointed at a key that didn't exist in the graph, and
column lineage failed to resolve.

## Fix

Switch the upstream key resolution to
`dagster_dbt_translator.get_asset_spec(manifest, parent_unique_id,
project).key`. This is already the canonical pattern in the same file
(`_to_model_events` at `dbt_cli_event.py:401`) and in
`asset_utils.py:823`.

Chose this over an `isinstance(translator,
DbtProjectComponentTranslator)` branch because:

1. **Consistency** — matches how the materialized asset's own key is
resolved a few lines away. Using a different mechanism for upstream
resolution is what caused this drift bug in the first place.
2. **Generality** — works for any translator subclass that customizes
via `get_asset_spec` (the documented extension point), not just
`DbtProjectComponentTranslator`.
3. **No layering violation** — avoids importing a component-layer class
into core event code.
4. **Default path preserved** — `DagsterDbtTranslator.get_asset_spec()`
internally calls `self.get_asset_key()`, so users who only override
`get_asset_key` are unaffected.

To make this work, `project: DbtProject | None` is plumbed through
`_build_column_lineage_metadata` → `_get_lineage_metadata` →
`_get_materialization_metadata`. `_to_model_events` already had
`project` available, and `DbtCliInvocation.project` is the source at the
`_fetch_column_metadata` call site.

### Out of scope

`_to_observation_events_for_test` (`dbt_cli_event.py:498`) and
`freshness_builder.py` use the same `get_asset_key()` pattern and likely
have the same bug for `DbtProjectComponent` users. Kept this PR tight to
the reported column-lineage issue; those are follow-ups.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression test
`test_column_lineage_uses_get_asset_spec_for_upstream_keys` in
`test_columns_metadata.py` — uses a translator that overrides only
`get_asset_spec` (mimicking `DbtProjectComponentTranslator`'s pattern)
and asserts every upstream key in the emitted `TableColumnLineage`
carries the translated `renamed/...` prefix.
- [x] Verified the new test **fails** without the fix (`AssertionError:
Upstream key AssetKey(['raw_source_customers']) in column lineage was
not translated via get_asset_spec`) and passes with it.
- [x] All 12 duckdb-based column-lineage tests in
`test_columns_metadata.py` pass locally (snowflake/bigquery variants
skipped — require cloud credentials).
- [x] `make ruff` clean.

subject: Skip BigQuery write for empty DataFrames to prevent wrong type inference (#22324)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes [dagster-io/dagster#14202](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/14202) (related: [dagster-io/dagster#13287](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/13287)).

When a database IO manager receives an empty DataFrame, the underlying write call either creates a table with incorrect data types (because there's no data to infer types from) or otherwise produces a degenerate table. This is especially problematic with partitioned assets where the first partition may be empty — the table gets created with wrong types, causing subsequent non-empty partitions to fail.

This PR skips the write when the DataFrame has 0 rows and logs a warning instead. Per Jamie's review, the fix is extended uniformly across all of the database IO managers and their type handlers (BigQuery, Snowflake, DuckDB × Pandas/PySpark/Polars) so they all behave the same way.

The known issue from dagster-io/dagster#13287 — that `DBIOManager` deletes existing rows for the asset partition before calling `handle_output` — is left alone: if you return an empty DataFrame, it's reasonable to treat that as "clear the associated data."

## Handlers updated

- `BigQueryPandasTypeHandler` — pandas `.empty`
- `BigQueryPySparkTypeHandler` — pyspark `.isEmpty()`
- `SnowflakePandasTypeHandler` — pandas `.empty`
- `SnowflakePySparkTypeHandler` — pyspark `.isEmpty()`
- `SnowflakePolarsTypeHandler` — polars `.is_empty()`
- `DuckDBPandasTypeHandler` — pandas `.empty`
- `DuckDBPySparkTypeHandler` — pyspark `.isEmpty()`
- `DuckDBPolarsTypeHandler` — polars `.is_empty()`

In each case, when the DataFrame is empty the write is skipped, a warning is logged via `context.log`, and output metadata (row count / column schema) is still emitted where applicable.

## Test Plan

Added a `test_handle_output_empty_dataframe` unit test to each handler's test module:

- `dagster_gcp_pandas_tests/bigquery/test_type_handler.py` (also `test_handle_output_nonempty_dataframe`)
- `dagster_gcp_pyspark_tests/bigquery/test_type_handler.py`
- `dagster_snowflake_pandas_tests/test_snowflake_pandas_type_handler.py`
- `dagster_snowflake_pyspark_tests/test_snowflake_pyspark_type_handler.py`
- `dagster_snowflake_polars_tests/test_snowflake_polars_type_handler.py`
- `dagster_duckdb_pandas_tests/test_type_handler.py`
- `dagster_duckdb_pyspark_tests/test_type_handler.py`
- `dagster_duckdb_polars_tests/test_type_handler.py`

Each new test constructs an empty DataFrame, calls `handle_output` with a mocked connection / writer, and asserts that no write call was made.

## Changelog

> Skip table writes when an empty DataFrame is returned from an asset for the BigQuery, Snowflake, and DuckDB IO managers (Pandas / PySpark / Polars type handlers). This prevents incorrect type inference / degenerate tables for empty partitions. A warning is logged instead.

subject: Fix dagster-dbt prepare to always run dbt deps when dependency files exist (#22308)
body:
## Summary

Fixes issue dagster-io/dagster#31885 where `dbt deps` would be skipped
if the dbt_packages directory already existed, even when dependency
files had been updated. The previous implementation relied on a
heuristic (checking for dbt_packages directory) that could incorrectly
skip dependency installation. The fix directly checks for the presence
of dependencies.yml or packages.yml files to decide whether to run dbt
deps, which is both more reliable and still efficient since dbt deps is
fast when packages are already up-to-date.

## Key Changes

- Modified `DbtProjectPreparer.prepare()` to check for dependency
manifest files directly instead of using the unreliable
`has_uninstalled_deps` heuristic
- Added regression test in CLI prepare-and-package workflow to verify
dbt deps runs with pre-existing dbt_packages directory
- Added regression test in core DbtProject.prepare() to validate package
installation behavior
- Removed unused `mcp` dependency from uv.lock

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Modified (3 files)
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dbt/dagster_dbt/dbt_project.py`
- Updated prepare() condition to check dependency files instead of
installation directory heuristic
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dbt/dagster_dbt_tests/cli/test_prepare_and_package.py`
- Added regression test for CLI workflow
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dbt/dagster_dbt_tests/core/test_project.py`

<details>
<summary>original-plan</summary>

# Fix dagster-dbt prepare-and-package to always run dbt deps

## Context

GitHub issue dagster-io/dagster#31885 reports that `dagster-dbt project
prepare-and-package` only runs `dbt deps` and `dbt parse` when invoked
via `dagster dev`.

The CLI command `prepare-and-package` correctly calls `prepare()`
directly (bypassing `prepare_if_dev()`), so `dbt parse` always runs.
However, `dbt deps` can be silently skipped due to the
`has_uninstalled_deps` optimization in
`DagsterDbtProjectPreparer.prepare()`. This attribute is computed in
`DbtProject.__new__()` as:

```python
has_uninstalled_deps = (
    dependencies_path.exists() or packages_path.exists()
) and not packages_install_path.exists()
```

If the `dbt_packages` directory already exists from a previous run,
`has_uninstalled_deps` is `False` and `dbt deps` is skipped — even if
dependencies have changed. This means on second and subsequent runs of
`prepare-and-package`, `dbt deps` does not execute.

For an explicit deployment preparation command like
`prepare-and-package`, `dbt deps` should always run to ensure
dependencies are current.

## Changes

### 1. Modify `DagsterDbtProjectPreparer.prepare()` to always run deps
when dependency files exist

**File**:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dbt/dagster_dbt/dbt_project.py`

In the `prepare()` method (line 88-111), replace the
`project.has_uninstalled_deps` check with a direct check for dependency
files:

**Current code (lines 98-105):**
```python
        if project.has_uninstalled_deps:
            run_with_concurrent_update_guard(
                project.project_dir.joinpath("package-lock.yml"),
                self._prepare_packages,
                project=project,
            )
```

**New code:**
```python
        # Always run dbt deps when dependency files exist, not just when
        # packages appear uninstalled. The has_uninstalled_deps check uses a
        # heuristic (dbt_packages dir existence) that can incorrectly skip
        # deps when dependencies have changed but the directory still exists.
        # dbt deps itself is fast when packages are already up-to-date.
        has_deps_files = (
            project.project_dir.joinpath("dependencies.yml").exists()
            or project.project_dir.joinpath("packages.yml").exists()
        )
        if has_deps_files:
            run_with_concurrent_update_guard(
                project.project_dir.joinpath("package-lock.yml"),
                self._prepare_packages,
                project=project,
            )
```

This ensures `dbt deps` runs whenever dependency files exist, regardless
of whether the `dbt_packages` directory is present. The `dbt deps`
command itself handles the "already installed and up-to-date" case
efficiently (it checks the lock file and skips downloads when nothing
has changed), so this adds minimal overhead.

### 2. Add test for `prepare-and-package` with pre-existing packages

**File**:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dbt/dagster_dbt_tests/cli/test_prepare_and_package.py`

Add a new test `test_prepare_and_package_runs_deps_when_packages_exist`
after the existing `test_prepare_and_package_with_packages` test (around
line 176). This test verifies that `prepare-and-package` runs `dbt deps`
even when the `dbt_packages` directory already exists:

```python
def test_prepare_and_package_runs_deps_when_packages_exist(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, dbt_project_dir: Path
) -> None:
    """Test that prepare-and-package runs dbt deps even when dbt_packages already exists.

    Regression test for https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/31885.
    """
    monkeypatch.chdir(dbt_project_dir)

    project_name = "jaffle_dagster"
    dagster_project_dir = dbt_project_dir.joinpath(project_name)

    result = runner.invoke(
        app,
        [
            "project",
            "scaffold",
            "--project-name",
            project_name,
            "--dbt-project-dir",
            os.fspath(dbt_project_dir),
        ],
    )

    assert result.exit_code == 0

    dependencies_path = dbt_project_dir.joinpath("dependencies.yml")
    packages_install_path = dbt_project_dir.joinpath("dbt_packages")
    manifest_path = dbt_project_dir.joinpath("target", "manifest.json")

    # Create a dependencies.yml file
    with open(dependencies_path, "w") as file:
        dependencies_yml = {
            "packages": [{"package": "dbt-labs/dbt_utils", "version": [">=1.1.1", "<2.0.0"]}]
        }
        yaml.dump(dependencies_yml, file)

    # Pre-create the dbt_packages directory to simulate a previous run
    packages_install_path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    assert dependencies_path.exists()
    assert packages_install_path.exists()
    assert not manifest_path.exists()

    result = runner.invoke(
        app,
        [
            "project",
            "prepare-and-package",
            "--file",
            os.fspath(dagster_project_dir.joinpath(project_name, "project.py")),
        ],
    )

    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert manifest_path.exists()
    # Verify that dbt deps actually ran and populated the packages directory
    # (an empty pre-existing directory would not have package contents)
    assert any(packages_install_path.iterdir())
```

Add `yaml` to the imports at the top of the file if not already present
(it is not currently imported in this file — add `import yaml` after the
existing imports).

### 3. Add test for `prepare()` directly running deps with pre-existing
packages

**File**:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dbt/dagster_dbt_tests/core/test_project.py`

Add a new test `test_prepare_runs_deps_when_packages_exist` to verify
the `prepare()` method behavior directly:

```python
def test_prepare_runs_deps_when_packages_exist() -> None:
    """Test that prepare() runs dbt deps even when dbt_packages dir exists.

    Regression test for https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/31885.
    """
    with copy_directory(test_jaffle_shop_path) as project_dir:
        my_project = DbtProject(project_dir)

        # Create dependencies.yml
        deps_path = Path(project_dir) / "dependencies.yml"
        deps_path.write_text(
            "packages:\n  - package: dbt-labs/dbt_utils\n    version: ['>=1.1.1', '<2.0.0']\n"
        )

        # Pre-create dbt_packages to simulate previous installation
        packages_dir = Path(project_dir) / "dbt_packages"
        packages_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

        # Recreate project so it picks up the new deps file
        my_project = DbtProject(project_dir)

        # Even though dbt_packages exists, prepare() should run deps
        preparer = DagsterDbtProjectPreparer()
        preparer.prepare(my_project)

        # dbt deps should have actually installed packages
        assert any(packages_dir.iterdir()), "dbt deps should have installed packages"
        assert my_project.manifest_path.exists(), "dbt parse should have created manifest"
```

## Files NOT changing

-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dbt/dagster_dbt/cli/app.py`
— The CLI `prepare_and_package()` function already correctly calls
`prepare()` directly. No changes needed here.
- `DbtProject.__new__()` — The `has_uninstalled_deps` attribute is kept
unchanged for backward compatibility (it's a public attribute on

subject: Fix tag value coercion for component YAML files (#22310)
body:
## Summary

Components now properly coerce non-string scalar tag values (integers,
floats, booleans) to strings during resolution, enabling users to write
cleaner YAML configurations without manual string conversion. This
resolves the issue where YAML tag values like `priority: 1` would fail
validation instead of being automatically converted to `"1"`.

## Key Changes

- New `_resolve_tags()` function coerces non-string scalar values to
strings during tag resolution
- Updated `SharedAssetKwargs` to use custom resolver for tags accepting
`Mapping[str, str | int | float | bool]` in YAML
- Added comprehensive test coverage for integer, float, and boolean tag
value coercion
- Minor dependency cleanup (removed unused mcp from ai extras)

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Modified (2 files)
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/resolved/core_models.py`
- Added tag resolution function and updated SharedAssetKwargs resolver
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster_tests/components_tests/unit_tests/test_spec_processing.py`
- Added tests for tag coercion behavior

### Modified (1 file)
- `uv.lock` - Removed mcp dependency from ai extras

</details>

## User Experience

**Before:**
```yaml
# This would fail - tag values must be strings
assets:
  tags:
    priority: 1
    enabled: true
    score: 3.5
```

**After:**
```yaml
# Non-string scalar values are automatically coerced to strings
assets:
  tags:
    priority: 1          # → "1"
    enabled: true        # → "True"
    score: 3.5           # → "3.5"
```

Users can now write more natural YAML configurations with scalar values
that are automatically converted to strings during asset resolution.

**Remotely executed:** [Run
#23952414616](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/actions/runs/23952414616)

---

```

```

<details>
<summary>original-plan</summary>

# Fix Tag Value Coercion for Component YAML Files

## Context

**GitHub Issue**: dagster-io/dagster#30954

When users define tag values as integers (or other non-string scalars)
in component YAML files, Dagster raises a pydantic `ValidationError`
instead of automatically coercing the values to strings. For example:

```yaml
tags:
  priority: 1
  tier: prod
```

This fails because the `tags` field on `SharedAssetKwargs` is typed as
`Mapping[str, str]`, and pydantic strictly validates the YAML-parsed
values (where `1` is an `int`) against this type. Since tags are
fundamentally string key-value pairs, non-string scalar values should be
automatically coerced to strings.

## Changes

### 1. Add a custom resolver function for tags

**File**:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/resolved/core_models.py`

Add a resolver function that coerces tag values to strings after
template resolution:

```python
def _resolve_tags(context: ResolutionContext, tags: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Mapping[str, str]:
    """Resolve tags, coercing non-string scalar values to strings."""
    resolved = context.resolve_value(tags)
    return {k: str(v) for k, v in resolved.items()}
```

Place this near the top of the file, next to the existing
`_resolve_asset_key` function (around line 33).

### 2. Update the `tags` field annotation on `SharedAssetKwargs`

**File**:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/resolved/core_models.py`

Change the `tags` field (lines 229-235) from:

```python
tags: Annotated[
    Mapping[str, str],
    Resolver.default(
        description="Tags for filtering and organizing.",
        examples=[{"tier": "prod", "team": "analytics"}],
    ),
] = {}
```

To:

```python
tags: Annotated[
    Mapping[str, str],
    Resolver(
        _resolve_tags,
        model_field_type=Mapping[str, str | int | float | bool],
        description="Tags for filtering and organizing.",
        examples=[{"tier": "prod", "team": "analytics"}],
    ),
] = {}
```

Key changes:
- Use `Resolver(...)` with a custom function instead of
`Resolver.default(...)`
- Set `model_field_type=Mapping[str, str | int | float | bool]` so
pydantic accepts scalar non-string values in the YAML
- The custom `_resolve_tags` function handles template resolution via
`context.resolve_value()` and then coerces all values to strings via
`str(v)`

### 3. Add tests for integer tag coercion

**File**:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster_tests/components_tests/unit_tests/test_spec_processing.py`

Add a test that verifies integer (and other scalar) tag values are
coerced to strings:

```python
def test_integer_tag_values_coerced_to_strings() -> None:
    """Test that non-string scalar tag values in YAML are coerced to strings (issue #30954)."""
    op = AssetPostProcessorModel.model()(
        attributes={"tags": {"priority": 1, "enabled": True, "score": 3.5}},
    )
    newdefs = apply_post_processor_to_defs(model=op, defs=defs, context=ResolutionContext.default())
    asset_graph = newdefs.resolve_asset_graph()
    assert asset_graph.get(dg.AssetKey("a")).tags == {
        "priority": "1",
        "enabled": "True",
        "score": "3.5",
    }
```

Also add a test via direct `SharedAssetKwargs` resolution to ensure the
coercion works at the model level:

```python
def test_shared_asset_kwargs_integer_tags() -> None:
    """Test that SharedAssetKwargs resolves integer tag values to strings."""
    from dagster.components.resolved.core_models import SharedAssetKwargs

    model_cls = SharedAssetKwargs.model()
    model = model_cls(tags={"priority": 1, "version": 2})
    resolved = SharedAssetKwargs.resolve_from_model(ResolutionContext.default(), model)
    assert resolved.tags == {"priority": "1", "version": "2"}
```

## Implementation Details

### Why a custom resolver instead of a pydantic validator?

The `SharedAssetKwargs` class uses the `Resolvable` framework which
derives pydantic models dynamically via `derive_model_type()`. The
derived model type is separate from the `Resolvable` class itself, so
adding a pydantic `field_validator` to `SharedAssetKwargs` wouldn't
affect the derived model. Using a custom `Resolver` with
`model_field_type` is the idiomatic way to control both the pydantic
model type and the resolution behavior in this framework.

### Why `str | int | float | bool` for model_field_type?

These are the scalar types that YAML parsers commonly produce for
unquoted values:
- `1` → `int`
- `1.5` → `float`
- `true` → `bool`
- `"hello"` → `str`

We don't accept `Mapping[str, Any]` to keep validation meaningful -
nested objects or lists as tag values should still be rejected.

### Template variable compatibility

The custom resolver calls `context.resolve_value(tags)` first, which
handles Jinja template resolution (e.g., `{{ my_var }}`). After
resolution, `str(v)` coerces any remaining non-string values. This
preserves full template variable support.

### The `inject_before_resolve` default

The `Resolver(...)` constructor defaults `inject_before_resolve=True`,
which means if the entire `tags` field is a string (template), it will
be resolved before calling `_resolve_tags`. This is correct behavior -
if someone writes `tags: "{{ my_tags_var }}"`, the template is resolved
first, then `_resolve_tags` handles the result.

## Files NOT Changing

-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/resolved/base.py`
- No changes to the resolution framework
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/resolved/model.py`
- No changes to the Resolver class
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/resolved/context.py`
- No changes to ResolutionContext
- `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/_utils/tags.py` - The
`normalize_tags` function already handles coercion in the broader
Dagster API; this fix is specifically for the component YAML resolution
path
- `CHANGELOG.md` - Never modify

## Verification

1. Run the existing spec processing tests to ensure no regressions:
   ```bash
cd dagster-oss && tox -e py312-default -- -xvs
python_modules/dagster/dagster_tests/components_tests/unit_tests/test_spec_processing.py
   ```

2. Run the new tests for integer tag coercion.

3. Run `make ruff` from the dagster-oss directory to ensure code
formatting is correct.

4. Run component resolution tests broadly to check for regressions:
   ```bash
cd dagster-oss && tox -e py312-default -- -xvs
python_modules/dagster/dagster_tests/components_tests/
   ```

</details>

subject: [dagster-dbt] Prevent unbounded recursive copy when dbt project is at the project root (#24988)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where loading a `DbtProjectComponent` could fill the disk
(reported up to ~90GB) when the dbt project is placed at the **root** of
the Dagster project and `prepare_if_dev` is left at its default
(`True`).

**Root cause:** under `dagster dev`/`dg`, `StateBackedComponent`
refreshes state via `DbtProjectArgsManager.sync`, which copies the dbt
project into a local snapshot dir at
`<defs_module>/.local_defs_state/<key>/project`. When the dbt project is
at the project root, that destination is **nested inside the copy
source**, so `shutil.copytree` recursed into its own destination and
copied the project into itself unboundedly (e.g.
`.../project/.../.local_defs_state/<key>/project/.../.local_defs_state/<key>/project/...`).
Setting `prepare_if_dev: false` only masked it because the copy then
never ran.

**Fix:** pass an `ignore` callable to `copytree` that excludes the
destination directory whenever it is nested within the source, breaking
the recursion. The normal case (dbt project not at the root) is
unchanged — `ignore` returns an empty set.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression test
`test_prepare_does_not_recurse_when_state_nested_in_project_dir` fails
on the old code (recursive copy → `Errno 63`) and passes with the fix.
- [x] Existing `test_basic_component_dev_mode` /
`test_basic_component_non_dev_mode` still pass.
- [x] `ruff check` clean.

```
tox -e py312-core-main-dbt111 -- -k "test_prepare_does_not_recurse_when_state_nested_in_project_dir or test_basic_component_dev_mode or test_basic_component_non_dev_mode"
```

## Changelog

- [dagster-dbt] fixed a bug in the DbtProjectComponent where the
`.local_defs_state()` directory grew unboundedly large if the dbt
project was at the root of the repository.

subject: test_k8s: make kind cluster teardown best-effort (#25039)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

[Internal build
153576](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153576#019e6f36-f40d-48e4-b0f9-08f1956325fd)
failed with a single error inside `:pytest:
k8s-test-suite-1-2-default-3-12`. Every test in the file passed (18
passed, 2 skipped); the error was raised during cluster-fixture
teardown:

```
kind.py:225  check_output(["kind", "delete", "cluster", ...])
→ docker rm -f -v cluster-...-control-plane
→ Error: cannot remove container ... could not kill container:
  tried to kill container, but did not receive an exit event
```

This is a known dind quirk. Under load (we'd just torn down 30+ pods),
containerd/runc can leave a shim hanging; Docker's SIGKILL completes but
the daemon never observes the exit event and surfaces this exact error.
Because pytest treats a fixture-teardown exception as a test error, a
successful run gets reported as failed.

This PR makes kind-cluster teardown best-effort:

1. Try `kind delete cluster` as before.
2. On failure, log + fall back to a direct `docker kill` + `docker rm -f
-v` against any container labeled `io.x-k8s.kind.cluster=<name>` (robust
to single- or multi-node kind configs).
3. Swallow remaining errors. The agent pod is ephemeral; leaking a
container inside it costs nothing, and a teardown race shouldn't turn a
green CI run red.

## Test Plan

- CI re-runs `k8s-test-suite` against the new teardown path; behavior on
the happy path is unchanged (same `check_output(["kind", "delete",
...])` call).
- The fallback path is exercise-only by induced failure; not easily
testable in CI without mocking `kind`.

# Fix: Incorrect docstring on load_defs() in dagster-components

## Context

GitHub Issue: https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/29654
(Linear: GHIR-222)

The `load_defs()` function in
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/core/load_defs.py`
has an incorrect docstring. The original issue reported that the
docstring documented a non-existent `resources` parameter instead of the
actual `project_root` parameter. While the `resources` parameter
documentation has since been replaced, the `defs_root` parameter is
still incorrectly documented as type `(Path)` with description "The path
to the defs root", when it is actually of type `ModuleType`.

## Changes

### File:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/core/load_defs.py`

**Lines 155-156** — Fix the `defs_root` parameter documentation in the
`load_defs()` docstring.

Change:
```python
        defs_root (Path): The path to the defs root, typically `package.defs`.
```

To:
```python
        defs_root (ModuleType): The root module containing Dagster defs, typically the `defs` submodule of your project package.
```

This corrects:
1. The type annotation from `Path` to `ModuleType` (matching the actual
function signature `defs_root: ModuleType`)
2. The description from "The path to" to "The root module containing"

subject: chore(ruff): enable DOC102 and fix stale docstring args (#25037)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Stacks on top of #25034 (enable lint preview mode) which stacks on
#25026 (ruff bump to 0.15.14).

Adds `DOC102` (pydoclint docstring-extraneous-parameter) to the shared
ruff `select` list. DOC102 flags `Args:` entries in a docstring whose
name doesn't appear in the surrounding function's signature — a
high-signal "stale doc" check. The rule is preview-status and must be
listed by exact code under `explicit-preview-rules = true` (enabled in
the parent PR).

## Fixes (50 files, +15 / -159)

66 violations fixed by walking each one and triaging in parallel via
sonnet subagents. Every case turned out to be a real stale-doc bug from
a past parameter rename or refactor — none were `**kwargs` passthroughs
that needed `# noqa: DOC102`.

Categories of fix:

- **Stale `Args:` entry deleted** (most cases): a `param: ...` line
whose name doesn't exist in the signature; deleted that line (and any
indented continuation), keeping the rest of the `Args:` block intact. If
it was the only entry, the `Args:` header was also removed.
- **Stale entry replaced with the actual parameter name** (a few cases):
e.g. docstring said `alert_policy` but signature has `alert_policies`
(plural); fixed the name. Same for `concurrency_keys` →
`concurrency_key`, `pipeline_context` → `job_context`, etc.
- **`Args: ... Returns: ...` block with no blank line between them** (2
cases): ruff parses the contents of `Returns:` as `Args:` entries when
there's no blank line separating the blocks. Inserted the blank line (or
removed the trailing block in one case where it was redundant).
- **Replaced all-stale `Args:` block** (1 case:
`switch_dagster_cloud_plan`): the docstring documented 5 parameters that
had all been refactored away into an `instance` object. Replaced with
up-to-date entries for the actual `instance` and `new_plan_type` params.

## Touched files

49 files across `dagster-cloud`, `dagster-oss/python_modules`,
`dagster-oss/examples`, internal `python_modules/automation-internal`,
and `python_modules/dagster-open-platform`. No production behavior
changed — these are docstring edits only.

## Verification

- `just ruff` — clean (DOC102 detection + check + format all pass).
- The exception path (`**kwargs` passthroughs → `# noqa: DOC102` rather
than delete) was not exercised — none of the 66 violations turned out to
be that pattern.

## Why not noqa-everything?

Considered (path A) mass `# noqa: DOC102` to enable the rule cheaply and
chip away later, vs. (path B) fix everything inline now. Picked B
because the inline edits were quick when parallelized across 49 sonnet
subagents (~one per file), and the resulting docstrings are now accurate
rather than carrying TODO noqa markers.

subject: Use Harbor repo per code location instead of per deployment (#24932)
body:
## Summary

Change the image naming scheme so each code location gets its own Harbor repository nested under the existing deployment prefix. Previously all code locations in a deployment shared a single repo and were differentiated only by tag.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Harbor repo** | `depl-42-prod` (one per deployment) | `depl-42-prod/my-loc` (one per code location) |
| **Full image** | `host/project/depl-42-prod:prod-my-loc-abc` | `host/project/depl-42-prod/my-loc:prod-my-loc-abc` |
| **Image prefix validation** | `host/project/` | `host/project/` (unchanged) |

## Changes

### Server-side
- **`serverless.py` (graphql)**: Updated `get_harbor_repo_name` docstring to clarify it produces a deployment-scoped *prefix*; updated `_get_harbor_info` comment. No functional change to the `RegistryURI` value — it still returns `{host}/{project}/{depl-prefix}`.
- **`serverless.py` (graphql)**: Added nullable `registryIsHarbor` boolean field so the CLI can distinguish Harbor from ECR backends.

### CLI-side
- **`docker_utils.py`**: Added `full_image_ref(registry_url, location_name, image_tag)` that appends `/{location_name}` when provided, falling back to legacy `{registry}:{tag}` for ECR.  Updated `build_image`/`upload_image` to accept `location_name`.
- **`gql.py`**: Queries `registryIsHarbor` and exposes it as `is_harbor` (defaults to `False` if the server doesn't have the field yet).
- **`serverless/__init__.py`**: `deploy_command` passes `location_name` to docker_utils only when `is_harbor` is true.
- **`ci/__init__.py`**: `_build_docker` passes `location_name` to docker_utils only when `is_harbor` is true.

## ECS serverless compatibility
The CLI gates per-location repo behavior on the `registryIsHarbor` field. ECR-backed orgs get `False` and continue using the existing `{registry}:{tag}` image format. The field is nullable so a new CLI against an old server defaults to ECR behavior.

## Backward compatibility
- Agent `DAGSTER_CLOUD_SERVERLESS_IMAGE_PREFIX` validation (`{host}/{project}/`) still works since all per-location repos fall under the same project prefix.
- Harbor auto-creates repos on first push, so no provisioning changes needed.
- Legacy CLI commands (`build`, `upload`, `upload-base-image`) don't pass `location_name` and are unaffected.
- The `dagster-cloud-action` GitHub Action repo should be checked if it calls `registry-info` and constructs image names directly (the standard `dagster-cloud ci build` path is handled).

subject: Add TypedDict and Required/NotRequired support to match_type function, fix dg CLI config bug (#22307)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where the dg CLI crashed with a `TypeError` when users set
`cli.telemetry.enabled` in `dg.toml`. The crash originated in
`match_type()` in dagster-shared, which called `isinstance(obj,
RawDgTelemetryConfig)` — but TypedDict classes don't support
`isinstance` checks at runtime.

Extended `match_type()` to validate TypedDict instances structurally,
including support for `Required` and `NotRequired` field wrappers. The
function now checks that dictionaries conform to TypedDict schemas by
validating required keys are present and present keys match their
annotated types.

Fixes
[dagster-io/dagster#32728](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/32728).

## Key Changes

- Added `is_typeddict()` type checking and structural validation logic
to `match_type()` for TypedDict instances — unblocks the dg CLI
telemetry config path
- Added support for `Required` and `NotRequired` type wrappers in type
matching
- Comprehensive test coverage for TypedDict matching scenarios (optional
fields, required fields, type validation)
- Added regression test for the dg CLI telemetry config
(`cli.telemetry.enabled` in `dg.toml`) that exercised the original crash

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Modified
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared/dagster_shared/match.py`
— Added TypedDict validation and Required/NotRequired wrapper handling
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared/dagster_shared_tests/test_match.py`
— Added TypedDict test classes and comprehensive validation test cases
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/test_telemetry.py`
— Added regression test for telemetry config

</details>

**Remotely executed:** [Run
#23952396356](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/actions/runs/23952396356)

---

To replicate this PR locally, run:

```
erk pr teleport 22307
```

<details>
<summary>original-plan</summary>

# Fix dg CLI TypedDict isinstance check (dagster-io/dagster#32728)

## Context

When users set `cli.telemetry.enabled` in `dg.toml`, the dg CLI config
validation crashes with a `TypeError` because `match_type()` in
`dagster-shared` attempts `isinstance(obj, RawDgTelemetryConfig)` — but
TypedDict classes don't support `isinstance` checks at runtime.

The root cause is in `dagster_shared/match.py:match_type()`. When
`type_` is a TypedDict class, `get_origin()` returns `None`, so
execution falls through to the `isinstance(obj, type_)` call on line 37,
which raises `TypeError`.

The bug is triggered via `_validate_dg_config_file_cli_section()` in
`dagster_dg_core/config.py` (line 772-773), which iterates
`DgRawCliConfig.__annotations__` and calls
`_validate_file_config_setting()` for each field. When it hits the
`telemetry` field (typed as `RawDgTelemetryConfig`), the TypedDict class
gets passed to `match_type()`.

## Changes

### 1. Add TypedDict handling to `match_type()` in `dagster-shared`

**File:**
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared/dagster_shared/match.py`

In the `match_type()` function, add a check for TypedDict types
**before** the final `isinstance` fallback (line 37). The check should:

1. Import `is_typeddict` from `typing` (available in Python 3.10+, which
matches the package's `requires-python = ">=3.10"`)
2. After the `ForwardRef` check (line 35) and before the `isinstance`
fallback (line 37), add:

```python
elif is_typeddict(type_):
    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        return False
    annotations = type_.__annotations__
    required_keys = getattr(type_, "__required_keys__", set())
    # Check all required keys are present
    for k in required_keys:
        if k not in obj:
            return False
    # Check all present keys have correct types
    for k, v in obj.items():
        if k in annotations:
            if not match_type(v, annotations[k]):
                return False
    return True
```

This validates:
- The object is a `dict`
- All required keys are present
- All present keys that have annotations match their expected types
- Extra keys not in annotations are allowed (TypedDict `total=False`
semantics)

Add `is_typeddict` to the imports from `typing`.

### 2. Add TypedDict tests to `test_match.py`

**File:**
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared/dagster_shared_tests/test_match.py`

Add test cases to the existing parametrized `test_match_type` test:

```python
# TypedDict - define a test TypedDict at module level
class SimpleTypedDict(TypedDict, total=False):
    name: str
    count: int

class RequiredTypedDict(TypedDict):
    name: Required[str]
    count: NotRequired[int]
```

Test cases to add:
- `({"name": "x", "count": 1}, SimpleTypedDict, True)` — valid full dict
- `({"name": "x"}, SimpleTypedDict, True)` — valid partial (total=False)
- `({}, SimpleTypedDict, True)` — valid empty (all optional)
- `({"name": 1}, SimpleTypedDict, False)` — wrong type for field
- `("not a dict", SimpleTypedDict, False)` — not a dict at all
- `({"name": "x"}, RequiredTypedDict, True)` — required key present
- `({}, RequiredTypedDict, False)` — missing required key
- `({"name": "x", "count": "bad"}, RequiredTypedDict, False)` — wrong
type for optional field

Add `TypedDict` import from `typing` and `Required`/`NotRequired` if
needed.

## Files NOT changing

-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-core/dagster_dg_core/config.py`
— No changes needed. The fix in `match_type()` will make the existing
validation code work correctly for TypedDict types without any changes
to the config validator.
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/test_telemetry.py`
— The existing `test_telemetry_disabled_dg_config` test should now pass
without errors, serving as an integration-level validation of the fix.
- CHANGELOG.md — Never modify.

## Implementation Details

- `typing.is_typeddict` (Python 3.10+) is the correct way to detect
TypedDict classes at runtime. The package requires `>=3.10`.
- TypedDict classes have `__annotations__`, `__required_keys__`, and
`__optional_keys__` attributes that can be used for structural
validation.
- `RawDgTelemetryConfig` uses `total=False`, meaning all keys are
optional — the validation should reflect this.
- The workspace validation (`_validate_file_config_workspace_section`)
already handles nested TypedDict types via dedicated methods, but the
CLI validation does not — this fix makes `match_type` handle TypedDict
generically so no special-casing is needed in validators.

## Verification

1. Run the `dagster-shared` match tests:
   ```bash
cd dagster-oss && python -m pytest
python_modules/libraries/dagster-shared/dagster_shared_tests/test_match.py
-xvs
   ```

2. Run the dg CLI telemetry test that exercises the bug path:
   ```bash
cd dagster-oss && tox -e py312-default -c
python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/tox.ini -- -k
test_telemetry_disabled_dg_config -xvs
   ```

3. Run the config validation tests to ensure no regressions:
   ```bash
cd dagster-oss && tox -e py312-default -c
python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-core/tox.ini -- -k
test_invalid_config -xvs
   ```

4. Run `make ruff` from the dagster-oss root to ensure formatting
compliance.

subject: chore(ruff): enable lint.preview mode and apply preview-mode fixes (#25034)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Stacks on top of #25026.

Enables `lint.preview = true` + `lint.explicit-preview-rules = true` in
the shared ruff config (`dagster-oss/config/ruff.toml`), then
auto-applies the preview-mode fixes those settings unlock for rules our
`select` list already includes. This unblocks `just ruff` from doing the
PERF401 auto-fix added in #25026, and tightens detection of several
other rules (PERF102, UP006/UP008/UP017, I001, F401, RUF100, RUF022,
PIE790, …).

`explicit-preview-rules = true` means category selectors like `select =
["PERF"]` *won't* sweep in unrelated preview-status rules — those must
be opted in by exact code. So this PR enables preview *behavior* without
enabling unrelated preview *rules*.

The specific impetus is to start turning on docstring linting, which is
currently in preview.

## Auto-applied preview fixes (54 files, +54 / -79)

Mostly mechanical:

- **PERF102** (~26): `for k, _ in d.items()` → `for k in d` or
`.values()` — tighter dict iterator usage.
- **F401** (~30): unused imports removed. Where the import was
load-bearing as a side-effect (alembic operation registration,
streamline consumer registration), the import is restored with an
explicit `# noqa: F401` annotation. Inspected files:
- `dagster-cloud-backend/.../alembic/run_migration.py` — 4 alembic-op
registration imports restored
-
`dagster-cloud-backend_tests/.../migration_tests/test_safe_constraint.py`
— 1 alembic-op registration import restored
- `dagster-cloud-worker/dagster_cloud_worker/cli/streamline.py` — 10
streamline-consumer registration imports restored
- **UP006/UP008/UP017** (~30 combined): `List` → `list`, `super(C,
self)` → `super()`, `timezone.utc` → `UTC`.
- **I001** (~handful): import-block reorderings.
- **RUF100** (~handful): unused `# noqa` directives removed where ruff
no longer fires the suppressed rule.
- **RUF022** (1): `__all__` reorder.

## Per-file-ignores added

Two new INP001 (implicit-namespace-package) exemptions, both for
legitimate cases:

- `**/templates/PROJECT_NAME_PLACEHOLDER/**/__init__.py` —
project-scaffold templates rendered into the user's workspace, not
packages themselves.
-
`python_modules/dagster/dagster/_core/storage/alembic/versions/__init__.py`
— alembic versions/ dir; we already exempt the sibling `env.py`.

## Verification

- `just ruff` — clean (check + format).
- Spot-checked F401 removals where the removed module name was still
referenced (`kubernetes`, `botocore`, `papermill`) — all valid: a
sibling `import foo.bar` line provides the parent-package binding via
Python's import semantics.
- F401 removals classified as side-effect (verified by adjacent
"register" comments and consumer-/operations- module patterns) were
explicitly restored with `# noqa: F401`.

## Follow-up

Stacking another PR on top to enable DOC102 (pydoclint, preview-status).
That's a small additive change now that preview mode is on.

Bumps ruff `0.15.13 → 0.15.14` and enables `PERF401`

required at check time — preview was only needed to apply the bulk fix).
The temporary-disable comment for `PERF401` is removed; `PERF402` stays
in the ignore list (still no auto-fix even in preview).

- `dagster-oss/config/ruff.toml`: `required-version` bump, `PERF401`

`extend(generator)`.

## Side effects the auto-fix exposed

The PERF401 transformation removed `xxx = []` initializers and `for`
bodies, which surfaced 4 latent lint errors:

- **3 × `D202`** (no blank line after docstring): the auto-fix left a
blank line between a docstring and the next statement. Auto-fixed in a

- **1 × `F841` (`specs` unused)** in

the test deliberately constructs `Spec(...)` instances inside a loop to

still constructs each `Spec`) but exposed the latent unused-variable
warning. Added `assert len(specs) == len(checks)` to make the variable
load-bearing while keeping the original test semantics.

## Verification

- `just ruff` — clean (check + format).
- `uvx ruff@0.15.14 check --select PERF401,PERF402 .` — only the 10
known `PERF402` violations remain (unchanged).

subject: fix(dagster-aws): guarantee ECS pipes interruption subprocess is reaped (#25004)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

On master build
[153444](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153444), the
`dagster-aws-3-12` step hung: every `pipes_tests` test from
`test_ecs_pipes_task_failed_to_start` onward took *exactly* 240.0s — the
global `pytest-timeout` fallback (`timeout = "240"`, `method: signal`)
killing each hung test and limping to the next. Every pipes test
*before* that point ran in seconds, which localizes the problem to
mid-module state corruption rather than a slow agent or network issue.

The corruption is introduced by
`test_ecs_pipes_interruption_forwarding`, which #24924 rewrote. Its
happy path was a single `p.terminate()` + `p.join(timeout=30)` + `assert
not p.is_alive()`, with `p.kill()` escalation present *only* in the
"task never launched within 60s" error branch. The subprocess under test
runs `materialize`, which installs Dagster's
SIGTERM→graceful-interruption handler — the whole point of the test.
When that graceful shutdown outlives the 30s join (or any of the
assertions fails), the happy path returns without ever calling
`p.kill()`, leaving the child **alive**.

That child is `fork()`ed from the test process and holds the inherited
moto server socket on `localhost:5193` (the shared, function-scoped
`moto_server` fixture port). A leaked orphan wedges that port, so every
subsequent moto-dependent pipes test blocks until the 240s timeout
fires. The build's 32.7s runtime for
`test_ecs_pipes_interruption_forwarding` (≈ startup + the full 30s join
cap) is consistent with the join expiring and the child surviving
SIGTERM.

## Changes

- **Always reap the child.** Wrap the test body in `try/finally` and
unconditionally `p.kill()` + `p.join()` the subprocess on every exit
path (assertion failure, join timeout, or the "didn't launch" branch),
so it can never be leaked.
- **Don't inherit the moto socket.** Start the subprocess from a `spawn`
multiprocessing context (`multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, used
for the `Manager`, `Event`, and `Process`). A spawned child gets a fresh
interpreter and does not inherit this process's file descriptors —
including the moto listening socket — and reaches moto over the network
as a client instead. Even a leaked child can then no longer wedge port
5193. Linux CI defaults to `fork`; macOS already defaults to `spawn`.
- **Gate on a real completion signal.** Add a
`materialization_done_event` that the subprocess sets in its `finally`
immediately after writing `return_dict`. The parent waits on this event
after `p.terminate()` instead of asserting `not p.is_alive()` within a
fixed window. Under spawn, instance/multiprocessing teardown after the
interruption can outrun a process-death check even when the
materialization data the test cares about is already ready — that timing
mismatch was the residual flake #24924 was originally chasing.

Together these turn what was a module-wide hang into a robust,
deterministic test.

## Test Plan

- `ruff format --check` / `ruff check` pass on the changed file.

subject: Remove overly strict dependency file check from Docker deploy path (GHIR-224) (#22453)
body:
Remove overly strict dependency file check from Docker deploy path

The `dagster-cloud serverless deploy` command required `setup.py`,
`requirements.txt`, or `pyproject.toml` in the source directory, even
for Docker image deployments where the Dockerfile already handles
missing dependency files gracefully. This fix removes the validation
from the Docker deploy path while keeping it for PEX deployments where
it's actually needed.

Resolves dagster-io/dagster#29605

## Key Changes

- Removed `_check_source_directory()` call from `deploy_command()` in
`dagster-cloud-cli` serverless module
- Updated `test_deploy_no_deps` to assert the dependency file error no
longer occurs for Docker deploys
- Aligns `serverless deploy-docker` behavior with `ci build`, which
already skips this check

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Modified (2 files)
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/dagster_cloud_cli/commands/serverless/__init__.py`
- Removed dependency file validation from Docker deploy path
-
`dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud-dagit/dagster_cloud_dagit_tests/serverless_tests/test_cli.py`
- Updated test assertion to match new behavior

</details>

## User Experience

**Before:**
```
$ dagster-cloud serverless deploy --location-name my_loc ./my_project
Error: Could not find a `setup.py`, `requirements.txt`, or `pyproject.toml` in the target directory
```

**After:**
```
$ dagster-cloud serverless deploy --location-name my_loc ./my_project
# Proceeds to Docker build step (dependency files are optional for Docker deployments)
```

Fixes https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/29605

<details>
<summary>original-plan</summary>

# Fix: dagster-cloud serverless deploy erroneously requires
setup.py/requirements.txt for Docker image deployments

GitHub Issue: https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/29605
Linear: GHIR-224

## Context

The `dagster-cloud serverless deploy` (alias for `deploy-docker`)
command calls `_check_source_directory()` at line 215 of
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/dagster_cloud_cli/commands/serverless/__init__.py`.
This function requires one of `setup.py`, `requirements.txt`, or
`pyproject.toml` in the source directory, raising an error if none are
found.

However, the built-in Dockerfile template
(`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/dagster_cloud_cli/commands/serverless/Dockerfile`)
already handles the case where these files are missing — it uses `if [
-f ... ]` conditionals to only install from these files if they exist.
The Docker `COPY` command on line 6 uses glob patterns (`*setup.py
*requirements.txt`) that won't fail if files are missing.

The validation is overly strict for Docker deployments because:
1. A user may have a Dockerfile or base image that already includes all
dependencies
2. The template Dockerfile already gracefully handles missing dependency
files
3. The `dagster-cloud ci build` command does NOT perform this validation
for Docker builds (see `_build_docker` function at line 820 of
`commands/ci/__init__.py`)

The validation IS appropriate for `deploy-python-executable` (PEX
deployments) because PEX builds must resolve dependencies from these
files.

## Changes

### File:
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli/dagster_cloud_cli/commands/serverless/__init__.py`

**Remove the `_check_source_directory()` call from `deploy_command()`**
(line 215).

The `deploy_command()` function (lines 196-254) handles Docker image
deployments. Remove line 215:

```python
    _check_source_directory(source_directory)
```

This is the only change needed. The `_check_source_directory()` call at
line 507 in `deploy_python_executable_command()` should remain — PEX
deployments legitimately need dependency files.

The `_check_source_directory()` function definition (lines 545-560)
should also remain since it's still used by the PEX deploy path.

### File:
`dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud-dagit/dagster_cloud_dagit_tests/serverless_tests/test_cli.py`

**Update `test_deploy_no_deps` test** (lines 69-78).

This test verifies that `deploy` rejects directories without dependency
files. Since we're removing this validation for Docker deploys, update
the test to verify the command proceeds past the validation step (it
will still fail later due to Docker not being available or ECR issues in
the test environment). Change the assertion to expect the command to NOT
fail with the "Could not find a `setup.py`" message.

Specifically, change:
```python
@pytest.mark.skip(reason="Depends on pulling from public ECR, subject to rate limiting in CI")
def test_deploy_no_deps(runner):
    runner = CliRunner()
    test_dir = file_relative_path(__file__, "repos/no_dep_files")
    result = runner.invoke(app, ["deploy", "--location-name", "for_test", test_dir])
    assert result.exit_code == 1
    assert (
        "Could not find a `setup.py`, `requirements.txt`, or `pyproject.toml` in the target"
        in result.output
    )
```

To:
```python
@pytest.mark.skip(reason="Depends on pulling from public ECR, subject to rate limiting in CI")
def test_deploy_no_deps(runner):
    """Docker deploys should not require setup.py/requirements.txt/pyproject.toml."""
    runner = CliRunner()
    test_dir = file_relative_path(__file__, "repos/no_dep_files")
    result = runner.invoke(app, ["deploy", "--location-name", "for_test", test_dir])
    # Should NOT fail with the dependency file check error
    assert (
        "Could not find a `setup.py`, `requirements.txt`, or `pyproject.toml` in the target"
        not in result.output
    )
```

## Files NOT changing

- `dagster_cloud_cli/commands/serverless/Dockerfile` — No changes
needed; it already handles missing files gracefully
- `dagster_cloud_cli/docker_utils.py` — No changes needed
- `dagster_cloud_cli/commands/ci/__init__.py` — Already correct (no
`_check_source_directory` call for Docker builds)
- `dagster_cloud_cli/core/pex_builder/deps.py` — Unrelated (PEX build
dependencies)
- `dagster_cloud_cli_tests/test_pyproject_toml_support.py` — Tests for
`_check_source_directory` itself; the function is still used by PEX
deploy so these tests remain valid

## Implementation details

- The fix is a single line removal (line 215 of `__init__.py`)
- The test update is straightforward — flip the assertion
- The `_check_source_directory` function and its other call site (line
507, PEX deploy) are unchanged
- This aligns the `serverless deploy-docker` behavior with the `ci
build` command, which already does NOT check for dependency files in
Docker builds
- Run `make ruff` after changes per repo conventions

## Verification

1. **Ruff**: Run `make ruff` from the dagster-oss root to ensure
formatting/linting passes
2. **Unit tests**: Run the existing test suite for the dagster-cloud-cli
package:
   ```
   cd dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-cloud-cli
tox -vv -e py312 -- -k "test_check_source_directory or
test_pyproject_toml"
   ```
These tests verify `_check_source_directory` still works correctly (it's
still used by PEX deploy).
3. **Manual verification**: Create a directory with only a `.py` file
(no setup.py/requirements.txt/pyproject.toml) and verify `dagster-cloud
serverless deploy --location-name test .` no longer fails with the
dependency file error (it should proceed to the Docker build step).

</details>

subject: ci(buildkite): factor out KIND_TEST_RESOURCES and migrate kind tests to KUBERNETES_EKS (#24373)
body:
## What this PR does

| Step | Repo | Before | After |
| ---- | ---- | ------ | ----- |
| `validating-admission-webhook-e2e-testing` | internal | `MEDIUM`
(broken — see #24371) | `KUBERNETES_EKS` |
| `k8s-test-suite` | dagster-oss | `DOCKER` | `KUBERNETES_EKS` |
| `celery-k8s-test-suite` | dagster-oss | `DOCKER` | `KUBERNETES_EKS` |

All three steps run a `kind` cluster inside a dind sidecar and share the
same resource shape. This PR adds a `KIND_TEST_RESOURCES` preset in
`buildkite_shared.step_builders.resource_presets` (1.5 CPU / 2 Gi main +
4 Gi req / 10 Gi limit dind + 30 Gi ephemeral, with a 20 Gi dedicated
emptyDir at `/var/lib/docker`), plumbs a `resources: ResourceRequests |
None` parameter through `build_tox_step → PackageSpec →
build_integration_suite_steps` so it can be applied to
`PackageSpec`-driven suites, and migrates the three call sites onto the
preset.

It also removes the manual `aws ecr get-login-password ... | docker
login` from the suite extra-cmds — the EKS pod-spec-patch's
`ecr-docker-login` init container
([infra/k8s/buildkite/base/conf/buildkite.yaml](../blob/master/infra/k8s/buildkite/base/conf/buildkite.yaml))
handles that at pod startup now.

## EKS-specific fixes bundled here

The DOCKER queue ran single-tenant agents with local-disk docker; EKS
runs many concurrent dind sidecars sharing a node's EBS, network egress,
and DNS. The migration surfaced several issues that needed fixing in
lock-step with the queue move:

- **IRSA AWS credentials**. EKS agents use IRSA (web-identity token),
not long-lived env keys, so step pods couldn't find creds via boto3's
default chain — `test_project` jobs failed with `NoCredentialsError`.
Fix: materialize the IRSA creds via `aws configure export-credentials
--format env` in `*_pytest_extra_cmds`, propagate them into step pods
through the existing `TEST_AWS_CONFIGMAP_NAME` configmap (now populated
from `os.environ` on Buildkite, fakes locally — no `IS_BUILDKITE`
branches in test code).

- **dind `/var/lib/docker` on EBS, not in dind's container writable
layer**. The default 3-layer overlayfs (dind container fs → pod
ephemeral → EBS) made `kind load docker-image` and
`local-path-provisioner` PVC binding slow enough to time fixtures out.
Added a `docker_storage_size` field to `ResourceRequests`; when set,
mounts a dedicated `emptyDir` at `/var/lib/docker` in the dind sidecar.
KIND_TEST_RESOURCES sets 20 Gi. Tmpfs was tried (commit `aba021a`) but
cumulative containerd state from `dagster-run-*` pods grew into the
cgroup memory budget and OOM-killed the sidecar mid-session, so the dind
storage is disk-backed.

- **docker.io pull-through registry for kind's containerd**. With
multiple agent pods sharing one NAT egress IP, kubelet pulls of
`postgres` / `rabbitmq` / `redis` / `localstack` inside kind tripped
Docker Hub's anonymous rate limit (100/6h). Fix: `kind.py` starts a
`registry:2` container in the dind sidecar configured as a docker.io
pull-through cache, writes a kind config with `containerdConfigPatches`
pointing kind's docker.io mirror at it, and attaches the registry to the
kind docker network after cluster creation. On Buildkite the proxy
chains through the EKS-level
`dockerhub-mirror.buildkite-agent.svc.cluster.local:5000` so the cache
is shared across all builds.

- **test-project ECR image preload**. The mirror only covers docker.io,
so the private-ECR `test-project` image is still loaded into kind via
`kind load docker-image`, with `imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent` so kubelet
uses the cached copy. `kind_load_images` is now parallelized via
`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)` for local-dev's larger preload set.

- **Webserver/user-code startup race**. With faster fixture setup, the
dagster-webserver pod won the race to user-code-deployment-1's gRPC port
and parked the code location in `ERROR` state. Hidden previously by the
DOCKER queue's slower postgres startup. Fix:
`_port_forward_dagster_webserver` now sends a `reloadRepositoryLocation`
mutation and polls until `loadStatus=LOADED` before yielding the URL to
tests; covers both `webserver_url` and
`webserver_url_for_k8s_run_launcher` fixtures.

- **pytest `--timeout` bumped 480s → 1200s** in both suites' `tox.ini`.
The first test in each session pays the full cluster + preload + helm
install setup cost; 480s was tuned for DOCKER-queue speeds.

## Test Plan

- [x] Both kind suites pass on EKS in CI.
- [x] Test runs that exercise the S3 io_manager succeed (validates IRSA
propagation).
- [x] Fixture setup completes well inside the new 1200s timeout.

## Notes

- The shared preset lives in `buildkite_shared` because both
dagster-oss's `dagster_buildkite` and the internal repo's
`dagster_internal_buildkite` need to import it; `buildkite_shared` is
the only package both depend on.
- Worst case for a busy PR: ~8 dind sidecars × 10 Gi limit ≈ 80 GiB
across the EKS pool during a fan-out wave. The agent autoscaler should
accommodate, but worth a glance on the first few master runs.
- The kind-registry container persists for the dind sidecar's lifetime,
so back-to-back kind clusters in the same pod share its cache (cheap
subsequent runs).

subject: Limit watch/unwatch regression test to SQL event log storage (#24996)
body:
## Summary

Restrict the newly re-enabled `TestEventLogStorage.test_watch_unwatch`
regression test to OSS `SqlEventLogStorage` implementations.

The test is specifically covering the deadlock fixed in
`SqlPollingEventWatcher`: a watch callback calls `end_watch` for its own
run while callbacks are being dispatched. That deadlock path is tied to
the SQL polling watcher implementation, not every storage implementation
that happens to inherit the shared `TestEventLogStorage` suite.

## Motivation

After unskipping this test, the internal `dagster-cloud-backend`
Buildkite suite started running it against Cloud archive-aware event log
storages inherited from the shared OSS test class. Those storages report
that they can watch, but this inherited test is not currently valid for
them and failed deterministically with no events delivered to the safe
watcher:

- `TestHostCloudEventLogStorage::test_watch_unwatch`
- `TestImmediatelyArchiveAwareEventLogStorage::test_watch_unwatch`
- `TestOccasionallyArchiveAwareEventLogStorage::test_watch_unwatch`
- `TestRenamedArchiveAwareEventLogStorage::test_watch_unwatch`

The failure was `assert 0 == 12` for the collected safe-run events. This
change keeps the regression test active for the SQL-backed storages
where the polling watcher bug applies, while skipping
non-`SqlEventLogStorage` implementations.

## Test Plan

Ran the OSS sqlite variants that should still exercise the regression:

```bash
cd dagster-oss
python -m pytest python_modules/dagster/dagster_tests/storage_tests/test_event_log.py \
  -k 'watch_unwatch and (TestSqliteEventLogStorage or TestConsolidatedSqliteEventLogStorage)'
```

```text
2 passed, 583 deselected
```

subject: Retry 5xx responses on dagster-cloud REST session (#24992)
body:
## Summary

- The dagster-cloud agent's "managed retries" REST session
(`requests_managed_retries_session` in
`dagster_cloud/instance/__init__.py`) was configured with
`urllib3.Retry(total=..., backoff_factor=...)` but no
`status_forcelist`, so it only retried on transport-level failures. HTTP
5xx responses propagated immediately to the caller as
`DagsterCloudHTTPError`.
- This is observable as code-location load failures when a transient 503
comes back from `<org>.agent.dagster.cloud/confirm_upload` (the error
body typically reads `upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before
headers. reset reason: connection termination` — an Envoy-style 5xx from
the proxy in front of ursula).
- Adds `status_forcelist=[502, 503, 504]` so transient proxy-layer 5xx
are retried with the existing backoff. urllib3's default
`allowed_methods` covers all current callers (GET/PUT only).

## Why this is safe

`requests_managed_retries_session` is currently used in nine call sites;
all are idempotent:

| Caller | Method | Endpoint | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user_code_launcher.py:624` | GET | `check_snapshot` | Read |
| `user_code_launcher.py:646` | PUT | presigned object-store URL |
Overwrite by key |
| `user_code_launcher.py:653` | PUT | `confirm_upload` |
Content-addressed by sha1 |
| `user_code_launcher.py:721, 758` | PUT | `code_location_update_result`
| Keyed by deployment+location; the code already calls it twice on the
same payload |
| `user_code_launcher.py:799, 840` | PUT | `upload_workspace_entry`
(legacy) | Same overwrite shape |
| `user_code_launcher.py:2500` | PUT | `upload_job_snap` |
Content-addressed snapshot |
| `agent/dagster_cloud_agent.py:1354, 1370` | PUT |
`upload_api_response[_batch]` | Keyed by `request_id` — server dedupes |
| `storage/compute_logs/compute_log_manager.py:110` | GET |
`gen_logs_url` | Read |
| `dagster_insights/metrics_utils.py:41` | (passes session through) |
insights upload | Keyed by opaque id |

The strongest argument is the server-side contract for
`upload_api_response`: ursula explicitly returns `503` with a
`Retry-After` header on Redis timeout and expects the agent to retry —
today the agent does not, which is a latent bug this PR fixes. urllib3
honors `Retry-After` by default.

The agent's `client_managed_retries_requests_session` (used for GraphQL)
is a separate session with its own application-layer retry logic and is
not changed here.

## Test plan

- [ ] `just ruff` clean on the changed file
- [ ] `just ty` clean
- [ ] Confirm with a manual repro (or unit test) that a 503 response now
triggers retry with backoff up to `dagster_cloud_api_retries`
- [ ] Watch agent logs / Datadog after rollout for reduced rate of
`confirm_upload` / `upload_api_response` 503 propagation to
code-location failures

---------
