subject: Fix jest findBy-in-waitFor flakes in ui-core and app-cloud tests (#24994)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

The `AssetTable › Materialize button › is enabled when rows are
selected` test (`ui-core/.../AssetTables.test.tsx`) flaked on slow CI
([Buildkite internal
#153303](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153303)), failing
on `expect(checkboxes.indexOf(goodAssetCheckbox)).toBe(1)`.

**Root cause.** `useAllAssets` returns `[...softwareDefinedAssets,
...externalAssets]`, and the table renders rows in
`Object.entries(groups)` insertion order (not the sorted `displayKeys`).
Until the `WorkspaceContext` query resolves, the SDA nodes aren't known,
so every materialized record is classified "external" and renders in
fixture order — putting `good_asset` at checkbox index 3 instead of 1.
The steady state is deterministic and correct; the test just has to wait
for that convergence. But the `waitFor` used the testing-library default
1000ms timeout and nested async `findBy*` queries (each with its own
1000ms timeout, so they compound) — on a loaded CI worker the workspace
+ asset-records + Apollo + re-render chain exceeds 1000ms and the
`waitFor` times out. This is the same class the repo already documented
at `ui-core/src/nav/__tests__/useRepositoryLocationReload.test.tsx` ("On
slow CI workers this chain can exceed waitFor's default 1000ms timeout,
so give it more room").

Fixed that test and swept the same `findBy`-inside-`waitFor`
anti-pattern across the other JS suites.

## What changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `ui-core/.../AssetTables.test.tsx` | Synchronous `getBy*` inside
`waitFor` + `{timeout: 5000}`; explanatory comment on the load-ordering
convergence. |
| `ui-core/.../AssetView.test.tsx` | Same fix shape (sync `getBy*`
inside `waitFor` + `{timeout: 5000}`). |
| `ui-core/.../BackfillLogsTab.test.tsx` | Its two `waitFor` calls were
**never awaited**, so the "both pages load" (Event 1 + Event 4) and
"refreshing indicator clears" assertions never effectively ran — the
suite only checked the initial spinner. Awaited them, switched to
synchronous queries, used `queryByText(...).not.toBeInTheDocument()` for
the cleared indicator, and added `mockViewportClientRect()` so the
virtualized `InstigationEventLogTable` renders rows in jsdom. The test
now genuinely exercises pagination. |
| `app-cloud/.../AlertPolicyPage.test.tsx` | 5 blocks converted to sync
`screen.getByTestId` inside `waitFor` + `{timeout: 5000}`. |
| `app-cloud/.../EditVariableForm.test.tsx` | Dropped the redundant
`waitFor` wrapping a `findByRole` (the same query already follows);
assert visibility on it directly. |
| `app-cloud/.../StartFromAtemplate.test.tsx` | Dropped redundant
`waitFor`-wrapping-`findBy`; passed the timeout to `findByTestId`'s own
waitFor options. (Suite is `describe.skip`'d.) |
| `app-cloud/.../ImportAnExistingProject.test.tsx` | Dropped the
redundant `waitFor` wrapping `findByTestId`. (Suite is
`describe.skip`'d.) |

The two `describe.skip`'d suites don't run in CI and can't flake; they
were cleaned up for the same anti-pattern so they're correct if
re-enabled.

## Test Plan

- `ui-core`: ran `AssetTables` (5×), `AssetView` (3×), and
`BackfillLogsTab` (3×) under jest — all green; `BackfillLogsTab` now
fails correctly without the viewport mock, confirming it actually
asserts on rows.
- `app-cloud`: ran `AlertPolicyPage` and `EditVariableForm` (3×) —
green; the two skip'd suites verified via eslint + `tsgo`.
- `eslint` and `tsgo` clean on all changed files in both packages; `just
ruff` clean (no Python changed).

subject: chore(buildkite): remove unused Test Engine / quarantined-test plumbing (#24977)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

We no longer use Buildkite Test Engine, so this removes the dead
plumbing for it and for the associated quarantined-test management.
Nothing built or consumed these tokens/repos anymore.

Removed:

- **Pipeline builders** (`buildkite_shared` is the single source of
truth for both OSS and internal pipelines): the
`BUILDKITE_STEP_SUITE_SLUG` / `BUILDKITE_TEST_QUARANTINE_TOKEN` env-var
entries in `context.py`; the `BUILDKITE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` /
`BUILDKITE_TEST_QUARANTINE_TOKEN` / `BUILDKITE_TEST_SUITE_SLUG` Docker
passthrough; and the `INTERNAL_*` / `DOGFOOD_*` `*_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`
`secretKeyRef` injections in `command_step_builder.py` and in
`buildevents.py`'s honeycomb-trace step. The AI-assessment step's
Bedrock/API secrets are untouched.
- **Infra**: deleted the orphaned `buildkite-manage-quarantined-tests`
ECR repo + policy (`ecr.tf` — no Dockerfile or service ever built that
image) and removed its ARN from the buildkite `iam.tf`.
- **CI config**: the `DAGSTER_BUILDKITE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` passthrough in
`unit-tests.yaml`, and the `…_TEST_ANALYTICS_TOKEN=disabled` /
`…_TEST_SUITE_SLUG=disabled` lines in the public-buildkite env file.
- **Secrets**: `sops unset` of the 11 now-dead keys (quarantine token
plus the DAGSTER / INTERNAL / DOGFOOD analytics tokens and suite slugs)
from the `buildkite-eks` overlay, and the matching comment block in
`base/secrets.yaml`. The removed `secretKeyRef`s land in the same
change, so no pod ends up referencing a missing key.
- **Test + docs**: the `buildkite_test_collector` freezegun-ignore line
in `test_serverless_manager.py` (the still-used `freezegun` import
stays), the Test-Engine MCP-tool references in the `buildkite-expert`
agent, and the `buildkite-test-collector` mentions in the pytest-perf
skill.

Left in place deliberately: the generic `soft_fail` step primitive and
the dagster-open-platform `soft_failed` data-ingestion field (both are

subject: fix(dagster-aws): make ECS pipes interruption test robust under CI load (#24924)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

`test_ecs_pipes_interruption_forwarding` has been flaking on `internal`
builds when CI is under load (e.g.
https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152968,
https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152985), failing with
`KeyError: 0` at the final assertion.

Root cause is a race in the test itself, not a CI resource issue. The
test spawns a subprocess that runs `_materialize_asset`, then sleeps a
hardcoded 4 seconds before sending `SIGTERM` and asserting that the
subprocess populated `return_dict[0]` with the stopped ECS task state.
`return_dict[0]` is only written from a `finally` block, gated by
`assert len(pipes._client._task_runs) > 0`. Under load, Python startup +
`DagsterInstance.from_config()` + moto setup take longer than 4 seconds,
so the subprocess receives `SIGTERM` before `materialize()` has launched
the ECS task. The `finally`-block precondition fails, the child dies
without writing `return_dict[0]`, and the parent's assertion blows up.
The captured stderr in both failing builds shows the child died inside
`instance_for_test()` → `unified_storage = instance_ref.storage`, well
before any task was launched.

Replace the fixed sleep with an explicit "task launched" signal. The
child monkey-patches `mock_client.run_task` to set a
`multiprocessing.Event` as soon as `run_task` returns; the parent
`event.wait(timeout=60)` before sending `SIGTERM`, guaranteeing there is
a live ECS task to interrupt. The unbounded `while p.is_alive():
sleep(4); terminate()` retry loop is replaced with a single
`terminate()` + bounded `join(timeout=30)`.

## Test Plan

- `tox -e py312 -- -k test_ecs_pipes_interruption_forwarding` in
`python_modules/libraries/dagster-aws` (from `dagster-oss/`).
- Watch the dagster-aws step on this PR's Buildkite run; it should pass
without retries.

subject: fix(airlift): tolerate teardown race in airlift-migration-tutorial tests (#24976)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a flaky failure in `:pytest: airlift-migration-tutorial-3-10`
(e.g. [build
153251](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153251#019e6a15-ac03-41c9-ab53-9b0317e017c7)).
The tests themselves pass (`7 passed, 5 skipped`); the job fails in
**session-fixture teardown**:

```
Captured stderr teardown: rm: cannot remove '.../.airflow_home': Directory not empty
make: *** [Makefile:29: wipe] Error 1
ERROR test_proxy_operators.py::test_dag_override_operator
  - subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['make', 'wipe']' returned non-zero exit status 2.
```

(The error is attributed to `test_dag_override_operator` only because it
was the last test in the session — that's just where pytest hangs a
session-scoped finalizer error.)

The session-scoped `local_env` fixture ran `make wipe` (`rm -rf
$AIRFLOW_HOME $DAGSTER_HOME`) with `check=True` at teardown. Each
`test_*_loads` test stands up a full `airflow standalone` (scheduler +
gunicorn webserver + triggerer) writing into the persistent
`.airflow_home`, then SIGKILLs the process group. On a constrained CI
node a child can still be flushing writes when `rm` walks the tree, so
`rm` intermittently fails with `Directory not empty` and `check=True`
turns that into a build failure.

This is a known dagster-airlift flake class. The *shared* `airflow_home`
fixture already documents and tolerates this exact race
(`shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)`, added in #24625 and #23351),
but the tutorial example's own teardown path was never hardened.

## Changes

- **`conftest.py`** — replace the `make wipe` teardown call with a
tolerant Python cleanup (`shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True)` over
`.airflow_home` and `.dagster_home`), mirroring the shared
`airflow_home` fixture. The `make wipe` target is left untouched (still
used at session setup and as a documented tutorial command, where
failing loudly is desirable).
- **`utils.py`** — bump the Airflow-run poll timeout in
`start_run_and_wait_for_completion` from 30s to 60s, matching the
kitchen-sink polling fixes (#22472) for slow CI. This helper is
currently only exercised by the e2e tests, which remain
`@pytest.mark.skip(reason="Flakiness, @benpankow to investigate")`; the
bump is latent but addresses the same bug class.

## Test plan

- `airlift-migration-tutorial-3-10` passes on Buildkite without the
teardown error.
- Ruff clean (`ruff 0.15.13`).

subject: Fix JS tox step CWD regression and openlineage docs prettier (#24978)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Two master-red fixes, bundled at request.

**1. `admin-cloud` lint failure — JS tox step CWD regression from
#24923.** #24923 unified the internal and OSS tox-step factories into
`buildkite_shared.tox.build_tox_step`. The shared factory assembles
commands as `[*extra_commands_pre, "cd {directory}", …, tox]` — it runs
`extra_commands_pre` from the repo root, *before* `cd`-ing into the
package directory (the OSS convention). The internal JS steps
(`app-cloud`, `login-app`, `admin-cloud`) were written for the *old*
internal convention where `cd {directory}` ran first, so their `pushd
../../..` (intended: package dir → repo root) overshot from the repo
root all the way to `/`. The "install the root yarn workspace" step
became a silent no-op — corepack fell back to yarn 1.22.22 at `/`, found
no lockfile, and finished in 0.1s.

Only `admin-cloud` broke. It's a standalone yarn project (its own
`.yarnrc.yml` + `yarn.lock`) and pulls in `@dagster-io/eslint-config`
via `link:`, which does not install that package's transitive deps. So
`eslint-config-prettier` is only resolvable when the *root* workspace
was installed — which it wasn't — and `yarn lint` failed with `Cannot
find module 'eslint-config-prettier'`. `app-cloud`/`login-app` are
root-workspace members, so their in-tox `yarn install` resolved the root
workspace anyway and masked the bug.

Fix: target the repo root explicitly via
`$BUILDKITE_BUILD_CHECKOUT_PATH` (the same escaping/pattern the
app-cloud backcompat steps in this file already use) instead of the
CWD-relative `../../..`, and run `admin-cloud`'s `yarn -v` pre-download
inside its own directory. The shared factory is left untouched, so OSS
steps — whose `extra_commands_pre` are already repo-root-relative
(`pushd {oss_path(...)}`) — are unaffected.

**2. `build-docs` prettier failure.** The markdown table in
`dagster-oss/docs/docs/integrations/libraries/openlineage.md` (added in
#33854) wasn't column-aligned and failed `yarn lint-check`. Reformatted
to satisfy prettier.

## Test Plan

- Rendered the `admin-cloud` step and confirmed the command order:
`corepack enable` → `pushd $BUILDKITE_BUILD_CHECKOUT_PATH` → `yarn` →
`popd` → `pushd
$BUILDKITE_BUILD_CHECKOUT_PATH/dagster-cloud/js_modules/admin-cloud` →
`yarn -v` → `popd` → `cd dagster-cloud/js_modules/admin-cloud` → `tox`.
The balanced `pushd`/`popd` leaves CWD at the repo root, so the
factory's relative `cd {directory}` still resolves.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on the edited step file.
- `prettier --check` clean on `openlineage.md` after the reformat; the
diff touches only the table.
- Relying on Buildkite on this PR to confirm `admin-cloud-default-3-12`
and `build-docs` go green.

## Changelog

NOCHANGELOG

subject: Use parameterized ClickHouse partition queries (#24777)
body:
## Summary

Fixes ClickHouse static partition query generation to use
`clickhouse-driver` parameter binding instead of interpolating partition
key values into SQL literals.

This updates:
- `ClickhouseDbClient.delete_table_slice()` to pass params to
`connection.execute(...)`
- ClickHouse SELECT generation to expose `(query, params)` via
`get_select_statement_and_params()`
- pandas and polars ClickHouse type handlers to pass params through
`query_dataframe(...)`
- SQL unit coverage for single quotes and backslash-quote payloads in
partition keys

Identifiers are still quoted via `_quote_ident`; dynamic partition
values are now passed as driver parameters.

## Test plan

```bash
cd dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-clickhouse
uvx --with tox-uv tox -q -- dagster_clickhouse_tests/test_db_client_sql.py

cd dagster-oss
uvx ruff check python_modules/libraries/dagster-clickhouse/dagster_clickhouse/db_client.py \
```

subject: ci(buildkite): mount /var/lib/docker as dedicated emptyDir on dind sidecar (#24947)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Targets the disk-I/O-contention hypothesis behind the persistent 60s
`UnixHTTPConnectionPool` ReadTimeouts on `dagster-docker-3-12` (and the
related signature on `dagster-celery-docker-3-12`), after the CPU bump
in [#24902](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24902) and the
memory-limit bump in
[#24936](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24936) failed to
eliminate the pattern. Build
[153109](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153109) — the
merge commit of #24936 itself — still produced
`requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: UnixHTTPConnectionPool ... read
timeout=60` on `containers.create`, proving the bottleneck wasn't CPU or
memory.

The diagnostic probe in
[#24946](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24946) (still
un-merged) further showed that the EKS dind sidecars are already running
on the containerd image store (`Storage Driver: overlayfs`,
`driver-type: io.containerd.snapshotter.v1`), not the legacy overlay2
graphdriver — so dockerd lock-contention from the legacy driver was
already off the table.

That leaves disk I/O on `/var/lib/docker` as the leading hypothesis.
Today the dind sidecar mounts only `/var/run` and `/tmp` as dedicated
emptyDirs; `/var/lib/docker` (where dockerd writes image snapshots,
layers, and container state) falls through to the dind container's
writable layer on the node's overlay filesystem. That filesystem is
shared at the kernel level with every co-resident pod's writable layer
on the same node, so heavy snapshot/layer ops serialize at the FS layer
— and dockerd holds its internal locks across that serialization, which
is exactly the shape of a 60s blocked `containers.create` call under
burst load (e.g. the docker step-health-retry loop in
`test_docker_executor_check_step_health`).

## Change

Adds a `docker-data` `emptyDir` (`sizeLimit: 10Gi`) and mounts it at
`/var/lib/docker` on every EKS dind sidecar in
`dagster-oss/.buildkite/buildkite-shared/buildkite_shared/step_builders/command_step_builder.py`.
Two locations:

- Inline `volumeMounts` entry on the dind sidecar spec.
- `self._k8s_volumes.append(...)` to declare the pod-level emptyDir.

The main test container does **not** get the mount — it has no reason to
see dockerd's internal storage.

## Cost

Minimal:
- ~10Gi of ephemeral storage reservation per dind-using job pod.
Buildkite-eks Karpenter nodes have ~300Gi data disks per the
dockerhub-mirror.yaml topology notes — room for ~30 dind pods per node
before Karpenter scales out.
- **Zero memory cost** — disk-backed, not tmpfs, so the 8Gi
`docker_memory_limit` from #24936 is untouched.
- No code complexity, no change to `PackageSpec`, no `packages.py`
changes.
- Applies globally to every `.with_docker()` EKS step. Benign for jobs
that don't push much through dind.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR.
- [ ] Watch the next ~10 master builds post-merge. `dagster-docker-3-12`
and `dagster-celery-docker-3-12` should stop producing the 60s
`UnixHTTPConnectionPool` ReadTimeout signature.
- [ ] Spot-check kubelet eviction count via Datadog over the same window
— `emptyDir` sizeLimit triggers pod eviction if exceeded. 10Gi is
comfortable headroom for the test-project image (~2-3Gi) plus scratch.
- [ ] If the signature persists after this: the next candidates are CPU
throttling at the cgroup level (despite `docker_cpu=4000m` request, no
limit) and test-side concurrency burst overwhelming the daemon
regardless. Both are higher-effort to diagnose — the diagnostic probe
from #24946 could be extended to capture cgroup CPU stats per-job if
needed.

## Changelog

NOCHANGELOG

---------

subject: ci(buildkite): bump airlift EKS pods to 4 vCPU to fix SQLite lock (#24970)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

#24950 migrated `examples/airlift-federation-tutorial` and
`python_modules/libraries/dagster-airlift/kitchen-sink` off the DOCKER
queue (a dedicated c5.xlarge — 4 vCPU) to `KUBERNETES_EKS` with
`cpu=2000m`. That halving broke the federation tutorial on the first
master build to actually run it (build 153210): the two host-process
`airflow standalone` stacks plus `dagster dev` share a single pod, and
on 2 vCPU the SQLite metadata-DB writers starved. The scheduler's
`DagFileProcessor` crashed with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is
locked`, the triggered dag run never progressed, and `test_load_metrics`
failed with `Timed out waiting for airflow run … to finish`.

These jobs only run post-merge on master
(`force_run_fn=has_dagster_airlift_changes`, and #24950 touched only
`packages.py`), so the regression wasn't visible on that PR's own CI.

This bumps both packages back to `cpu=4000m`, matching the c5.xlarge
sizing they ran on before the migration. kitchen-sink runs one airflow
stack per split (`splits=2`) but carries the same SQLite-lock risk, so
it gets the same treatment. Memory is unchanged (no OOM was observed;
airlift stays at 6Gi, kitchen-sink at 4Gi).

## Test Plan

CI on this PR. Because it edits `packages.py`, the build re-runs the
migrated airlift jobs (and the rest of the suite): confirm
`airlift-federation-tutorial-3-10` and the `dagster-airlift
kitchen-sink` splits complete within their timeouts on the 4 vCPU
budget, with no `database is locked` in the scheduler logs.

## Changelog

Not user-facing (CI / Buildkite only).

subject: test: add @pytest.mark.quarantined plugin for flaky-test isolation (#24956)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Add a `@pytest.mark.quarantined` mark + tiny pytest plugin (`dagster._utils.test.quarantine`) so chronically flaky tests can be pulled out of their existing suites without deleting them or per-tox-env edits.

Behavior:

- `RUN_QUARANTINED` unset (default): every test carrying `@pytest.mark.quarantined` is skipped — it vanishes from whatever suite it lives in.
- `RUN_QUARANTINED=1` / `true` / `yes` (case-insensitive): inverts; non-quarantined tests are deselected so the invocation runs only quarantined tests. This is what a future "flakes" meta-suite uses to aggregate quarantined tests across packages.

The mark vanishes from existing suites with no per-env work because the plugin auto-loads in every pytest invocation under the rootdir (registered via `pytest_plugins` in `dagster-oss/conftest.py`, re-exported from the internal repo's root `conftest.py`).

Scoping: deliberately chose `pytest_plugins` in the rootdir conftest over a `pytest11` entry point on the dagster distribution, so downstream users who `pip install dagster` and run their own pytest suite don't accidentally inherit the mark. The registration is guarded on `importlib.util.find_spec("dagster")` so test envs under the rootdir that don't install dagster (e.g. `.buildkite/dagster-internal-buildkite/`) don't crash on conftest load.

The Buildkite fan-out that actually runs quarantined tests as a soft-fail meta-suite is a follow-up PR stacked on this one.

## Test Plan

12 pytester-based tests in `dagster_tests/utils_tests/test_quarantine.py` covering:

- `RUN_QUARANTINED` unset → quarantined tests get `SKIPPED`, others pass/fail normally.
- `RUN_QUARANTINED=1` → quarantined tests run, others get `deselected`.
- Parametrized truthy/falsy env values (`1`/`true`/`TRUE`/`yes`/`Yes` and `""`/`0`/`false`/`no`).
- `--strict-markers` accepts the registered `quarantined` marker.

Also manually verified end-to-end from inside both `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/` and `internal/python_modules/automation-internal/` that the marker is auto-recognized without explicit `-p` flag, in both modes.

subject: ci(buildkite): migrate remaining OSS DOCKER-queue packages to KUBERNETES_EKS (#24950)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Migrates the remaining DOCKER-queue OSS packages off
`buildkite-docker-october22` (c5.xlarge, single-tenant) to
`KUBERNETES_EKS`, following #24373 which moved the three kind suites.
After this lands the DOCKER queue has zero remaining OSS callers
(internal-repo pipelines still use it for release / canary / cloud-suite
plumbing).

| Package | Workload | Resources |
| ------- | -------- | --------- |
| `examples/airlift-federation-tutorial` | 2 host-process airflow
instances + dagster (no docker access) | `cpu=2000m, memory=6Gi`; dind
defaults |
| `python_modules/libraries/dagster-airlift/kitchen-sink` | 1 airflow +
dagster per split (`splits=2`) | `cpu=2000m, memory=4Gi`; dind defaults
|
| `python_modules/libraries/dagster-clickhouse{,-pandas,-polars}` |
`clickhouse-server` in dind via testcontainers | shared
`_CLICKHOUSE_TESTCONTAINERS_RESOURCES`: `cpu=1000m, memory=1Gi,
docker_memory=2Gi, docker_memory_limit=4Gi` |

## Resource sizing

The two airlift tutorials run airflow + dagster as host subprocesses
(see ``airlift_federation_tutorial_tests/conftest.py`` and
``kitchen-sink/kitchen_sink_tests/integration_tests/conftest.py``), so
the dind sidecar that ``build_tox_step`` unconditionally attaches is
idle — the constraint is main-container memory, not dind. The federation
tutorial's existing in-tree comment ("use docker queue to ensure beefier
instance") points at the same conclusion: it needed ``c5.xlarge``-class
room for two airflows, not docker access. 6 Gi covers two
scheduler+webserver+sqlite stacks plus dagster headroom; kitchen-sink
halves the per-pod budget because ``splits=2`` means one airflow per
pod.

The clickhouse trio uses testcontainers to spin up
``clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.8`` inside dind, so the work moves
into the sidecar. The shared preset bumps ``docker_memory_limit`` to 4
Gi — same shape as the dagster-test fixtures bump from #24661 and the
airbyte integration bump already in this file. Pulls of the clickhouse
image route through the EKS-level
``dockerhub-mirror.buildkite-agent.svc.cluster.local:5000``
automatically: the dind sidecar is launched with ``--registry-mirror``
pointing at it on the EKS queue (``command_step_builder.py``), so no
per-package wiring is needed. None of the five packages talk to AWS
APIs, so no IRSA ``aws configure export-credentials`` shim is required
(unlike the kind suites in #24373).

## Test Plan

- [x] `tox -e py312` in `dagster-oss/.buildkite/dagster-buildkite` — all
12 buildkite pipeline-generation tests pass, including
`test_dagster_produces_valid_yaml`.

complete inside their existing timeouts (30 min for federation, default
for kitchen-sink) on the new pod budget.
- [ ] CI on this PR: clickhouse trio's testcontainers can reach the dind
socket and pull `clickhouse-server:24.8` through the dockerhub mirror
without rate-limit flakes.

subject: dagster-airlift: support Python 3.12-3.14 (#24828)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Lifts the `requires-python` cap on `dagster-airlift` from `<3.12` to
`<3.15`, and enables Buildkite testing on Python 3.12 and 3.14.
Previously the package was capped at `<3.12` because the airflow 2.x
line (`apache-airflow==2.9.3`) was the only one wired up. The package
now installs and tests against the airflow 3.x line (3.2.x) on 3.12+.

The Buildkite spec for `dagster-airlift` previously listed
3.12/3.13/3.14 as unsupported with the comment `# airflow`. That list is
removed — the package now exercises the default `get_all()` rotation
(3.10, 3.12, 3.14). 3.10/3.11 keep using airflow 2.9.3 via conditional
markers; 3.12+ uses airflow 3.x.

Also bundles a fix for an airlift master flake unrelated to the cap lift
(`test_dagster_operator`, "Never reached terminal status") since it
touches the same files.

## Changes

### `python_modules/libraries/dagster-airlift/pyproject.toml`

- `requires-python` lifted from `>=3.10,<3.12` to `>=3.10,<3.15`.
- `apache-airflow` constraint on `python_version >= '3.12'` tightened
from `>=2.9.0` to `>=3.0.0` (airflow 2.x doesn't support 3.12+; the old
lower bound was misleading).
- Airflow-2.x-only constraints (`flask-session<0.6.0`,
`connexion<3.0.0`, `fastapi<0.118`) gated on `python_version < '3.12'`.
On 3.12+, airflow 3.x's own metadata pins these to compatible versions
naturally, so an unconditional cap was actively preventing airflow 3.x's
required `fastapi>=0.116` from resolving.
- `dagster-dbt==1!0+dev` and `dbt-duckdb` in the `test` extra gated on
`python_version < '3.14'`. `dagster-dbt` has `requires-python =
">=3.10,<3.14"` (dbt-core blocks 3.14), so an unconditional pin would
break test-extra resolution on 3.14. The airlift tests don't actually
import `dagster_dbt` — references are string-only — so dropping it on
3.14 is safe.

### Test DAGs: `schedule_interval=` → `schedule=`

The `schedule_interval` kwarg on `DAG()` was removed in airflow 3.x
(renamed to `schedule` in 2.4; the alias has now been dropped). Renamed
across `conftest.py`, `integration_tests/dags/simple_dag.py`,
`materialize_assets_operator_test_project/dags/dag.py`,
`scaffold_test_airflow_home/airflow_dags/dags.py`,
`operator_test_project/dags/migrated_dag.py`, and
`mwaa_integration_tests/airflow_project/simple_dag.py`. `schedule=` is
accepted on 2.9.3 too, so this works on both branches.

### Integration test poll loop (unrelated master flake)

`test_proxy_task_operator.py::test_dagster_operator` and
`test_materialize_assets_operator.py::test_dagster_operator` had a
30-second inline `while get_current_timestamp() - start_time < 30:`
deadline to observe a dag run reaching terminal status. After
cold-starting `airflow standalone` + `dagster dev` + queuing +
executing, that budget is too tight; the test recently flaked on master
([build
152664](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152664#019e50f4-8d88-45c1-9c51-6b07c7195cc2))
on 3.10 with airflow 2.9.3 — independent of this PR.

Replaced the inline deadline with a `while True:` poll loop and a
`@pytest.mark.timeout(180)` safety net (pytest-timeout is already a test
dep). This separates "I observed a non-success terminal state"
(assertion failure with the actual state) from "the run never reached
terminal" (pytest-timeout kills the test with a clear timeout message).
Resources are not the bottleneck (the package is on
`BuildkiteQueue.MEDIUM` and doesn't use dind), so this is purely a
wall-clock-budget fix.

### `.buildkite/dagster-buildkite/dagster_buildkite/steps/packages.py`

- Removed the `unsupported_python_versions=[V3_12, V3_13, V3_14]` list
from the `dagster-airlift` `PackageSpec` so the package tests on the
default `[3.10, 3.12, 3.14]` rotation.

### `python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml`

- Dropped the `fsspec<2024.5.0` pin from `dagster[test]`. This was added
in May 2024 (dagster-io/dagster#21874) to work around a
`morefs.asyn_local` incompatibility: fsspec 2024.5.0 renamed
`LocalFileSystem.mv_file` to `mv`, which broke
`morefs.asyn_local.AsyncLocalFileSystem`'s class-time reference.
**morefs 0.2.1 (June 2024) added explicit handling** (`_mv =
wrap(getattr(LocalFileSystem, "mv", None) or LocalFileSystem.mv_file)`),
and the current lock already uses morefs 0.2.2. Keeping the pin was
transitively preventing airflow 3.2.x from being installable, because
airflow 3.2.x → `universal-pathlib>=0.3.8` → `fsspec>=2024.5.0`. Without
lifting this pin, 3.14 testing for `dagster-airlift` would have been
blocked indefinitely.

### Lockfiles

Both `python_modules/dagster/uv.lock` and
`python_modules/libraries/dagster-airlift/uv.lock` regenerated via
`dagster-oss/scripts/update_lockfiles.py`. Notable bumps:

- `fsspec`: 2024.3.0 → 2026.4.0 (in both locks)
- `apache-airflow` (airlift, 3.12+ branch): 3.1.8 → 3.2.1
- `apache-airflow-task-sdk`: 1.1.8 → 1.2.1
- `fastapi` (airlift, 3.12+ branch): 0.117.1 → 0.136.1
- `universal-pathlib`: 0.2.6 → 0.3.10

## Test Plan

- Dependency resolution verified locally with `uv sync --extra test
--extra core --extra in-airflow --extra tutorial --extra mwaa --group
test --python <ver> --frozen --dry-run` on 3.10, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14. All
resolve. 3.10 picks airflow 2.9.3; 3.12/3.13/3.14 pick airflow 3.2.1.
- Buildkite CI on this PR will run the `dagster-airlift` tox suite on
3.10/3.12/3.14. Some integration tests may still need airflow 3.x
API/auth migration (the `/api/v1` calls in `airflow_instance.py`,
basic_auth backend); CI will surface what's left.

## Changelog

[dagster-airlift] Now supports Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.

subject: buildkite: re-roll with_env() without the docker-config leak (#24907)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Re-rolls [#24834](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24834),
reverted in [#24895](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24895)
to unblock master.

**Root cause of the original regression:** #24834's k8s branch of
`CommandStepBuilder.build()` auto-promoted every `KEY=value` entry from
`_docker_settings["environment"]` into the pod's container env. That
list is populated by `with_ecr_passthru()` (called on every pytest step
from `tox.py`), which adds `DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/.docker`. On the docker
queue this is fine: the docker plugin bind-mounts the host's auth blob
into the container at `/tmp/.docker/config.json` and `DOCKER_CONFIG`
redirects Docker CLI there. On EKS pods that volume mount doesn't exist
— ECR auth flows through the `ecr-docker-login` initContainer writing
`/work/.docker/config.json` and Docker CLI finding it via `HOME=/work`.
Setting `DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/.docker` in the pod env points Docker CLI at
a non-existent path, and every `docker compose up` fails with
`authorization failed: no basic auth credentials`. Build
[152887](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152887) — the
first build with #24834 — saw 32 EKS pytest jobs fail in this exact
pattern (cloud-admin-panel, all backend splits, ursula, all dagit
splits, agent-tests, e2e, etc.).

**This re-roll:**

- Adds `CommandStepBuilder.with_env(env_vars: dict[str, str])` as the
queue-agnostic source of truth for concrete per-step env vars.
- On k8s: appends `_env` entries to `podSpec.containers[0].env`.
**Intentionally does NOT** iterate `_docker_settings["environment"]` —
that list holds docker-plugin-specific settings (e.g.
`DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/.docker`) that have no meaning on k8s and actively
break ECR auth here.
- On docker: appends `_env` entries to the docker plugin's `environment`
list as `KEY=value`. Also uses `setdefault("environment", [])` so
`on_specific_image` callers that don't pass an environment list don't
`KeyError`.
- On both queues: `SM_PLUGIN` is appended when `_secrets` is non-empty
(`setdefault("plugins", [])` on the k8s side as a defensive guard for
the unusual case of `_secrets` without `_docker_settings`).
- Migrates `cypress_test_login` from
`extra_docker_plugin_args={"environment": [KEY=value, ...]}` to
`.with_env({"KEY": "value", ...})` + `.with_secret(...)`. This is the
step #24834 was originally trying to fix on EKS.
- Migrates two `docs.py` steps from
`on_test_image(env=["COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0"])` to
`on_test_image().with_env({"COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT": "0"})`.
The legacy `env=[...]` parameter is now bare-name-passthrough-only;
`KEY=value` entries belong in `with_env({...})`.

## Test Plan

- [x] **Byte-identical rendered output for pytest steps:** locally
rendered a `cloud-admin-panel`-shaped step
(`on_test_image("3.12").with_docker().with_ecr_passthru()`) against
pre-#24834 master and against this branch. `diff` is empty — no
`DOCKER_CONFIG` leak, no `PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT` leak in the pod env.
This is the EKS regression fix.
- [x] **`with_env({...})` threads through both queues:** a step with
`.with_env({"FOO": "bar", "BAZ": "qux"})` renders `FOO`/`BAZ` into
`podSpec.containers[0].env` on k8s and as `FOO=bar`/`BAZ=qux` in the
docker plugin's `environment` list on docker.
- [x] **`with_secret(...)` triggers SM_PLUGIN on both queues:** appears
as a sibling plugin alongside `kubernetes` on k8s and alongside `docker`
on docker.
- [ ] **`[NO_SKIP]` in subject** so full CI exercises every EKS-routed
pytest step — the regression cohort from build 152887.
- [ ] **dogfood cypress-login on EKS** — the step this PR was originally
trying to fix. (Not exercised by the internal pipeline; verifiable on
dogfood post-merge.)

## Summary & Motivation

This PR changes three things about the selection inputs:

- They now use the default instead of the monospace font. This matches
the presentation of asset keys in the Catalog and makes the placeholder
state in particular look less out of place.

- Items in selection autocomplete use 14pt font. (Matching the design
mocks in
https://dagsterlabs.slack.com/archives/C03CCE471E0/p1778874131599029?thread_ts=1778874013.194079&cid=C03CCE471E0)

- Focus on this element was actually a bit awkward:
+ Clicking the Search icon focused the wrapper, not the text element and
showed a blue outline
+ Clicking the Search text focused the text, but there is no blue
outline!

the container into the input. The CSS for focus was changed to
focus-within, which allows the blue border to appear when Codemirror's
input is focused.

subject: Refactor backend-supported asset selection filters to use allowlist (#24179)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes
https://linear.app/dagster-labs/issue/FE-1127/asset-selection-syntax-misalignment-with-backend-implementation
- my new filters didn't work on the `insights` tab of the asset catalog,
because I forgot to add them to a "backend_unsupported" array.

Refactored the `BackendUnsupportedSelectionVisitor` to use an
allowlist-based approach for determining which asset selection filters
can be resolved by the Insights backend. Previously, the code explicitly
listed unsupported filters (column, column_tag, table_name, status,
changed_in_branch) with individual visitor methods. This approach was
fragile—new filters would default to "supported" unless explicitly added
to the unsupported list.

The new implementation inverts this logic: only filters explicitly in
`BACKEND_SUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTE_EXPR_TYPES` are treated as
backend-supported. All other filters (including future ones)
automatically fall back to client-side resolution. This is safer and
more maintainable.

**Key changes:**
- Replaced individual `visitColumnAttributeExpr`,
`visitTableNameAttributeExpr`, etc. methods with a single
`visitAttributeExpression` method that checks against the allowlist
- Created `BACKEND_SUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTE_EXPR_TYPES` constant listing only
filters that have `resolve_inner` implemented in the backend's
`AssetSelection` subclasses
- Added comprehensive documentation in the grammar README explaining the
workflow for adding new filters
- Updated the test suite to use parameterized tests (`it.each`) for
better coverage and maintainability
- Added tests for composition (AND/OR expressions) and traversal
operators

## Test Plan

Existing and new unit tests in
`BackendUnsupportedSelectionVisitor.test.ts` cover:
- All currently unsupported filters (column, column_tag, table_name,
status, changed_in_branch, automation_type, sensor, schedule, job)
- All currently supported filters (key, code_location, group, kind,
owner, tag, partitions)
- Composition scenarios (OR/AND with mixed supported/unsupported
branches)
- Traversal operators around supported and unsupported filters

## Changelog

Internal refactoring to improve maintainability of asset selection
filter validation. No user-facing changes.

Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

8.20.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed an uninitialized memory disclosure issue in websocket.close() (c0327ec1).

Providing a TypedArray (e.g. Float32Array) as the reason argument for websocket.close(), rather than the supported string or Buffer types, caused uninitialized memory to be disclosed to the remote peer.

import { deepStrictEqual } from 'node:assert';
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws';

const wss = new WebSocketServer(
{ port: 0, skipUTF8Validation: true },
function () {
const { port } = wss.address();
const ws = new WebSocket(ws://localhost:${port}, {
skipUTF8Validation: true
});


ws.on('close', function (code, reason) {
  deepStrictEqual(reason, Buffer.alloc(80));
});



}
);


wss.on('connection', function (ws) {
ws.close(1000, new Float32Array(20));
});

The issue was privately reported by Nikita Skovoroda.

subject: ci(buildkite): bump dind memory_limit to 8Gi + airbyte test startup timeout (#24936)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Two flake fixes in one PR, both observed on master in the post-#24902
window (16:48 UTC onward on 2026-05-26).

### 1. `docker_memory_limit` 4Gi → 8Gi for `dagster-docker` and
`dagster-celery-docker`

Continuation of the
[#24779](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24779) →
[#24902](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24902) escalation
ladder. The `docker_cpu=4000m` bump in #24902 did not eliminate the 60s
`UnixHTTPConnectionPool` ReadTimeouts. Across the first 5 settled master
builds after #24902 merged, the signature recurred 4 times (~44% rate):

- [152968](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152968) —
`dagster-celery-docker-3-12`: `Failed: Timeout (>240.0s) from
pytest-timeout` + `ReadTimeoutError("UnixHTTPConnectionPool ... read
timeout=60")` (the exact signature #24902 cited in its description, on
the very first build off the merge commit)
- [152985](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152985) —
`dagster-docker-3-12`: multiple `requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout:
UnixHTTPConnectionPool ... read timeout=60`
- [153001](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153001) —
`dagster-docker-3-12`: `test_launch_docker_no_network` ReadTimeout +
cascading `test_recovery` poll timeout
- [153056](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153056) —
`dagster-docker-3-12`: `test_docker_executor_job_that_fails_run_worker`
asserts False because the captured run event stream contains
`UnixHTTPConnectionPool` ReadTimeout events the test didn't expect

#24902's test plan pre-committed to this exact next step:

> If they do persist past this, the next escalation is bumping
`docker_memory_limit` (rate-limited pulls and concurrent decompression
both pressure memory under faster CPU) or splitting the celery test into
its own queue with higher headroom.

Both packages share identical resource shape and identical observed
failure mode, so they get bumped together (consistent with how they were
paired in #24779 and #24902).

### 2. `STARTUP_TIME_SEC` 120 → 240 in `dagster-airbyte`
`test_managed_elements.py`

Separate root cause from #1: `dagster-airbyte-integration-3-12` saw the
module-scoped `docker_compose_airbyte_instance` fixture time out polling
Airbyte's `POST /api/v1/workspaces/list` for 200, then cascade as 4
ERRORs across the tests sharing it. Same signature on
[152985](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152985) (16:50
UTC) and [153062](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/153062)
(19:01 UTC); `pytest-rerunfailures` retries also failed.

dagster-airbyte's dind sidecar is already at `cpu=4000m, memory=4Gi,
memory_limit=6Gi` (#23997), so this is not outer-dind saturation. The
bottleneck is the **inner** Airbyte stack — webapp + server + scheduler
+ worker + db + temporal — cold-starting under EKS contention within a
120s budget. Temporal especially is a known slow starter. Bumping to
240s; pytest-timeout is 600s and the recent failing sessions ran
256-278s, so there is plenty of headroom.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR.
- [ ] Watch the next ~10 master builds. `dagster-docker-3-12` and
`dagster-celery-docker-3-12` should stop producing 60s
`UnixHTTPConnectionPool` ReadTimeouts;
`dagster-airbyte-integration-3-12` should stop producing the `Airbyte
instance failed to start in time` cascade.
- [ ] If the dind ReadTimeouts still persist past 8Gi: next escalation
per #24902's plan is splitting celery into its own queue with higher
headroom (e.g. `queue=BuildkiteQueue.DOCKER`).
- [ ] If the airbyte fixture still fires the timeout: add per-container
readiness diagnostics inside the polling loop so we can see which
Airbyte container is the slowpoke.

## Changelog

NOCHANGELOG

subject: enable ty on dagster_graphql/implementation and fix surfaced type errors (#24912)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Enables ty on `dagster_graphql/implementation` (previously excluded due
to a ty 0.0.35 runaway-memory bug that has since been resolved) and
fixes the 237 diagnostics that surfaced.

### ty config

Extends the existing Graphene metaclass override in
`dagster-oss/ty/master/pyproject.toml` to also cover
`dagster_graphql/implementation/**`. The same Graphene
`__init__`-from-class-body-fields pattern that motivated the schema
override applies here, so the same rules are suppressed
(`unknown-argument`, `unresolved-attribute`, `invalid-argument-type`,
`not-subscriptable`), plus `too-many-positional-arguments` which is the
positional-arg variant of the same metaclass issue. This knocks ~225
diagnostics down to 12 real bugs.

### Real bugs fixed

- **Redundant casts removed** in `execution/backfill.py` (×2) and
`execution/launch_execution.py` — `AssetKey.from_graphql_input` already
returns `AssetKey`, and `parent_run` is already `DagsterRun`.
- **Return-type annotations widened** to cover the error/migration
variants actually returned by the function:
`terminate_pipeline_execution`,
`fetch_asset_condition_evaluation_records_for_asset_key`,
`fetch_asset_condition_evaluation_records_for_evaluation_id`,
`get_backfill`, `get_utilized_env_vars_or_error`,
`partition_statuses_from_run_partition_data` /
`get_partition_set_partition_statuses`, `get_run_group`,
`resolve_run_config_schema_or_error`. These all had annotations that
named only the happy-path Graphene type while the implementation also
returned `*NotFoundError` or `*NeedsMigrationError` variants.
- **`entity_key_from_graphql_input`** in
`fetch_asset_condition_evaluations.py` used `"path" in graphene_input`
on a value typed as a Graphene `InputObjectType`. At runtime
graphql-core delivers `InputObjectType` values to resolvers as plain
dicts, so the `in` check works — but the static type doesn't admit it.
Resolved by casting to `Mapping[str, Any]` with a comment explaining the
runtime contract.

## Test Plan

`just ty` reports 0 errors, 0 warnings (was 237 errors when
implementation was first un-excluded). `just ruff` clean.

subject: Make flaky test signatures more robust (#24910)
body:
## Summary

Bundles four targeted fixes for flaky-test signatures hit on master
(builds 152935 and 152941). All are root-cause fixes (no auto-retries,
no `pytest-rerunfailures` tags).

### 1. `dagster-cloud-worker` SIGSEGV at `test_send_events` teardown

`workers/confluent.py` and `workers/kafka.py` cancel their
consume/background tasks at lifespan exit but don't await them before
calling `consumer.close()` / `consumer.stop()`. The cancelled task can
still be mid-`consumer.poll()` in an `asyncio.to_thread` worker, racing
librdkafka cleanup and segfaulting the interpreter. Fix: `await
asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` after cancellation, before
close.

### 2. `backcompat-test-suite` 20s run-launch timeout

`MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20` in `tests/test_backcompat.py` is too tight
for the earliest-tested-release user-code container under Buildkite
resource pressure (cold-start has been observed >30s). Bumped to 120s.

Note: the other docker-heavy integration suites (`celery-k8s`, `k8s`)
use `queue=BuildkiteQueue.DOCKER` for additional resources. Backcompat
does not. Moving backcompat to that queue is a reasonable follow-up if
the timing bump alone proves insufficient.

### 3. Engine-tests `OSError: [Errno 39] Directory not empty` at
teardown

`engine_tests/conftest.py`'s `instance` fixture uses
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`. Multiprocess executor subprocesses are
still flushing files into `temp_dir` when the fixture tears down, racing
`rmtree`. Added `ignore_cleanup_errors=True`.

### 4. `dagstermill::test_reexecute_result_notebook` brittle
full-notebook diff

The test compared a re-executed notebook against the on-disk original,
only stripping `metadata.execution`. Cell outputs (warning streams) and
`papermill` metadata (timestamps) are not deterministic across runs.
Replaced with a structural source-only comparison;
`ExecutePreprocessor.preprocess()` already raises on any cell failure,
which is the property under test.

## Test plan
- [ ] Buildkite green on this PR
- [ ] Subsequent master builds no longer surface the four signatures

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

subject: ci(buildkite): bump dind cpu to 4000m for dagster-docker, dagster-celery-docker (#24902)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #24779 that I flagged in that PR's test plan: *"if 60s
UnixHTTPConnectionPool ReadTimeouts persist after this lands, bump
docker_cpu to 4000m (precedent: the dagster-airbyte integration bump)."*
They have persisted. The exact same signature
(`docker.errors.ImageNotFound` + `urllib3.exceptions.ReadTimeoutError:
UnixHTTPConnectionPool ... Read timed out (read timeout=60)` +
pytest-timeout at 240s) is firing on `dagster-celery-docker-3-12` across
builds [152905](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152905),
[152906](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152906),
[152907](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152907),
[152912](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152912). The
upstream `:docker: test-project-3-12` step succeeded in those builds —
the image is in ECR — so the 404 is a side-effect of dind giving up
mid-pull rather than a real missing-image / auth problem.

`dagster-docker` shares the saturation shape (same `test-project` pulls,
same dind sidecar profile), so it gets the same bump in this PR.

## Change

Add `docker_cpu="4000m"` to the `ResourceRequests` for the
`dagster-celery-docker` and `dagster-docker` `PackageSpec` entries in
`dagster-oss/.buildkite/dagster-buildkite/dagster_buildkite/steps/packages.py`.
Memory limits (`docker_memory=2Gi`, `docker_memory_limit=4Gi`) and
main-pod sizing are unchanged. Same shape as the dagster-airbyte
integration bump in #23997, which uses cpu=4000m, memory=4Gi,
memory_limit=6Gi — I'm keeping the memory tier from #24779 since the
symptom we're seeing is pull-rate starvation, not OOM.

Also tightened the existing comments to point at this PR's evidence
rather than the now-stale "default 2Gi / 2000m" wording (those defaults
haven't been the active state since #24779).

## Not changed

- `dagster-test` (line 956) keeps its current sizing. That bump in
#24779 was for a different symptom (90s compose-down timeouts in
`fixtures_tests`), and there's no recent recurrence in the builds I
sampled.
- `dagster-mysql` (line 1310) is unrelated — sibling mysqld containers,
not test-project pulls.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR.
- [ ] Watch the next ~10 master builds. `dagster-celery-docker-3-12` and
`dagster-docker-3-12` should stop producing the 60s
`UnixHTTPConnectionPool` ReadTimeout + downstream 240s pytest-timeout.
- [ ] If they do persist past this, the next escalation is bumping
`docker_memory_limit` (rate-limited pulls and concurrent decompression
both pressure memory under faster CPU) or splitting the celery test into
its own queue with higher headroom.

## Changelog

NOCHANGELOG

subject: bump ty 0.0.38 → 0.0.39 and fix surfaced type errors (#24905)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Bumps `ty` from 0.0.38 → 0.0.39 in both pin sites (root `pyproject.toml`
+ `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/pyproject.toml`) and fixes the 110
errors that the new ty version surfaces across the data-platform,
internal, and master ty environments. After the bump + fixes, `just ty`
is clean (0 errors / 0 warnings on 7035 files).

The fixes split into two buckets:

### Suppressions (`# ty: ignore[...]`) for upstream stub / library churn

These are cases where ty 0.0.39 reports against typing in an external
library, not in our code. Each is a narrow per-line ignore with a
specific rule code.

- **Stripe**: `Subscription.create` (`update_subscription.py`),
`SubscriptionSchedule.modify` (`schedule_pricing_changes.py`,
`reset_billing_anchor.py`) — the stripe stubs no longer accept our
`**additional_params` splat / typed-dict list mixes.
- **boto3**: `client(...)` overloads in `s3_client.py` and
`Session(...)` in `automation_internal/ecr/cli.py` (×3).
- **pytest**: `pytest.raises(exception_cls, **kwargs)` in
`dagster-airbyte/.../beta/utils.py`.
- **Click generics**: the `T_Callable`-bound decorator helpers in
`dagster/_cli/workspace/cli_target.py` and
`dagster-dg-core/dagster_dg_core/shared_options.py` — ty can't see
through the lambda-fallback's return type vs. the bound TypeVar.
- **Pydantic**: `ValidationError.from_exception_data(line_errors=...)`
in `pydantic_yaml.py` — the TypedDict-list variance against
`list[InitErrorDetails]`.
- **Misc internal-API variance** in `platform_perf/repo.py`,
`streamline_storage/storage.py`, `dep_operators.py`,
`components/core/decl.py`, `components/resolved/base.py`,
`dagster-airbyte/asset_defs.py`, `dagster-airflow/utils.py`,
`dagster-internal-buildkite/tox.py`, `assets_definition.py`.

### Code fixes

These are real type issues that ty 0.0.39 now catches. Most are missing
`None` guards or overly narrow annotations.

- **`None` guards / asserts**: `test_managed_kafka_state.py` (×8
aiokafka `message.value`), `test_asset_backfill.py` (×4
`instance.get_backfill(...)` may return `None`), `ursula/cli/debug.py`
(×2 snapshot-id guards), `asset_failure_emitter.py` (skip records with
no `asset_key`), `test_interrupt.py` + `dagster-celery/test_execute.py`
(`in` against `str | None`),
`automation_internal/cloud/shadow/instance.py` (filter `None`s before
`environ`).
- **`bool(...)` coercion** of `bool | None` permission-lookups in
`dagster-cloud-backend/permissions/constants.py` (×3) so
`dict[CloudPermissions, bool]` is honored.
- **Tighter annotations**: switched `check_names_by_asset_key` from
`list[str]` to `set[str]` in `op_invocation.py` + `compute_generator.py`
to match `resolve_target_check_key`'s expected `Mapping[AssetKey,
AbstractSet[str]]`; widened `asset_methods.get_status_by_partition`
return to `Mapping[str, AssetPartitionStatus | None] | None` (which
already matches the implementation) and matched the override in
`instance.py`; narrowed dict variance in
`dagster-airlift/event_stream.py`, `dg-cli/formatters.py`,
`databricks_pyspark_step_launcher.py`,
`dagster-graphql/schema/asset_graph.py`, `reporting/query.py`.
- **Real bugs touched**:
- `dagster-looker/lkml/asset_utils.py` was constructing raw tuples but
the function signature took `list[LookMLStructure]` — wrapped in
`LookMLStructure(...)`.
- `dagster-airbyte/test_resources.py:493` mutated
`existing_jobs_data[-1]["jobId"]` on what `get_job_details_sample()`
returns as `Mapping[str, Any]` — wrapped in `dict(...)`.
- `test_multi_partitions.py:882` accessed `.keys_by_dimension` on items
that are `str | MultiPartitionKey`; filtered to `MultiPartitionKey` via
`isinstance`.
- **Removed two redundant `cast(...)` calls** inside
`isinstance`-narrowed blocks: `notification_processor.py`,
`notification_test_specs.py`.
- **`uv.lock` updates**: pulled forward `ty` (`0.0.37` → `0.0.39` on the
internal lock, `0.0.38` → `0.0.39` on dagster-oss). The internal lock
also pulled forward unrelated transitives (`mcp`, `opentelemetry-*`,
`jsonschema*`, `referencing`, `rpds-py`, `uvicorn`, `pathable`) that had
drifted under the pre-existing pin.

### Second commit — `DagsterModule: declare build() on base class`

`automation_internal/release/cli.py:302` calls `module.build(outdir)`
where `module: DagsterModule`. The concrete subclass
`PyProjectDagsterModule` does implement `build(outdir)`, but
`DagsterModule` was missing the "fake-abstract" stub it has for sibling
methods (`distribution_name`, `wheel_command`, `project_file_path`,
`set_pin_info`). Adds the stub, types the subclass override's `outdir:
str`, and no `# ty: ignore` is needed in `cli.py`.

## Test Plan

- \`just ty\` → 0 errors / 0 warnings across data-platform, internal,
master.
- \`just ruff\` → clean.
- Behavioral fixes are tight enough (None guards, set-vs-list,
dict-vs-Mapping) that the existing test suites should cover regressions;
CI on this PR is the real validation.

subject: fix(k8s-tests): require successful load, not just LOADED, before yielding webserver url (#24904)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Follow-up to #24825, which did not fully eliminate the
`PipelineNotFoundError` race in `k8s-test-suite-*` first-launch tests.
Example failure on `master`: build 152884 job
`019e6475-1eff-4ad4-b18c-030e4c5986a9` —
`test_k8s_run_launcher_default[no_subchart]` failed one second after
starting, immediately after the previous fix's `Code locations loaded`
print.

The previous fix polled `locationStatusesOrError` and returned as soon
as the location reported `loadStatus == "LOADED"`. The bug:
`CodeLocationLoadStatus` is a two-value enum where `LOADED` means
*"finished loading (may be an error)"* (see
`dagster/_core/workspace/workspace.py:18`).
`WorkspaceProcessContext._load_location` always returns an entry with
`load_status=LOADED`, even when it caught an exception and
`code_location is None` / `load_error` is set. So the poll happily
returned the instant the first load attempt completed — racing the
workspace's watch-thread reload triggered by the first
`LOCATION_UPDATED` event from the user-code gRPC server. When the test
then issued `launchPipelineExecution`, `WorkspaceRequestContext.has_job`
checked `has_code_location` (which is `code_location is not None`), got
False, and the launch failed with `PipelineNotFoundError`. The race is
short enough that every subsequent test in the suite passes (the
watch-thread reload completes by then), which matches the observed
"first test only" pattern.

This PR switches `wait_for_workspace_loaded` to use the per-location
`workspaceLocationEntryOrError(name)` query and requires
`locationOrLoadError.__typename == "RepositoryLocation"` (not
`PythonError`, not null). That is the only field that distinguishes a
successful load from an errored one. The timeout error message is also
enriched to report each location's last observed state (`MISSING` /
`LOADING` / `LOAD_ERROR: <msg>` / `POLL_ERROR: <exc>`) so future
failures are easier to diagnose.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `:pytest: k8s-test-suite-1-2-default-3-12` passes on this branch
- [ ] `:pytest: k8s-test-suite-2-2-default-3-12` passes
- [ ] `:pytest: celery-k8s-test-suite-default-3-12` passes (same
fixture, different namespace)
- [ ] Re-run the suite 2–3× to gain confidence the flake is gone
(originally surfaced as a one-second-after-fixture-yield failure)

subject: Add test coverage for dg list defs with automation conditions (#22451)
body:
## Summary

Adds test coverage for the `dg list defs` command to verify proper
handling and serialization of automation conditions on assets. The test
validates that assets with automation conditions correctly include
`label` and `expanded_label` fields, while assets without automation
conditions have `null` values.

## Key Changes

- Add `test_list_defs_with_automation_condition()` test validating
automation condition serialization in JSON output
- Add `_sample_defs_with_automation_condition()` helper providing test
assets with and without automation conditions
- Verify automation condition structure including label and
expanded_label fields

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Modified (1 file)
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/test_list_commands.py`
- Added test for automation condition handling in dg list defs command

</details>

**Remotely executed:** [Run
#24146498798](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/actions/runs/24146498798)

---

To replicate this PR locally, run:

```
erk pr teleport 22451
```

<details>
<summary>original-plan</summary>

# Fix: `dg list defs` crashes with AttributeError on
AndAutomationCondition

## Context

GitHub Issue: https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/28839

Users running `dg list defs` on projects with automation conditions
(e.g., `AutomationCondition.eager()`) crash with:
```
AttributeError: 'AndAutomationCondition' object has no attribute '__name__'
```

The bug was in the old `dagster-components` package (v0.26.6) at
`dagster_components/cli/list.py:108`, where the code did
`node.automation_condition.__name__` directly on an automation condition
instance. `__name__` is not an instance attribute on `@record`-decorated
classes like `AndAutomationCondition`.

**Current state**: The `dagster-components` package has been replaced by
`dagster.components` (merged into the main dagster package). The current
`list_definitions()` function in
`dagster/components/list/list.py:183-190` already handles automation
conditions correctly using `get_snapshot()`:

```python
automation_condition={
    "label": node.automation_condition.get_snapshot().node_snapshot.label,
    "expanded_label": list(
        get_expanded_label(node.automation_condition.get_snapshot())
    ),
}
if node.automation_condition
else None,
```

**The core code fix is already in place.** However, there is **zero test
coverage** for `dg list defs` with automation conditions. The existing
test fixtures (`_sample_defs`, `_sample_complex_asset_defs`) don't
include any assets with automation conditions.

## Changes

### 1. Add test coverage for `dg list defs` with automation conditions

**File to modify:**
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/test_list_commands.py`

Add a new test function `test_list_defs_with_automation_condition` that:

1. Creates a test project using the existing
`isolated_example_project_foo_bar` helper
2. Scaffolds a `DefsFolderComponent` (same pattern as other tests)
3. Writes a definitions file containing assets with automation
conditions, specifically:
- An asset with `AutomationCondition.eager()` — this creates an
`AndAutomationCondition` internally (the exact class from the bug
report)
- An asset without an automation condition (to verify mixed scenarios
work)
4. Runs `dg list defs --json` and verifies:
   - The command succeeds (exit code 0)
   - The JSON output parses correctly
- The asset with an automation condition has a non-null
`automation_condition` field with `label` and `expanded_label` keys
   - The `label` field is `"eager"` (from `.with_label("eager")`)
   - The `expanded_label` field is a non-empty list of strings
- The asset without an automation condition has `automation_condition:
null`

**New test fixture to add** (in the same file, following the pattern of
`_sample_defs` and `_sample_complex_asset_defs`):

```python
def _sample_defs_with_automation_condition():
    import dagster as dg

    @dg.asset(automation_condition=dg.AutomationCondition.eager())
    def eager_asset(): ...

    @dg.asset
    def plain_asset(): ...

    defs = dg.Definitions(assets=[eager_asset, plain_asset])  # noqa: F841
```

**New test function:**

```python
def test_list_defs_with_automation_condition():
    with (
        ProxyRunner.test() as runner,
        isolated_example_project_foo_bar(runner, in_workspace=False, uv_sync=True) as project_dir,
    ):
        with activate_venv(project_dir / ".venv"):
            subprocess.run(
                ["dg", "scaffold", "defs", "dagster.DefsFolderComponent", "mydefs"],
                check=True,
            )

            with Path("src/foo_bar/defs/mydefs/definitions.py").open("w") as f:
                defs_source = textwrap.dedent(
                    inspect.getsource(_sample_defs_with_automation_condition).split("\n", 1)[1]
                )
                f.write(defs_source)

            result = subprocess.run(
                ["dg", "list", "defs", "--json"], capture_output=True, check=True
            )
            output = json.loads(result.stdout.decode("utf-8"))

            assets_by_key = {a["asset_key"]: a for a in output["assets"]}

            # Asset with automation condition should have label and expanded_label
            eager = assets_by_key["eager_asset"]
            assert eager["automation_condition"] is not None
            assert eager["automation_condition"]["label"] == "eager"
            assert isinstance(eager["automation_condition"]["expanded_label"], list)
            assert len(eager["automation_condition"]["expanded_label"]) > 0

            # Asset without automation condition should have null
            plain = assets_by_key["plain_asset"]
            assert plain.get("automation_condition") is None
```

**Add `import json`** at the top of the file if not already present.

### 2. Update snapshot file (if using snapshot testing)

**File:**
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/__snapshots__/test_list_commands.ambr`

The new test uses assertion-based validation rather than snapshots, so
no snapshot update is needed. This is intentional — the exact
`expanded_label` values may change as automation condition
implementations evolve, so asserting on structure rather than exact
values is more robust.

## Files NOT changing

- `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/components/list/list.py` —
The fix is already in place, using `get_snapshot()` instead of
`__name__`
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/_core/definitions/declarative_automation/operators/boolean_operators.py`
— `AndAutomationCondition` class itself is fine; the bug was in the CLI
code that consumed it
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/_core/definitions/declarative_automation/automation_condition.py`
— Base class is correct
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster/dagster/_core/definitions/declarative_automation/serialized_objects.py`
— `get_expanded_label()` function is correct
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli/cli/list.py`
— CLI command delegates to `list_definitions()` correctly
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli/dagster_dg_cli/cli/schemas/list_schemas.py`
— Schema conversion is correct
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Not modified per instructions

## Implementation details

### Key patterns to follow

- Follow the existing test pattern in `test_list_commands.py`: use
`isolated_example_project_foo_bar` with `uv_sync=True`, scaffold a
component, write definitions, run `dg list defs`
- The test fixture function (e.g.,
`_sample_defs_with_automation_condition`) is extracted via
`inspect.getsource()` and written to a file, so it must be
self-contained (all imports inside the function body)
- Use `json.loads()` for structured assertions rather than snapshot
matching for this test — the expanded label content is complex and may
evolve
- Place the new test fixture near the other `_sample_*` fixtures (around
line 627-680)
- Place the new test function near the other `test_list_defs_*` tests
(around line 500-526)

### Why `AutomationCondition.eager()` is the right test case

`AutomationCondition.eager()` returns an `AndAutomationCondition` — the
exact class from the bug report. It also produces a complex condition
tree (with nested AND, OR, NOT operators) that exercises the
`get_expanded_label()` recursive logic. This single test case covers:
- `AndAutomationCondition` (root)
- `OrAutomationCondition` (nested)
- `NotAutomationCondition` (nested)
- Various leaf conditions
- Label handling (`.with_label("eager")`)

## Verification

1. Run the test:
   ```bash
   cd dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli
tox -vv -e py312-default -- -k test_list_defs_with_automation_condition
   ```

2. Run linting:
   ```bash
   cd dagster-oss && make ruff
   ```

3. Verify existing tests still pass:
   ```bash
   cd dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-dg-cli
   tox -vv -e py312-default -- -k test_list_defs
   ```

</details>

subject: buildkite: add with_env() and propagate env/secrets on k8s (#24834)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes the EKS-routed cypress step (failing on dogfood since the
default-queue flip to `KUBERNETES_EKS`) by teaching
`CommandStepBuilder.build()` to propagate step-level env vars and
AWS-Secrets-Manager secrets on the k8s branch. Previously both
`_docker_settings["environment"]` and `_secrets` were silently dropped
when a step landed on a k8s queue, because the k8s branch only emitted
the `kubernetes` plugin and skipped the docker/SM plugin wiring. For
cypress this meant `CYPRESS_BASE_URL` and
`CYPRESS_DAGSTER_CLOUD_API_TOKEN` were missing inside the pod, so
Cypress fell back to `http://localhost:3000` and got "Cypress could not
verify that this server is running."

Rather than patching the docker-plugin shape into k8s (we're moving away
from the docker plugin on k8s anyway), this PR introduces a
queue-agnostic `with_env()` method as the source of truth for per-step
env vars, and wires both queue paths to consume it.

## Changes

- `CommandStepBuilder.with_env(**env_vars: str)` — new builder method,
concrete values only. Bare-name passthroughs continue to flow through
the agent's envFrom k8s secret (`buildkite-dagster-secrets`) on k8s and
through docker-plugin passthrough on docker, so they don't belong here.
- `build()` k8s branch now: (1) extends `podSpec.containers[0].env` with
`_env` entries, (2) also picks up any `KEY=value` entries left in
`_docker_settings["environment"]` (so legacy `env=[...]` callers benefit
without code changes), and (3) appends `SM_PLUGIN` alongside the
`kubernetes` plugin when `_secrets` is non-empty. `SM_PLUGIN` runs as a
buildkite-agent bootstrap hook, which executes inside the user container
under agent-stack-k8s, so the exported env vars are visible to
subsequent command hooks without any docker-plugin involvement.
- `build()` docker branch is unchanged behaviorally — just refactored to
merge `_env` entries via `setdefault("environment", [])` so
`on_specific_image` callers that don't pass `extra_docker_plugin_args`
no longer KeyError on the docker queue path.
- `cypress_test_login` dropped `extra_docker_plugin_args={"environment":
[...]}` and now uses `.with_env(CYPRESS_BASE_URL=...,
COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT="0")`. The token passthrough entry is
gone — `with_secret(...)` + `SM_PLUGIN` covers it.
- Both `docs.py` steps migrated from
`env=["COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0"]` to
`.with_env(COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT="0")` for consistency.

## Test Plan

- [x] Smoke-test cypress step output on both queues: k8s renders the
kubernetes plugin with `CYPRESS_BASE_URL` and
`COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT` in `podSpec.containers[0].env` plus
`SM_PLUGIN` alongside; docker renders the same env vars inside the
docker plugin's `environment` list with the token as a passthrough —
unchanged from prior behavior.
- [x] `just ruff` clean.
- [ ] dog-dogfood pipeline rerun lands cypress-login successfully on
EKS.

subject: Fix master: regen app-cloud graphql artifacts, satisfy catalog view invariant (#24884)
body:
## Summary

Fixes two master breakages from the catalog-views stack
([#24540](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24540) /
[#24541](https://github.com/dagster-io/internal/pull/24541)):

- **`dagster-cloud-host` image build** ([build
152865](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152865)) — the
committed app-cloud graphql artifacts (`types.ts`, `builders.ts`,
`schema.graphql`, `possibleTypes.generated.json`) were never regenerated
after the Python schema added `EDIT_OTHER_USERS_CATALOG_VIEWS`, so `next
build` failed with `Property 'EDIT_OTHER_USERS_CATALOG_VIEWS' does not
exist on type 'typeof CustomRolePermission'`. The `app-cloud-default` TS
step silently regenerated in-memory via `yarn generate-graphql` and
passed, masking the drift.
- **`dagster-cloud-e2e`** ([build
152863](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152863#019e626c-a7d2-4aec-8af5-2149d5e10295))
— two tests built `CatalogView(creator_id=1)` with no `created_by`,
violating the new storage invariant. Added `created_by="1"`.

To stop this class of drift from leaking past the TS step in the future,
added `git diff --exit-code` after `yarn generate-graphql` in
app-cloud's tox `default` env — if regen produces any diff, the step
fails with a clear signal that committed artifacts are stale.

## Test plan

- [ ] `app-cloud-default` passes (will fail loudly now if anyone forgets
to commit regen)
- [ ] `dagster-cloud-host` image builds
- [ ] `dagster-cloud-e2e` passes
(`test_materialization_asset_selection_target_upstream_selection_view`,
`test_data_generation[on,on-metric-alert-saved-selection]`)

subject: Order RUN_FAILURE_REASON_TAG write before run status update (#24730)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

In `SqlRunStorage.handle_run_event`, the PIPELINE_FAILURE handler used
to write the run status update and the `dagster/failure_reason` tag in
**two separate transactions**:

1. `with self.connect() as conn:` — UPDATE `runs.status = FAILURE`
(commits on exit).
2. `self.add_run_tags(run_id, {RUN_FAILURE_REASON_TAG: ...})` — opens
its own connection.

A caller polling for `run.is_finished` could observe `status=FAILURE`
between those two writes and then read `run.tags` without the tag —
`KeyError: 'dagster/failure_reason'`.

This is the source of the flake in
`test_retry_failure_all_steps_with_reexecution_params` ([example
failure](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152044#019e4b21-52ee-4964-807d-47d28eed96a5)):
the test calls `wait_for_runs_to_finish` (status-only) then reads the
tag immediately.

## Fix

- Compute the `failure_reason` tag value upfront and include it in the
`run_body` serialized into the runs UPDATE.
- Inside the same `with self.connect() as conn:` block, write the
`RunTagsTable` row **first**, then the runs UPDATE.
- On `SqliteRunStorage`, `connect()` wraps in `conn.begin()` so the two
writes commit as a unit.
- On `PostgresRunStorage`, the engine is configured with
`isolation_level="AUTOCOMMIT"`, so each `conn.execute` commits
independently. Ordering the tag write first ensures that by the time a
reader observes the new status, the tag row is already there.
- `update_timestamp` is written exactly once on the runs row (using the
event timestamp), avoiding the regression that calling `add_run_tags`
separately would introduce (where `runs.update_timestamp` could be
written as `now()` and then overwritten with an earlier event timestamp,
breaking `RunsFilter(updated_after=...)` cursors).
- Use the in-memory `run.tags` to choose UPDATE vs INSERT against
`RunTagsTable`, mirroring `add_run_tags` — no extra SELECT round-trip.

## Test Plan

- [x] `tox -e py312-storage_tests -- -k test_failure_event_updates_tags`
— all 3 variants (Sqlite, InMemory, Legacy) pass.
- [x] Full `dagster_tests/storage_tests/test_run_storage.py` suite —
1007 passed, 105 pre-existing skips.
- [ ] CI green on `dagster-graphql` suites that previously surfaced the
flake.

## Changelog

Eliminate a race where readers polling for a run to reach FAILURE could
miss the `dagster/failure_reason` tag.

subject: test(dagster-celery): wait for worker readiness in start_celery_worker fixture (#24837)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

`dagster_celery_tests/test_launcher.py::test_crashy_run[run_config0]`
failed on master in [build
152582](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152582#019e5043-9d0d-40ac-9eb6-29b1d580f64b)
with `Exception: Timed out` from `poll_for_step_start(timeout=5)`.
Reconstructed timeline from the worker logs:

| time (UTC) | event |
|---|---|
| `15:31:26.694` | pytest enters `test_crashy_run` |
| `15:31:35` | Dagster code server starts (workspace fixture) |
| `15:31:36` | Celery worker subprocess starts |
| `15:31:38.689` | Celery worker reports **ready** |
| `15:31:38.690` | Celery worker receives the `execute_job` task |
| `15:31:41.165` | `RUN_START` event emitted in ForkPoolWorker |
| `15:31:41.671` | **`poll_for_step_start` times out at t=5s → pytest
prints FAILED** |
| `15:31:42.229` | `STEP_START` emitted (0.5s too late) |

`start_celery_worker` in `dagster_celery_tests/utils.py`
`subprocess.Popen`s the worker and yields immediately. Under CI load the
worker took ~12s to connect to rabbitmq and register, and the test's
`poll_for_step_start(timeout=5)` ran entirely inside that gap. This is
the same shape as the `rabbitmq` fixture race fixed in #24780 ("yield
before the resource is actually usable"), one layer down.

## Fix

Add `_wait_for_worker_ready(queue)` that polls
`app.control.inspect().active_queues()` until at least one worker is
consuming from the expected queue. `start_celery_worker` calls it before
yielding, so test bodies only run once the worker is actually ready to
dequeue tasks. 60s budget, 1s inspect timeout per poll, 0.25s sleep
between polls.

Chose this over simply bumping the test's `poll_for_step_start` timeout
to 30s because the readiness race affects every consumer of the fixture
(`test_launcher.py`, `test_queues.py`, `test_priority.py`) — fixing the
root cause is the same effort as bandaging one symptom.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI: `:pytest: dagster-celery-3-12` passes on this branch.
- [ ] CI watch: 5 consecutive master builds of `:pytest:
dagster-celery-3-12` after this lands.

subject: fix(dagster-dask): cap local-cluster n_workers to dodge SQLite event-log races (#24800)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

`dagster_dask_tests::test_composite_execute` flaked on the
post-EKS-migration master build
(https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152480#019e4fd1-8027-4064-aabd-1bc7bcc415e8)
with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` thrown while a
step's `RESOURCE_INIT_SUCCESS` event tried to INSERT into the SQLite
event log. One failed INSERT cascades to `RUN_FAILURE` → `result.success
== False`.

Root cause: the test spins up a `LocalCluster()` with no `n_workers`
override, so Dask defaults to `nproc` workers — 32 on the EKS node we
saw in the log. The deeply nested test graph (`nesting_graph(6, 2)` =
~128 ops) fans those out hard, and all workers concurrently write events
to one SQLite file. The default `busy_timeout` lapses and a writer gives
up.

More CPU/memory does not help — faster cores make the race tighter. The
fix is to cap concurrency at the test boundary.

## Changes

- `test_composite_execute`: pin `n_workers=2, threads_per_worker=1`.
- `test_execute_hammer_through_webserver` (same suite, also uses
`LocalCluster()` with default workers + 4-way parallel hammer ops): pin
`n_workers=2, threads_per_worker=1` as a pre-emptive fix — same root
cause, same risk class.

Single-op tests in the suite (`test_execute_on_dask_local`,
`test_pandas_dask`, `test_dask`) are not at risk: with only one step
there's no concurrent SQLite writer, regardless of worker count. Left
unchanged.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI passes (especially `dagster-dask-3-12`).
- [ ] Test still exercises the dask-executor multi-process path (2
workers is still parallel).

subject: test(dagster-celery): fix flaky test_start_worker and test_terminate_job_on_celery (#24780)
body:
## Summary

Two recurrent flakes in the `dagster-celery` suite on master, both bugs
in the test code (not the executor):

### `test_cli.py::test_start_worker` (and the five sibling
`test_start_worker_*` tests)

`[Errno 111] Connection refused` against the broker. The Buildkite
branch of the `rabbitmq` session fixture sets `TEST_BROKER` and yields
immediately:

```python
if IS_BUILDKITE:
    with environ({"TEST_BROKER": os.getenv("DAGSTER_CELERY_BROKER_HOST", "localhost")}):
        yield
    return
```

But `celery_extra_cmds` only ran `docker compose up -d` on the rabbitmq
sibling container, which returns once the container is *created* — not
once rabbitmq's TCP listener is *bound*. First test in the suite races
the broker and fails.

**Fix:** wait for port 5672 (with a 60s timeout) before yielding.
Mirrors the existing "Waiting for rabbitmq to be ready..." poll the
fixture already does in the local-dev branch.

### `test_execute.py::test_terminate_job_on_celery`

Asserts at least one `ENGINE_EVENT` with the literal message `"was
revoked."` reaches the iterator. That's only true when the interrupt
fires *before* a later step starts, so celery revokes the not-yet-queued
task. Under load the interrupt sometimes fires after every step has
already started, so revoke hits the worker mid-execution and the test
observes `STEP_FAILURE` instead — both outcomes are legitimate evidence
that the interrupt propagated.

Recent failure logs ([build
152307](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152307), [build
152374](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152374)) show the
worker termination did happen (`Terminating … (15)`, `RPC backend
missing task request`) but no `"was revoked."` engine event reached the
iterator before the run ended.

**Fix:** accept either `"was revoked."` engine events OR a
`STEP_FAILURE` in `result_types` as evidence the interrupt was observed.
Include `result_types` in the assertion message for triage.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR.
- [ ] Watch the next ~10 master builds; both `test_start_worker` and
`test_terminate_job_on_celery` should stop showing up in flake reports.
- [ ] Note: the docker-daemon `ReadTimeout` flakes in `dagster-docker` /
`dagster-celery-docker` / `dagster-test` are a separate root cause (dind
sidecar saturation under default sizing); fixed in #24779 with a
`ResourceRequests` bump.

## Changelog
