body:
## Summary & Motivation

Follow-up to #24661. Drops three more OSS test suites off the MEDIUM
(EC2) queue onto `kubernetes-eks`.

The three suites were on MEDIUM with `env_vars=[AWS_*]` or
`env_vars=[TEST_AZURE_*]` configured, which made it look like a
secrets-provisioning blocker. On inspection it isn't:

| Suite | Reality |
|---|---|
| **`dagster-aws`** | `conftest.py` autouse fixture sets fake creds with
`monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "test")` etc., tests use
`moto.mock_aws` — no real AWS access. The `env_vars=[AWS_*]` was
vestigial. |
| **`dagster-dask`** | Tests don't import boto3 or touch AWS at all. The
`env_vars=[AWS_*]` was fully vestigial. |
| **`dagster-azure-live-tests`** | `TEST_AZURE_*` keys already live in
the EKS K8s secret `buildkite-dagster-secrets`
(`infra/k8s/buildkite/overlays/buildkite-eks/secrets.yaml:62-67`), which
is auto-mounted on every step pod via `envFrom`
(`command_step_builder.py:582-589`). So the suite's
`env_vars=[TEST_AZURE_*]` just allowlists the names through the
docker→pod boundary, and the actual values reach the test process for
free. |

So there's no secret-provisioning work to do — just dropping the
`queue=BuildkiteQueue.MEDIUM` toggle and cleaning up the dead AWS
`env_vars` lists on `dagster-aws` / `dagster-dask`.

-
`dagster-oss/.buildkite/dagster-buildkite/dagster_buildkite/steps/packages.py`

the `env_vars=[TEST_AZURE_*]` allowlist (still needed at the docker
boundary).

Starting with default EKS sizing on all three (outer pod 1000m cpu / no
memory request → BestEffort QoS, dind sidecar 2000m / 1Gi req / 2Gi
limit / 10Gi ephemeral storage). The Azure suite runs `just rebuild_ui`
plus a `dagster-webserver` subprocess, which could be RAM-hungry;
flagging that as the likely candidate for a follow-up bump if it OOMs.

subject: fix(tests): poll subprocess in asset daemon failure recovery tests (#24761)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes a flake in `test_failure_recovery` and the neighboring
`test_asset_daemon_failure_recovery` tests where the daemon subprocess
hadn't finished its work within the 60-second `process.join(timeout=60)`
deadline under heavy buildkite-eks load — the test killed the subprocess
mid-tick, leaving the tick in `STARTED` state, and the subsequent
assertion failed with a confusing `STARTED != SUCCESS` rather than a
clear timeout error.

Original flake:
https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152023#019e4af3-dd73-452c-b88e-e57cf3845cb9.
Reconstructed timeline showed each run submission taking 9–21 seconds on
the failing worker; the daemon got through only 3 of 5 submissions
before the 60-second deadline.

Replaces the 6 `process.join(timeout=60)` sites across
`test_failure_recovery.py` and `test_asset_daemon_failure_recovery.py`
with a shared `wait_for_daemon_subprocess` helper (in `test_e2e.py`)
that polls `is_alive()` against a 180-second deadline (3× the previous
timeout) and, if the subprocess is still alive at the deadline,
terminates it and raises `RuntimeError`. Slow CI workers now get the
headroom they need, and true hangs surface as explicit errors instead of
stale-tick assertions.

## Test Plan

- [x] Ran
`dagster_tests/declarative_automation_tests/daemon_tests/test_failure_recovery.py::test_failure_recovery[False-EVALUATIONS_FINISHED]`
locally — passes (8.45s)
- [ ] CI exercises the full parametrization matrix (10 × 2 in
`test_failure_recovery`, 10 + 8 in `test_asset_daemon_failure_recovery`)
— relying on the existing buildkite job
`dagster-2-2-declarative-automation-tests-3-12`

subject: [NO_SKIP] ci(buildkite): migrate docker-dependent OSS tests to EKS (#24661)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Moves seven docker-using OSS test suites and the `test-project-image`
build step off the MEDIUM (EC2) queue onto EKS. After this lands, the
only OSS step keys still on MEDIUM are airflow- / airlift-bound suites
(`dagster-airlift`, `dagster-airlift/perf-harness`, `dagster-test`,
`daemon-test-suite`, `backcompat-test-suite`,
`dagster-azure-live-tests`*, `dagster-aws`*, `dagster-dask`*,
`dagster-graphql`), and a couple of per-factor outliers
(`dagster-dg-cli` `slow`, `dagstermill` `papermill2`).

*Also being migrated in parallel PR #24716.*

## What this PR migrates

EKS defaults: outer pod `1000m` cpu / no memory request (BestEffort
QoS), dind sidecar `2000m` cpu / `1Gi` memory request / `2Gi` memory
limit / `10Gi` ephemeral storage.

| Suite | Outer pod | Dind sidecar | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|
| `examples/deploy_docker` | defaults | defaults | Single user-code
container + `postgres:11`; both come from docker.io via the
dockerhub-mirror sidecar. |
| `dagster-celery` | defaults | defaults | Single `rabbitmq` sibling
container (docker.io). |
| `dagster-mysql` | `1000m / 1Gi` | `2000m / 2Gi req / 4Gi limit` |
Three sibling mysqld containers up at once (`test-mysql-db`,
`test-mysql-db-pinned`, `test-mysql-db-pinned-backcompat`); each
~300-500MB at steady state, so the default 2Gi dind limit is the tight
bound. Same shape as the airbyte integration bump in #23997. |
| `dagster-postgres` | defaults | defaults | Single sibling postgres
container via `dagster_test.fixtures` (docker.io). |
| `test-project-image` (build) | defaults | defaults | `docker build` of
a single Python image, then `docker push` to elementl ECR via IRSA. |
| `dagster-celery-docker` | defaults | defaults | Pulls the test-project
image; uses the same celery/rabbitmq fixtures as `dagster-celery`. |
| `dagster-docker` | defaults | defaults | Pulls the test-project image;
uses dagster-test docker fixtures. |

Outer-pod `memory=1Gi` on `dagster-mysql` promotes the test container
from BestEffort to Burstable QoS so the kubelet doesn't pick it as a
first-line eviction target during fan-out waves.

## Mechanism

Two files changed:

-
`dagster-oss/.buildkite/dagster-buildkite/dagster_buildkite/steps/packages.py`:
- Adds a new optional `resources: ResourceRequests | None = None` field
to `PackageSpec`, mirroring the existing `queue: BuildkiteQueue | None =
None`.
- In `PackageSpec.build_steps`, changes resources resolution to a
per-factor → package-level fallback (`other_factor.resources or
self.resources`), so per-factor `ToxFactor.resources` continues to win
for factor-level bumps (`storage_tests`, `daemon_tests`, etc.) but a
package-level `resources=...` now applies to factor-less PackageSpecs
(`dagster-mysql` is the only one using it here).
- Drops `queue=BuildkiteQueue.MEDIUM` from `examples/deploy_docker`,
`dagster-celery`, `dagster-mysql`, `dagster-postgres`,
`dagster-celery-docker`, `dagster-docker`.
- Adds an inline `resources=ResourceRequests(...)` for `dagster-mysql`.
-
`dagster-oss/.buildkite/dagster-buildkite/dagster_buildkite/steps/test_project.py`:
- Drops `.on_queue(BuildkiteQueue.MEDIUM)` from the test-project-image
build step. Default queue is `KUBERNETES_EKS`.
  - Drops the now-unused `BuildkiteQueue` import.

## Cross-account pull dependency

The test-project-image build step runs inside the
`buildkite-build-test-project-image` outer-pod image, which the
dagster-dev EKS kubelet has to pull cross-account from the elementl ECR
account (968703565975). The corresponding `pull-from-eks-clusters`
repository policy was added in #24713 and applied to AWS on 2026-05-21,
so the kubelet pull is now authorized.

The base image (`test-project-base`) and the output image
(`test-project:${BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID}-{ver}`) are pulled / pushed by the
dind sidecar's docker client, which authenticates as the pod's
`buildkite-job` IRSA in the same account — no cross-account policy
needed for those. `test-project` is in the IRSA write allowlist as of
#24713.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR.
- [ ] On a representative build: the migrated step keys
(`test-project-*`, `dagster-celery-*`,
`dagster-mysql-*-storage-tests-*`, `dagster-postgres-storage-tests-*`,
`dagster-celery-docker-*`, `dagster-docker-*`,
`examples-deploy-docker-*`) all report `agent: kubernetes-eks` rather
than `medium`. Spot-check a `dagster-mysql-storage-tests-1-2-3-12` pod
spec for `cpu: 1000m, memory: 1Gi` on the test container and `cpu:
2000m, memory: 2Gi (limit: 4Gi)` on the dind sidecar.
- [ ] `test-project-3-12` pod successfully pulls
`buildkite-build-test-project-image` (no `exit_status: -1` "agent lost"
like 151765 / 151775). The PR was punted-and-restored once already;
cross-account pull is the variable that changed.
- [ ] Watch the first ~10 master builds post-merge. Expectation: no new
compose-stack startup timeouts or dind OOM kills on the migrated suites.
If `dagster-mysql` flakes, follow up with a larger dind limit (`6Gi` is
the next step up). If `test-project-image` flakes on docker-build memory
pressure, bump the dind sidecar memory similarly.

subject: fix(test): pin test_earliest_step_failure_on_failed_job to in_process_executor (#24751)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

`dagster_tests/core_tests/test_event_logging.py::test_earliest_step_failure_on_failed_job` is flaking on master. Two failures observed within ~30 minutes on `internal` CI:

- [build 152117 job](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152117#019e4b9d-0c62-4f3b-a267-dbe70a0aeb09) — got `mapped_op[2]` instead of `mapped_op[0]`
- [build 152151 job](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/152151#019e4bb7-37eb-4890-8594-940765916d98) — got `mapped_op[1]` instead of `mapped_op[0]`

The test relies on `failing_job_concurrent_events`, which fans out three subprocesses (`mapped_op[0..2]`) under the multiprocess executor and uses `time.sleep(i)` (0s, 1s, 2s) to enforce a failure order where `mapped_op[0]` fails first. The assertion `step_failure.step_key == "mapped_op[0]"` then verifies the `first_step_failure_event` reporting.

The problem is that the sleep spread (max 2s) is on the same order of magnitude as subprocess-startup jitter under the multiprocess executor on CI. From build 152117's captured stderr:

| step | STEP_WORKER_STARTING | STEP_START |
|---|---|---|
| `mapped_op[0]` | 17:48:27 | 17:48:32 |
| `mapped_op[1]` | 17:48:28 | 17:48:30 |
| `mapped_op[2]` | 17:48:28 | 17:48:30 |

`mapped_op[2]` started executing 2s before `mapped_op[0]` did, so its 2s sleep finished while `mapped_op[0]` was still spinning up — making `mapped_op[2]` the first to raise.

## Fix

The test is checking event-log data integrity (does `first_step_failure_event` correctly point to the earliest failure), not the multiprocess executor's race-resolution logic. Pinning the job to `in_process_executor` makes dynamic-mapped steps run sequentially in mapping-key order, so `mapped_op[0]` is deterministically the first failure. The sleeps become unnecessary and are removed.

Also rewrote the misleading docstring (it previously said "fails last" while the test checks the first failure).

This is faster than the previous test (no sleeps, no subprocess startup) and eliminates the flake class entirely rather than just making the race window larger.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI: `:pytest: dagster-core-tests-3-12` passes on this branch
- [ ] Local: `tox -e py312-core_tests -- -k test_earliest_step_failure_on_failed_job` passes

subject: fix(dagster-test): explicit IPAM-settle barrier in buildkite_hostnames_cm (#24712)
body:
## Summary

Permanent fix for the recurring `KeyError: 'airbyte-webapp'` flake in
`:pytest: dagster-airbyte-integration-3-12`. Replaces the
localhost-fallback band-aid (#24675, reverted by #24688) with the actual
right shape — keep the bridge-IP code path intact, and make the
IPAM-settle barrier explicit so `hostnames()` doesn't race docker IPAM.

Re-arms `dagster-airbyte` `integration` by dropping the `soft_fail=True`
the revert installed as a temporary quarantine. The PR build itself runs
the previously-flaky test, so this PR is its own validation.

## Why #24675 was wrong

#24675 switched the EKS path from bridge IPs to `localhost` + published
port mappings. That broke every other `docker_compose_cm` consumer (~25
dagster-cloud test jobs in [build
151863](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151863)) because:

- `dagster-cloud/docker-compose-test.yaml` publishes ports on
**remapped** host ports (e.g. `5433:5432` for postgres).
- Storage fixtures hard-code the container-side port
(`psycopg2.connect(host=hostnames["test_main_shard"], port=5432)`).
- Pre-PR those tests worked because `hostnames(...)` returned bridge IPs
(e.g. `172.18.0.2`), which the EKS pod can reach via its shared netns
with the dind sidecar — port 5432 on the bridge IP is the container
port. `localhost:5432` had nothing listening on it.

So switching the address shape is a non-starter. The bridge-IP path is
correct for everyone — the issue was just that it wasn't waiting for
IPAM to populate.

## Root cause

In `buildkite_hostnames_cm`:

1. `current_container()` reads `/etc/hostname` and runs `docker ps
--filter id=<hostname>` to find the agent's own container name.
2. `connect_container_to_network(<container>, <network>)` joins the
agent to the compose network.
3. `hostnames(<network>)` reads
`NetworkSettings.Networks[<network>].IPAddress` from `docker inspect`
for each running container.

On the legacy buildkite-agent layout (agent is a docker container on an
EC2 host), all three work. On the EKS layout (kube pod + dind sidecar) —
which `dagster-airbyte/integration` uses, since it declares
`docker_cpu`/`docker_memory` resource requests in `packages.py` — step 1
returns empty (pod hostname is not a container ID dind knows), and step
2 silently runs `docker network connect <network> ""` and is rejected by
docker.

The empty container value is **not directly the cause of the
`KeyError`**. Step 3 reads each container's per-network IP regardless of
who's connected. The actual failure is that step 2 was doubling as an
**implicit IPAM barrier**: `docker network connect` doesn't return until
docker's IPAM is in a settled state for that network. Without it, step 3
races IPAM. `docker compose up --detach` returns when containers are
`Started`, but the per-network `IPAddress` field is populated
asynchronously around container start. If `docker inspect` runs before
IPAM has populated, the container is either missing from `docker ps` or
present with empty `IPAddress` — either way the `if hostname:` guard in
`hostnames()` drops it from the returned dict. Next lookup → `KeyError`.

Two recent master runs illustrate the flake:

- [Build 151730](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151730)
(FAIL): IPAM hadn't populated `airbyte-webapp`'s IP by the time
`hostnames()` ran. Dict missing the key. `KeyError` on every test/rerun.
- [Build 151763](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151763)
(mostly PASS, 6/7): IPAM had populated in time. Dict had the key with
bridge IP `172.18.0.2`. Test proceeded.

## Fix

Two changes in
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-test/dagster_test/fixtures/docker_compose.py`:

1. **Add `_wait_for_network_ipam(network, *, timeout=30, settle_polls=3,
interval=0.5)`** — polls `hostnames(network)` until it returns the same
non-empty dict for `settle_polls` (3) consecutive ticks. On settle,
return. On timeout (30s), log a warning and return whatever we have.
Makes the IPAM barrier explicit on both layouts.
2. **Conditionally call connect/disconnect in `buildkite_hostnames_cm`**
— only when `current_container()` returns non-empty (legacy layout). On
EKS there's no container to join; the pod shares its netns with the dind
sidecar so the compose bridge networks already exist in our namespace,
and skipping the call avoids the no-op `docker network connect <network>
""` failure.

Bridge IPs continue to be the values returned by `hostnames(network)` on
both layouts — no consumer needs to special-case `localhost`, and the
revert's regression on dagster-cloud consumers does not recur.

And one change in
`dagster-oss/.buildkite/dagster-buildkite/dagster_buildkite/steps/packages.py`:

3. **Drop `soft_fail=True` on `dagster-airbyte/integration`** — the
temporary quarantine from #24688 is no longer needed once the underlying
race is fixed. This is what makes the PR self-validating: the airbyte
integration suite is once again a hard gate, so the PR build runs it and
a green CI signal demonstrates the fix.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI on this PR. `dagster-airbyte-integration-3-12` runs without
`soft_fail`, and passes.
- [ ] All other `docker_compose_cm` consumers (dagster-cloud-backend,
dagster-cloud-dagit, ursula, dagster-cloud-worker, dagster-postgres,
dagster-docker, etc.) continue to pass — bridge-IP semantics are
unchanged.
- [ ] Watch ~5 master builds post-merge. Expectation: no `KeyError:
'airbyte-webapp'`, no `psycopg2.OperationalError: connection to server
at "localhost"` regression.

subject: K8s run pods inherit nodeSelector, tolerations, and podSecurityContext from user deployments (#22636)
body:
When `includeConfigInLaunchedRuns.enabled` is true, the Helm chart
serializes user deployment configuration into
`DAGSTER_CONTAINER_CONTEXT` so run pods inherit settings. However,
`nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, and `podSecurityContext` were missing
from this serialized context, causing run pods to potentially schedule
on wrong nodes or lack required security contexts.

This fix adds the three missing fields to the
`dagsterUserDeployments.k8sContainerContext` Helm helper under
`run_k8s_config.pod_spec_config`. No Python changes are needed — the
existing deserialization path already supports these fields.

## Key Changes

- Add `node_selector`, `tolerations`, and `security_context` to the
container context Helm helper template (`_helpers.tpl`)
- Fields are conditionally rendered only when set in Helm values,
preserving backward compatibility
- Add `test_code_server_cli_with_scheduling_fields` test covering
`DAGSTER_CONTAINER_CONTEXT` (code server CLI path)
- Add `test_container_context_with_pod_scheduling_fields` test covering
`DAGSTER_CLI_API_GRPC_CONTAINER_CONTEXT` (gRPC API path)

<details>
<summary>Files Changed</summary>

### Modified (2 files)
-
`dagster-oss/helm/dagster/charts/dagster-user-deployments/templates/helpers/_helpers.tpl`
- Add nodeSelector, tolerations, podSecurityContext to container context
payload
-
`dagster-oss/helm/dagster/schema/schema_tests/test_user_deployments.py`
- Add two new tests verifying fields appear in serialized container
context

</details>

## Critical Notes
- Fixes dagster-io/dagster#9924

<details>
<summary>original-plan</summary>

# Fix: K8s run pods inherit nodeSelector, tolerations, and
podSecurityContext from user deployments

## Context

When `includeConfigInLaunchedRuns.enabled` is true in a Helm user
deployment, the deployment's configuration is serialized into the
`DAGSTER_CONTAINER_CONTEXT` / `DAGSTER_CLI_API_GRPC_CONTAINER_CONTEXT`
environment variable so that launched K8s run pods inherit the user
deployment's settings. However, three important pod-level fields —
`nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, and `podSecurityContext` — are **not**
included in this serialized container context, even though they are
rendered on the user deployment pod itself.

This means run pods launched by the Dagster run launcher will not
inherit scheduling constraints from the user deployment, causing them to
potentially run on incorrect nodes or without required security
contexts.

**GitHub issue:** dagster-io/dagster#9924

## Changes

### 1. Helm helper: Add missing fields to container context payload

**File:**
`dagster-oss/helm/dagster/charts/dagster-user-deployments/templates/helpers/_helpers.tpl`
**Lines:** 147-207 (the `dagsterUserDeployments.k8sContainerContext`
helper)

Add the three missing fields into the `run_k8s_config.pod_spec_config`
section of the container context YAML. Insert them after the existing
`automount_service_account_token` line (line 192) and before the
`containers` block (line 193).

**What to add** (inside the `run_k8s_config: / pod_spec_config:` block):

```yaml
        {{- if .nodeSelector }}
        node_selector: {{- .nodeSelector | toYaml | nindent 10 }}
        {{- end }}
        {{- if .tolerations }}
        tolerations: {{- .tolerations | toYaml | nindent 10 }}
        {{- end }}
        {{- if .podSecurityContext }}
        security_context: {{- .podSecurityContext | toYaml | nindent 10 }}
        {{- end }}
```

**Key details:**
- The Helm values use camelCase (`nodeSelector`, `tolerations`,
`podSecurityContext`) but the container context YAML uses snake_case
(`node_selector`, `tolerations` stays the same, `security_context` for
the pod-level security context).
- `tolerations` is the same in both camelCase and snake_case since it's
a single word.
- `podSecurityContext` maps to `security_context` at the
`pod_spec_config` level (NOT `container_config.security_context` which
is container-level).
- These are placed under `run_k8s_config.pod_spec_config` because they
are V1PodSpec-level fields that affect the launched run jobs.

### 2. No Python changes needed

The `K8sContainerContext.__new__` constructor already accepts
`run_k8s_config` as a parameter (line 80 of `container_context.py`), and
the Helm template constructs the `run_k8s_config` block directly in the
serialized JSON. When this JSON is deserialized, it goes through
`UserDefinedDagsterK8sConfig.from_dict()` which already handles
`pod_spec_config` fields including `node_selector`, `tolerations`, and
`security_context` via `k8s_snake_case_dict` validation against
`kubernetes.client.V1PodSpec`.

The existing merge logic in `K8sContainerContext._merge_k8s_config` /
`_deep_merge_k8s_config` will correctly deep-merge these fields with any
run-level overrides.

**No changes required in:**
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-k8s/dagster_k8s/container_context.py`
— the Python deserialization path already supports these fields via
`run_k8s_config`
- `dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-k8s/dagster_k8s/job.py`
— `UserDefinedDagsterK8sConfig` already validates `pod_spec_config`
against `V1PodSpec`
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-k8s/dagster_k8s/models.py`
— no model changes needed

### 3. Update Helm schema test: `test_code_server_cli`

**File:**
`dagster-oss/helm/dagster/schema/schema_tests/test_user_deployments.py`
**Function:** `test_code_server_cli` (line 1539)

Update the test to include `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, and
`podSecurityContext` in the deployment, then assert they appear in the
serialized `DAGSTER_CONTAINER_CONTEXT`.

**Current deployment construction (line 1540):**
```python
deployment = UserDeployment.construct(
    name="foo",
    image=kubernetes.Image(repository="repo/foo", tag="tag1", pullPolicy="Always"),
    codeServerArgs=["-m", "foo"],
    port=3030,
    includeConfigInLaunchedRuns=UserDeploymentIncludeConfigInLaunchedRuns(enabled=True),
)
```

**Change to:**
```python
deployment = UserDeployment.construct(
    name="foo",
    image=kubernetes.Image(repository="repo/foo", tag="tag1", pullPolicy="Always"),
    codeServerArgs=["-m", "foo"],
    port=3030,
    includeConfigInLaunchedRuns=UserDeploymentIncludeConfigInLaunchedRuns(enabled=True),
    nodeSelector=kubernetes.NodeSelector.parse_obj({"disktype": "ssd"}),
    tolerations=kubernetes.Tolerations.parse_obj(
        [{"key": "key1", "operator": "Exists", "effect": "NoSchedule"}]
    ),
    podSecurityContext=kubernetes.PodSecurityContext.parse_obj(
        {"runAsUser": 1000, "runAsGroup": 3000}
    ),
)
```

**Update the env count assertion** (line 1552): The number of env vars
stays at 3 (DAGSTER_CURRENT_IMAGE, DAGSTER_PG_PASSWORD,
DAGSTER_CONTAINER_CONTEXT).

**Update the container context assertion** (line 1568) to expect the new
fields in `run_k8s_config.pod_spec_config`:
```python
assert json.loads(container_context.value) == {
    "k8s": {
        "image_pull_policy": "Always",
        "env_config_maps": ["release-name-dagster-user-deployments-foo-user-env"],
        "namespace": "default",
        "service_account_name": "release-name-dagster-user-deployments-user-deployments",
        "run_k8s_config": {
            "pod_spec_config": {
                "automount_service_account_token": True,
                "node_selector": {"disktype": "ssd"},
                "tolerations": [
                    {"key": "key1", "operator": "Exists", "effect": "NoSchedule"}
                ],
                "security_context": {"runAsUser": 1000, "runAsGroup": 3000},
            },
        },
    }
}
```

**Important note on the `security_context` key casing:** The Helm
template outputs the raw YAML values as-is from the Helm values. The
`podSecurityContext` values may come through in camelCase (e.g.
`runAsUser`) since they come directly from Helm values without
snake_case conversion. The Python deserialization
(`UserDefinedDagsterK8sConfig.from_dict`) handles this conversion. Check
the actual rendered output to determine whether the test assertion
should use camelCase or snake_case keys inside `security_context`. The
Helm `toYaml` filter preserves the input casing, so if the Helm values
use `runAsUser`, the JSON will contain `runAsUser`. Adjust the test
assertion accordingly.

### 4. Add new Helm schema test:
`test_container_context_with_pod_scheduling_fields`

**File:**
`dagster-oss/helm/dagster/schema/schema_tests/test_user_deployments.py`

Add a new focused test after `test_env_container_context` (after line
1620) that specifically tests all three fields with `dagsterApiGrpcArgs`
(to cover `DAGSTER_CLI_API_GRPC_CONTAINER_CONTEXT`):

```python
def test_container_context_with_pod_scheduling_fields(
    template: HelmTemplate, user_deployment_configmap_template
):
    deployment = UserDeployment.construct(
        name="foo",
        image=kubernetes.Image(repository="repo/foo", tag="tag1", pullPolicy="Always"),
        dagsterApiGrpcArgs=["-m", "foo"],
        port=3030,
        includeConfigInLaunchedRuns=UserDeploymentIncludeConfigInLaunchedRuns(enabled=True),
        nodeSelector=kubernetes.NodeSelector.parse_obj(
            {"disktype": "ssd", "region": "us-east-1"}
        ),
        tolerations=kubernetes.Tolerations.parse_obj(
            [
                {"key": "dedicated", "operator": "Equal", "value": "dagster", "effect": "NoSchedule"},
            ]
        ),
        podSecurityContext=kubernetes.PodSecurityContext.parse_obj(
            {"runAsUser": 1000, "runAsGroup": 3000, "fsGroup": 2000}
        ),
    )
    helm_values = DagsterHelmValues.construct(
        dagsterUserDeployments=UserDeployments.construct(deployments=[deployment])
    )

    [dagster_user_deployment] = template.render(helm_values)
    container_context = dagster_user_deployment.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[2]
    assert container_context.name == "DAGSTER_CLI_API_GRPC_CONTAINER_CONTEXT"
    parsed = json.loads(container_context.value)

    pod_spec_config = parsed["k8s"]["run_k8s_config"]["pod_spec_config"]
    assert pod_spec_config["node_selector"] == {"disktype": "ssd", "region": "us-east-1"}
    assert pod_spec_config["tolerations"] == [
        {"key": "dedicated", "operator": "Equal", "value": "dagster", "effect": "NoSchedule"},
    ]
    assert pod_spec_config["security_context"] == {
        "runAsUser": 1000,
        "runAsGroup": 3000,
        "fsGroup": 2000,
    }
```

### 5. Verify fields are absent when not set

Confirm that the existing `test_code_server_cli` and
`test_env_container_context` tests (which do NOT set these fields)
continue to pass — the Helm template only emits these fields
conditionally with `{{- if ... }}` guards, so they should not appear in
the JSON when unset. (If you modify `test_code_server_cli` per step 3,
create a separate test for the "fields present" case and keep the
original test verifying the "fields absent" case.)

**Recommended approach:** Keep the original `test_code_server_cli`
unchanged (verifying the fields are NOT present when not set), and
create a new test `test_code_server_cli_with_scheduling_fields` that
adds the three fields and verifies they appear.

## Files NOT Changing

-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-k8s/dagster_k8s/container_context.py`
— no Python changes needed; the `run_k8s_config` deserialization path
already supports these fields
- `dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-k8s/dagster_k8s/job.py`
— `UserDefinedDagsterK8sConfig` already handles `pod_spec_config`
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-k8s/dagster_k8s/models.py`
— no model changes
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-k8s/dagster_k8s_tests/unit_tests/test_container_context.py`
— existing Python-side tests already cover `pod_spec_config` field
handling (including `security_context` merge); no new Python unit tests
are required since the fix is purely in the Helm template
-
`dagster-oss/helm/dagster/charts/dagster-user-deployments/templates/deployment-user.yaml`
— the deployment template already renders these fields on the pod; no
changes needed there
-
`dagster-oss/helm/dagster/schema/schema/charts/dagster_user_deployments/subschema/user_deployments.py`
— the `UserDeployment` model already has `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`,
and `podSecurityContext` fields
- CHANGELOG.md — never modify

## Verification

1. **Run the Helm schema tests:**
   ```bash
   cd dagster-oss/helm/dagster/schema
tox -e py312 -- -k "test_code_server_cli or test_env_container_context
   ```

subject: [NO_SKIP] ci(buildkite): migrate dagster-graphql and dagster-test off MEDIUM to EKS (#24646)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Drops the package-level `BuildkiteQueue.MEDIUM` opt-out on
`python_modules/dagster-graphql` and `python_modules/dagster-test`, and
applies a per-factor resource bump on dagster-graphql's gRPC-instance
factors. `dagit` was already moved off MEDIUM in #24406
(`test_cli_logs_to_dagit` polling fix), so it's untouched here.

After this lands, the only OSS step keys still pinned to `MEDIUM` are in
`examples/`, `libraries/`, and the standalone integration test suites —
every core package (`dagster`, `dagit`, `dagster-graphql`,
`dagster-test`) runs on EKS.

This PR is two commits — the first does the queue/resource changes, and
the second is a per-test fix that the migration surfaced (see "Test fix"
below).

## Per-suite resource picks

EKS default is `500m` CPU / no memory request.

### dagster-graphql

The package's tox factor matrix has 13 entries. 7 of them spin up
`GrpcServerProcess` subprocesses through `graphql_context_test_suite`
(the package's `tox.ini` sets `STRICT_GRPC_SERVER_PROCESS_WAIT=1`, so
any flaky subprocess shutdown surfaces as a hard timeout). That's the
same subprocess-heartbeat starvation profile that motivated the
daemon_tests / scheduler_tests bumps to `2000m / 4Gi`, so those 7
factors get the same bump via a shared `_GRAPHQL_GRPC_RESOURCES`
constant. The 6 non-gRPC-instance factors stay on defaults.

| Factor | Splits | Resources | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `not_graphql_context_test_suite` | 2 | default | non-context tests; no
gRPC subprocess |
| `sqlite_instance_multi_location` | 1 | **2000m / 4Gi** | gRPC
multi-location workspace |
| `sqlite_instance_managed_grpc_env` | 2 | **2000m / 4Gi** | managed
gRPC server subprocess |
| `sqlite_instance_deployed_grpc_env` | 2 | **2000m / 4Gi** | deployed
gRPC server subprocess |
| `sqlite_instance_code_server_cli_grpc_env` | 2 | **2000m / 4Gi** |
code-server CLI gRPC subprocess |
| `graphql_python_client` | 1 | default | Python client tests |
| `postgres-graphql_context_variants` | 1 | default | graphql-context
variants only, no instance |
| `postgres-instance_multi_location` | 1 | **2000m / 4Gi** | postgres +
gRPC multi-location |
| `postgres-instance_managed_grpc_env` | 2 | **2000m / 4Gi** | postgres
+ managed gRPC |
| `postgres-instance_deployed_grpc_env` | 2 | **2000m / 4Gi** | postgres
+ deployed gRPC |
| `gql_v3` | 1 | default | gql v3 schema-validation |
| `gql_v3_5` | 1 | default | gql v3.5 schema-validation |

### dagster-test

No bump. 18 test files / 46 test functions / 2 concurrency-using files.
Small package; just drop MEDIUM. Runs on Python 3.10 / 3.11 only (the
`unsupported_python_versions` list already excludes 3.12+ because of
dagster-airflow).

## Test fix (commit 2)

The first push of this branch failed on `dagster-test-3-10 ::
test_python_packages_md_completeness` with "Packages in
python_packages.md but not found in repository: [every documented
package]". Root cause: the test's `find_actual_packages` helper walks
`python_modules/` for `setup.py`/`pyproject.toml`, then filters out
package dirs whose path parts include any of `skip_patterns = {"_tests",
"build", "kitchen-sink", ...}`. The check ran against the **absolute**
`package_dir.parts`, so on EKS where the workspace path is
`/workspace/build/buildkite/dagster-oss/python_modules/...`, every
single package gets skipped because the absolute path contains the
segment `"build"`. The Docker (MEDIUM) queue's workspace path didn't
include `"build"`, so the bug was masked.

Fix: scan `package_dir.relative_to(python_modules_dir).parts` instead of
the absolute parts. Verified locally — both `documented` and `actual`
now report 78 packages with empty diff.

Bundling the test fix into the same PR as the queue migration per the
team convention (the queue toggle is the thing that surfaces the test
bug, so they belong together; same pattern used for the `dagit-3-12` and
`declarative-automation` toggles).

## Mechanism

Two files changed:

-
`dagster-oss/.buildkite/dagster-buildkite/dagster_buildkite/steps/packages.py`
— adds a `_GRAPHQL_GRPC_RESOURCES` module constant
(`ResourceRequests(cpu="2000m", memory="4Gi")`); reformats the 7
gRPC-instance `ToxFactor` entries in dagster-graphql's factor list to
pass `resources=_GRAPHQL_GRPC_RESOURCES`; drops
`queue=BuildkiteQueue.MEDIUM` from both PackageSpec entries.
-
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-test/dagster_test_tests/test_package_registry.py`
— switches the skip-pattern scan in `find_actual_packages` to use
`package_dir.relative_to(python_modules_dir).parts`.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR — in particular `dagster-test-3-10` and
`dagster-test-3-11` (the previously-failing step keys).
- [ ] Verify on a representative build: the migrated step keys
(`dagster-graphql-*` family — all 22 splits across the 13 factors and
Python versions, plus the `dagster-test-*` family) report `agent:
kubernetes-eks`. Inspect a
`dagster-graphql-sqlite-instance-managed-grpc-env-1-2-3-12` pod spec and
confirm `cpu: 2000m, memory: 4Gi` is in the resource requests.
- [ ] Watch the first ~10 master builds post-merge. Expectation: no new
wave of `GrpcServerProcess` timeout / heartbeat-loss flakes on the
bumped factors; no flakes on `dagster-test` or the unbumped
dagster-graphql factors. If anything flakes, follow up with a targeted
per-factor bump.

subject: Unblock master: bump k8s pin, add dagster-cloud to docs, fix agent label test (#24707)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Master has been red on the `internal` Buildkite pipeline for ~6+ hours
straight — only ~4 of the last ~30 master builds passed, and the four
that did slipped through only because their path filters skipped the
affected pytest jobs. The same three deterministic failures recurred on
every other build (confirmed via the AI assessment annotations on builds
#151960, #151959, #151973, etc.). Bundling all three single-line fixes
here so one PR unblocks CI.

## Fixes

### 1. `dagster-k8s` — bump `KUBERNETES_VERSION_UPPER_BOUND` to `"37"`

`kubernetes` 36.0.0 was published to PyPI, which trips
`dagster_k8s_tests/unit_tests/test_version.py::test_latest_version_pin`:

```
assert latest_version.major < parse(KUBERNETES_VERSION_UPPER_BOUND).major   # 36 < 36 → False
```

The actual pyproject pin is already `kubernetes<37` (see
`dagster-oss/python_modules/libraries/dagster-k8s/pyproject.toml` line
14), so the `kubernetes_version.py` tripwire constant is just lagging
the real pin — bumping it to `"37"` syncs them. No production code
changes; no `PatchedApiClient` compatibility surface is touched. Fixes
both `dagster-k8s-default-3-12` and `dagster-k8s-old-kubernetes-3-12`.

### 2. `python_packages.md` — add `dagster-cloud` entry

PR #20797 moved `dagster-cloud` from
`dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` to
`dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` but did not update the
package registry doc.
`dagster_test_tests/test_package_registry.py::test_python_packages_md_completeness`
walks `dagster-oss/python_modules/` and diffs against
`dagster-oss/.claude/python_packages.md`, so the moved package now reads
as undocumented. Adding the entry under "core packages" alongside the
other top-level user-facing publishables (`dagster`, `dagster-graphql`,
etc.) — the path `python_modules/dagster-cloud` is interpreted relative
to `dagster-oss/` by the test's repo-root resolution. Fixes
`dagster-test-3-10`.

### 3. `test_build_agent_deployment` — add new label to expected dict

PR #24129 added a third label (`app.kubernetes.io/name:
serverless-agent`) to the serverless agent pod template in
`k8s_serverless_manager.py::_build_agent_deployment`, for log-trace
correlation. The snapshot-style dict-equality assertion in the unit test
wasn't updated, so it fails deterministically with a `KeyError`-style
diff on the missing key. Adding the label to the expected dict. Fixes
`dagster-cloud-backend-daemon-3-12`.

**Supersedes #24703**, which was Semur's draft fix covering only this
third item.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI green on this branch — specifically `dagster-k8s-default-3-12`,
`dagster-k8s-old-kubernetes-3-12`, `dagster-test-3-10`, and
`dagster-cloud-backend-daemon-3-12` should all pass.
- [ ] After merge, the next clean master build should drop from ~3–5
deterministic failures back to whatever real flakes remain.

subject: [exec] do not gate downstream on missing blocking asset check outputs (#24641)
body:
## Summary

Fixes [dagster#33351](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/issues/33351). A blocking check that does not emit a result (e.g a dbt test that dbt declined to run under `indirect_selection: cautious` or `buildable`) no longer silently skips downstream assets — a warning is logged instead. Failed blocking checks continue to fail the step (and the run) as before.

## Root cause

PR [dagster#32194](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/pull/32194) changed the planner wiring so that the asset output and blocking-check output for an asset are separate gating dependencies (rather than a `FromMultipleSources` fan-in). That correctly fixed the case the PR targeted — asset skipped + check produced → downstream incorrectly ran — but also changed the **inverse** case as wellt:

|  | asset output | check output | pre-#32194 | post-#32194 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #32194's target | skipped | produced | downstream ran (bug) | downstream skips ✓ | downstream skips ✓ |
| **#33351 regression** | **produced** | **missing** | **downstream ran** | **downstream skips ✗** | **downstream runs ✓** |
| failure path | produced | failed (ERROR) | step fails, run fails | step fails, run fails | step fails, run fails |

## Fix

In `active.py` (`_should_skip_step` and `_all_upstream_outputs_produced`), distinguish asset-check output deps from regular asset output deps via `StepOutputProperties.asset_check_key`. Asset output absence still gates downstream (preserving #32194's intended fix); check output absence is logged as a warning but does not gate. The existing failure path (which raises `DagsterAssetCheckFailedError` in `execute_step.py` when a blocking check yields `passed=False, severity=ERROR`) is untouched, so failed blocking checks still fail the step and the run.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_blocking_check_optional` (existing test from #32194) still passes — asset skipped + check produced → downstream skips.
- [x] New `test_blocking_check_missing_result_does_not_skip_downstream` — asset produced + blocking check not emitted → downstream runs, warning logged.
- [x] All 26 tests in `test_dynamic_execution.py` pass.
- [x] All 109 tests in `dynamic_tests/` + `execution_plan_tests/` pass.
- [x] All 115 asset-check-related tests in `definitions_tests/` pass.
- [ ] CI sweep across the rest of the suite.

## Changelog entry (suggested)

> **Bugfixes** — Fixed a regression introduced in [version containing #32194] where a blocking asset check that did not emit a result could silently cause downstream assets to be skipped. Missing blocking check results now allow downstream assets to proceed (matching the documented contract that `blocking` gates on a _failed_ check result, not on _absence_), and a warning is logged so the absent evaluation is visible. Failed blocking checks continue to fail the step and the run as before. This restores pre-1.12.x behavior for dbt users on `indirect_selection: cautious` or `buildable`.

subject: Move dagster-cloud package to dagster-oss/python_modules (#20797)
body:
## Summary Relocates the `dagster-cloud` user-facing agent package from `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` to `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/`, alongside the other core Dagster packages (`dagster`, `dagster-graphql`, `dagster-cloud-cli`, etc.). The package itself is unchanged — only its location. ## What changed - **Physical move** of the package tree via `git mv`, preserving history. - **Workspace config** (root `pyproject.toml`): updated `[tool.uv.sources]`, pyright/ty `extraPaths` and `executionEnvironments`, ruff `per-file-ignores`, and removed it from `[tool.uv.workspace].members`. - **Buildkite pipeline** (`.buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/`): updated `KUBERNETES_TOX_MODULES`, `get_tox_env_suffixes`, `get_tox_splits`, `get_tox_steps`, and dogfood path detection to point at the new location. - **Release automation** (`automation_internal/release/dagster_module_publisher.py`): `dagster-cloud` now created with `is_cloud=False, internal_oss_repo_path` and removed from `expected_cloud_modules_subdirectories`. - **Shadow CLI** (`automation_internal/cloud/shadow/cli.py`): `dagster_cloud_dir` now resolves under `dagster-oss/python_modules/`. - **Docker image build defs** (`automation_internal/image/defs/{agent,user_code,serverless,examples,release,dagster_cloud_pex}.py`): `copy_directories` entries point at the new path. - **Service Dockerfiles + lockfiles** (`services/{dagster-cloud-agent-pre-license,dagster-cloud-examples,dagster-cloud-serverless-{agent,base,k8s-agent},dagster-cloud-user-code,release-pipeline}/`): updated each service's `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock` to reference the new editable path; dropped now-unused `COPY build_cache/dagster-cloud/python_modules` lines in Dockerfiles whose image defs no longer stage anything at that path (kept it for serverless-agent and serverless-k8s-agent, which still stage sibling packages there). - **Root `uv.lock`**: editable path updated in all 12 locations. - **Shell scripts** (6 files), integration test + module `tox.ini` files (~14 files), and the `python_modules/{toys,insights-consumption-test}` + `dagster-dg-cli` Dockerfile templates: relative/absolute path references updated. ## Test plan - [ ] CI green on this branch (this PR exists primarily to validate that — the previous build's 311 cascading `broken` jobs were all downstream of the Cloud Docker image builds failing on stale `build_cache/dagster-cloud/python_modules` references) - [ ] `just ruff`, `just pyright`, `just ty` clean for the moved package - [ ] `tox -e py312-default` from `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` - [ ] A dependent package (e.g. `dagster-cloud-backend`) still resolves its dagster-cloud dep - [ ] `just host-cloud` smoke test Closes #20663 ## Implementation Plan
Implementation Plan (Plan #20797) This change relocates the `dagster-cloud` user-facing agent package from `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` to `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/`, aligning it with other core Dagster packages like `dagster`, `dagster-graphql`, and `dagster-cloud-cli`. This consolidation improves the repository structure by colocating all user-facing Python packages under `dagster-oss/`. ## Files Changed
Files Changed ### Moved (1 directory tree) - `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` → `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` - User-facing agent package with all source, tests, and configuration ### Modified (50+ files) - `pyproject.toml` - Updated workspace members, uv sources, pyright paths, and ruff config - `.buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/pipeline.py` - Updated tox module path and test configurations - `.buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/steps/dogfood/__init__.py` - Updated file change detection paths - `python_modules/automation-internal/automation_internal/release/dagster_module_publisher.py` - Updated module creation and validation logic - `python_modules/automation-internal/automation_internal/cloud/shadow/cli.py` - Updated dagster_cloud_dir resolution - `python_modules/automation-internal/automation_internal/image/defs/*.py` - Updated package paths in all Docker image builders - Integration test `tox.ini` files (5 files) - Updated relative dependency paths - Service shell scripts (4 files) - Updated pip installation paths - Module `tox.ini` files (9 files) - Updated relative dependency paths - Dockerfiles (3 files) - Updated COPY and pip install commands
## Key Changes - Physical move of package directory tree with git history preservation - Updated uv workspace configuration to reference new path via editable path dependency - Modified all CI/CD paths in Buildkite pipeline configuration and dogfood test detection - Updated release automation to resolve package from new OSS location with `is_cloud=False` - Fixed all relative and absolute path references across 50+ configuration files and shell scripts - Removed dagster-cloud from workspace members list while keeping path-based dependency resolution - Updated ruff linter configuration with new path for test file ignores
## Implementation Plan
Implementation Plan (Issue #20663) # Plan: Move `dagster-cloud` package to `dagster-oss/python_modules` ## Context The `dagster-cloud` Python package (the user-facing agent package published to PyPI) currently lives at `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` within the internal repo. The goal is to move it to `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` so it sits alongside other core packages like `dagster`, `dagster-graphql`, etc. The package path is hardcoded in 50+ locations across the repo: workspace config, type checker paths, Buildkite CI, Docker image builds, release automation, shell scripts, tox.ini files, and Dockerfiles. --- ## Phase 1: Physical Move **Action:** Move (git mv) `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/` to `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/`. This includes `dagster_cloud/`, `dagster_cloud_tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `tox.ini`, etc. --- ## Phase 2: Root `pyproject.toml` **File:** `pyproject.toml` | Section | Change | |---------|--------| | `[tool.uv.workspace].members` (L426) | Remove `"dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` | | `[tool.uv.sources]` (L369) | `dagster-cloud = { workspace = true }` -> `dagster-cloud = { path = "dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud", editable = true }` | | `[tool.pyright].extraPaths` (L120) | `"dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` -> `"dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` | | `[tool.pyright].executionEnvironments` (L199) | `root = "dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` -> `root = "dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` | | `[tool.ty.environment].extra-paths` (L212) | `"dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` -> `"dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` | | `[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]` (L343) | `"dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/..."` -> `"dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/..."` | --- ## Phase 3: Release Pipeline ### `python_modules/automation-internal/automation_internal/release/dagster_module_publisher.py` 1. **L102-104** -- Change dagster-cloud module creation: ```python # Before DagsterModule.create_dagster_module("dagster-cloud", internal_repo_path, is_cloud=True, is_internal=True) # After DagsterModule.create_dagster_module("dagster-cloud", internal_oss_repo_path, is_cloud=False, is_internal=True) ``` With `is_cloud=False` and `git_root=internal_oss_repo_path`, `_get_module_path` resolves to `{internal_repo}/dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud` -- the correct new location. 2. **L213-223** -- Remove `"dagster-cloud"` from `expected_cloud_modules_subdirectories`. 3. **`check_cloud_module_publishing()` (L273-291)** -- No change needed; `dagster-cloud` is still in `self.cloud_modules` so the check still finds it. 4. **`get_cloud_module_directories()` (L506-518)** -- No change needed; scanning `dagster-cloud/python_modules/` just won't find dagster-cloud there anymore, which is correct since it was removed from the expected list. ### `dagster_module.py` -- No changes needed `_get_module_path` handles the new case automatically via the existing `is_library=False` fallback. --- ## Phase 4: Buildkite CI ### `.buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/pipeline.py` | Line | Change | |------|--------| | L78 (KUBERNETES_TOX_MODULES) | `"dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` -> `"dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` | | L85 (get_tox_env_suffixes) | `== "dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` -> `== "dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` | | L94 (get_tox_splits) | `== "dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` -> `== "dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` | | L310-329 (get_tox_steps) | The `glob.glob("dagster-cloud/python_modules/*")` loop (L321) will no longer find `dagster-cloud`. Add an explicit entry for `"dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` to the tox_build_steps, using the same pattern (env_suffixes, splits, timeout, queue selection). | ### `.buildkite/dagster_internal_buildkite/steps/dogfood/__init__.py` Update `files_changed(...)` paths: - `"dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/dagster_cloud/workspace/ecs/"` -> `"dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/dagster_cloud/workspace/ecs/"` - `"dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/dagster_cloud_tests/workspace_tests/ecs_tests/"` -> `"dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/dagster_cloud_tests/workspace_tests/ecs_tests/"` --- ## Phase 5: Docker Image Definitions All in `python_modules/automation-internal/automation_internal/image/defs/`: | File | Change | |------|--------| | `agent.py` L35 | `"dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` -> `"dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud"` | | `agent.py` L163 | Same change (serverless agent context) | | `serverless.py` | Same change | | `release.py` | Same change | | `examples.py` | Same change | | `dagster_cloud_pex.py` | Same change | Note: References to `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud-serverless-agent` (agent.py L164) stay unchanged -- that's a different package. --- ## Phase 6: Shadow CLI **File:** `python_modules/automation-internal/automation_internal/cloud/shadow/cli.py` The `dagster_cloud_dir` construction (~L365) currently resolves via `cloud_modules_dir = os.path.join(internal_dir, "dagster-cloud/python_modules")` then `os.path.join(cloud_modules_dir, "dagster-cloud/dagster_cloud")`. Change the dagster_cloud_dir line to: ```python os.path.join(internal_dir, "dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/dagster_cloud") ``` The `cloud_modules_dir` variable is still used for `dagster-cloud-dagit` and `dagster-cloud-backend`, so it stays. --- ## Phase 7: Shell Scripts | File | Change (old path -> new path) | |------|------| | `services/dagster-cloud-pex/local_build.sh` | `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud` -> `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud` | | `scripts/buildkite/deploy_user_cloud_ecs.sh` | Same | | `scripts/buildkite/release/launch_release_pipeline.sh` | Same | | `scripts/buildkite/release/sync_release_pipeline.sh` | Same | | `dagster-cloud/sandbox/user_cloud/from_source/docker_pex/build.sh` | Same | | `dagster-cloud/sandbox/host_cloud_docker/build.sh` | Same | --- ## Phase 8: Dockerfiles | File | Change | |------|--------| | `python_modules/toys/Dockerfile` | `-e './internal/dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud[insights]'` -> `-e './internal/dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud[insights]'` | | `python_modules/insights-consumption-test/Dockerfile` | Same | | `dagster-oss/.../dagster-dg-cli/.../deploy_uv_editable_Dockerfile.jinja` | `COPY --from=internal dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud ...` -> `COPY --from=internal dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud ...` | The host cloud Dockerfile (`services/dagster-cloud-host/Dockerfile`) already copies `dagster-oss/` (and the new location is within it), so the package will be included. The bulk `COPY dagster-cloud/ dagster-cloud/` line just won't include the dagster-cloud package anymore. Verify the uv lockfile install step resolves correctly after lockfile regen. --- ## Phase 9: tox.ini Files (Relative Path Updates) All `../../dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud` -> `../../dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud` (and similar for deeper paths): **Internal python_modules (depth 2):** - `python_modules/product-operations/tox.ini` - `python_modules/web-performance-telemetry/tox.ini` - `python_modules/toys/tox.ini` - `python_modules/dagster-yaml-demo/tox.ini` - `python_modules/purina-sales/tox.ini` - `python_modules/dogfood/tox.ini` - `python_modules/dagster-cloud-examples/tox.ini` **Infrastructure (depth 4: `../../../../`):** - `infra/k8s/agent/agent-schema/tox.ini` - `infra/k8s/multitenant_host/host-schema/tox.ini` **Integration tests (depth 4: `../../../../`):** - `dagster-cloud/integration_tests/test_suites/local_dagster_cloud/tox.ini` - `dagster-cloud/integration_tests/test_suites/prod_canary_tests/tox.ini` - `dagster-cloud/integration_tests/test_suites/kubernetes_dagster_cloud/tox.ini` - `dagster-cloud/integration_tests/test_suites/dogfood_serverless_tests/tox.ini` - `dagster-cloud/integration_tests/test_suites/multitenant_canary_tests/tox.ini` **Dev requirements:** - `python_modules/purina/dev_requirements.txt` --- ## Phase 10: Cloud Package tox.ini Files Other packages under `dagster-cloud/python_modules/` that depend on `dagster-cloud` (backend, dagit, worker, ursula, insights, etc.) likely have tox.ini entries referencing `../dagster-cloud`. After the move, this relative path changes -- the package is no longer a sibling. These need to become absolute or differently-relative paths. For a package at `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud-backend/tox.ini`, the old relative path `../dagster-cloud` becomes `../../../dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud`. Check all tox.ini files under `dagster-cloud/python_modules/*/tox.ini` for references. --- ## Phase 11: Lock File and Sync ```bash just rebuild_uv_lock_file # Regenerate uv.lock just sync # Sync environment ``` --- ## Phase 12: Verification 1. `just ruff` -- formatting/lint passes 2. `just pyright` -- type checking resolves the new path 3. Run dagster-cloud tox suite from new location 4. Run a dependent package's tox suite (e.g., dagster-cloud-backend) to verify cross-package deps resolve 5. Verify `just host-cloud` still starts (smoke test) --- ## Open Questions 1. **OSS install script** (`dagster-oss/scripts/install_dev_python_modules.py`): Should `dagster-cloud` be added to this list? This script is for OSS-only development. Since dagster-cloud won't be in the public mirror, it likely should NOT be added. 2. **dagster-cloud's own tox.ini**: After moving, its relative paths to other dagster-cloud packages (backend, dagit) and to dagster-oss libraries change. The tox.ini at `dagster-cloud/python_modules/dagster-cloud/tox.ini` (which will move to `dagster-oss/python_modules/dagster-cloud/tox.ini`) needs inspection -- relative paths like `../../dagster-cloud-backend` would no longer work from the new location.

subject: Revert "fix(dagster-test): localhost fallback in buildkite_hostnames_cm for non-container runners (#24675)" (#24688)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Reverts #24675 and quarantines the airbyte integration suite it tried to
fix.

#24675 added a `localhost` fallback in `buildkite_hostnames_cm` so the
EKS runner could survive the `KeyError: 'airbyte-webapp'` flake in
`dagster-airbyte-integration`. The fallback broke nearly every other
consumer of `docker_compose_cm` — see [build
151863](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151863), where ~25
dagster-cloud test jobs failed with `psycopg2.OperationalError:
connection to server at "localhost" ... port 5432 failed: Connection
refused`.

### Why the fallback broke things

The PR claimed: "the failure mode will shift from KeyError to a
connection error if their compose files don't publish ports — strictly a
better failure mode" and "None of those consumers are currently red on
master with this signature." Both turned out to be wrong:

- `dagster-cloud/docker-compose-test.yaml` **does** publish ports, but
on remapped host ports (`5433:5432` for postgres, `6380:6379` for redis,
`6433:6432` for pgbouncer). The storage fixtures hardcode the
container-side port (e.g.
`psycopg2.connect(host=hostnames["test_main_shard"], port=5432)`), so
`localhost:5432` had nothing listening.
- Pre-PR those tests worked because the old code returned bridge-network
IPs (e.g. `172.18.0.2`), which the EKS pod can reach via shared netns
with the dind sidecar — port 5432 on `172.18.0.2` is the container port,
which works.

dagster-cloud-backend / dagster-cloud-dagit / ursula /
dagster-cloud-worker are all `docker_compose_cm` consumers, not just
airbyte; the PR's scope analysis missed them.

### Soft-failing airbyte integration

Reverting brings back the `KeyError: 'airbyte-webapp'` flake. Until a
real fix lands (one that keeps the bridge-IP path intact and just waits
for IPAM to settle), this PR quarantines `dagster-airbyte` `integration`
with `soft_fail=True`. The unit factor is unaffected. The job still runs
and reports its status; failures no longer fail the build.

Adds a `soft_fail` field on `ToxFactor` and threads it through
`build_tox_step` → `CommandStepBuilder.soft_fail()`.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI on this PR is green (and in particular, every dagster-cloud
test job that was red on 151863 is green).
- [ ] Master builds post-merge no longer show the `Connection refused` /
`port 5432` signature.
- [ ] `dagster-airbyte-integration-3-12` shows up as soft-fail when it
flakes, not as a build-blocker.

## Changelog

NOCHANGELOG

Internal-RevId: ff12c4a9cbcfcf2e88cdb24f016ee75e34c54bd7

subject: fix(dagster-test): localhost fallback in buildkite_hostnames_cm for non-container runners (#24675)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring `KeyError: 'airbyte-webapp'` flake in `:pytest:
dagster-airbyte-integration-3-12` on master (e.g. [build
151730](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151730),
[151754](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151754)). The
previous fixes that targeted this job — pytest-timeout bump (#24654),
per-request timeout (#24562) — addressed a different symptom (the
`sync_and_poll` timeout); the dominant failure mode on master is now a
`KeyError` at fixture setup, before any test body runs.

## Root cause

The fixture `docker_compose_airbyte_instance_fixture`
(`test_managed_elements.py:54`) does `webapp_host =
hostnames["airbyte-webapp"]`. That dict is built by
`buildkite_hostnames_cm` in
`dagster-test/dagster_test/fixtures/docker_compose.py`:

1. `current_container()` reads `/etc/hostname` and runs `docker ps
--filter id=<hostname>` to find the buildkite agent's own container
name.
2. `connect_container_to_network(<container>, <network>)` joins the
agent to the compose network.
3. `hostnames(<network>)` iterates `list_containers()` and, for each
running container, reads `NetworkSettings.Networks[<network>].IPAddress`
from `docker inspect`.

On the legacy buildkite-agent layout (agent is a docker container, runs
on EC2 host), all three steps work. On the EKS layout (kube pod + dind
sidecar) — which `dagster-airbyte/integration` now uses, since it
declares `docker_cpu`/`docker_memory` resource requests in `packages.py`
— step 1 returns empty: the pod's `/etc/hostname` is the kube pod name,
which is not a container ID dind knows about. Step 2 then runs `docker
network connect <network> ""` and gets `invalid container name or ID:
value is empty` from docker — silently logged as `WARNING
root:docker_compose.py:352 Unable to connect to network
integration_default.` (note the double space).

The empty `current_container()` is not directly the cause of the
`KeyError`, though. Step 3 is independent of step 2 — `docker inspect`
returns each container's per-network IP regardless of who's connected.
The real failure is that step 2 doubled as an implicit IPAM barrier on
the legacy layout: `docker network connect` doesn't return until
docker's IPAM is in a settled state for that network. Without it, step 3
races IPAM. `docker compose up --detach` returns when containers are
`Started`, but the per-network `IPAddress` field is populated
asynchronously around container start. If `docker inspect` runs before
IPAM has populated, the container is either missing from `docker ps` or
present with empty `IPAddress` — either way the `if hostname:` guard in
`hostnames()` drops it from the returned dict. Next lookup → `KeyError`.

This is why the flake is intermittent. Comparing two recent master runs:

- [Build 151730](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151730)
(FAIL): IPAM hadn't populated `airbyte-webapp`'s IP by the time
`hostnames()` ran. Dict missing the key. `KeyError` on every test/rerun
(4 errors, identical stack).
- [Build 151763](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151763)
(mostly PASS — 6 passed, 1 unrelated): IPAM had populated in time. Dict
had the key, with value `172.18.0.2` (the bridge-network IP). Test
proceeded and one test failed for an unrelated reason (`Max retries
exceeded with url: http://172.18.0.2:80/api/v1/sources/discover_schema`
— Airbyte HTTP API not yet healthy).

Both runs log the same `Unable to connect to network …` warning.
`current_container()` empty is constant on EKS; the IPAM race is the
actual flake.

## Fix

In `buildkite_hostnames_cm`, when `current_container()` returns empty,
skip the doomed `docker network connect`/`disconnect` calls and yield
`{container_name: "localhost" for container_name in list_containers()}`
— the same dict the non-BUILDKITE path already yields for local-dev
runs. This sidesteps the IPAM race entirely: port mappings published by
docker-compose are baked in at container creation, not allocated
asynchronously, so `localhost:<published-port>` works as soon as the
container is `Started`. The pod and dind sidecar share their network
namespace in the EKS layout, so port-mapped services on the dind daemon
are reachable from the test process via localhost.

The airbyte integration fixture already special-cases this:

```python
webapp_host = hostnames["airbyte-webapp"]
webapp_port = "8000" if webapp_host == "localhost" else "80"
```

and the compose file declares `ports: - 8000:80` for `airbyte-webapp`.
So nothing needs to change in the test or compose — `webapp_host =
"localhost"` → `webapp_port = "8000"` → matches the published port →
test's existing connection-retry loop handles the brief window before
the webapp is actually listening.

## Scope

- This affects every consumer of `docker_compose_cm` on the EKS agent
layout (also `dagster-postgres`/`dagster-airflow`/`dagster-docker` test
fixtures), not just airbyte. For consumers whose tests don't already
handle the `localhost` value, the failure mode will shift from
`KeyError` to a connection error if their compose files don't publish
ports — strictly a better failure mode than `KeyError`, and a signal to
add a port mapping. None of those consumers are currently red on master
with this signature; airbyte was the only one regularly flaking, because
it's the only EKS-migrated `docker_compose_cm` consumer that exercises a
multi-service compose stack with timing-sensitive IPAM.
- The legacy buildkite-agent path is unchanged: when
`current_container()` resolves (it does on the legacy layout), the
existing code path runs and the agent still joins the compose network as
before.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI on this PR runs `dagster-airbyte-integration-3-12` and it
passes.
- [ ] Watch the next ~10 master builds post-merge — the `KeyError:
'airbyte-webapp'` signature should not recur. If a different airbyte
failure surfaces (e.g. Airbyte HTTP API timeouts), that's the separate
`sync_and_poll` flake also seen on master and needs its own fix.

Internal-RevId: eabd3abf090fb53a7a0bf22938ff6e81bfe9618d

subject: fix: tolerate airflow subprocess teardown race in airflow_home fixture (#24625)
body:
Fixes a flaky teardown in `:pytest: dagster-airlift-3-10`. Test passes;
fixture teardown errors:

```
__________________ ERROR at teardown of test_dagster_operator __________________
E   OSError: [Errno 39] Directory not empty: '/tmp/tmph7migukh'
```

Repro: [build
151604](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151604#019e41fd-51fe-4286-9bfb-4a69e4cfab22)
— `83 passed, 2 skipped, 1 error in 180.64s`.

The `airflow_home` fixture is a `TemporaryDirectory`. Airflow standalone
spawns webserver/scheduler/triggerer subprocesses; after
`_graceful_kill_process_group` returns, a straggler can still flush
log/sqlite state into `AIRFLOW_HOME`, so `TemporaryDirectory.__exit__`'s
final `os.rmdir` races and raises `ENOTEMPTY`.

Fix: swap to `tempfile.mkdtemp()` + `shutil.rmtree(...,
ignore_errors=True)` in a `finally`. Same pattern the perf-harness
conftest already uses for the same race.

subject: Fix two concurrency test flakes (#24597)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Two CI flake mitigations surfaced by [build
#151488](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151488):

- `TestLocalE2E::test_concurrency` — when the pool limit is set to 0,
the block can fire at either the launch→`STARTED` transition or at step
execution. Only the second path matched the existing regex, so the first
path raised `"Timed out waiting for launched run to start"` and tripped
`pytest.raises`. Widened the regex to accept both messages; both prove
the same invariant.
- `TestSqliteEventLogStorage::test_threaded_concurrency` — 100 threads
contending a 5-slot SQLite pool inside `TOTAL_TIMEOUT_TIME=30`
periodically blows the budget on noisy BK agents. Bumped to 90s. Test is
already `@pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=2)`; this addresses the underlying
timing sensitivity rather than papering over with more retries.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI on this PR.

subject: ci(buildkite): migrate remaining python_modules/dagster MEDIUM tests to EKS (#24644)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Drops the `BuildkiteQueue.MEDIUM` opt-outs from the last five `python_modules/dagster` tox factors and moves them to `KUBERNETES_EKS`, applying per-suite resource bumps where the test content warrants one. The MEDIUM deny-list introduced in #24276 has been peeled off incrementally as per-test fixes and per-suite resource bumps landed (#24393 storage, #24485 declarative_automation, the daemon/scheduler bumps); this PR clears the remaining `python_modules/dagster` entries.

After this lands, `python_modules/dagster` has no `MEDIUM` queue overrides left. The MEDIUM annotations elsewhere in `packages.py` (examples, `dagster-graphql`, `dagster-test`, library packages) are out of scope.

## Per-suite resource picks

EKS default is `500m` CPU / no memory request. Each picked bump has a specific in-suite justification:

| Suite | Resources | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| `cli_tests` (splits=2) | `cpu=2000m, memory=2Gi` | 24 files spawn subprocesses (Click `dagster …` invocations) and several spin up gRPC workspace/dev servers (`test_grpc_server_workspace`, `test_dagster_dev_command`). Same CPU-starvation profile that drove `daemon_tests` to its bump. |
| `core_tests` | default | 1491 tests but no concentrated gRPC / threading / subprocess pattern. The "mixed timing" note from #24276 plausibly traces to cluster-level pressure since fixed by #24021 (Karpenter cap 2000→4000) and #24241 (k8s pod-CPU rebalance). Ship on defaults; if it flakes, follow up with a targeted bump or per-test fix. |
| `general_tests` | `cpu=2000m, memory=4Gi` | Houses the `grpc_tests/` subtree — `test_heartbeat`, `test_persistent`, `test_watch_server`, `test_grpc_server_registry`, `test_health_check`. This is the same subprocess-heartbeat starvation pattern that drove the `daemon_tests` 4Gi bump (gRPC code-server's heartbeat thread getting starved on the default CPU budget). |
| `general_tests_old_protobuf` | `cpu=2000m, memory=4Gi` | Runs the same `general_tests/` suite against an older protobuf install matrix; matches `general_tests`. |
| `execution_tests/misc_execution_tests` | `cpu=2000m, memory=4Gi` | Contains `test_interrupt`, `test_run_cancellation_thread`, and `test_run_metrics_thread` — timing-sensitive threading tests with the same CPU-scheduling sensitivity as `daemon_tests`. |

## Mechanism

One file changed: `dagster-oss/.buildkite/dagster-buildkite/dagster_buildkite/steps/packages.py`.

- Each of the five `ToxFactor` entries above is rewritten: the `queue=BuildkiteQueue.MEDIUM` opt-out is removed (defaulting to EKS), and `resources=ResourceRequests(...)` is added where justified, with an inline comment naming the in-suite tests that motivate the bump.
- For the `execution_tests/misc_execution_tests` case, `tox_factors_for_folder` is extended with a new optional `resources_overrides: Mapping[str, ResourceRequests]` parameter that parallels the existing `queue_overrides`. This keeps the execution_tests auto-discovery intact (so new subfolders pick up steps automatically) while still letting us pin resources on individual entries. The existing `queue_overrides` parameter is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR (build runs on the new queue layout itself).

subject: fix: mcp crashes but stays "healthy" to kubernetes (#24594)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Keep the MCP from going down in a way that is undetectable to kubernetes. This was a known issue in older versions of the python `mcp` library, which was fixed by https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/841 . We have to update to at least the oldest version with that fix (we are currently on a very old one).

This seems to have transitively updated a few dependencies, and also picked up some updates that existed in root, but not in the lockfiles subprojects (ty, for instance), which is a red flag for how our dependencies are currently managed.

## Test Plan

ci/cd, continuing to monitor deployed dogfood to see if the issue reoccurs.

subject: Propagate UV_* env vars into tox testenv passenv via TOX_OVERRIDE so subprocess uv resolves inherit UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER (#24607)
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Follow-up to #24601 (which set `UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER=48h` in the buildkite
pre-command hook). That fix only got us partway — `tox` strips host env
vars via per-testenv `passenv` allowlists, so for any pytest job that
spawns a subprocess `uv sync` (most prominently the scaffold-based tests
like `dagster-cloud-dagit-auth-tests-3-12`'s
`subprocess.run([create-dagster, project, …, --uv-sync])`), the env var
never made it into the test subprocess, and the inner `uv sync --group
dev` continued to resolve freely against PyPI.

Evidence on master after #24601 landed ([build
151553](https://buildkite.com/dagster/internal/builds/151553)): the
pre-command hook log shows `# UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER added` and tox-uv's own
env-build phase honored the cutoff (airbyte tox env: `Solving with
exclude-newer: global: 2026-05-17T19:38:43Z` → `yarl==1.23.0`), but the
`dagit-auth-tests` test fixture's inner `create-dagster project
--uv-sync` still failed with `subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command
['uv', 'sync', '--group', 'dev']` because tox had stripped
`UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER` from the test process's env.

## Fix

This PR appends `UV_*` to every tox testenv's `passenv` via tox's
`TOX_OVERRIDE` env var:

```bash
export TOX_OVERRIDE='testenv.passenv+=UV_*'
```

`TOX_OVERRIDE` injects CLI-style overrides into every `tox` invocation
in the buildkite step. `testenv.passenv+=UV_*` appends `UV_*` to the
existing `passenv` (without replacing it), so we don't have to touch the
161 individual `tox.ini` files. Any future `UV_*` env we add to the hook
(`UV_INDEX_URL`, etc.) is automatically covered.

Applied to both pre-command hooks for symmetry with #24601:
- `.buildkite/hooks/pre-command` (internal pipeline)
- `dagster-oss/.buildkite/hooks/pre-command` (oss-tests / community PRs
/ `DAGSTER_OSS_STEP=1` paths)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Master goes green once this lands — specifically the
scaffold-based pytest shards (`dagster-cloud-dagit-auth-tests`, plus any
future PRs that re-run `create-dagster-3-12` / `dagster-dg-cli-*`) stop
seeing the `cp310-only` wheel error on subprocess `uv sync`.
- [ ] A representative job log shows `Resolving … with --override
testenv.passenv+=UV_*` from tox's startup banner, and the inner scaffold
`uv sync` shows `Solving with exclude-newer: <date>` in debug output.

## Followup

[FW-895](https://linear.app/dagster-labs/issue/FW-895/proxy-ci-pypi-traffic-through-devpi-with-a-48h-upload-date-filter)
tracks the longer-term fix: wire CI through the
already-deployed-but-unused devpi mirror
(`infra/k8s/buildkite/base/devpi.yaml`) with a 48h upload-date filter,
baked into test images so we don't need either env-var workaround.
